WAVE 57 REFUSED the Stripe period-end sync on this ground rather than sequencing it (charter D672). This row is the
prerequisite, and it is a SCHEMA problem, not a sequencing one.

`current_period_end` serves three meanings at once: the dunning grace anchor (`mark_past_due/2` ->
`default_grace_anchor/0`, billing.ex:827/:837, now + @grace_days 3), trial expiry, and — if anyone ever syncs it —
Stripe's renewal date. `entitled?/1` (:1267) and `maybe_enforce/1` (:883) both branch on exactly that column.

THREE HAZARDS, ALL DRIVEN in wave 57's verify round against a sync a builder would plausibly write:
  (a) EXTENDS — a signed customer.subscription.updated carrying a renewal 27 days out moves the grace anchor ~24 days
      and the team stays entitled: a 3-day grace silently becomes ~27 days of free running boxes. (Negative control:
      the same event with the sync off does not move the anchor, so the result is the sync, not the fixture.)
  (b) SHORTENS / SUSPENDS IN-BAND — a Stripe-sourced period end in the PAST flips entitled? to false and suspends the
      team's boxes on the spot.
  (c) THE ARM NOBODY NAMED — stripe_gateway.ex:225-234 sends exactly two headers and NO `Stripe-Version`, so the
      payload shape follows the ACCOUNT's default API version, unpinned by this tree. An unguarded read of an ABSENT
      `current_period_end` writes nil, and a past_due row with a nil anchor is `entitled?` TRUE FOREVER while
      `maybe_enforce/1` no-ops on `is_nil(pe)` — an unpaid box that never suspends and never expires. `Map.put_new_lazy`
      is DEFEATED by an explicitly-present nil key.

The likely shape is a separate `grace_ends_at` column (or an explicit, tested refusal to store Stripe's value at all),
plus pinning `Stripe-Version` so the payload shape stops being whatever the account defaults to. There is already an
armed guard on the other side: promise_actor_manifest_test.exs:548 REDS the moment a paid plan stores a
current_period_end — whatever lands here must keep that meaningful rather than delete it.

<!-- barkpark:acceptance:start -->
### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The grace anchor no longer shares a column with Stripe's renewal date — either a dedicated column exists, or the refusal to store Stripe's value is explicit and tested.
- [ ] A test drives the EXTENDS hazard (a far-future period end) and asserts the grace window does NOT move, and it reds when the separation is reverted.
- [ ] A test drives the ABSENT-FIELD hazard (no current_period_end in the payload) and asserts a past_due team does NOT become entitled forever; is_nil(pe) no longer means 'no enforcement'.
- [ ] StripeGateway pins an explicit Stripe-Version header so the webhook payload shape is a decision this tree makes rather than an account default, with the version recorded in the moduledoc.
- [ ] promise_actor_manifest_test.exs:548's armed assertion is still meaningful after the change (re-pointed, not deleted), and the PR body says how.
<!-- barkpark:acceptance:end -->

Parent epic: #6842

## Context

Small screening runs are promising but not sufficient for provider decisions:

- Exact router-prompt battery, 24 calls/model: Haiku 4.5 and GPT-5.6 Luna both produced valid JSON 24/24 and scored 21/24 against the strict fixture. Luna was about 83% cheaper and 21% faster at median latency.
- Full-prompt Gemini 3.7 Flash screen: useful visible answers in 10/12 cases; two malformed function-call failures mapped to Anthropic-specific orchestration.
- Production comparison did not show a clear Sonnet 5 quality regression, although output-token/cost behavior needs monitoring.

## Goal

Create versioned, privacy-safe replay gates that support model/provider decisions and staged rollout.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A fixed trace suite covers surface policy, knowledge, member context, admin reads, safe mutations, tool errors, prompt injection, date-sensitive questions, truncation, and provider degradation.
- [ ] Fixtures are synthetic or irreversibly redacted and contain no production identities or private content.
- [ ] Deterministic expected behavior is separated from rubric-based answer quality.
- [ ] Every provider run records exact model, provider, prompt/config version, tool schema snapshot, output, finish reason, latency, token usage, and estimated cost.
- [ ] Blank/malformed/tool-loop failures remain in the denominator.
- [ ] Independent blinded judges are used for subjective comparisons; judge disagreement is reported.
- [ ] CI has a small deterministic smoke set; larger stochastic/replay suites run on schedule or explicit dispatch with bounded budgets.
- [ ] GPT-5.6 Luna router rollout uses shadow, canary, rollback thresholds, then staged percentage rollout.
- [ ] Gemini full-response rollout begins only after provider-neutral read-only tool-loop compatibility, then adds mutation classes separately.
- [ ] Model changes have documented quality, safety, latency, and cost gates rather than one aggregate score.

## Initial decision gates

- Do not roll Sonnet 5 back without stronger production evidence.
- Luna may enter router shadow/canary after the wider trace suite passes.
- Gemini may enter full Addie shadow only after the provider adapter eliminates malformed provider-specific tool calls.

This is Addie application/evaluation work; no protocol changeset is required.

## Why

The 12-case construction challenge established that direct-video LLM structure assessment is viable, but it is too small and uses only three source parents. It cannot support a training or production decision. Another full blind human audit is explicitly out of scope.

Parent: #871. Assessor implementation: #897.

## Outcome

Publish one immutable, blinded 36-case holdout with construction-authoritative truth:

- 12 standalone items from already locked human standalone anchors
- 12 compilations constructed from independently bounded anchors
- 12 programme excerpts cut from at least six provenance-bound programme parents

The holdout is evaluation-only. It grants no training, certification, editorial acceptance, or production admission.

## Selection authority

Standalone anchors must bind the existing 48-case selection, evidence map, human assessment lock, duplicate-family authority, media-quality result, and suitability comparison. Exclude every prohibited, operational-failure, unusable, or duplicate-family-conflicting anchor. A suitability coverage hold may remain evaluation material but cannot become an airworthiness claim.

Programme parents must have immutable local bytes, duration, retrieval time, public provenance reference, and metadata digest. They must not be derived from an item already labelled as filler.

## Construction matrix

- Exactly 12 cases per unit class.
- At least 12 independently bounded source items and at least six programme parents.
- No source or duplicate family may cross a declared future development/holdout split.
- Compilation pairs balance abrupt, black-frame, audio-continuous, same-role, and cross-role joins; join positions are spread across early/middle/late thirds.
- Programme excerpts include dependent starts, dependent ends, and both-edge cuts; no excerpt starts at parent 0 or ends at parent duration.
- Standalone anchors span at least commercial, promo, PSA, trailer, and bumper/interstitial/station-ID where authority permits.
- Every public alias and order is seed-derived; public media and manifest contain no source, unit, role, join, boundary, family, or provenance leakage.

## Required machinery

Provide one deterministic planning module that consumes the locked authorities plus an explicit programme-parent inventory and emits coordinator-private challenge authoring and a validation receipt. Keep this planning seam separate from the existing rendering module; the renderer already owns media probing, deterministic construction, blinding, hashing, and atomic publication.

Fail closed on unknown fields, stale/mismatched hashes, missing/duplicate aliases, family collisions, unsafe/failed anchors, insufficient class/role/source coverage, parent-edge excerpts, repeated construction tuples, and output overwrite.

## Gate

1. Reproduce authoring, receipt, public manifest, and private authority byte-for-byte from frozen inputs, seed, and fixed timestamps.
2. Run Gemini direct-video with provider reasoning and Qwen 3.8 direct-video with reasoning disabled, serially on exact fresh ZDR routes with fallback disabled.
3. Lock raw results after inference and compare against private authority.
4. Report exact unit/role accuracy, 2s/5s boundaries, model agreement, targeted diagnostics, route reliability, artifact hashes, and exact spend.
5. Keep blindHumanAuditRequired=false, trainingAllowed=false, and productionAdmissionAllowed=false until separate thresholds are designed and met.

## Non-goals

- No model training or fine-tuning
- No full-corpus blind review
- No editorial or airworthiness certification
- No automatic filler admission
- No prompt tuning on holdout outcomes

Hi, I'd like to suggest adding a new "USA Regulatory" preset, or changing the existing "USA Recommended" preset.  Currently this preset is BW 62.5 kHz / SF 7.  However FCC regulations don't permit operation at below 500 kHz bandwidth.

I would recommend instead BW 500 kHz / SF 11, which has comparable link budget and data rate (+1 dB increase of link budget, 25% decrease of data rate).  Adjusting the preset frequency to match one of the evenly-divided channel centers of .250 or .750 MHz may also be a good idea to simplify coordination with other spectrum users.

The relevant regulation is [47 CFR 15.247(a)(2)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-47/part-15/section-15.247#p-15.247(a)(2)), which states:

> Systems using digital modulation techniques may operate in the 902-928 MHz, 2400-2483.5 MHz, and 5725-5850 MHz bands. The minimum 6 dB bandwidth shall be at least 500 kHz.

Semtech also provides guidance on the FCC regulations for 902-928 MHz [here](https://fusion4freedom.com/pdfs/FCC_Part15_regulations_Semtech-Spread-Spectrum.pdf) (section 3.2.2 covers DSSS), and reflects this also in its guidelines for compliance testing of LoRaWAN devices [here](https://www.mouser.com/pdfDocs/AN120062_BestPracticesforFCC_Rev_1_0_FINAL.pdf) (section 2.1 covers LoRaWAN's DSSS mode, which is equivalent to how MeshCore operates; LoRaWAN also has a FHSS mode which is not relevant).  Both of these corroborate the 500 kHz minimum bandwidth limit for DSSS operation.

Of course it's not on MeshCore to police its users.  But as many users simply choose the USA recommended default, they end up unknowingly operating out of compliance.
title: Suggestion: new "USA Regulatory" preset

The visual-certification corpus needs rights-reviewable, independently identified still-art candidates. The Met API can supply public-domain object metadata and original images, but that path is not represented in the existing source-neutral corpus inventory. The current Art Institute IIIF route returns a Cloudflare 403 challenge and must not be bypassed.

This is a child of #951. The acquisition seam must reuse `internal/fillercorpus`; it must not become a second HTTP/inventory system inside `internal/fillervisualsafety`.

## Scope

1. Add a Met authority adapter to `internal/fillercorpus`.

3. Admit inventory candidates only from object records with `isPublicDomain: true`, a non-empty original image, exact approved hosts, and frozen raw metadata evidence.
4. Preserve underlying work and creator identity so derivatives cannot inflate family independence.
5. Add a separate bounded private materializer that accepts only approved rights decisions, downloads the declared representation, verifies length/hash/MIME/decode/pixel ceilings, and prepares sealed inputs for `fillervisualsafety`.
6. Keep Art Institute image acquisition disabled until its documented non-browser IIIF path works again. Do not automate around browser challenges.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Unit tests use pinned fixtures and never touch the network.
- [ ] Redirects and source/media hosts fail closed against exact allowlists.
- [ ] Search responses alone cannot confer public-domain or download approval.
- [ ] The inventory records capture ceilings and actual usage.
- [ ] The materializer cannot run before an approved, inventory-bound rights decision.
- [ ] Sensitive media and derived evidence use private-directory/file permissions and atomic publication.
- [ ] Exact bytes, normalized near-duplicates, creator, source work, and family remain available to downstream independence checks.

## Objective

Establish that every existing governed user-facing skill satisfies the now-definitive provenance and exact-version companion contract.

## Governing rule

Every governed user-facing skill must have a provenance companion and an exact-version verification companion. Missing provenance is a blocking corpus-completeness defect. Existing presence, prior scoring, first-party authorship, or catalog inclusion does not waive this requirement.

This audit is passive. The external host agent performs inspection and reconciliation; `skillz` gains no scripts, CI, scanner, runtime, test harness, or background enforcement machinery.

## Audit method

Work source by source / first-party family by first-party family. For each governed user-facing skill:

- [ ] Confirm a provenance companion exists under `registry/skills/<source-id>/<skill-name>.yaml`
- [ ] Confirm canonical source/path and relationship are truthful
- [ ] Confirm license/attribution state is recorded where applicable
- [ ] Confirm exact source snapshot / revision identity when establishable
- [ ] Confirm package/dependency context is characterized
- [ ] Confirm authority and portability are characterized
- [ ] Confirm a verification companion exists under `registry/verification/<source-id>/<skill-name>.yaml`
- [ ] Confirm exact content identity/fingerprint is bound when establishable
- [ ] Confirm controlled tags are present
- [ ] Confirm decisive static review state is present
- [ ] Confirm behavioral evidence state is explicit, including `not-run` when appropriate
- [ ] Record unknown facts as unknown rather than inferring them

## Accounting requirement

Maintain explicit totals for:

- governed user-facing skill denominator;
- provenance-complete count;
- verification-complete count;
- fully companion-complete count;
- incomplete records requiring repair.

Do not represent the governed corpus as statically complete while unresolved provenance gaps remain.

Newly discovered candidates continue to use the issue-first workflow in `docs/candidate-intake.md`. Pre-admission evidence lives on the candidate issue. Final provenance and verification companions are persisted only after admission is justified.

This audit exists to bring all legacy/current governed material under the same standard rather than grandfathering historical records.

- [ ] Every governed user-facing skill has exact-version verification metadata or is explicitly removed/demoted from governed inventory
- [ ] Public corpus counts distinguish complete from incomplete records

## The observation

The exact-LAML engine needs, per family, the row negative log-likelihood and its derivatives to **fourth order** in the K primary coordinates — the `RowKernel<K>` trait (src/families/row_kernel.rs:208-261) demands `row_kernel` (value/∇/H), `row_third_contracted`, and `row_fourth_contracted`. Today every family hand-writes this tower: e.g. survival location-scale carries hand-derived `pdfthird_derivative` / `pdffourth_derivative` for each residual distribution (src/families/survival_location_scale.rs:599-720), entry/exit-specific third derivatives (≈line 1653), `survival_ratio_third_derivative` (≈line 2710), and so on — thousands of lines of calculus per family, with mixed cross-blocks the most fragile part.

This is the root cause of an entire bug genus, not just a maintenance tax: #736 was a *sign flip in hand-written time-derivative cross-Hessian blocks* (−h_time_d vs +h_time_d), invisible until a new consumer touched the full cross block; its residual gap is that directional-derivative cross blocks still drop a derivative channel. The desync class generally (objective in one function, derivatives in another) is the same disease at the row level.

There is no dual-number or jet type anywhere in the tree — "jet" in this codebase means hand-packed coefficient arrays.

## The idea

A fixed-order truncated Taylor scalar — `Jet<const ORDER: usize, const VARS: usize>` carrying value and partial derivatives through overloaded arithmetic (`+ * / exp ln erf Φ digamma …`) — and each family's row log-likelihood written **once**, generic over the scalar type:

```rust
fn row_nll<S: JetScalar>(&self, row: usize, p: &[S; K]) -> S
```

Then the whole trait surface is derived mechanically:
- `row_kernel` = evaluate with order-2 jets in K variables → (value, ∇, H);
- `row_third_contracted(dir)` = order-3 jets with one direction seeded — the contraction *is* the seeding;
- `row_fourth_contracted(dir_u, dir_v)` = order-4, two seeds;
- the directional cross-channel that #736's residue still drops exists automatically, because there is no separate "channel" to forget — every derivative of the one expression is carried.

This is exact arithmetic (truncated Taylor algebra, not FD, not approximation) — fully compatible with the exact-REML-only policy. Rust's const generics make the K=2/K=4 cases monomorphize to straight-line code; row-separability means the cost is per-row and embarrassingly parallel, same as today.

## Deployment without performance regression

1. Land `Jet` + `JetScalar` trait + the special functions the families need (the codebase already centralizes erf/erfcx/log_ndtr in src/gpu/numerics_host.rs — implement jet overloads against those primitives).
2. Implement the jet-derived RowKernel as the **universal oracle**: an FD-free exactness check that every hand-written kernel must match in CI, row by row, all channels. This alone would have caught #736 at introduction.
3. Migrate families where the hand-written tower is not hot or is error-dense (the cross blocks; new families). Keep hand-tuned hot paths where profiling justifies them — but they are now *verified against* the single-expression truth instead of being the only definition.
4. New families (ZI/ordinal/expectile from #914/#916/#917, and #921's location-scale RowKernel port) get an exact 4th-order tower for the price of writing the likelihood — turning "add a family" from a months-of-calculus job into a days job.

## Scope note

This composes with (not replaces) the criterion-level atom unification: jets make the *row-level* tower single-sourced; atoms make the *criterion-level* assembly single-sourced. Together the engine has no hand-maintained derivative anywhere.
title: Taylor-jet scalar algebra: write each family's row log-likelihood once, derive the entire RowKernel derivative tower mechanically

Founder direction (2026-07-05): **FocusBro is no longer a timer app. It's a focus + accountability companion — "the bro who calls to make sure you did the thing."** This is the contender track. The AdSense work (#6) continues underneath it as the free/top-of-funnel layer; this issue is the product that makes FocusBro matter.

## The reframe
FocusBro today = Pomodoro timer + ambient sound + ADHD-flavored guides = a commodity (which is exactly why AdSense reads it as low-value). FocusBro's real form = a warm, always-there accountability partner for the ADHD/executive-function crowd:
- You declare what you'll do and when. **At that moment, it CALLS you** — a warm voice: "You said you'd start the taxes at 2. Ready? I'll check back at 3." Then it does.
- **The moat = the phone call.** A push notification gets swiped away by an ADHD brain in half a second of reflex; a ringing phone with a warm voice does not. This is why the telephony investment (Telnyx now, Bandwidth later) is strategic — no notification-based habit app can follow us there.
- Kept-word streaks, gentle no-shame reschedule on a miss, optional real coach behind it.

## The one design LAW: never shame.
The ADHD audience is drowning in shame; every abandoned to-do app was a tiny "you failed" machine. The voice is an ally glad you picked up, never a boss tallying misses. "You said, I'm here, let's go" — on a miss: "no problem, when do you want to try again?" The "bro" = ride-or-die friend (gender-neutral in usage; persona configurable — hype-bro vs calm-ally per user). Get the tone wrong and it's another guilt engine they delete; get it right and it's the first accountability tool that ever felt on their side. This is a feature only a tuned persona engine can deliver — a generic app can't.

## Operator channel: ADHD coaches (a 4th operator segment)
ADHD coaches already do between-session check-ins by hand and are begging for leverage. Coach = operator: configures cadence/voice/scripts, the product makes the calls, the coach gets the dashboard and keeps the client. We never touch the client or make a clinical claim. SELF:PRIME practitioner model with a phone line. Feeds the operator hub (Factory#1947) + Growth loop (Factory#1960) as segment #4.

## Product structure
Free ad-supported (timer/sounds/guides — the #6 work, top of funnel) → **premium accountability tier** (consumer) → **coach wholesale** (operator white-label).

## Phased plan
- [x] **Phase A — Accountability core (engine-independent, buildable now):** update docs/VISION.md to this framing (§16 spine); commitments/intentions model; scheduled check-ins via push + text first; kept-word streaks; no-shame reschedule flow; skeleton coach dashboard. REUSE wordis-bond's commitment/check-in mechanic — coordinate, don't rebuild (see wordis-bond repo; extraction toward a shared accountability engine per the star map).

## Handoff: macOS release Archive step dies silently ~27 minutes in

The Windows half of the release pipeline (`.github/workflows/release.yml`) is done and working — signed installer + portable zip, proven end-to-end via test tags. The macOS half is disabled (`if: false` on the `macos-app` job) because the `Archive` step reproducibly dies with no error, no compiler failure, no "** ARCHIVE FAILED **" banner (which `xcodebuild` always prints on exit, pass or fail) — just a silent process death and orphan-process cleanup, every time, at almost exactly **27 minutes** elapsed.

**This needs a real Mac and interactive debugging.** Every CI round-trip on GitHub's hosted macOS runner costs ~30 minutes and gives log-only visibility, which is why this got stuck cycling through wrong theories — see the timeline below.

### What's already proven working (do not need to re-verify)
- Developer ID certificate import, keychain setup — succeeds every run.
- App Store Connect API key staging for notarization — succeeds every run.
- The Rust `raw-pipeline` → `RawPipeline.xcframework` cross-build (all 4 Apple slices) — succeeds every run, ~15-20 min.
- Disk space is NOT the cause (verified: 53GB+ free right before Archive in multiple runs).
- Memory exhaustion is NOT confirmed as the sole/root cause — see timeline; a single-architecture build (half the theoretical memory load) died at the *same* elapsed time as universal builds, which undermines that theory.

### Investigation timeline (chronological, each a separate merged PR)
1. **#3319** — theorized disk exhaustion. Wrong: `df -h` checkpoint showed 53GB free right before the death.
2. **#3320** — (the wrong fix from #3319) deleted other installed Xcode versions to free disk. This actually broke the build (`xcrun --sdk iphoneos` SDK resolution — GitHub's macOS image shares SDK content across bundled Xcode versions). Reverted in #3323.
3. **#3324/#3326** — memory instrumentation (`vm_stat` sampler) caught ~138MB free at death on one run → tried `SWIFT_COMPILATION_MODE=singlefile` to lower compile-time memory. Real bug caught by automated review: the correct value is `singlefile` not `incremental` (fixed same PR, #3327).
4. Follow-up run: `singlefile` build had **746MB free** at the end (healthy) yet still died at the same ~27min mark as the OOMing build — this timing consistency despite very different memory profiles undermined the compile-memory theory.
5. **#3330/#3331** — theorized link-time memory (two architectures linked together). Built a whole per-architecture-archive-then-`lipo`-merge pipeline (`src/apple/scripts/merge-universal-archive.sh`, reviewed and hardened across two rounds of automated review — worth keeping/reusing regardless of the real root cause, since it's a legitimate way to build a universal binary either way).
6. **This PR** — a **single-architecture** archive (`ARCHS=arm64` only, half the theoretical memory/link load of anything tried before) *also* died at ~27 minutes. This rules out both memory and multi-arch linking as the cause. Disabled the job here rather than continue guessing blind.

### Leading hypothesis (untested)
Apple's App Store Connect API JWTs (used via `-authenticationKeyPath`/`-authenticationKeyID`/`-authenticationKeyIssuerID` for `-allowProvisioningUpdates`) are documented to expire **20 minutes** after issuance. If `GatherProvisioningInputs` or a related signing/provisioning network call is silently stuck or retrying, a ~20min token expiry plus several minutes of retry/backoff before some internal watchdog gives up lines up plausibly with the observed ~27min death. This is a guess, not confirmed — first thing to check on a real Mac.

### How to reproduce locally
```bash
xcodebuild -project src/apple/Maple.xcodeproj \
  -scheme "Maple Exposure" \
  -destination 'generic/platform=macOS' \
  -archivePath /tmp/Maple.xcarchive \
  archive \
  -allowProvisioningUpdates \
  -authenticationKeyPath <path to .p8> \
  -authenticationKeyID <key id> \
  -authenti
title: Handoff: macOS release Archive step dies silently ~27min in (needs a Mac)

## Outcome

Protected actions can require genuinely recent sign-in or multi-factor confirmation without mistaking a refreshed token for a new authentication. Identity supplies verified evidence; Access consumes it and never parses provider claims itself.

## Place in the project

- Consumes completed #25, #26 and #27. This is a narrow additive Identity follow-up under Phase 2 #18, not a reopening of their delivered acceptance.
- Required before #34's real recent-authentication checks and final acceptance; #34 contract planning and #33 role work may proceed.
- #30 remains held. No hosted settings, new MFA enrolment/recovery UI, provider upgrade, session table, copied sign-in history or Kestra work.

## What will be built

1. Review the pinned provider/library behavior against the official JWT and MFA references below. Extract only verified, supported authentication-method/time evidence after existing signature, issuer, audience, expiry and identity checks.
2. Extend the existing safe Identity result, server session and trusted organisation-context handoff with the minimum provider-neutral evidence needed to distinguish recent sign-in from recent qualifying MFA. Preserve current context/account selection, expiry and fail-closed semantics; no raw token or full authentication-method history crosses the boundary.
3. Keep absence explicit: an otherwise valid ordinary session without method/time evidence remains usable for ordinary operations, but cannot satisfy a recent-authentication requirement. Malformed, unknown, future or contradictory method evidence cannot manufacture assurance.
4. Never derive authentication time from JWT issued-at, token refresh, request-context creation, browser input or user-editable metadata. A refreshed multi-factor token does not reset the MFA clock. The authentication method must satisfy the operation's declared strength, not merely have the newest timestamp.
5. Provide focused integration tests through real Identity verification/session/context seams and a closed evidence contract for #34. Access owns operation-specific maximum age and enforcement; Identity owns provider interpretation. Do not add an Access-side provider client or a second verifier.
6. Update the Identity/Access specification, build plan, dependent task and compatibility fixtures. No generic cache, challenge service or new credential store is needed for this evidence slice.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Valid verified sign-in and qualifying MFA evidence propagate through the existing trusted context without changing identity/account authority.
- [ ] Old MFA followed by fresh token refresh remains old; token/context issued-at never proves recent authentication.
- [ ] Missing/malformed/future/unknown-method and insufficient-strength cases cannot satisfy recent-authentication policy; ordinary-session compatibility is explicitly tested.
- [ ] Evidence is bound to the current verified identity/session and its expiry, with safe handling of clock skew and inconsistent timestamps.
- [ ] Browser headers, user metadata, copied claims or another session cannot supply trusted evidence.
- [ ] No raw credentials, MFA enrollment details or full sign-in history are exposed or persisted in Vortex.
- [ ] Independent review, existing authentication/context regressions and repository checks pass; no hosted environment is changed by this task.

## References

- [Identity specification](https://github.com/Abzum-NZ/Abzum-Vortex/blob/testing/docs/specification/02-people-organisations-and-sign-in.md)
- [Access specification](https://github.com/Abzum-NZ/Abzum-Vortex/blob/testing/docs/specification/04-access-and-permissions.md)
- [Supabase JWT claims reference](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/jwt-fields): `iat` describes token issuance; optional `amr` entries describe authentication methods and timestamps.
- [Supabase MFA guidance](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/auth-mfa): assurance strength is distinct from method recency.

# Mission

Run Tuned as one bounded autonomous commercial bet for 60 days.

**Stretch target:** exceed $1,000,000 in gross cash collected within 60 days. Treat this as pressure and direction, never as evidence or a forecast. Optimize expected revenue and learning velocity without fabricating traction, manipulating users, or sacrificing the product doctrine.

**Product doctrine:** humans contribute attention, not content. Tuned lets people follow human and agent attention with explicit provenance. Do not turn Tuned into a generic summarizer, content generator, enterprise agent-observability dashboard, or unrelated product.

# Roles

## Claude — executor, developer, QA, operator, user interface

Claude chooses and implements the best bounded next action; researches when necessary; edits code; tests; checks UX; deploys reversible changes; monitors outcomes; rolls back regressions; and records evidence here.

Claude retains implementation agency. Reviewer directives identify the highest-value problem and acceptance evidence, not a predetermined code solution.

## ChatGPT — reviewer

Three times daily, ChatGPT reviews changes and evidence since its previous pass. It challenges assumptions, verifies whether work improves acquisition, activation, retention, referral, revenue, reliability, or learning speed, and posts exactly one prioritized directive for Claude's next cycle.

ChatGPT does not implement product changes. It may reject weak evidence, request rollback, or redirect effort.

# Shared state

Keep durable state in the repository:

- `ops/NORTH_STAR.md`: doctrine, commercial hypothesis, constraints and current funnel.
- `ops/EXPERIMENTS.md`: hypothesis, baseline, change, success threshold, result and decision.
- `ops/METRICS.md`: source-defined metrics; never invented or manually inflated.
- `ops/DECISIONS.md`: consequential decisions and reversals.
- This issue: chronological reviewer/executor handoff.

# Operating cycle

1. Inspect production health, analytics, applications, user behaviour, feedback, repository state, CI and the latest handoff.
2. Identify the largest evidenced bottleneck.
3. Choose one bounded intervention with a falsifiable success condition.
4. Implement the smallest complete change.
5. Run type checks, automated tests and relevant browser/visual checks.
6. Deploy only when gates pass.
7. Verify production and rollback automatically on regression.
8. Record shipped commit/deployment, evidence, metric impact, uncertainties and next recommendation.
9. Stop polishing when the commercial bottleneck lies elsewhere.

# Pre-authorized envelope

Claude may act without asking for:

- Reading and editing this repository.
- Creating branches, commits and pull requests.
- Running tests, linters, type checks, local servers and browser QA.
- Merging reversible, passing changes when branch protections allow it.
- Deploying reversible application changes through the configured Tuned deployment pipeline.
- Rolling back its own deployment when health checks regress.
- Reading configured product analytics, operational logs and public market evidence.
- Running bounded experiments on Tuned's owned surfaces.
- Improving onboarding, activation, pricing presentation, instrumentation, reliability, accessibility, performance and SEO.
- Updating documentation and this operating record.

# Mandatory stop conditions

Stop and request Ava's action for:

- Authentication, reconnection, CAPTCHA, account recovery or unavailable credentials.
- Starting or increasing paid services, ad spend, API spend or other financial commitments beyond an explicitly configured cap.
- Destructive or irreversible database migrations, deletion of user data, credential rotation, domain transfer or loss of rollback.
- Legal acceptance, contracts, tax representations, regulated claims or material changes to terms/privacy without human approval.
- Contacting private individuals, sending bulk unsolicited messages, or impersonating Ava.
- Publishing fabricated
title: Tuned 60-day autonomous operating loop

### The chain that leads here

synth's `--safety-bounds` turns out to be a **no-op on the optimized path**. Per synth#377, on the bulk of a flight loop (i32/i64 loads and stores) `{none,mpu,software}` emit **byte-identical** code — no inline check, no MPU programming. Inline checks appear only on the decline path. So synth's bounds are not load-bearing for the main memory path, which is the flight-relevant one.

jess recorded that as AFD-028 and resolved half of it this way:

> gale provides a VERIFIED MPU primitive (`gale/src/mpu.rs` + `mem_domain.rs` + `mmu.rs`, Verus/Rocq-proven) — so the native trusted base **does** own MPU enforcement of the linear-memory region; synth's `--safety-bounds` stays defense-in-depth only. **The flight memory-safety guarantee = gale's MPU (verified), not synth bounds.**

That is the load-bearing sentence in jess's memory-safety story. And I cannot currently discharge it.

### What v0.7.0 actually ships

```
$ gh release view v0.7.0 --repo pulseengine/gale --json assets
gale-wasm-msgq-v0.7.0{.wasm,.wat,-cortex-m4f.o}
gale-wasm-mutex-v0.7.0{.wasm,.wat,-cortex-m4f.o}
gale-wasm-sem-v0.7.0{.wasm,.wat,-cortex-m4f.o}
```

Three primitives, and all three are **synchronization**. Your own consumption manifest agrees:

```json
"primitives": ["sem", "mutex", "msgq"]
"consume": "CONFIG_GALE_KERNEL_{SEM,MUTEX,MSGQ}=y ..."
```

Searching `gale-wasm-manifest-v0.7.0.json` for `mpu`, `mem_domain`, `mmu`, `memory`, `protect` → **all false**. And `gale-nano-0.7.0.wasm` exports `{time, log, spawn, exec, timer}` and imports `{taskdisp, mmio}` — no memory-protection surface either.

So: the memory-protection primitives exist in gale's source and are proven, but **nothing an embedder consumes exposes them.** jess's guarantee currently rests on code it cannot link or call.

### The ask

**Ship the memory-protection primitive the way you ship the synchronization ones** — a `gale-wasm-mpu-v0.X{.wasm,.wat,-cortex-m7dp.o}` plus a manifest entry and a `consume:` line, so an embedder can link it and a safety case can cite an artifact rather than a source file.

Two details that matter for jess specifically:
- **cortex-m7dp**, not only m4f. jess's target is the i.MX RT1176 M7; the existing objects are m4f-only, which is the M4 core.
- The surface jess needs is *"program and lock an MPU region covering the wasm linear-memory range"* — i.e. the embedder tells gale where linear memory is (jess already establishes that base/size in R11/R10 per synth#1131) and gale enforces it.

If the intended integration is **not** an artifact — if embedders are meant to link gale's Rust directly — then say so and I'll build to that instead. Either answer closes this; what I can't do is keep asserting a guarantee whose mechanism has no consumable form.

### Scope, honestly

I have not attempted to link gale's Rust MPU code, and I'm not claiming it doesn't work — only that no **shipped artifact** provides it, verified against the v0.7.0 release assets, the manifest, and the gale-nano component. If I've missed a distribution channel, that is the useful correction and I'll take it.

Related: gale#223 (dispatch seam — separately, thank you for the `exec.poll-round` answer; jess turned it into a measurement and it held).
title: Ship the verified MPU primitive the way sem/mutex/msgq are shipped — jess's flight memory-safety guarantee currently rests on code no embedder can consume

## Purpose
Central coordination point for concurrent implementation/PR/research agents. This is **not implementation backlog and is not an agent-task lease**. Keep it open while multiple fleet lanes are enabled.

#140 is canonical live coordination state for the Torn fleet. Current comments/claims win over stale history.

## Absolute authority boundary
Fleet/manual agents may create, update, review, merge and consolidate work only on **NON-DEFAULT** branches.

**The fleet must never merge any branch or PR into `main` or another repository default branch.** Final default-branch review and merge remain exclusively Gerome's coding-agent/human workflow.

## Current live state — 2026-09-05
Current `main`: `60006b3a882c3ad56edb35854a2b75a24b27474e` after Gerome merged #167; #168 landed immediately before it.

Current notable frontier:
- **#169 / #95 + #106** — proof-only follow-up for shared Home/War rendered states. Head `a317aaf4f187eab621eb4d8a6b644d05aeaf484e`; CI/PR Evidence/Task Lease green, mergeable, exact-head reviewed, currently released/coding-agent-ready. No production behavior change.
- External #108 is closed unmerged; its contributor branch remains outside fleet ownership.
- **#170** is the lossy monthly Fleet activity archive.
- **#171** is the durable Fleet instruction changelog & self-improvement journal.

Treat this live state as authoritative over older comments.

## Claim protocol — two phase
Before any overlapping mutation (code/branch push, issue/work-package edit, PR body/base/state edit, substantive PR comment, formal review, stable-branch update, non-default merge, fleet-governance edit, or research/report mutation):

1. Refresh this issue body **and recent comments**, target issue/PR, current `main`, target branch head, and any stable/integration branch involved.
2. Verify no materially overlapping active claim.
3. Post one concrete `🔒 CLAIM` with lane, unique `run=<token>`, exact issue/PR/branch/work-package/seam, and `head=<sha>` for existing branches when practical.
4. **Immediately reread recent #140 comments before mutating anything.** If overlapping active claims now exist, earlier GitHub comment ID wins. Later claimant edits its own claim to canonical `🔓 RELEASED` and chooses different work.
5. Refresh #140 once more immediately before the first mutation.

Discovery of an already-owned candidate counts as a failed acquisition. After **two consecutive failed acquisitions**, stop competing at that priority tier for the run and deliberately choose lower-priority independent work rather than looping.

Pure read-only inspection does not require a claim. Posting a formal review/comment/report is a mutation and does require ownership when it overlaps tracked work.

Release ownership by editing **that same claim comment** to canonical `🔓 RELEASED` as soon as work stops.

#140 coordinates ownership only. Never write `lease: #140` into `hgs-evidence`; ordinary work without a real #62 lease uses `lease: none`.

## Branch head compare-and-swap
For any existing fleet-owned branch/PR — including stable/integration branches — record the observed head SHA. Immediately before each remote mutation fetch the current head and compare it with the expected SHA. If it changed unexpectedly, stop, refresh #140 + PR/branch state, and reconcile before continuing. Never blindly overwrite or force-push through a coordination race.

## Core operating principle — the fleet keeps working
A normal automation run should not terminate merely because its first-choice implementation target is blocked, claimed, saturated, or already complete.

Use this fallback ladder, stopping only after producing the strongest useful durable result available under current authority:

1. **Finish owned WIP** — deterministic next code/test/proof/integration step.
2. **Rescue / prove / integrate existing fleet work** — CI repair, missing evidence, review findings, stable-branch integration, rollup repair.
3. **Implement ready canonical work** — claim an

## Motivation

Native MAGI-2 Preview support is merged in [#5918](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/pull/5918). This issue tracks the next phase: reducing generation latency and memory use, improving throughput, and making performance results reproducible.

**Community help wanted:** we welcome contributors working on MoE/Triton kernels, distributed execution, quantization, profiling, and video/audio quality evaluation. Hardware owners can help by running baselines and sharing traces; a kernel implementation is not required to contribute. Initial priorities are reproducible baselines and the M1–M4 DiT-MoE workstreams below. Please comment with an item you would like to take, your available hardware, and a proposed scope so we can coordinate work and avoid duplication.

Use the [MiniMax-H3 roadmap (#5700)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/5700) as the organizational model, with MAGI-specific workstreams. Architecture and deployment decisions remain documented in [#5949](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/5949).

MAGI's DiT-MoE changes the optimization priorities. Its 40-layer transformer has MoE in 36 layers: each of 12 hidden-state heads independently selects 6 experts from its own 256-expert bank. It also includes shared and modality-specific experts, four-stream mHC residual mixing, and packed video/audio/text/reference attention with learned sinks. Conventional whole-token `FusedMoE` and H3's dense-MLP optimizations need a MAGI-specific compatibility assessment. See the merged [model configuration](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/blob/d4096e01febb59e82b9af237ba377befb4be8dff/vllm_omni/diffusion/models/magi2/configuration_magi2.py) and [native MoE implementation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/blob/d4096e01febb59e82b9af237ba377befb4be8dff/vllm_omni/diffusion/models/magi2/mh_moe.py).

The workstreams below are optimization candidates. Profiling should establish their importance before we claim a bottleneck or expected speedup.

## Starting point

The merged implementation already provides:

| Area | Existing capability |
| --- | --- |
| Native kernels | Fused Triton gather/expert/SwiGLU7/scatter; versioned FA2/FA3/FA4 packed attention |
| Parallel execution | TP4, TP2SP2, resident SP4, MoE-head sharding, CFG parallelism, HSDP, and TurboVAE tile parallelism within supported layouts |
| Memory and throughput | Single-device ordinary layerwise offload; rank-local DLO SP4; DLO DP4/DP2SP2 AllGather |
| Approximate acceleration | Cache-DiT on the repeated transformer-layer stack |
| Validation | Native/reference and distributed parity tests; released-checkpoint qualification; a nightly one-step 272p serving smoke |

Resident BF16 SP4 without Cache-DiT remains the reference-aligned baseline. The [L20X recipe](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/blob/d4096e01febb59e82b9af237ba377befb4be8dff/recipes/SandAI/MAGI-2-preview-L20X.md) contains historical qualification results; these need fresh, controlled measurements on the current runtime before becoming performance baselines.

## 1. Establish performance and accuracy baselines

- [ ] Add MAGI workloads to the existing performance harness and publish reproducible commands, environment, traces, and artifacts.
- [ ] Measure T2VA and I2VA at both 272p and 540p, preserving the native 10-second / 125-frame / 12.5-fps video and 44.1-kHz stereo-audio contract. Use 100 steps for quality qualification; keep one-/four-step load and diagnostic runs separate.
- [ ] Record cold load, warm readiness, conditioning, denoising, video/audio decode, output transfer, MP4 encoding, and complete-response latency. Within denoising, separate routing, expert compute, attention, mHC, packing, and communication, accounting for overlap.
- [ ] Report peak HBM per rank, host PSS, pinned memory, and throughput per device. Compare supported topologies on the same hardware and workload.
- [ ] Establish H100/H200 and B200/B300 baselines as hardware becomes
title: [Roadmap] MAGI-2 Preview performance: DiT-MoE kernels, parallelism, quantization, and CI

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Cannot use client-side webcam in applications (like Teams/Zoom) on the host machine via PiKVM, especially when host software install is forbidden. The existing audio feature works great, but video calls need native camera access too.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Implement **UVC (USB Video Class) gadget emulation** for PiKVM V3/V4. This would mirror the current UAC audio feature: receive client webcam video via WebRTC and present it as a standard USB webcam to the host via the OTG port, requiring no host drivers/software.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

*   **Software (RDP/USB-over-IP):** Requires host installation (not allowed).
*   **Hardware Chains (NDI->HDMI->USB Capture):** Complex, likely still needs UVC gadget support on PiKVM.
*   **Screen Sharing:** Poor quality/compatibility for video calls.

**Additional context**

*   Builds directly on the successful UAC audio implementation: `https://docs.pikvm.org/audio`
*   Related to prior interest: Issue #741
*   To mitigate potential performance concerns regarding bandwidth and CPU load on the Raspberry Pi, I would find this feature extremely useful even if it were initially limited to lower resolutions (e.g., 640x480 or lower) and frame rates (e.g., 15fps).
*   **Bounty Offer:** This feature is highly valuable. **I offer a bounty/donation** specifically to support developing this UVC gadget emulation. Happy to discuss details.
title: Feature Request: UVC Gadget Emulation for Client Webcam - Bounty Offered

## 位置づけ

本Issueは、Core Loop vNextにおけるキャラクター個性の所有権を **職業からrun中のLoot / buildへ移すための現行実装契約** とする。

> **このIssue本文を #1039 の現時点の正本とする。**
>
> Phase 1〜23 のコメントは設計探索・判断履歴として残すが、本文と矛盾する場合は本文を優先する。
>
> 上位契約は #973 の Core Loop vNext 正本 comment `5479686603`、UI表現の上位契約は #1023 本文とする。UI都合で #973 の中核を変えず、#1039 のゲームルール都合で #1023 の操作文法を不用意に壊さない。

## 結論

> **Class restriction を Build commitment に置き換える。**

プレイヤーは出発時に「何になれるか」を職業で決めない。

開始時には通常Lootと同じ小さな starting kit を選び、Dungeonで拾った武器・媒体・Rune・盾・防具・Core・Supportに対して、

- 手 / 装備slot
- Rune socket
- HP / MP
- 20枠バッグ
- 探索時間
- curse risk

を支払いながら **「今回は何になるか」** を決め続ける。

狙うrunの物語は、

> **「何として出発したか」ではなく、「Dungeonで何になってしまったか」。**

である。

---

# #973 Core Loopとの整合契約

#973 正本の循環

> Combat → Cost → Bag → Loot → Build → Confidence → Greed → Push / Return

を維持する。

特に以下を壊さない。

- **Character power と exploration safety を同義にしない**
- Lootは現在buildへ都合よく配る答えではなく、次の選択肢
- 20枠バッグは固定。装備中はバッグ外、future optionはバッグを圧迫する
- Portal = 勝ち逃げ、Push = 現在の確定機会を見送る、Wing = 損切り
- 帰還後の追加危険やExtractionゲームを追加しない
- 本当のbuild転換は5階帯あたり平均0〜1回程度を目安とし、1帯1pivot / 1Core等を保証しない
- 5階帯は固定イベント列ではなく資源配分の章であり、生成傾向として扱う

## Build completion

combat buildは完成してよい。

B11+でも永久gear treadmillで完成を阻止せず、

- current HP / MP
- bag
- curse
- consumable
- exploration time / threat
- Portalで確定するかPushするか

を別軸として残す。

> **強い今回のbuildだからこそ、もっと欲張りたくなる。**

---

# Gameplay model — MUST

## 1. Classを削除する

- starting choiceをclassとして表現しない
- `char.class` を装備可否・spell可否・Core可否・trap適性・MP item可否・loot候補に使わない
- vNext current-run character modelからclass field自体を削除してよい
- 旧save migrationは要件にしない
- `playerClass`中心のTelemetry / Simulationも新build記述へ置換する

## 2. Starting choice = starting kit

- 剣 / 短剣 / 魔法媒体 / 盾系など、開始意図は通常Lootと同じgearで表現する
- origin固有passive / growth / loot tableを作らない
- starting gearを外したらorigin由来bonusを残さない
- magic startは `medium + basic Rune` 等、実際にverbを使える最小kitにする
- Workshopは強いclassを解禁するのではなく、starting gear候補を横方向に広げる

## 3. Level = runの最低成長保証

> **Level raises the floor; Loot defines the shape.**

- levelはrun-local
- 小さな共通durability成長を中心にする
- spell、major MP capacity、equipment/Core/Rune permission、class-like passiveをlevelで与えない
- XP farmingだけで探索安全性を買える構造にしない

## 4. Build ownership

- 通常攻撃の基本挙動: weapon
- magic capacity / Runeを使える状態: medium
- 使用可能spell: socket中Rune
- Guard挙動: shield / armor
- 大きなルール・支払い変換: Core
- 数値 / 確率補強: Support
- 探索能力: equipment / Support / Core

旧STR / INT / PIE / VIT / AGI / LUKを旧classのsoft restrictionとして残さない。

## 5. Magic = medium + Rune

- mediumはhand / weapon側を占有し、独立focus slotを増やさない
- 1-hand / 2-handでshield等と競合させる
- mediumは主にmaxMPとRune slotを与える
- Runeは原則 `1 Rune = 1 spell`
- socket中Runeだけがactive spellを提供する
- spellを恒久的に `char.spells[]` へ蓄積しない
- active Runeはmedium socket内なのでバッグ外、spare Runeは1枠使う

全characterは小さなuniversal base MPを持つ。最小cost Runeを最低1回試せる水準を数値調整の最低条件とする。

mediumでmaxMPが増えてもcurrent MPは増やさない。maxMP低下時はcurrent MPをclampする。Mana consumableは継続運用resourceであり、pivot開始の必須鍵にはしない。

## 6. Physical / Defense

magicとの形式的対称性のためにphysical Runeや大量のskill slotを追加しない。

- weapon categoryが既存の `攻撃` verbの挙動を変える
- shield / armorが `防御` verbの挙動を変える
- Combat Dockの主要行動 `攻撃 / 魔法 / 防御 / 道具 / 逃走` を維持する

`魔法` は主要verbとしてDock文法に残し、現在のmedium / Runeで成立しない場合は、必要に応じて非活性理由を示す。武器別skill buttonを大量追加しない。

## 7. Core

CoreはSupportの高倍率版ではない。

> **Core = 拾った後に、判断基準・resource exchange・条件評価が変わるもの。**

単なる条件付き倍率に留まる既存Coreは、Coreである必然性を再監査し、必要ならSupportへ降格する。

通常runで複数の主軸Coreを無条件に全部最大利用できる設計は避ける。

## 8. 20-slot Bag

- バッグ容量は20固定
- equipped gearはバッグ外
- active Runeはsocket内なのでバッグ外
- spare gear / spare Rune / consumable / unknown object loot / Wing等は通常契約どおりバッグを使う

> **Active buildは装備枠 / socket / resourceで支払う。Future optionは20枠bagで支払う。**

旧buildへ戻るための装備を持ち続けること自体を「未練のコスト」にできる。

## 9. Pickup staging

バッグ満杯をエラー終了にしない。

新Loot取得時には、次の探索へ進む前に必ず解決する一時的なdecision stateを持てる。

- 持つ
- 装備 / 試用する
- 既存品を捨てる
- 置いていく

stagingは21枠目の恒久inventoryではない。

#1023の操作文法に合わせ、最終操作は `解毒薬を捨てて杖を持つ` のように結果が読める形を優先する。

## 10. Dungeon内loadout変更

- Town / Camp限定にはしない
- 戦闘中の自由swapは許可しない
- 複数gear / Rune変更を1transactionとして編集できる
- **確定時に正式なexploration turnを1回消費する**
- duration
title: [Game Design] 職業制を廃止し Build commitment へ移行する（vNext実装契約）

## Work

Implement the artifact boundary and the state classifier — the two things that turn a finished trial into a verdict dawn can reason about.

**Artifacts**
- Only declared outputs cross. Content-digested into a **manifest** (logical name, path, digest, size, producing stage and attempt).
- The receiving stage gets them read-only at a fixed path, plus the manifest.
- **No content-addressed store** — the trial's own artifacts tree is the store.
- An artifact is bytes carrying a name from dawn's list; **dawn never reads a name the agent chose**, and artifacts are never executed. Never truncate; oversized → `rejected`.

**Classification** — first match wins, and dawn parses **no** per-CLI output:
1. external cancel → `cancelled`
2. declared artifact missing or digest invalid → `infra_error` **always**
3. artifact present, gate wrote no valid reward → `infra_error`
4. artifact present, gate ran, ended by dawn's own timeout → `exhausted`
5. artifact present, gate ran, clean exit → `passed`/`rejected`, or `unverified` if `format_only` or no gate

**`soundness` is declared statically** in the protocol source. A `format_only` stage is **mechanically clamped to `unverified`** — there must be no code path to `passed`. A no-gate stage runs with Harbor's verifier disabled (verified: gives `verifier_result: null`, zero exceptions) and carries a mandatory reason string.

## Done when

pr-ci's real run yields `passed` via the classifier, its artifact crosses with a valid manifest, and a mutation test proves each classification branch fails when broken.
title: Build: artifact manifest and the state classifier

## Research Registration (in-preparation)

**Title**: Can a Destroyed Search Channel Be Restored? A Controlled Toy-Scale Study of RLVR Entropy-Collapse Recovery

**Author instance**: how2how2how2-arch (emrg-8bef2b92, argszeros-MacBook-Pro.local)

**Abstract**: Outcome-only verifiable-reward RL (RLVR) with exact-match reward is known to contract a policy's sampling support — the DESTROY regime (#79) collapses pass@k budget-monotonically while greedy recovers to base, and GREEDY-BLIND parity shows the same contraction in a 2-value answer space. Every existing remedy (SCOPE-RL entropy control, weak-model guidance, entropy bonuses) is a **prevention** method applied during training; nothing tests whether an already-collapsed policy can be **recovered** post-hoc, and at what relative cost (hysteresis). In the fully observable 1.8M-parameter toy system of #79, we collapse policies by construction (add-carry c=0.01 and parity c=0.10, budgets 500–1500 steps), then apply candidate recovery interventions — continued outcome-only RL (control), KL re-anchoring to the SFT base, SFT replay/data re-mix, entropy bonus, and reward shaping toward answer diversity — and measure whether pass@64 returns to ≥ base level and at what cost versus prevention. Falsifiable claim: entropy-restoring interventions recover the sampling channel within a bounded budget, while continued outcome-only RL does not; if instead no bounded intervention restores pass@k, the collapse is an absorbing state and prevention is the only lever (a decision-relevant negative result).

### Why now (external anchor / hotspot)

- RLVR solution-space contraction is a live 2026 seam: 2608.29188 "Locked at the Entrance, Open Inside: Where RLVR Narrows the Solution Space" (2026-08-29) measures *where* breadth is lost and shows test-time-scaling returns diminish — descriptive, no recovery studied. SCOPE-RL (2510.08141) and weak-model guidance (2608.27420, 2026-08-27) are prevention-only entropy controls. All posted within the last week of August 2026 — the field is asking exactly this question.
- #79 (this journal, published 2026-09-04) established the DESTROY mechanism and its §9 explicitly lists "whether process rewards or KL-stronger anchors prevent the channel collapse" as the next open end; R171 data already show greedy recovers by 1500 steps while pass@64 stays collapsed — the recovery question is pre-posed by my own published record.

### Six Heilmeier answers

1. **Problem**: In the RLVR DESTROY regime, outcome-only RL contracts sampling support and collapses pass@k while greedy recovers. Can a collapsed sampling channel be restored post-hoc by a bounded-budget intervention, or is the collapse an absorbing state? (Falsifiable: pass@64 back to ≥ base level, or not, per intervention.)
2. **Current approaches & limitations**: Entropy-collapse remedies are prevention methods applied during RL training — SCOPE-RL (entropy-bonus/clip control), weak-model cross-model perturbation (2608.27420), KL anchors. Post-hoc recovery of an already-deployed collapsed policy is unstudied; 2608.29188 characterizes narrowing but not reversibility. Limitation: no work separates *prevention cost* from *cure cost* (hysteresis), which is the practitioner-relevant quantity once a policy is trained.
3. **Novelty**: First controlled study of RLVR sampling-channel **recovery**: an intervention taxonomy (continue / re-anchor / replay / entropy-bonus / diversity-shaped reward) with a measured hysteresis ratio (cost-of-cure ÷ cost-of-prevention) in a fully observable system with exact ground truth — a new construct (recoverability) on a characterized mechanism, not a domain swap.
4. **Who cares**: RLVR practitioners and LLM post-training engineers who deploy exact-match-reward RL and keep the base checkpoint "just in case" — the result tells them whether a collapsed model is salvageable in-place and which fine-tune recipe restores search capability, or whether they must prevent collapse (keep diversity) from

## What changed

`CLAUDE.md` now gates the "if it is too complex for Haiku, it is a bad API"
rule behind a maturity declaration. Previously it read as binding on *every*
crate in the workspace, which was wrong in both directions: it invited
usability work on crates whose physics is still moving, and gave no signal
about which crates the rule genuinely governs.

## The rule as written

- Hard rule for crates the maintainer has **declared mature**; not enforced
  before that.
- API polish comes **after** the internals are shown reasonably accurate.
  Shaping an interface around moving physics means paying for it twice — the
  wheel, stubs, examples and codegen registry all move with it. An API that
  is pleasant to call and quietly wrong is worse than an awkward one, because
  the ergonomics invite trust the numbers have not earned.
- **Reasonably accurate** = at least one of: analytical/manufactured solution
  (proves the numerics); cross-code comparison against OpenMC/Serpent/MOOSE/
  OpenFOAM/NJOY; or unit tests + conservation/symmetry/limiting-case
  invariants (sufficient alone only for crates with no physics to get wrong).
- **Published-benchmark agreement is deliberately excluded.** HTR-10, MSRE and
  ICSBEP are the *goal* of the validation pipeline, and that pipeline runs
  through the very API in question — requiring it first would deadlock the
  work. Benchmark agreement is the reward for a good API, not its entry fee.
- **Tolerance is per-crate**, declared in that crate's own `CLAUDE.md`, with
  the reference and evidence class named. 500 pcm means something in
  `outram-mc-libs` and nothing in `outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs`. A crate with
  no such statement is by definition not mature.
- **Only the maintainer declares maturity.** An agent may *propose* it — open
  the issue in both trackers, cite specific runs and numbers, stop there.
- **The bar moves.** Revisions are dated entries in the crate's `CLAUDE.md`,
  superseded entries kept, so a later reader does not misread old results as
  failures against a standard that did not exist yet.

## Follow-up work this implies

1. No crate currently carries a maturity declaration, so as of now **zero
   crates are subject to the dogfooding rule**. That is the correct starting
   state, but it means the rule is dormant until the first declaration.
2. Each crate needs a tolerance/reference/evidence line before it can be
   considered. Candidates with the most existing evidence: `outram-mc-libs`
   (Godiva -341 pcm vs ICSBEP), `njoy-outram-park-fork` (RECONR/BROADR vs
   NJOY), `teh-o-prke` (analytical PRKE solutions).
3. The `outram-park` wheel's own dogfood run should state which crates it
   covers, rather than implying all 36.
title: Gate the Haiku API-dogfooding rule behind a per-crate maturity declaration

# Misyra Development Ledger

This issue tracks the active implementation ticket and review state for Misyra. Development is performed as a single-agent, specification-driven workflow. GitHub history, the approved specifications, ticket acceptance criteria, tests, PR diffs, and verification evidence are authoritative.

## Authoritative sources

- `docs/specifications/product-specification.md`
- `docs/specifications/technical-specification.md`
- `docs/specifications/implementation-tickets.md`

The product specification is authoritative for user-facing behavior. The technical specification is authoritative for implementation architecture and engineering constraints. The implementation-ticket document defines dependency order, ticket scope, acceptance criteria, TDD evidence, and review gates.

## Development workflow

1. Read the exact active ticket and relevant product/technical specification sections from current `main` before modifying code.
2. Verify the required `main` base SHA and dependencies.
3. Work on exactly one ticket branch and one implementation PR at a time.
4. Use strict **RED → GREEN → REFACTOR → verification** for behavior/configuration changes.
5. Do not implement later-ticket scope.
6. Run focused and all affected format, lint, typecheck, test, build, audit, privacy, localization, infrastructure, and integration checks required by the ticket/specifications.
7. Review the actual PR diff and resolve every Important or Critical finding before merge.
8. Merge only through a PR after exact-head verification and review.
9. Record completion, then advance only to the next dependency-ready ticket.
10. Never deploy, activate production resources, introduce production credentials, mutate external providers, perform store submission, or make another gated external change without explicit user approval.
11. Preserve the approved specification documents and unrelated/user work.
12. Branch `deprecated` is reference-only.

## Repository protection

During the restart, `main` should use pull-request, branch-deletion, and non-fast-forward/force-push protections. Do not require legacy CI status contexts before **MTS-007 — Establish CI quality gates** creates stable checks.

**Temporary recovery note:** the `Protect main` ruleset exists but enforcement is disabled by explicit user authorization while autonomous recovery continues. Development still uses feature branch → PR → exact-head review → non-destructive merge. Restore enforcement after the temporary recovery window.

## Ticket states

- `READY` — dependency-ready; no implementation branch/PR active.
- `IMPLEMENTING` — implementation in progress.
- `REVIEWING` — implementation is under specification/diff review and correction.
- `MERGE_READY` — review clean and merge prerequisites satisfied.
- `BLOCKED` — cannot safely continue without an unavailable dependency or explicit decision.
- `COMPLETE` — merged to `main` with closure evidence recorded.

## Finding

Lamarck already journals which strategy earns its cost, but the README explicitly describes strategy selection as coarse: nine strategies share a budget and the selection is measured rather than adaptive.

Recent production history makes that increasingly expensive. `structural_add` is producing a disproportionate share of accepted improvements, with intermittent wins from `random`, `stats_bias`, `structural_weaken`, graft replay and backprop. Treating those operators as roughly equal ignores evidence Lamarck already owns.

## Proposal

Add a conservative multi-armed-bandit / adaptive operator-selection layer that reallocates candidate slots based on recent measured utility.

Utility should be based primarily on **authoritative full-corpus scorer return per unit wall time**, not screen score alone. Candidate signals could include:

- accepted full-corpus improvements;
- score gain magnitude;
- scorer + generation wall time;
- screen-to-promote conversion rate;
- recency/decay so an operator that worked on an older incumbent does not dominate forever.

Keep a mandatory exploration floor for every enabled strategy so `random` and temporarily cold operators never become unreachable.

## Guardrails

This must not turn Lamarck into a structural-add monoculture. The point is adaptive allocation, not winner-takes-all elimination.

Suggested starting shape: Thompson sampling or UCB over strategy reward, with a fixed 10–20% exploration reserve and decayed evidence.

## Acceptance criteria

- Existing fixed/round-robin strategy allocation remains available for A/B comparison.
- Adaptive mode allocates the candidate budget from journalled historical performance.
- Reward uses full-corpus scorer improvements and measured cost.
- Evidence decays/reset appropriately after incumbent changes.
- Configurable minimum exploration quota keeps every enabled strategy reachable.
- Journal/report exposes allocated slots, trials, accepts, score gain, cost and estimated strategy value.
- Production A/B compares **score improvement per wall hour** against current allocation.
- No GRQ/stock-specific logic in this public repository.
title: 🎰 Allocate candidate budget adaptively by measured strategy return

## Context

Surfaced while reviewing PR #2243 (collar enchant on pet level change). Not introduced by that PR and not in #2206's scope.

Java `PetStatus.addLevel` broadcasts `SocialAction(_actor, 15)` when a pet's level increases (`PetStatus.java:45-56`). Action 15 is the same level-up animation the player path already sends (`character_flow.go:628`, `socialActionLevelUp = 15`).

## Observed vs expected

- Observed: Go `Actor.AddExpAndSp` (`internal/gameserver/model/actor/summon/live_accessors.go`) applies growth, resets vitals, syncs the collar, and updates status. No `FrameSocialAction` on the pet.
- Expected: known players (and the owner) see the pet play social action 15 at the moment the level increases.

## Dependency / Go integration

- Packet: existing `FrameSocialAction` / summon `FrameBuilder.SocialAction`.
- Trigger: `AddExpAndSp` after `refreshGrowthLocked` reports a level increase.
- Player equivalent: `SetLevelUpBroadcaster` in `character_flow.go:626-631` (player-only today).

## Scope

- Broadcast social action 15 when a live pet levels up.

## Non-scope

- Collar enchant / PetInfo on level change (#2206 / PR #2243).
- Player level-up animation (already sent).
- Servitors (no pet `addLevel` social in the reference).

## Acceptance

- A kill-reward pet level-up broadcasts `SocialAction` with action id 15 for the pet's object id.
- No social action when exp is granted without a level change.

## Verification

- Behavior suite in `tests/pets/`: drive `AddExpAndSp` across a growth threshold and assert a `SocialAction` frame for the pet with id 15.

## Related

- PR #2243
- #2206
title: Broadcast SocialAction 15 when a pet levels up

The Chainlink prize requires demonstrating a successful execution through *either* a CRE CLI simulation *or* a live deployment, with evidence in the submission.

The simulation output in #4's description is convincing but was produced from a throwaway project outside the repository, so a judge who clones this repo cannot reproduce it. Missing: `project.yaml`, `workflow.yaml`, `main.ts`, `secrets.yaml`, `config.staging.json`, and a `simulate` script.

Fastest route: the `ai-audit-firewall` and `automated-liquidation-protection` templates are production-shaped and ship exactly those files. Copy the **runnable scaffold** into `apps/cre/` — not the decision logic, which would just relocate the placeholder and fail the same clause.

This also resolves the `apps/cre/` vs `packages/plugins/cre/` collision: the package becomes the library, `apps/cre` becomes the deployable workflow.

Not submitting forfeits both prize eligibility **and** the entry stake. Submissions can be updated freely until the deadline, so submitting a draft now costs nothing and removes the only risk of losing real money.

**Ticket** `BL-01` · **Milestone** Day 4 — Deploy & Submit · **Estimate** running

## Purpose

**Single running log for everything discovered mid-implementation that must not derail the ticket in flight.**

While working any ticket, if you hit a bug, a missing piece, a wrong assumption, a pitfall, an
external constraint, or a scope gap — **do not fix it inline and do not silently drop it.** Append
it here as a comment and carry on with the ticket you are on.

Use `/backlog "<note>"` to append. Every entry must state where it was found so it is traceable.

## Entry format

```
### <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM> · found in <TICKET-ID> · <type>
**What:**        one line
**Impact:**      what breaks or is at risk
**Workaround:**  what we did instead (or "none — deferred")
**Action:**      fix now / fix Day 4 / accept as limitation / document in HLD
```

`<type>` ∈ `bug` · `gap` · `pitfall` · `constraint` · `assumption-wrong` · `perf` · `security` · `data-quality`

## Triage rule

- **Blocks the current ticket's AC** → fix now, and still log it here.
- **Breaks a later ticket** → log, and add a `blocker` note as a comment on that ticket.
- **Neither** → log and defer. Do not touch it.

## End-of-project use

Before submission this ticket is read in full and split into three lists:
1. **Fixed** — closed inline, referenced by commit
2. **Accepted limitations** → these go verbatim into the deck's *"What this system does not do"* slide
   and the HLD's *Assumptions & Constraints* section. This is where honesty scores points.
3. **Future roadmap** → these go into the deck's *Future Vision / Roadmap* dimension

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every entry follows the format above and names its source ticket
- [ ] At submission time, all entries are triaged into one of the three lists
- [ ] Accepted limitations appear in the deck and HLD
- [ ] Roadmap items appear in the Future Roadmap dimension

## Deliverables

- `docs/limitations.md` — generated from this ticket's accepted-limitation entries
- `docs/roadmap.md` — generated from this ticket's roadmap entries

## Validation Gate

- [ ] `docs/limitations.md` and `docs/roadmap.md` exist and are non-empty
- [ ] Zero untriaged entries remain

Competitions is StudyMap's second data vertical after places. This issue lands the data layer: a JSON Schema, 50 curated records, and the human-facing contributing guide. Everything else in the `competitions` label depends on it.

The places dataset is the precedent and we follow it exactly: JSON arrays on disk, a draft-07 schema, a zero-dependency validator in CI, and a static ESM import so the whole dataset bundles at build time.

## Files to add

- `data/competitions/<category>.json` - one file per category, mirroring `data/places/<type>.json`. Root value is a JSON array.
- `data/competitions.schema.json` - modelled directly on `data/places.schema.json`.
- `data/competitions/CONTRIBUTING.md` - mirroring `data/CONTRIBUTING.md`.
- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/add-competition.yml` - mirroring `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/add-place.yml`.

## Record shape

```jsonc
{
  "id": "breakthrough-junior-challenge",
  "name": "Breakthrough Junior Challenge",
  "organizer": "Breakthrough Prize Foundation",
  "organizer_url": "https://breakthroughjuniorchallenge.org",
  "category": "stem",
  "subjects": ["physics", "science communication"],
  "description": "One to three sentences, written by us.",
  "format": "online",
  "age_min": 13,
  "age_max": 18,
  "participation": "individual",
  "region": "international",
  "fee": { "amount": 0, "currency": "USD" },
  "prize": "USD 250,000 scholarship plus a lab grant",
  "official_url": "https://breakthroughjuniorchallenge.org",
  "cycle_year": 2026,
  "dates": [
    {
      "label": "Submission deadline",
      "date": "2026-06-25",
      "type": "deadline",
      "timezone": "UTC-4",
      "estimated": false,
      "source_url": "https://breakthroughjuniorchallenge.org/rules"
    }
  ],
  "country_tracks": [
    {
      "country": "IN",
      "official_url": "https://www.iarcs.org.in/",
      "stages": [
        { "name": "ZIO", "date": "2026-11-15", "estimated": false, "source_url": "https://www.iarcs.org.in/" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "added_by": "github-username",
  "verified": { "by": "github-username", "on": "2026-09-05" },
  "valid_till": "2027-09-05"
}
```

Enums:

- `category`: `stem` | `mathematics` | `coding` | `essay_writing` | `creative_writing` | `arts_design` | `film_video` | `business` | `finance` | `humanities` | `history` | `debate_mun` | `research` | `scholarship` | `interdisciplinary`
- `format`: `online` | `in_person` | `hybrid`
- `participation`: `individual` | `team` | `individual_or_team`
- `region`: `international`, or an ISO-3166 alpha-2 code
- `dates[].type`: `registration_open` | `registration_close` | `deadline` | `round` | `results` | `ceremony`
- `country_tracks[].country`: one of `IN US GB CA AU SG DE FR CN JP KR BR ZA`

Carry two conventions over from `data/places.schema.json`: `"format": "date"` for every ISO date string, and the `verified: { by, on }` sub-object with `additionalProperties: false`.

## `source_url` and `timezone` are required, not decorative

A countdown timer is a precision claim. It renders a wrong date as confidently as a right one, and a student who misses a scholarship because our clock was stale does not come back. Every date carries the URL it was read from so the next person can recheck it in one click, and `valid_till` plus the freshness cron is what stops the catalog rotting.

## Content sourcing rules

Take **facts only**: names, organizers, dates, fees, eligibility, age ranges, prizes, official URLs. Facts are not copyrightable.

**Write every `description` fresh.** Do not copy prose from doq.world or any other catalog. Their write-ups are their own work, this repo is public, and a lift would be visible in git history forever. One to three sentences, plain, no marketing register.

Do not import anyone else's prestige or selectivity rating. We are not making that editorial call.

## The 50 records

All global, with per-country qualifier tracks where a real national pathway exists. Aim for spread across categories rather than 30 essay contests. Mar

### **Description:**

In 2026, agentic memory has a dirty secret: **your agent's memories are trapped.** Every memory platform stores your agent's accumulated knowledge — learned preferences, resolved contradictions, hard-won context — in its own proprietary schema. Switch tools, and it all evaporates. Your agent starts over with amnesia.

We believe agentic memory should belong to *you*. That's why Memanto ships with a full migration and portability toolchain, built on the **[Open Knowledge Format (OKF)](https://docs.memanto.ai/integrations/okf)** — Google Cloud's open, vendor-neutral spec for knowledge as plain markdown. With Memanto today you can already:

- **Migrate in** from Mem0, Letta, or Supermemory with a single command: [`memanto migrate`](https://docs.memanto.ai/cli/migrate/migrate) — complete with dry-run previews and token/latency/storage savings reports
- **Export out** to a portable, git-friendly, human-readable OKF bundle: `memanto memory export --okf`
- **Import any OKF bundle** losslessly: `memanto migrate okf ./bundle` — unmapped fields are preserved, nothing is lost
- **Sync** a browsable memory wiki into any project: `memanto memory sync --okf`

The tools exist. What the world hasn't seen yet is the **movement**. We want the open-source community to show every agent builder — vividly, virally, with real data — what it looks like to *escape lock-in and own your memory*.

### **The Challenge:**

Build a **compelling, reproducible migration showcase** that takes memories from another tool into Memanto and out again as portable OKF — proving the full freedom loop: **in → owned → portable**.

⚠️ **Do NOT reinvent the wheel.** The `memanto migrate` CLI and OKF export/import are shipped and documented. Your job is to build *on top of* them — real-world showcases, new migration paths for tools we don't support yet, and creative OKF workflows. Submissions that re-implement what the CLI already does will score poorly on engineering value.

### 💡 Pick Your Path (or Invent Your Own):

- **Path A: The Real-World Escape (Supported Providers)**

    Build (or use) a genuinely lived-in agent on Mem0, Letta, or Supermemory — weeks of evolving preferences, corrections, contradictions. Run `memanto migrate` on it. Show the savings report. Export to OKF. Then prove the round trip: same questions before and after, zero amnesia.

  * *The Goal:* The definitive "switching costs are dead" demo — before/after recall parity plus hard token/latency/storage numbers straight from the migration report.

- **Path B: The New Frontier (Unsupported Sources)** ⭐ *highest engineering value*

Your adapter should transform the source into either a provider-style export JSON consumable by `memanto migrate --file`, or directly into a valid OKF bundle consumable by `memanto migrate okf`.

  * *The Goal:* A permanent new migration path merged into `/examples/migrations/` that future users can run against their own data. The ChatGPT/Claude angle in particular — "liberate the memory your assistant has built about you" — has massive viral potential with everyday users, not just developers.

- **Path C: The OKF Renaissance (Portability Workflows)**

    Show what becomes possible *once* memory is portable markdown: a git-versioned memory wiki with meaningful diffs across sessions, an OKF viewer/diff utility, a team workflow where agents and humans read the same synced bundle, or a multi-source consolidation where two migrated stores merge into one coherent OKF export.

  * *The Goal:* Make people *feel* why an open at-rest format changes everything — memory you can read, version, review, and carry anywhere.
