# 市场事实与通知分流：唯一实施规格

> **本正文是 Issue #553 的唯一实施规格。** 下方历史评论只保留证据，不再提供并行方案；旧 A–G PR 计划、固定 15 分钟摘要、峰值翻倍、统一整窗等待、解析失败不通知、约 95/141 条每天等旧提案或估算均不作为实施依据。
>
> 状态：方案已重写，**尚无实现 PR，未修改生产代码、配置或部署**。以下数字是拟实施的 **v1 工程默认值**，不是已上线参数，也不宣称它们经过收益优化。实现者按本正文执行，不再从旧评论选择另一组默认值。

审计基线：`28b32b8d76115886556542eb769caaf694b78023`；schema `20260904_0363`。实施从当时最新 main 建任务 worktree，先检查本正文所述接口是否变化；已经消失的问题不得重新制造后再修。

## 1. 要解决的问题与交付边界

当前 OI 被设计为 drop/stored；2083 清算与 2026 聪明钱被分类为 unsupported；OI 结构化事实在新闻 Triage 才写，recovery 缺事实。新闻标题去重可能压缩不同时间的市场观测。确定性市场结算还受 News history/CAS 影响。Trading 或 sender 的局部故障可以传播到整个 Workers。

本 Issue 交付：

1. 普通 News/listing 的接收、新闻去重、模型评审、首卡、历史和预算维持既有业务行为。
2. OI、清算、聪明钱以及未知市场来源先完整保存，前端可读；保存和阅读不以模型、Signal、推送成功或可交易合约为前提。
3. 来源提醒按信息类型降噪，重启可恢复，能解释为何未推；不逐条重复打扰，也不删除原始观测。
4. Trading 继续从 app 组合接口读取完整 OI 事实；通知合并不压缩它的输入。
5. 市场解析、通知和可选业务能力的故障不关闭健康的信息入口。

明确不做：新微服务、通用 NoticeEngine/事件总线/插件注册表、市场 DSPy Agent、自动跟单、清算或钱包交易策略、交易参数调优、通道迁移、通知设置后台、全仓命名重构。

**OpenNews alert ≠ Tracefold TradeSignal ≠ Nautilus 成交。** 当前策略的 smart_money 是 OI 帧中的鲸鱼占比，不是 2026 的账户交易。清算/聪明钱接入不会自动改变交易决策。执行端授权、订单幂等、对账和仓位保护保留在 Nautilus 执行职责内。

## 2. 唯一数据流与职责

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  W[OpenNews live / history] --> R[既有 Receiver / Recovery / news.raw]
  R --> I[入口按来源分类]
  I --> N[普通 News / listing 现有路径]
  N --> NT[Event / Triage / 新闻决策]
  NT --> NQ[既有 news.deliver]
  I --> M[市场：保存 Item 原文与来源 payload]
  M --> F[同一事务写解析结果与类型事实]
  F --> UI[市场列表 / 明细：直接读事实]
  F --> P[提交后：单个市场通知循环]
  P --> D[PG 跟踪状态与待发送意图]
  D --> S[现有发送器执行入口与一处限速]
  NQ --> S
  S --> RC[各自送达回执]
  F --> AP[app 读取 News 公共 OI 投影]
  AP --> T[Trading Case / TradeSignal]
  T --> X[Nautilus 执行]
```

| 所属模块 | Interface / 职责 | 不允许承担的职责 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `news/opennews.py`、`source_contracts.py` | 保存业务 payload，识别来源类别 | 以展示名、目录或模型评分决定市场信息是否存在 |
| 现有 OI、清算 parser；新增 `news/smart_money.py` | 一次解析，返回已证明的字段及原文降级原因 | 查询模型、交易账户、行情目录；把 unknown 猜成数字 |
| `pipeline/admission.py` + storage | 入口事务保存 Item、分类/解析状态、类型事实 | 运行通知规则、修改通知 track、等待发送或 News Triage |
| 市场读取模块 | 从 Item 与类型事实提供列表/明细、独立状态 | 通过 News verdict 或 Event leader 才能找到市场事实 |
| 一个 `market_notifications.py` 内部循环 | 读已提交观测；按三种明确规则处理；持久化 track/发送意图 | 每币一个 task、策略插件系统、LLM 打分、新队列平台 |
| 现有 delivery/sender | 一处外部发送与限速；市场卡直接使用已准备内容 | 为市场加载 News evidence、storyline、quote/tradability、模型或交易状态 |
| `app/workers/wiring/news_to_trading.py` | 跨 News/Trading 公共接口传递事实 | Trading 读取 News 私表，或 News 调用 Trading 才能推送 |

**市场通知不再经过 RabbitMQ。** 入口继续使用现有 news.raw；普通新闻继续使用 news.triage/news.deliver。市场的 PostgreSQL 发送意图已承担持久待办作用，发送执行方直接领取到期意图，不再叠加 broker 发布标记、补投扫描和第二套 outbox。一个循环、一个发送入口即可；无需新增进程。

## 3. 数据与身份契约

### 3.1 来源记录和类型事实

- `news_items` 继续保存来源记录；市场观测使用稳定 Item 身份。相同 provider record 重放幂等；不同 record 即使文本、数值、时间相同，也分别保存。
- 为市场 Item 增加来源类别、解析状态/原因，以及通知处理标记。它们只属于市场分支，不参与普通 News 判断。不要为了这些共同字段再建一张复制 Item 的通用 Observation 主表。
- 新增业务 `provider_params jsonb`，保存 wire params 的业务内容，包括 relatedAddress、strategy.metrics 及未知业务扩展；不保存 HTTP/认证传输头。保留首份市场业务 payload；重放不改写已入账事实。沿用传输入口已有大小约束，不额外凭空截成 16 KB。
- 现有 `provider_metadata` 是普通 News 使用的归一化投影，保留其现有证据语义；原始 payload 和归一化投影用途不同，不视为两套业务真相。
- 复用 `news_oi_signals`、`news_market_liquidations`，增加 `news_market_smart_money`；不另加通用 Fact 基类、策略注册器或统一 metrics 字典。
- OI 类型事实以 `(source_item_id, metric_version)` 唯一；清算/聪明钱按 Item 的对应类型唯一。parser version 是解析证据，重新解析不是新的来源观测，也不能自动产生第二次通知或交易。
- 原文始终存在；解析器可用明确 nullable 字段表达未提供的数据。模板/单位无法证明时，该 Item 为 `parse_status=raw`，保存原因，展示原文卡；`parsed` 只表示对应模板字段已解析，不表示具备交易资格或来源覆盖完整。
- 市场入口不做 News 标题 exact/minhash/near-dup、storyline、通用 News Gate、evidence snapshot 或伪 TriageVerdict。停止为新市场观测创建 News Event。
- source 事件时间、接收时间、首次可用时间分别保存。不得用它们的先后关系 CHECK 拒绝来源记录；窗口调度使用本机接收/处理时间，卡片保留原始事件时间。

### 3.2 来源路由和解析

| 来源 | v1 处理 |
| --- | --- |
| 1019 OI | 使用既有 OI 数字 parser；保留源场所、原生标的、指标口径/窗口。展示名变化不取消类别；没有证明的窗口仍为 unknown，不能默认 5 分钟。 |
| 2083 清算 | 接入清算类别与已核对的模板；不沿用只允许 binance/hyperliquid 的白名单。保存来源场所字符串，不把支持某 venue 的信息展示当作支持其交易。 |
| 2000 清算 | 保留契约覆盖，与 2083 分别记录 source_strategy_id。生产接入验收以确有流量的 2083 为主。 |
| 2026 聪明钱 | 解析来源标签、Open/Close、Long/Short、原生标的、来源报告金额、价格、可选 PNL/地址；Withdraw 或新模板走原文卡，不能因此不入库或不通知。
title: [Architecture][P1] 市场事实与通知解耦：OI、清算、聪明钱的三 PR 实施方案

This unit makes the fast lane shed real cost with two new skips, each provably safe or escape-hatched: (1) SDD's final whole-branch review (and its fix wave / re-review) is skipped when `ceremony-profile: fast-lane` **and** the plan has exactly one task — the task review's diff *is* the whole branch, and every cross-task incident in the `[IL-02]/[IL-04]/[IL-10]/[IL-97]/[IL-101]` cluster needs two or more tasks; (2) the `polish` step is skipped under `fast-lane` — polish is refinement, not correctness, and on a fast-lane record it can modify code and trigger a re-verify. It also creates `_shared/ceremony-profile.md`, the single roster of every skip each profile makes and every step no profile may skip, with a test that pins every skip named in a skill to the roster. The two-call split is explicitly kept.

**Complexity:** Medium
**Estimated tasks:** 6

## Non-Goals

- Collapsing the two Task calls — rejected (Decision Rationale).
- New header fields or labels: `ceremony:` on the record and `ceremony-profile` in `config.yml` already carry the tier.
- Skipping `/claude-tweaks:review` Steps 2, 3, 5, or Step 6's rendered-UI check; build Common Step 5; reflect's Near-misses/Fresh-start/Friction lenses; the escape hatch; `[IL-116]`'s cleanup floor; any HARD-GATE.
- Propagating a fast mode into superpowers' brainstorming/writing-plans (#1886), micro-plans (#1911), model tiering by diff facts (#1912), fast-lane bundling (#1910) — separate records.
- Changing the review-effort derivation (`review/review-effort-derivation.md`).

## Prerequisites

| Spec | Title | Status |
|------|-------|--------|
| Phase 1 sub-issue | `build/dispatch.md` reviewer seam already edited (reviewer does not run the suite) | blocked-by |

## Current State

- Tier sources: `ceremony:fast-lane|standard` label stamped by `/specify` (`assess-agent-autonomy ceremony-check`; `docs/decisions/0006-ceremony-tiering-owned-by-specify.md`); `config.yml` `ceremony-profile` AND-folded by `flow/manifesto.md`; `wrap-up/ceremony-derivation.md` narrows `standard` → `fast-lane` from diff facts (headless only today); the escape hatch in `wrap-up/SKILL.md` ("Ceremony escape hatch") sets `standard` via `bin/set-config.js` on a review finding of any severity or a reflect safety finding.
- Existing fast-lane skips are scattered: `review/code-mode-steps.md` (Steps 1, 1.6, 4), `build/SKILL.md` + `build/plan-audit.md` + `build/architecture-alignment.md` (plan audit, architecture alignment), `wrap-up/SKILL.md` (reflect light mode), `wrap-up/ceremony-derivation.md`, `specify/red-team.md` (one persona). No roster exists (`plugin/skills/_shared/ceremony-profile.md` does not exist).
- SDD invocation seam: `build/dispatch.md`'s "Whole-branch review model" paragraph — model pinned via `resolve-profile.js capable`; after Phase 1 it also says the reviewer must not run the suite. The plan file's task count is authoritative and already parsed by `build/plan-audit.md` (`bin/plan-audit.js`, Checks A/B/C).
- Polish: `flow/steps-and-gates.md` polish row (line ~15) — "Skipped on non-frontend specs (wrapper detection)", `no-polish` arg (line ~120), re-verify bundled (line ~20); `flow/polish-execution.md` holds the execution; `/review` Step 6.5 (design quality, read-only) still runs regardless.
- Incident: `[IL-145]` — the one recorded case where a fast-lane skip (review Step 1 spec compliance) let a defect through; the escape hatch exists because of it.

## Objective
Define whether supported shared-anchor ledger surfaces may expose the caller-supplied mutable `AttestedCatchup` / provider capability as a reachable public object, and if not, replace that exposure with a least-capability view without breaking internal authenticated read/reconcile/activation flows.

## Audit finding
LAB-092 post-construction provenance guards correctly cover ledger-mediated durable SQLite writes and public `provider_history.store_receipt()`. However, every ledger inherits `self.attested = attested`, where the exact same object was supplied by the caller. `AttestedCatchup.catch_up_one()` can advance the external monotonic anchor; `attested.provider` exposes provider mutation APIs, and LAB-090 `FencedActivationProvider` additionally exposes activation reservation/commit/release state.

This is **not currently treated as a LAB-092 provenance bypass** because the caller already owns the same mutable object before constructing the ledger. Deleting LAB-092 migration provenance does not grant a new capability: direct external-provider mutation was already possible independently of the ledger. Attempting to wrap it only inside LAB-092 would therefore invent a stronger authority boundary at the wrong layer and could conflict with LAB-080/090 exact-type/provider integration contracts.

## Acceptance questions
- Is `ledger.attested` part of the supported public API or merely an implementation attribute?
- Must a supported ledger prevent callers from recovering the raw mutable external provider through the ledger object?
- If yes, what capability interface is sufficient for internal authenticated read/reconcile and LAB-090 activation without exposing direct increment/prepare/commit/release?
- Can the runtime retain an internal private mutable handle while exposing only an immutable/read-only identity/status view?
- How does this compose with LAB-087's sole-writable-handle/process boundary?

## Required proof before changing code
Demonstrate a concrete security/correctness property that is violated specifically by capability exposure, rather than by a caller who already possesses the provider object. Do not add LAB-092 provenance guards around caller-owned external capabilities without first defining this ownership boundary.

## Origin
Discovered during LAB-092 audit of remaining externally reachable mutable handles after post-construction provenance deletion.

## Status
READY — architecture/capability-boundary follow-up; does not supersede LAB-086 priority or LAB-092 exact execution gate.
title: [LAB-093] Encapsulate caller-owned attested/provider mutation capabilities

Part of #548 and #899. Blocks the fresh replacement challenge required by #1085. The source-level safety and suitability work remains separately owned by #903 and #1086.

## Why

The v5 holdout is burned diagnostic evidence. Its immutable replacement lineage excludes every original source, all 36 rendered request videos, all selected anchor families, and every programme-parent provenance.

A deterministic audit of the frozen authorities proves the current inventory cannot produce a replacement:

- programme parents: 0 unexposed against 6 required;
- bumper anchors: 1 otherwise eligible and unexposed against 2 required;
- PSA anchors: 0 against 2 required;
- trailer anchors: 2 against 3 required;
- promo anchors: 2 against 2 required;
- commercial anchors: 9 against 3 required.

Those are raw role counts only. Duplicate-family, source, duration, transition-band, transition-stratum, same-role/cross-role pair, media-quality, and suitability constraints can reject additional candidates.

## Outcome

Acquire, condition, measure, and truth-lock a source-diverse replacement pool that can satisfy holdout-plan v4 without any prior source/request hash, family, or programme-provenance leakage.

Target a buffer rather than the mathematical minimum:

- at least 10 eligible programme parents from 10 distinct provenance records, so 6 can survive selection;
- at least 4 newly eligible bumpers;
- at least 6 newly eligible PSAs;
- at least 4 newly eligible trailers;
- at least 2 additional promos and 2 additional commercials when they add underrepresented transition strata.

The hard floor remains 6 programme parents, 1 bumper, 2 PSAs, and 1 trailer. The buffered target exists because a pool that merely meets counts can still fail the joint transition solver.

## Source rules

- Prefer primary, rights-traceable audiovisual collections with stable item metadata and direct media bytes.
- Bind licence or public-domain basis, item URL, retrieval time, exact source bytes, and immutable metadata bytes.
- One item URL or edition is one provenance parent; mirrors and alternate encodes do not create independent truth.
- Reject material already present in any v5 source or rendered request by exact hash and perceptual duplicate family.
- Do not use Met Open Access images as programme-video substitutes. They may support later visual interstitial controls, but they do not satisfy this moving-image corpus gap.
- Keep source acquisition separate from truth, safety, and production admission.

## AI-first review

This must not become another blind full-corpus human labeling exercise.

1. Run deterministic rights, decode, audio/video coverage, duration, duplicate-family, and transition measurements first.
2. Use local ASR/OCR/vision plus bounded multimodal models to propose unit, role, boundaries, and hazard observations.
3. Reject obvious non-candidates mechanically.
4. Show the maintainer only surviving candidates, prefilled with evidence and model disagreements.
5. Require complete audiovisual playback only for the small set proposed as truth anchors or disputed at decisive boundaries.
6. Model agreement nominates evidence; it never becomes truth authority by vote.

## Gates

1. A pre-download search manifest states desired role, source authority, item identity, rights basis, and expected media before bytes are fetched.
2. Every downloaded candidate has a content-addressed ledger and complete decode/coverage measurement.
3. Exact-byte and duplicate-family checks run against the full v5 exposure set before review.
4. The accepted pool meets the buffered targets or documents why the joint solver succeeds with less.
5. A dry replacement plan using #1085 adjudication lineage succeeds and reproduces byte-for-byte with a fresh private seed and fixed time.
6. New challenge aliases, cases, source hashes, request hashes, and provenance are absent from v5.
7. No provider spend, training export, ingestion, scheduling, certification, or production admission is implied by

**Requirements:** none listed (no level, no karma).

**Steps**
1. Nagnang Rogue Guild (020, 141) — interact with **Master Dagger**.

3. After the assassins vanish, tap Dagger again and pick **"Blue Rooster"** from the menu. Find the Blue Rooster wandering southern Buya, observe it, return to Dagger.
4. Dagger tells you to steal a **Silver acorn** from **Maro** at the Kugnae Rogue Guild (022, 188). Steal it and leave — a crow intercepts and flies east with the prize.
5. Travel to the north-east of Dae Shore to find the enchanted crow, actually a cursed boy: "a Tiger turned me into this dull bird", and "the answer would drop from the stars".
6. Get a **Stardrop** and trade it to the crow for a **Silvered acorn**.
7. Return to Dagger; he gives you a scroll to deliver to **Maso**, the Buya Rogue Master, to frame Maro.
8. Speak to Dagger once more for the reward.

**Rewards:** Dagger Uniform spell (Spells.csv 2124), Daggers Guild legend mark, unlocks the Rogue Shield quests

- `stardrop` (29005) and `silvered_acorn` (29019) already exist in Items.csv; spell `dagger_uniform` (2124) exists in Spells.csv.

## 目的

Crownless を、スケジュール実行するAIエージェントが自分で次の遊びを考え、Issue化し、実装まで進める「自律プロダクト開発」のPOCとして記録する。

将来の出版・振り返りで、単なるGit履歴では分からない **AIが何を考え、なぜそれを選び、人間がどこで介入したか** を一次資料として残す。

このIssueは実装タスクではなく、実験ログの正本として扱う。原則closeせず、各自律開発サイクルをコメントで追記する。

## 各サイクルで残す内容

### 1. Cycle
- 実行日時（Asia/Tokyo）
- 起動種別: scheduled / human-triggered
- 対象main SHA（取得できる場合）

### 2. AI proposal
- 直近3〜5サイクルで新しい遊びが増えたか
- 新機能候補3案
- 各候補の4軸スコア
  - プレイヤーが気づく変化
  - 新しい判断
  - リプレイ性
  - Canonとの整合

### 3. Decision
- 今回選んだIssue / 新規アイデア
- なぜそれを選んだか
- 他候補を選ばなかった主な理由
- bug-fix / maintenance / innovation の区分

### 4. Execution
- 新規Issue / 既存Issue
- 実装した縦切り
- PR / commit
- test / CI
- merge / close結果

### 5. Human intervention
前回サイクル以降、人間による方向修正がGitHub上または実行コンテキストから確認できる場合に記録する。

例:
- 新しいIssueを人間が追加した
- AI案を却下・修正した
- 優先順位を変更した
- 実装済み機能の作り直しを指示した
- 直接エージェントへ割り込んだ

介入が確認できなければ `なし / 確認できず` とし、推測で人間介入を作らない。

### 6. Outcome / observation
- プレイヤーから見て何が変わったか
- 新しい遊び・判断が増えたか
- AIの判断で気になった点
- 次回観察したいこと

## 記録原則

- 事実とAIの評価を分ける
- 後から書き換えず、原則コメントを追加して時系列を保つ
- Issue/PR/commitへリンクできる情報を残す
- 長い実装ログやCI全文は複製せず、意思決定に必要な要約だけを残す
- 人間介入は確認できたものだけを記録し、推測しない
- 成功だけでなく、`no_action`、失敗、誤った提案、revert、方向修正も残す

## このPOCで検証したい問い

> AIは、与えられたIssueを消化するだけでなく、自分で「次に何を作るべきか」を考え、ゲームを継続的に面白くできるか。

> 人間は常時開発ループを回さず、必要なときだけIssue追加や直接指示で介入する運用へ移れるか。

Related: #228
title: POC: AI自律開発の意思決定・人間介入ログ

## Anlass
Der Live-Check am 20.08.2026 zeigt für Baden-Württemberg auf `/laender/baden-wuerttemberg/mandat-und-praxis` nur die verifizierte Mandatsbasis. Die Seite sagt selbst: `vollständige Commitment-Zerlegung wird fortlaufend ergänzt`.

Der kanonische WÖk-Bestand bestätigt die Fachlücke:
- `/WOEK/WOEK-LAENDER-DAILY/BASELINE/baden-wuerttemberg/BASELINE-2026-08-18.md`: offene Aufgabe `Koalitionsvertrag vollständig in CoalitionCommitments zerlegen`.
- `/WOEK/WOEK-LAENDER-DAILY/CONTROL/LAENDER-COVERAGE-AND-HANDOFF-FINAL-2026-08-18.md`: Koalitionsvertrag 2026-2031 nur `als Mandatsbasis vorgesehen`.
- `/WOEK/WOEK-LAENDER-DAILY/FACHREVIEW/baden-wuerttemberg/INITIAL-IMPACT-CASES-2026-08-18.md`: fünf initiale Regierungswirkungsfälle, aber keine vollständige Koalitionsvertrags-Wirkungsanalyse.

Aktuelle Production ist nicht stale: `dpl_6CefNPFgRYrVXzYTFZeEezsArEX2`, READY/production, Git SHA `fb07fab799a34bbda0e2efc03f90066945c95802`, entsprechend aktuellem main-Basisstand von PR #235. Das BW-Problem ist daher nach aktuellem Befund keine bloße falsche Vercel-Promotion, sondern eine echte fachliche/Publikations-Coverage-Lücke - vorbehaltlich historischem Restore-Fund.

## Rollen
Human out of loop. **CodeX ist technischer Ausführungs- und Deployment-Aktor.** WÖk/Controller liefert Fachbestand, Priorität, Audit und exact-commit Freigabe. CodeX implementiert, testet, merged und deployt bis Production, sobald die Gates grün sind. Kein zusätzliches Human-Gate.

## P0-1 Baden-Württemberg: Restore-first
Vor Neuanalyse Git-Historie, Branches und kanonischen `/WOEK`-Bestand nach einer früher bereits fachlich freigegebenen Koalitionsvertragsanalyse durchsuchen. Wenn vorhanden: exakt/provenienzgebunden wiederherstellen. Keine Neufassung, die einen vorhandenen historischen Fachstand still ersetzt.

Wenn keine vollständige freigegebene Analyse existiert, ist die Fachlücke ausdrücklich zu schließen: amtlichen Koalitionsvertrag 2026-2031 vollständig sichern/versionieren, Commitments mit Source Locator extrahieren und dem WÖk-Fachreview zuführen. CodeX erzeugt **keine** Wirkungsurteile selbst.

## P0-2 Vollständigkeitsaudit alle 16 Länder
Für jedes Land getrennt inventarisieren und öffentlich korrekt abbilden:
- `election_cycle_state` und `government_lifecycle_state` - strikt getrennte Achsen,
- ElectionDocuments/Wahlprogramme und freigegebene Programmanalysen,
- Koalitions-/Mandatsdokumente und Coalition-/MandateCommitments,
- GovernmentActions und WÖkImpactCases,
- AnalysisVersions/RecommendationVersions,
- EvidenceEvents/RealityChecks,
- Quellen, Kompetenz, höherrangiges Recht/Schutzgrenzen,
- öffentliche Routen, Navigation, Overview-Projektion und Detailakten.

Fehlende Fachlayer nicht technisch erfinden. Vorhandenen Fachbestand niemals verkürzen oder verstecken.

## P0-3 Übersicht: Wirkungspotenzial klar sichtbar
Portalweit auf Wahlprogramm-, Koalitions-/Mandats-, Regierungs-, Parlament-, EU- und Länderübersichten muss die WÖk-Einordnung vor Prozessmetadaten verständlich sichtbar sein. Soweit fachlich freigegeben mindestens:
- qualitativer Wirkungspotenzialbefund,
- stärkste positive Potenziale,
- wichtigste materielle Risiken/Zielkonflikte,
- Evidenz/Unsicherheit getrennt von Richtung,
- Richtungsprofil nur für redaktionell/fachlich geprüfte Pfade,
- Nichtkompensation/Schutzgrenzen,
- **alle** freigegebenen Key Findings - keine `slice(0,2)`-Verkürzung,
- keine Partei-/Regierungs-Gesamtnote oder künstliche Saldierung.

Detailseiten müssen die vollständige freigegebene Fachakte und Quellen enthalten, nicht nur Mandats-/Fakten-Teaser.

## P0-4 Golden-State / kein Datenverlust durch Release
Jeder Kandidat gegen letzten akzeptierten Production-Stand **und** kanonischen `/WOEK`-Fachbestand prüfen:
- vorhandene Routen/Navigation,
- Fachakten/Analyseachsen,
- `required_content_paths` vs. `rendered_content_paths`, Pflichtbestand `unrendered_content_paths=[]`,
- Wirkungspotenzial/Key Findings/Wirkpfade/Evidenz,
- Kompetenz/Higher Law/Schutzgrenzen,
- Rec
title: P0: Länder-Fachvollständigkeit - Mandate, Wirkungspotenzial und Golden-State für alle 16 Länder

## Description:

In a previous bounty, we asked the community to stress-test **Memanto** in order to find bugs, logic loops, and performance bottlenecks. We got an unexpectedly large number of PR's and we’ve spent a great deal of time meticulously reviewing them, you’ve all helped us make a huge step forward in improving the security and quality of Memanto!

Now, we are taking it a step further and focusing exclusively on what matters most for AI in production: **Security**.

As memory layers become the backbone of autonomous agents, they also become a prime target for attacks. Whether it's a cross-tenant data leak, a broken access control, or a malicious payload hidden in a retrieved memory, we want to know about it. We’ve fixed a majority of bugs and issues with Memanto and resolved many of its security issues, but as Memanto starts to be utilized in more sensitive workflows, we want to ensure our defenses are as robust as possible and we need the developer community to help us do that.

Your mission is simple: **Help us audit our memory management and backend infrastructure to uncover potential vulnerabilities before they can be exploited.** 

---

## 🎯 Threat Model & Scope
Your target is the `memanto` core package and its interaction with the `moorcheh.ai` serverless backend. We are prioritizing traditional application security flaws, data isolation failures, and API vulnerabilities. 

### 🔴 Security Focus Areas (In Scope)
- **Tenant Isolation & Cross-Account Leaks:** Can User A query, retrieve, or overwrite memories belonging to User B through the core package or backend API?
- **Authentication & Authorization Bypasses:** Finding ways to read or write to the memory layer without a valid API key, or bypassing intended role/access restrictions.
- **API Vulnerabilities:** Standard backend flaws such as Insecure Direct Object References (IDOR), broken object level authorization, or injection flaws in the `moorcheh.ai` backend.
- **Data Exfiltration:** Tricking the system or bypassing controls to extract raw vector data, plaintext logs, or sensitive hidden context from the memory store.
- **AI-Specific Exploits (Indirect Prompt Injections):** Exploiting the retrieval process to inject dormant malicious payloads into memory that later hijack the agent's core instructions when recalled (i.e., treating memory as a trojan horse).

### 🚫 Rules of Engagement (Out of Scope)
- Volumetric DDoS attacks against `moorcheh.ai` infrastructure.
- General LLM hallucinations or standard logic bugs unrelated to security.
- Attacks that require compromising the underlying operating system or Docker host to succeed.

---

### **📝 Submission Guidelines**
Because this bounty is hosted on BountyHub, **a public Pull Request is required to award funds.** 

- **Primary Method:** Fork the repository and open a Pull Request containing your fix, a summary of the flaw, and reproduction steps. This acts as your official bounty claim.
- **Sensitive Findings:** If you believe you've found a sensitive vulnerability that shouldn't be public yet, you can optionally email the Proof of Concept to `support@moorcheh.ai` for our team to review first. However, you will still need to open a redacted PR to claim the bounty.

---

### 📊 Judgment Method (The Success Matrix)
To ensure we reward actual engineering value and meaningful security research, submissions will be scored on a 100-point matrix split between **Technical Rigor** and **Impact**.

### Problem or use case

A Bazaar catalog entry, and the quality counters attached to it, cannot be distinguished between **a payment that happened** and **a payload that was merely checked**. Both produce an entry, and the spec is the reason.

`specs/extensions/bazaar.md` Facilitator Behavior says a facilitator receiving a `PaymentPayload` containing the `bazaar` extension should validate `info` against `schema` and extract the discovery information. **Settlement appears nowhere in that section.** The response-header section is consistent with this: a facilitator MAY append `EXTENSION-RESPONSES` to **"the verify or settlement response"**, and `status: "success"` there means the discovery info was validated and successfully cataloged.

So the verify path is written into the spec, and every conforming catalog inherits it. This is not one implementation misbehaving, which is why this is filed as a spec proposal rather than a bug against a facilitator.

**Measured, not inferred.** On 2026-08-21T14:10:40Z I sent a `PaymentPayload` for a resource I operate, carrying `extensions.bazaar`, to a facilitator's `/verify`, and never settled:

```
status                200
body                  {"isValid":true,"payer":"0x9f54460FED..."}
EXTENSION-RESPONSES   eyJiYXphYXIiOnsic3RhdHVzIjoicHJvY2Vzc2luZyJ9fQ==
decoded               {"bazaar":{"status":"processing"}}
```

**No tokens moved.** Our chain-versus-ledger invariant was unchanged across the call.

I am claiming exactly what that shows and no more: the payload was **accepted for discovery processing at verify**. Whether a row always follows `processing` is unresolved on my side, and I have said so publicly rather than assert the stronger version.

Two independent lines of evidence from others point the same way and are worth reading together with it: the 17-route natural experiment reported in #2112, where routes settled with the declaration attached indexed and routes settled without it did not, which isolates the **declaration** rather than the settlement as the variable; and the census work in #3045, which found catalogued rows whose payee addresses show no inbound transfers, credited with calls and unique payers. I am citing those rather than speaking for their authors.

**Impact.** The counters are being read as a demand signal. If an entry can be produced by a verify, then `l30DaysTotalCalls` and `l30DaysUniquePayers` may count payloads seen rather than payments made, and an entry plus its counts costs one HTTP request and requires **no balance**, since an authorization that would fail at settle still verifies. Anyone selecting a service on those numbers is reading something a stranger can mint.

### Proposed solution

**Do not close the door. Label what came through it.**

Record provenance on the catalog entry and expose it in discovery results, minimally as a two-valued field distinguishing an entry whose declaration arrived on a **verify** from one that arrived on a **settlement**, and correspondingly separate the call counters, or mark them with the same provenance.

That achieves three things at once:

1. **The counters stop being ambiguous.** A reader can tell a payload that was checked from a payment that happened.
2. **Nothing breaks for honest services.** Many legitimately verify far more often than they settle, and they keep their entry and their visibility.
3. **The free-minting path stays open and stops mattering**, because an entry marked verified-only is not worth minting.

**Non-goals.** Not proposing that verify stop cataloging, not proposing a new authentication requirement, and not proposing that verified-only entries be hidden or ranked down. The ask is a label, not a gate.

### Related

- #3005 is adjacent but a different axis: whether client-echoed metadata is **truthful**. This one is whether an entry reflects a **payment**. Both concern what a reader may infer from a catalog row, and neither subsumes the other.
- #3178 established that the declaration must
title: [Feature]: Label catalog provenance, verify-only versus settled, so Bazaar counters mean something

Unblocks the **secondary** shipping route. Needed for milestone **M0 (Sun 7 Sept)**.

Galaxy Store is our store route — free to join, free to publish. It unlocks the store-dependent categories (Grand Prize, Design, Growth Loop, OneSignal). It is **not** load-bearing: Next Gen is the primary entry and requires no store release at all, so nothing here blocks the critical path. If it stalls, we still have a complete submission.

## Tasks

This is risk **R2** in PLAN.md. Commercial-seller status is what lets you sell in-app on Galaxy Store, and it can require a D-U-N-S number and bank verification, each up to 10 business days. That's most of the runway to 30 Sept for a route we've already agreed is a bonus.

body_excerpt:
Opt-in per project. An absent block changes nothing, byte for byte, exactly like `reward.reviewBudget`.

## Problem

Wasting a maintainer's attention costs the submitter nothing. Merge-gated scoring already means low-value work is never paid, but it is still reviewed, and review is the one input that does not scale. #261 documents the local version: coverage farming, one-helper PR swarms, copied test bodies. The scoring contract cannot fix this because the cost lands before scoring does. Every analog that paid for submissions without pricing attention (OnlyDust, Code4rena, the curl bounty) was closed by volume, not by tooling.

## Proposal

A project may set a price a contributor pays to have a pull request reviewed under Slop. The fee goes directly to the project's published receiving address. If the PR is merged, the fee is refunded at cycle settlement on top of whatever the recipient's allocation is. If it is not merged, the project keeps it as compensation for the review it did.

The sponsor sets whether it is on, the amount, and the mode. Different projects can set different prices, and later different prices for different kinds of PR.

### Manifest sketch

```json
"reward": {
  "postage": {
    "mode": "required",
    "currency": "USDC",
    "chain": "solana",
    "amountMinor": "5000000",
    "refund": "on-merge-at-settlement",
    "effectiveAt": "2026-11-01T00:00:00.000Z",
    "overrides": [
      { "match": { "label": "documentation" }, "amountMinor": "1000000" }
    ]
  }
}
```

v1 is one flat amount per project and `required` mode only. `mode` is an enum so a softer `priority` mode (unpaid PRs still score, paid PRs are surfaced first to reviewers) can be added later without a breaking change, but v1 accepts only `required`. Priority needs a reviewer-facing queue Slop does not own, and it delays the attention cost instead of pricing it. Keeping the enum also leaves a fallback if the legal read below says a hard gate is a problem. Per-label or per-path overrides are a follow-on.

### Flow

1. The contributor's run reaches intake. For a project with postage on, intake answers `402` with the project's receiving address, the amount, and a binding memo (project id, actor node id, PR identity). This is the x402 shape.
2. The client pays directly from the contributor's wallet to the project address. Slop is not in the transfer. The receipt binds the transaction signature.
3. Slop's existing read-only verifier confirms exact recipient, exact amount, memo, success, and finality. Same code path as `verified-on-chain` funding records. Network errors fail closed.
4. Scoring: in `required` mode a merged PR with no verified postage is `held`, not scored. Verified postage never changes score, rank, reward share, or payment. This is the same rule Score v2 already applies to token evidence.
5. Cycle close: the proposal carries a `lines.postageRefund` entry per merged PR next to `lines.sharedPool` and `lines.reviewBudget`. The creator signs one transfer per recipient for the combined total, the way #322 already handles two lines. The dust floor is evaluated on the combined total. Postage on unmerged PRs is not a cycle line at all; it already belongs to the project.

### Where the money sits

Nowhere new. Payer to project, directly, exactly like `funding.mode: direct-noncustodial`. Slop never receives, holds, or refunds a fee.

No escrow. An escrow contract has to be told "this PR merged" before it releases, and whoever holds that key is the admin position this project refuses to have. It is also the custody exposure the design was built to avoid. The refund is instead a public settlement obligation, enforced the same way every payout is enforced: it is on the record in the proposal, verified fail-closed on chain, and shows as unpaid if the project does not send it.

### Guardrails

- Postage may only be enabled on a pool that is `committed` and payment-enabled. A project must not collect fees while its refund path is unfunded. Same a

**Ticket** `BL-01` · **Milestone** Day 4 — Deploy & Submit · **Estimate** running

## Purpose

**Single running log for everything discovered mid-implementation that must not derail the ticket in flight.**

While working any ticket, if you hit a bug, a missing piece, a wrong assumption, a pitfall, an
external constraint, or a scope gap — **do not fix it inline and do not silently drop it.** Append
it here as a comment and carry on with the ticket you are on.

Use `/backlog "<note>"` to append. Every entry must state where it was found so it is traceable.

## Entry format

```
### <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM> · found in <TICKET-ID> · <type>
**What:**        one line
**Impact:**      what breaks or is at risk
**Workaround:**  what we did instead (or "none — deferred")
**Action:**      fix now / fix Day 4 / accept as limitation / document in HLD
```

`<type>` ∈ `bug` · `gap` · `pitfall` · `constraint` · `assumption-wrong` · `perf` · `security` · `data-quality`

## Triage rule

- **Blocks the current ticket's AC** → fix now, and still log it here.
- **Breaks a later ticket** → log, and add a `blocker` note as a comment on that ticket.
- **Neither** → log and defer. Do not touch it.

## End-of-project use

Before submission this ticket is read in full and split into three lists:
1. **Fixed** — closed inline, referenced by commit
2. **Accepted limitations** → these go verbatim into the deck's *"What this system does not do"* slide
   and the HLD's *Assumptions & Constraints* section. This is where honesty scores points.
3. **Future roadmap** → these go into the deck's *Future Vision / Roadmap* dimension

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every entry follows the format above and names its source ticket
- [ ] At submission time, all entries are triaged into one of the three lists
- [ ] Accepted limitations appear in the deck and HLD
- [ ] Roadmap items appear in the Future Roadmap dimension

## Deliverables

- `docs/limitations.md` — generated from this ticket's accepted-limitation entries
- `docs/roadmap.md` — generated from this ticket's roadmap entries

## Validation Gate

- [ ] `docs/limitations.md` and `docs/roadmap.md` exist and are non-empty
- [ ] Zero untriaged entries remain

## Status

**PRODUCT ACCEPTANCE / RELEASE-BOUNDARY OWNER.**

This Issue defines when Tachiko Work is allowed to call one first-party graphical product **publicly usable as an Excel-like product** even though the repository still has unresolved research, architecture, ecosystem, collaboration, and long-tail compatibility work.

It is intentionally **cross-stage and unmilestoned**. It does not replace `docs/product/product-roadmap.md`, create a second milestone system, redefine Accepted semantic authority, or make every open Issue a release blocker.

## Decision

Tachiko Work does **not** wait for the backlog to reach zero.

The first public Excel-like product may launch when one supported first-party graphical distribution proves a complete, trustworthy ordinary-spreadsheet workflow:

> **Tachiko Work satisfies the Excel-like Driver Common Profile for ordinary office spreadsheet workflows.**

This claim must **not** imply full Excel parity, enterprise readiness, Tachiko Work 1.0, realtime collaboration, a stable public plugin ecosystem, or support for every legacy workbook.

The key release rule is:

> **An unresolved problem blocks launch only when it prevents the declared Driver workflow from being completed safely, threatens the correctness/durability of user work, removes the user's escape path, prevents ordinary distribution/use, or legally prevents the actual release/commercial action being taken.**

Everything else may remain open.

## Why this is needed

The repository deliberately contains long-horizon questions that can remain open for years. A research Issue, future architecture problem, or M07/M08 platform promise must not become a current release blocker merely because it exists.

Existing authority already points this way:

- Product Constitution: freeze fewer irreversible contracts; keep the stable core small.
- Design Principles: generalize from real pressure; Office parity is not the goal.
- #170: a graphical product is accepted through a complete end-to-end user workflow, not a GUI demo.
- #215: Driver users should receive value without learning Tachiko internals.
- #240: the evidence-backed first spreadsheet boundary is a **Driver Common Profile**, not an exact global Top 20.
- #18: adoption and migration must remain gradual with usable escape paths.

## Gate A — Driver Common Profile

Use #240's completed research conclusion as the initial product profile. The first release should cover these **15 capability bundles as a task-complete set**, not as a popularity ranking:

1. **Project/workbook lifecycle** — create, open, save, reopen, dirty-state handling, undo/redo, recovery.
2. **Grid navigation, selection, retrieval** — mouse/keyboard navigation, selection, go-to, find/replace, useful large-sheet navigation.
3. **Direct editing and structural operations** — multi-cell editing; insert/delete/move rows, columns, and ranges.
4. **Clipboard interoperability** — cut/copy/paste with other apps; paste values/formulas/formats where supported.
5. **Fill and copy semantics** — fill down/across, series, relative/absolute reference behavior.
6. **Multiple sheets** — add/delete/rename/reorder/duplicate; navigate and reference across sheets.
7. **Values, types, display formats** — at least Text, Number, Boolean, Date/Time, Currency, Percentage with declared locale behavior.
8. **Basic visual formatting/layout** — emphasis, alignment/wrapping, borders/fills, row/column dimensions, freeze/hide where in profile.
9. **Formula/reference/recalculation profile** — arithmetic, comparison, ranges, deterministic recalculation, visible errors/cycles, bounded common functions.
10. **Sort and filter** — stable behavior across declared value/error/blank cases.
11. **Structured table/range workflow** — headers, stable columns, append rows, totals/range expansion, progressive semantic strengthening where useful.
12. **Data validation/dropdowns** — constrained entry and visible invalid-data feedback.
13. **CSV + common-profile XLSX impo

Across the app there are a lot of places where we load rows out of Postgres and then throw most of them away in Ruby — paginating an already-materialized relation, filtering with a block where a scope exists, summing in Ruby, or fanning out one query per row. This is an audit of those, grouped by root cause. **108 distinct sites: 14 critical, 40 high, 41 medium, 13 low.** Full table at the bottom.
Method & caveats — please read before acting on a line item Findings were produced by a code audit and then adversarially re-verified, with each verifier asked to *refute* rather than confirm. That pass changed a lot: of 32 initial claims, 16 survived intact, 15 needed their framing or blast radius corrected, and 1 was wrong outright and cut (`User.where(id: versions.pluck(:whodunnit))` in `Reimbursement::Report` — `whodunnit` is a `string` and `users.id` is `bigint`, so the "obvious" subquery rewrite is a type error Postgres rejects. Left as-is deliberately; noted here so nobody else tries it). Query counts are mechanism-derived, not measured in production. The repo has a benchmark fixture (`Event` "BENCHMARK-SEED Org", 100 CTs) — **reproduce against that before sizing any of this work.** Anything below marked with row counts like "N per page" is a claim about shape, not a measured p99. Nothing here is a correctness bug. It's all load.
## Top 3 by impact ÷ effort **1. Delete two dead `json_agg` sub-selects in the transaction grouping engine.** ~6 lines, no behavior change. [`all.rb:306-313`](app/services/transaction_grouping_engine/transaction/all.rb#L306-L313) and [`:324-331`](app/services/transaction_grouping_engine/transaction/all.rb#L324-L331) make every ledger query carry the **full JSON body of every canonical and pending transaction** in the group, on top of the ids. `#build` ([`:66-77`](app/services/transaction_grouping_engine/transaction/all.rb#L66-L77)) reads five keys and neither of these is among them; a repo-wide grep for `["canonical_transactions"]` / `["canonical_pending_transactions"]` returns nothing. `CanonicalTransactionGrouped`'s `attr_writer`s for those names are only ever written by `FilterTypePreloader`, from a separate query. This pays off on *every* ledger read — org page, v4 index, v3 API, `#home_stats`, `#money_movement`, exports, the Discord job, the running-balance CTE. Nothing else in this issue has that ratio. **2. One set query for `User#hcb_code_ids_missing_receipt`, plus four `.count` → `.size` edits.** Collapses ~9 findings at once (root cause R3 below). **3. Bound the public v3 API.** The only cluster that is both unauthenticated *and* unbounded — see below. ## R1 — Pagination applied after materialization `Kaminari.paginate_array` builds a `PaginatableArray < Array` whose `initialize` does `original_array[offset, limit]`. `ActiveRecord::Relation` delegates `[]` and `to_ary` to `#records`, which calls `load`. **So handing it a Relation loads the entire relation to render one page.** 12 call sites; at 5 the argument is still a Relation. | Site | Effect | |---|---| | [`events_controller.rb:666`](app/controllers/events_controller.rb#L666) | Every non-pending donation the org ever received, instantiated with `recurring_donation` preloaded, to show 25. Fix is a drop-in `.page().per()` — the view's `.any?`/`.pluck`/`.none?` calls all still work, and the count badge is preserved (`build_count_subquery?` honors the LIMIT). Line 649's `@all_donations =` assignment is also dead. | | [`events_controller.rb:228`](app/controllers/events_controller.rb#L228) | The org ledger. `TransactionGroupingEngine::Transaction::All#all` has no LIMIT/OFFSET and maps **every** row into an object, to slice 75 (`TRANSACTIONS_PER_PAGE`). Note `set_cacheable` + `cache_if @cacheable` is a *view fragment* cache — a cache hit still pays the full controller-side build. We've already had to rate-limit this: [`rack_attack.rb:207-234`](config/initializers/rack_attack.rb#L2

- `backlog-recovery-audit`: Terra Medium, native 100,000 token budget; read-only reconciliation of the 15 detached/no-PR/closed-unmerged/diverged copies. Identify unique work, durable recovery evidence, successor acceptance, and safe retirement blockers.

`site.domains` is the best NEW cruel family this epic has found, and it carries a trap that would make a
careless builder record a FALSE refusal on it (charter D269).

WHY IT QUALIFIES. Cap 253, enforced by `validate_change` + `@domain_format` (registry/site.ex:28, :431-436) —
so it is INVISIBLE to a `validate_length` census, which is exactly D252's point about census-driven ledgers.
Member-reachable: `POST /v1/sites/:id/domains` (router.ex:6551) goes through the 2-arity `with_team_site`,
whose `:session` branch is bare `Auth.require_user` (router.ex:10403, :10408) — NO role gate, against twelve
sibling site routes that pass `{:ability, "write"}`. And it is an ARRAY, so it is a population, not a scalar.
A member driving it created a site with a 255-char name (201) and pushed a 253-char domain (200).

THE TRAP. A cruel string here must be a LEGAL HOSTNAME. A 212-char single label is refused with 422. A
builder writing `String.duplicate("q", 253)` records a false NONE-POSSIBLE on the ledger's best family. THE
ADMISSIBLE MAXIMUM IS `3 x 63-char labels + "." + a 61-char label = exactly 253` -> 200, persisting as
`[253]`; 254 -> 422. That construction is the ledger row's `admissible` field and it belongs in the FIXTURE,
not in a charter paragraph. Charter D269 names the class this creates: FORMAT-LEGAL.

TWO REFUSALS THE ROW MUST CARRY, both measured:
  (a) APPEND-ORDER. `add_site_domain` does `Enum.uniq(existing ++ [norm])` (registry.ex:4818), so a member's
      cruel domain lands at `domains[N]`. Every site-list renderer paints `domains[0]` only, so on a site
      that already has a domain the cruel value is INVISIBLE in the list view. The family is cruel-reachable
      in the list only on a site whose `domains` is `[]` — fixtures `acme-labs` and `acme-previews`.
  (b) THE CORPUS CANNOT CURRENTLY MAKE IT CRUEL. Across all 101 scenarios the longest domain is 15 chars
      (`guides.acme.com`) and the longest site name 13 (`acme-previews`), against caps of 253 and 255, and
      `fleet-cruel-content` carries ZERO sites. Clause 4 verbatim.

WHAT TO BUILD: the `site.domains` (and `site.name`, same rung, uncontested) rows in `CRUEL_ROUTES` with their
cap, class, predicate and a FORMAT-LEGAL generator, plus the fixture that produces them. This RIDES
cch-w23-s4, which lands the per-family shape those rows need — do not start before s4 is merged, or the row
shape you write will not exist.

DO NOT DOUBLE-FILE THE GUARD LEG. `task-696a2fcf95e9c4da` ("Permanent guard leg: the site row's three text
hosts, cruel by fixture (W22-S2 follow-on)") is already open, unclaimed, priority 1, parented to this epic,
and already specifies both scenarios (`sites` + `sites-on-instance`, both of which exist), the widths,
"EVERY `.site-row` iterated — never row 0 (the GR109 lesson)", the 253-char domain citing `validate_change`,
the anti-shred height clause, and the fixture problem. ITS `acceptance_criteria` ARRAY IS EMPTY — it needs
perfecting, not re-filing. Whoever takes this row should perfect that one and build them together.

CONTEXT ON THE SCREEN HALF: `.site-name` and `.site-host` are already bounded by cch-w22-s2 (f7886f46c), so
the SCREEN is paid — what is missing is the permanent guard leg proving it stays paid. That is why this is a
ledger/instrument row and not a person-facing slice. The separate person-facing defect on this family — the
list saying a site has one domain when it has two — is being built this wave as
cch-w23-s3-site-row-second-domain-visible.

## Distinct research mandate

Treat persistence and evolving world models as the primary problem. Research event sourcing, bitemporal data, append-only ledgers, materialized views, incremental/differential computation, dependency-directed invalidation, provenance indexing, entity resolution, ontology/schema evolution, scalable graph/log storage, integrity, redaction and governed retention.

## Required output

- compare storage/world-model architectures independent of current implementation;
- define immutable source/semantic/event identities and bitemporal/current views;
- incremental derivation invalidation and recomputation;
- reversible entity/ontology reconciliation;
- schema/IR version migration without rewriting history;
- millions-to-billions-record query/index strategy assumptions;
- crash/replay/idempotency semantics;
- separation of authoritative ledger from rebuildable indexes/views;
- governed deletion/redaction, integrity and admission semantics;
- recommendations for symbolic-memory #4/#6/#10 and Prolog-RLM interfaces.

Do not center model prompting or NLP extraction in this depth.

## Four-subpass status

### A — foundations / representative formalisms: COMPLETE

Adopt **BSLPF — Bitemporal Semantic Ledger + Projection Fabric** as the baseline architecture:

```text
immutable/versioned semantic objects
            +
authoritative append-only bitemporal semantic ledger
            +
versioned rebuildable projections/checkpoints/indexes
```

Hard A distinctions:

```text
semantic object identity
    != assertion/support episode identity
    != ledger event identity
    != commit/batch identity
    != materialized view-row identity
```

The ledger owns durable ordered commit/knowledge history; semantic records retain independent world-valid time. Atomic commit batches, idempotency keys/digests, stable logical frontiers, crash-after-commit replay, versioned projection checkpoints, reversible identity/ontology mappings, and non-destructive schema evolution are part of the logical contract. Current/support/warrant/entity/procedure/retrieval indexes are rebuildable views, not canonical truth.

The current Symbolic Memory whole-snapshot rewrite backend is explicitly a bootstrap implementation, not the durable world-model architecture. Historical `SYMBOLIC-MEMORY-RESEARCH-006` remains preserved as backend/bootstrap research, but its earlier position that a full replayable semantic event history could be optional is superseded at the semantic world-model contract layer by requirements accumulated in #398-#401.

Full A research, primary sources, candidate architectures, typed sketches, rejected alternatives, A1-A24 fixtures and downstream handoffs are preserved in the #402A comment.

### B — semantic / adversarial deepening: COMPLETE

Refine BSLPF with **GRIE — Governed Redaction & Integrity Envelope**.

Hard B correction:

```text
append-only logical commitment history
    != permanent payload retrievability
```

The architecture now separates immutable semantic/event identity from retention/encryption-scoped payload availability and from current epistemic admissibility. Governed lifecycle events distinguish correction, withdrawal, invalidation, quarantine, archive, access revocation, payload redaction, cryptographic erase and physical purge. None of those operations silently manufactures semantic negation.

B also adds:

- explicit admission receipts separating claimed issuer, authenticated submitter/issuer evidence, local authorization decision and commit/registration receipt;
- exact redaction/sanitization completion states (`complete|partial|pending|blocked|failed`) rather than treating a tombstone as proof of physical erasure;
- replay-capability classes such as `exact`, `semantic_only`, `commitment_only`, `redacted`, `corrupt`, `unavailable`;

## Outcome

One organisation owns its assignable roles, Groups, memberships and access assignments. Published applications supply immutable templates. All human access changes use authorised IAM journeys; the sole pre-IAM exception is the explicit trusted bootstrap/adoption handoff described below. Registration, tenant-administrator status, ordinary membership, matching labels and historical grants never create authority by themselves.

## Simplicity guard — required for remaining work

- Preserve three guarantees: role changes are atomic and revision-checked; broadened or restored authority requires explicit fresh acceptance; competing role/assignment changes serialize or refuse stale with no partial effect.
- Use the smallest implementation that meets those guarantees. A new counter, fingerprint, state, abstraction or compatibility layer requires a concrete failure that existing identities, revisions and transactions cannot prevent. Do not add speculative frameworks or extra human approval stages for implementation evidence.
- Reviewers must challenge unnecessary machinery as well as missing safeguards. Collapse duplicated mechanisms only after checking their distinct failure cases; do not weaken removed-permission, existing-activation or policy-return protection simply to reduce the number of fields.
- Fix the root cause instead of adding compensating guard layers. Test distinct required outcomes and relevant failures, not speculative combinations. Unresolved business behaviour is held for the product owner; missing technical prerequisites are dependency-blocked; low-priority maintenance is deferred; engineering/security details are decided by the architect. Do not drift into unrelated maintenance.
- Access version orders access changes; its changed timestamp is observation metadata, not another authorization decision. Local clock defects are environment verification work, not new IAM semantics. Real start/expiry checks remain enforced.

## Purpose
Central durable coordination log for concurrent TornHappyGymStats fleet/Codex work. This is **not implementation backlog**. GitHub live repository/PR/issue state plus the latest valid protocol transitions below are authoritative.

Actual default branch is `main`.

## Absolute authority boundary
Fleet/manual agents may work only on **NON-DEFAULT** branches and must **never merge any branch or PR into `main`** or weaken protections. **Codex is Gerome's designated final reviewer/merger.** Fleet may request Codex review/merge or advisor intervention under the protocol below; the fleet itself never performs the default merge.

Never mutate production or perform state-changing Torn actions. Never commandeer outside-contributor/human branches.

# 🚦 Reliable coordination protocol
Gerome policy update — 2026-09-06. This replaces the old `🔒 CLAIM` / same-comment `🔓 RELEASED` protocol for new work. Treat this issue as an **append-only connection/state log**. The system must remain recoverable when an OpenAI run is cut off before cleanup.

## State machine

### 🟢 OPEN
Default/unowned state. No active fleet lease. No comment is required for never-started work; append an explicit OPEN transition when releasing/abandoning unfinished assigned work.

### 🟡 ASSIGNING — phase 1 / SYN
Before mutation, append a new transition with `seq=1`, unique `run=`, lane, exact issue/package/seam, intended branch, observed default/head and target refs. Then reread this issue's recent transitions. Earlier overlapping ASSIGNING GitHub comment ID wins.

### 🔵 ASSIGNED — phase 2 / ACK
The winner appends a **new** transition with `seq=2`, references the ASSIGNING comment ID as `ack=`, and repeats the exact scope, intended branch and expected head(s). Mutation is forbidden until this ACK exists.

If the assignment loses a collision, append `🟢 OPEN` for that run/scope and choose independent work.

### 🛠️ WORKING @ branch
Immediately after selecting/creating the branch and before useful branch mutation, append a new transition with the exact `branch=` and `head=`. After **every remote head change**, append another WORKING transition with the next sequence number and current head. Include current PR when one exists.

This is the primary crash-recovery record. A future agent must be able to discover the exact branch/head even if the worker disappears mid-run.

### 🧪 WAITING ON PR CR
The work package is coherent and waiting on Codex code/final review. Record PR, exact head/base, required/observed checks, review status and handoff URL/marker. This state **releases the fleet implementation lease**; do not remain WORKING while merely waiting for Codex.

### 🆘 WAITING ON ADVISOR
The fleet cannot safely reconcile work selection, state, branch topology or repeated failures itself. Record an anomaly fingerprint and evidence and send **one deduplicated `@codex` advisor request** on this issue asking Codex to investigate **and repair** the live coordination/branch/PR state. This state releases the fleet lease.

### ✅ FINISHED
The issue/package is actually done: required default incorporation or an explicit completed/not-planned disposition is verified and issue completion semantics are satisfied. Record the final PR/default SHA/disposition. A branch push or PR creation is not FINISHED.

## Wire format
Every transition is a **NEW comment**; do not edit an older transition into another state.

Minimum fields:

`<emoji> <STATE> | seq=<monotonic integer> | run=<token> | lane=<lane> | issue/package=<id> | branch=<name-or-none> | head=<sha-or-none> | pr=<number-or-none> | prev=<prior-state/comment-id> | ts=<ISO8601> | note=<short result>`

Rules:
- Unknown values are explicit `none` / `unknown`; never silently omit load-bearing metadata.
- Before retrying an ambiguous write, reread recent comments and suppress an existing identical `run+seq` transition.
- Sequence gaps, contradictory latest states, unexpected branch/head movement or duplicate active ownership fail closed un

## Bounty Verification Bot

We spend hours every session manually checking star counts, follow status, wallet existence, and article links. A bot that auto-verifies claims would save massive time.

### What to Build

A GitHub Action or bot that monitors bounty issue comments, detects claims, and posts automated verification results.

### Payout

| Milestone | Reward |
|-----------|--------|
| Star/follow verification (reads comment, checks GitHub API, posts result) | **30 RTC** |
| Wallet existence check (queries RustChain node API) | **+10 RTC** |
| Article/URL verification (checks dev.to/Medium links are live) | **+10 RTC** |
| Dev.to article word count + quality check | **+10 RTC** |
| Duplicate claim detection (checks if user already claimed) | **+15 RTC** |

### How It Should Work

1. **Triggered by**: New comment on bounty issues containing keywords like "Claiming", "Wallet:", "Stars:", "GitHub:"
2. **Checks performed**:
   - Does user follow @Scottcjn? (`GET /users/{user}/following/Scottcjn` → 204 = yes)
   - How many Scottcjn repos has user starred? (paginate `/users/{user}/starred`)
   - Does the claimed wallet exist? (`GET https://50.28.86.131/wallet/balance?miner_id={wallet}`)
   - Is the claimed article URL live? (HEAD request, check 200)
   - Has this user already been paid? (check for "PAID" in previous comments)
3. **Posts a verification comment**:
```
## Automated Verification for @username

| Check | Result |
|-------|--------|
| Follows @Scottcjn | ✅ Yes |
| Scottcjn repos starred | 45 |
| Wallet `my-wallet` exists | ✅ Balance: 10.5 RTC |
| Article link | ✅ Live (dev.to, 612 words) |
| Previous claims | ⚠️ Paid 25 RTC on #665 |

**Suggested payout**: 45 stars × 1.0 RTC (follows + 45+ multiplier) = 45 RTC
```

### Technical Requirements

1. **GitHub Action** (preferred) — runs on `issue_comment` webhook
2. **Secrets needed**: `GITHUB_TOKEN` (for API), `RUSTCHAIN_NODE_URL`
3. **Rate limit aware** — GitHub API has limits, batch requests efficiently
4. **No payment execution** — bot ONLY verifies, human approves payment
5. **Configurable** — bounty rules (rate per star, follow multiplier) in a config file
6. **Open source** on GitHub

### Why This Matters

Manual verification takes 2-5 minutes per claim. With 20+ claims per session, that's over an hour of repetitive API checking. The bot does it in seconds and never makes math errors.

The human (Scott) still decides whether to pay — the bot just eliminates the grunt work.

### Submit As

Standalone repo with GitHub Action workflow, or PR to a new `Scottcjn/bounty-bot` repo.

**Wallet:** Include your wallet address when claiming.

## Context

AWS Bedrock AgentCore Payments (announced this week) makes x402 the enterprise rail for agent commerce at scale. The x402 protocol handles settlement cleanly. x402-signals (#2291) covers post-settlement fulfillment obligations from the provider side.

The gap that remains: **a third party — regulator, auditor, counterparty — cannot independently verify what the agent did after settlement without trusting the operator's infrastructure.**

## The problem

`payment_hash` proves the payment completed. It does not prove:
- What action the agent took after receiving payment
- That the action record wasn't modified after the fact
- That the agent acted within its authorized scope

For regulated deployments (EU AI Act Art. 12 enforcement August 2, 2026; FCA SYSC 9.1; SOC 2 CC7.x), this gap is the compliance blocker. Logs can be rewritten. An external anchor cannot.

## Proposed pattern

A `TrailRecord` anchored externally after agent action completes, keyed by the same `action_ref` that `payment_hash` references:

```
payment_hash (x402 settlement proof)
    └── action_ref = SHA-256(agent_id || action_type || scope || timestamp_ms)
            └── TrailRecord (tamper-evident, external anchor)
                    └── anchor_id (Sigstore Rekor / on-chain tx)
```

The audit property: a verifier with the `payment_hash` can follow the chain to the `TrailRecord` and confirm the action record hasn't been modified — without access to the operator's infrastructure.

## Relationship to existing work

- x402-signals (#2291): fulfillment SLA + refund patterns — **provider obligations**
- This proposal: tamper-evident proof of action — **auditor verification**

Complementary, not overlapping. x402-signals answers "what should the provider do." This answers "how does a third party verify it happened."

## Implementation

We've built this as Mycelium Trails — an external anchoring layer that uses `payment_hash` as the cross-surface key between x402 settlement and post-execution evidence. The spec is in [argentum-core](https://github.com/giskard09/argentum-core) and a community plugin for the AGT EvidenceAnchor SPI is in review at microsoft/agent-governance-toolkit#2244.

Happy to contribute a reference spec or fixture if the Foundation wants to document this pattern alongside x402-signals.
title: Post-settlement accountability layer: tamper-evident proof of agent action after payment

## 目的

Crownless を、スケジュール実行するAIエージェントが自分で次の遊びを考え、Issue化し、実装まで進める「自律プロダクト開発」のPOCとして記録する。

将来の出版・振り返りで、単なるGit履歴では分からない **AIが何を考え、なぜそれを選び、人間がどこで介入したか** を一次資料として残す。

このIssueは実装タスクではなく、実験ログの正本として扱う。原則closeせず、各自律開発サイクルをコメントで追記する。

## 各サイクルで残す内容

### 1. Cycle
- 実行日時（Asia/Tokyo）
- 起動種別: scheduled / human-triggered
- 対象main SHA（取得できる場合）

### 2. AI proposal
- 直近3〜5サイクルで新しい遊びが増えたか
- 新機能候補3案
- 各候補の4軸スコア
  - プレイヤーが気づく変化
  - 新しい判断
  - リプレイ性
  - Canonとの整合

### 3. Decision
- 今回選んだIssue / 新規アイデア
- なぜそれを選んだか
- 他候補を選ばなかった主な理由
- bug-fix / maintenance / innovation の区分

### 4. Execution
- 新規Issue / 既存Issue
- 実装した縦切り
- PR / commit
- test / CI
- merge / close結果

### 5. Human intervention
前回サイクル以降、人間による方向修正がGitHub上または実行コンテキストから確認できる場合に記録する。

例:
- 新しいIssueを人間が追加した
- AI案を却下・修正した
- 優先順位を変更した
- 実装済み機能の作り直しを指示した
- 直接エージェントへ割り込んだ

介入が確認できなければ `なし / 確認できず` とし、推測で人間介入を作らない。

### 6. Outcome / observation
- プレイヤーから見て何が変わったか
- 新しい遊び・判断が増えたか
- AIの判断で気になった点
- 次回観察したいこと

## 記録原則

- 事実とAIの評価を分ける
- 後から書き換えず、原則コメントを追加して時系列を保つ
- Issue/PR/commitへリンクできる情報を残す
- 長い実装ログやCI全文は複製せず、意思決定に必要な要約だけを残す
- 人間介入は確認できたものだけを記録し、推測しない
- 成功だけでなく、`no_action`、失敗、誤った提案、revert、方向修正も残す

## このPOCで検証したい問い

> AIは、与えられたIssueを消化するだけでなく、自分で「次に何を作るべきか」を考え、ゲームを継続的に面白くできるか。

> 人間は常時開発ループを回さず、必要なときだけIssue追加や直接指示で介入する運用へ移れるか。

Related: #228
title: POC: AI自律開発の意思決定・人間介入ログ

## Summary

`docs/src/DEPLOYMENT.md`'s mainnet-readiness checklist has no documented rationale for what `bond_amount`, `challenge_window_secs`, resolver committee size, or `finalize_reward_bps` should actually be set to on a real mainnet deployment. The values currently used in `scripts/testnet-load.sh` (`BOND_AMOUNT=1000000`, `CHALLENGE_WINDOW_SECS=120`) are explicitly test-convenience values (a 120-second challenge window exists so the load test finishes quickly, not because it's a real candidate for production), and nothing analyzes what production values should be or why.

`docs/src/V2_BOND_SIZING.md` already did exactly this kind of grounded economic analysis for v2's registration/reveal windows and minimum bond. v1 has no equivalent document.

## Scope

- A written proposal (a new doc, e.g. `docs/src/V1_BOND_SIZING.md` or an extension to `DEPLOYMENT.md`) covering: recommended `bond_amount` relative to expected assertion value and griefing cost, `challenge_window_secs` relative to real-world dispute-response time (120 seconds is a load-test artifact, not a production candidate), resolver committee size and composition trade-offs, and `finalize_reward_bps` sized to actually incentivize prompt finalization without being wasteful.
- Should be grounded in real usage data from running `scripts/testnet-load.sh` at realistic N/D values, not purely theoretical, following the same evidence-based approach `V2_BOND_SIZING.md` used.
- Explicitly state assumptions (expected assertion value range, expected dispute frequency) since the right parameters depend entirely on what Tholos is actually securing.

## Proposed approach

Not prescribed beyond the above. This is analysis and documentation work, no contract changes. The assignee should run `scripts/testnet-load.sh` at a few different N/D scales, record actual gas/timing/economic behavior, and use that data to ground the recommended values rather than picking round numbers.
title: [Feature] Written mainnet parameter-selection proposal for tholos v1

Build a small, attractive, playable town demo around Crystal Cascade's normal jewel game. The town gives the player a story, familiar characters, and a visible reason to play another level and return later. Keep each decision easy: earn money, help with one basic need, and enjoy what changes.

**This issue covers brainstorming and a working frontend demo without a backend.** Use local saves to evaluate the feel. Accounts, cloud recovery, synchronization, and stronger security are tracked in [the Symfony backend follow-up #10](https://github.com/Starbugstone/Crystal-Cascade/issues/10) and must not block this demo. The scope below replaces the earlier, larger town simulation proposal.

**The story begins with bare plots in an abandoned Old West settlement.** The player is a jewel miner rebuilding *Prospect Hollow*. Ada introduces the empty town. Choose any first building; its materials are free. Each completed puzzle adds visible work. New buildings take two to five completed puzzles, with later improvements taking up to seven; only completion activates a benefit. A completed well, farm, and home welcome the first family, in any build order. Later, a saloon opens, horses arrive, and a sheriff brings protection. Short, skippable conversations give each change some personality.

1. Open a warm English/French landing page explaining the game, then enter the village. Click the mine to play the next unfinished match-3 level and collect jewels.
2. Receive town coins on completion, alongside existing chest rewards.
3. Choose any plot; the suggested goal is guidance only. See the materials cost, required wins, and eventual benefit.
4. Start as many buildings as you can afford, with one project per plot and materials paid up front. Each completed puzzle, including a replay, adds one saved step to every active construction.
5. Watch materials become foundations, framing, and a completed building. Benefits activate on completion; the home extension takes four wins. Click the mine model or its label to enter the next unfinished level.

Progress, curiosity, and attachment to the town should encourage players to return. There are no daily chores, construction timers, worker assignments, resource trading, maintenance bills, or penalties for taking a break. Town activity never prevents starting the next unfinished puzzle. Results return to the village; the standalone level-selection page is replaced by the museum. Keep Welcome, Village, and Mine tabs in the header, plus Museum once built; Mine starts the next unfinished level and keeps an active run when clicked during play. Make the map the center of the experience. Tapping a plot opens a focused dialog, presented as a bottom sheet on phones. Starting work returns to the map. All plots opens a directory for off-screen and locked sites; locked entries link to their prerequisite. Keep stories in a collapsible journal and remove the permanent sidebar/list/bottom action bar.

**Basic needs should read like requests from townspeople.** Show coins, population, and small statuses for water, food, and homes: “Water ready,” “We need a farm,” or “A family needs a home.” One suggested action explains what to do next. The player does not calculate consumption or balance production chains.

| Building | Simple purpose | Visible result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Well | Supply drinking water | Repaired roof and bucket; residents collect water |
| Farm | Provide food | Crops appear, fences improve, a farmer works outside |
| Homes | Welcome people | Repaired roofs, warm windows, porches, new families |
| Saloon / bar | Give people somewhere to meet | Lit frontage, music, people gathering outside |
| Horse stable | Bring horses and travel into town | Horses, hitching posts, a wagon |
| Sheriff's office | Protect the town | A sheriff arrives and patrols; protection matters in bandit stories |
| Museum | Replays and continuous play | A crystal display porch and collection of discovered levels |
| Upgradeable armory
title: Playable demo: A simple story-driven town funded by jewel mining

## Purpose

Persistent intake queue for **gathered but not-yet-implemented scientific/data enrichment**. This queue is deliberately separate from implementation WIP: research can be collected, verified, deduplicated, and ranked here even when the sprint has no legal implementation slot.

This is **not** a second scientific authority and does not bypass the enrichment governor, source registry, workbook/normalized-data contracts, provenance requirements, or merge gates. Canonical mutation still requires the normal governed implementation path and a legal WIP slot.

## Queue lifecycle

Each candidate moves through:

`DISCOVERED → VERIFIED → DEDUPED → READY_FOR_GOVERNED_IMPLEMENTATION → IMPLEMENTING → MERGED`

Other terminal/holding states:

- `REJECTED` — source/entity/claim is unsuitable or misleading.
- `BLOCKED_TOOLING` — evidence is good but current ingestion tooling cannot represent it safely.
- `BLOCKED_SEMANTIC` — identity/claim boundary needs resolution.
- `STALE_REVALIDATE` — evidence or external assumption needs freshness review before promotion.

## Required fields per queue item

- target entity / slug
- candidate source identity: PMID / DOI / canonical URL / title
- study class and population
- formulation / preparation / species boundary
- exact claim or field the source can support
- important null findings / limitations / uncertainty
- safety / interaction boundaries when relevant
- funding / conflict / supplier provenance when relevant
- repository dedup result
- current-site defect or missing field addressed
- proposed normalized destination
- status
- confidence
- priority rationale
- dependency / blocker
- discovered date / last verified date

## Ranking guidance

Highest priority generally goes to:

1. published factual/source integrity defects;
2. held profiles that can be safely unlocked with human evidence;
3. missing human evidence on already-indexed profiles;
4. high-value safety/interaction evidence;
5. recent systematic reviews/meta-analyses/RCTs that materially change certainty;
6. entity-resolution fixes that prevent a class of bad enrichment;
7. depth-only enrichment for already well-covered profiles.

Safety/scientific integrity overrides numeric convenience. Negative/null evidence is first-class and must not be discarded merely because it does not support a positive claim.

## Seed queue — 2026-08-27

### Q-001 — Sage (`sage`) — HIGH / integrity
**Status:** VERIFIED / READY_FOR_GOVERNED_IMPLEMENTATION once a legal WIP slot exists

**Current defect:** published Sage profile says none of the recorded studies measured outcomes in people, while genuine human clinical evidence exists. Current source set also contains PMID `40302443`, *Huntington's disease clinical trials update: March 2025*, which concerns SAGE-718 / Sage Therapeutics rather than botanical *Salvia officinalis*.

**Candidate evidence:**
- PMID `24836739` — systematic review of clinical studies of *Salvia officinalis* / *S. lavandulaefolia*; includes human cognition evidence and important heterogeneity limitations.
- PMID `18350281`, DOI `10.1007/s00213-008-1101-3` — randomized double-blind crossover human trial of *Salvia officinalis* extract in older adults.
- PMID `33466627` — randomized placebo-controlled human cognition study using a combined *S. officinalis* polyphenol + *S. lavandulaefolia* terpene preparation; combination boundary must remain explicit.

**Required implementation boundary:** remove/reject the unrelated SAGE-718 source, correct the human-evidence rationale, preserve species/preparation differences, and add a resolver regression so `sage` cannot match company/drug uses such as Sage Therapeutics / SAGE-718 solely by token overlap.

### Q-002 — Kanna (`kanna`) — HIGH / held-profile evidence
**Status:** VERIFIED / READY_FOR_GOVERNED_IMPLEMENTATION once a legal WIP slot exists

**Current defect:** generated profile says none of the recorded studies measured outcomes in people; current sources are reviews/metabolism wor

body_excerpt:
## 背景

Crownless は現在、Canonical core loop として

> **Walk → Discover → Prepare → Dispatch → Wait → Report → Adapt**

を採用し、Location × Expedition RPG として多数の縦切りを積み上げてきた。

一方、直近の開発では以下のような価値ある機能が個別に増えている。

- World Atlas / 周辺調査
- NPC signal / World Traces / 追跡
- 地点固有のPrepare判断
- 仲間の意見・夜番・地縁
- Geographic Loot
- 負傷・撤退・回収・follow-up destination
- 帰還Report / 遠征絵巻

これらは個別には面白いが、増分実装が続いた結果、プレイヤーから見ると **「機能や選択肢は増えたが、一つのゲーム体験としてのつながりが弱い」** 状態へ寄るリスクがある。

また #426 でモバイル1 viewport中心のゲームシェル改善が入り、current main では UI / Atlas / expedition 周辺が大きく更新された。ここを土台に、次は小さな機能追加ではなく、既存の良い実装を残しながら **探索から次の探索までを一本の体験として再構成する**。

このIssueはスクラッチからの作り直しではない。

> **既存Canon・有用なdomain state・位置情報/privacy・決定論的resolverを正本として維持し、プレイヤー体験を阻害している継ぎ目を大胆に作り直す Reforge である。**

開始時点で観測した main SHA: `9c71aedadbf92c902d23426c6743c8c2345da07c`

ただし実装開始時は必ず最新 `main` を再取得し、このSHAを現状決め打ちの正本として扱わないこと。

---

## Product hypothesis

Crownless の価値は、個々の機能数ではなく次の因果がプレイヤーの中で一本につながることにある。

> **自分が現実を歩いて何かを見つけた → そこへ誰を何の準備で送るか迷った → 待った → 何が起きたか気になって戻った → 結果によって世界・仲間・装備・次の行き先が変わった → 次はどうするか迷った**

Phase 1 の仮説は次の通り。

> **既存の探索・遠征・Report・Adapt の断片を一本の cohesive な黄金ループへ再構成すれば、「機能を操作するWebアプリ」感が減り、「自分が開拓した世界へ人を送り、その結果を待つゲーム」として明確に感じられる。**

### North Star

Canonical validation question を最優先する。

> **After dispatching an expedition, does the player want to reopen the game to see what happened?**

---

## Canon boundary — ここは変えない

実装前に最低限以下を読むこと。

1. `AGENTS.md`
2. `docs/game-system-design.md`
3. `docs/expedition-system-spec.md`
4. `docs/exploration-location-spec.md`
5. `docs/hearth-presentation-spec.md`
6. `docs/autonomous-development-policy.md`
7. 視覚変更を伴う場合は `docs/visual-design-guide-v0.2.md` と Visual Canon 一式

以下はこのIssue内では固定する。

- Location × Expedition RPG という方向性
- `Walk → Discover → Prepare → Dispatch → Wait → Report → Adapt`
- real-time player-controlled action combat は復活させない
- 現実移動は step reward ではなく discovery を増やすために使う
- raw latitude / longitude / exact route history を永続化しない
- discovered place / world knowledge の stable identity を維持する
- expedition は deterministic / seeded resolution を基本とする
- active expedition の resolution / report apply は idempotent
- Grey Hearth は管理ダッシュボードではなく「戻る場所」である
- companion / equipment / trait は数字だけでなく判断・分岐を変える
- runtime LLM 呼び出しを gameplay resolution の必須条件にしない

---

## Astra / coding agent に与える裁量

### 大胆に変更してよいもの

このIssueの目的に必要なら、以下は現状実装へ強く拘らず再構成してよい。

- World Atlas / Grey Hearth / Expedition presentation の画面遷移
- UI shell / modal / drawer / folio / overlay の責務配置
- presentation module の分割・統合
- Atlas → Prepare → Report → Adapt の orchestration
- 同じ状態を別々に描画している重複presentation
- legacy entrypoint / synthetic click / fallback flow
- 近年増えた sidecar module の接続方法
- Report / 遠征絵巻の構成方法
- player-facing wording / information hierarchy
- DOM構造・CSS構造
- 明確に superseded した旧UI/runtime path

ただし削除前に参照元・tests・runtime loader・deployment を追跡すること。

### 勝手に変更してはいけないもの

以下が必要になったらその時点で止め、別Issue / human gate とする。

- gameplay Canon / core loop の変更
- save schema migration / irreversible player-state migration
- GPS / privacy boundary の変更
- raw location の追加保存
- framework全面置換
- backend / always-on server 導入
- hosting strategy の変更
- monetization
- faction war / large simulation の新設
- production visual direction の変更
- production asset の大量生成
- 大規模な既存データ削除
- real-time combat の復活

---

## 実装開始時の必須監査

コードを書く前に、最新mainについて次を確認する。

1. Canon / ADR / subsystem specs
2. open Issues / open PRs / recent merged PRs
3. current runtime loader / entrypoints
4. Atlas / Hearth / Expedition / Report の authoritative state source
5. localStorage / save state / world knowledge / expedition state の責務
6. recent sidecar modules がどこで読み込まれ、何をdecorate/applyしているか
7. legacy combat / legacy expedition / hidden button / fallback flow が残っている箇所
8. mobile viewportで実際に主要ループを通したときの遷移

PR説明には最低限、触れた主要領域について次の分類を残す。

- **Keep** — そのまま利用
- **Consolidate** — 統合して利用
- **Replace** — presentation/orchestrationを置換
- **Remove** — 明確にsupersededかつ参照確認済み
- **Defer** — 今回は触らない

新しい巨大な設計文書を作ること自体を成果にしない。

---

## Phase 1 の Golden Loop

Phase 1 は全ゲームを完成させるIssueではない。

**
title: Crownless Reforge Phase 1: 探索→遠征→報告→次の判断を一本のゲーム体験として再構成する
