### L01b — Apply for an SCF Build Award

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Code** | L01b |
| **Phase** | Contract Phase 2 — hardening (readiness sub-task for L01) |
| **Size** | M |
| **Depends on** | Ideally after #5 (E03, contract vertical-slice demo) so the application can point at a real testnet deployment, not just a plan |
| **Money path** | No |
| **Screenshot required** | No |
| **I18n required** | No |

**Executive summary**
This is the longest-lead task in either build plan and has no issue today despite gating the entire mainnet path. The chain is fixed: **SCF award → Audit Bank → mainnet**. The Audit Bank will not even begin its readiness assessment for a project without an existing SCF award — there is no way to apply to the Bank while an SCF application is still under review. SCF Build itself typically runs **3–6 months**, with no fixed round dates published. Every week this isn't submitted is a week added to the mainnet timeline, independent of how fast the rest of the product ships.

**Product context**
See [docs/contracts-build-plan.md](https://github.com/Astrea-Payouts/astrea/blob/develop/docs/contracts-build-plan.md)'s "Funding L01: the Soroban Audit Bank" section for the full chain and timeline math (SCF 3–6 months + Audit Bank intake 1–4 weeks + audit + a 20-business-day remediation window ≈ half a year end to end).

**User stories**
- As the team, we want mainnet planning to start from a realistic half-year number, which only happens once this application is actually in.

**Prerequisites**
- A testnet-functional project with a clear architecture and visible mainnet preparation — the SCF Build criteria explicitly allow applying before the product is fully complete, so this should not wait for Phase 2/3 to finish. Best timed once #5 (E03, contract vertical-slice demo) is live, so the application has a real deployment to point at.
- No registered company required — individuals can apply (KYC/KYB depending on the case), so there's no organizational blocker either.

**Scope — In**
- Prepare the SCF Build Award application: ecosystem value, technical feasibility, roadmap clarity, team capability — the four things it's evaluated on.
- Reference the testnet deployment, the ADRs, and the spike findings as evidence of "visible preparation for mainnet."
- Submit it.
- Track the application's status and update `docs/contracts-build-plan.md` once a decision lands.

**Scope — Out**
- The Audit Bank application itself — that's a separate step, gated on this one's outcome, and effectively L01b's successor once awarded.
- Any code changes made specifically to look better for the application — if a gap surfaces while writing it, file an issue; don't rush a fix into this task's scope.

**Architecture & conventions**
None — this is a grant application, not a code task. Ground every claim in what's actually merged (don't overstate readiness).

**Files to create/modify**
- `docs/contracts-build-plan.md` — update the L01 readiness checklist once submitted, and again once decided.

**Implementation guide**
1. Read the SCF Build Award's current application requirements at communityfund.stellar.org.
2. Draft the application referencing Astrea's actual state: testnet spikes (K01, K06), the production contract's design (ADR-002, ADR-006), and the product's real-world use case (hackathon/bounty prize payouts).

### Problem or use case

A Bazaar catalog entry, and the quality counters attached to it, cannot be distinguished between **a payment that happened** and **a payload that was merely checked**. Both produce an entry, and the spec is the reason.

`specs/extensions/bazaar.md` Facilitator Behavior says a facilitator receiving a `PaymentPayload` containing the `bazaar` extension should validate `info` against `schema` and extract the discovery information. **Settlement appears nowhere in that section.** The response-header section is consistent with this: a facilitator MAY append `EXTENSION-RESPONSES` to **"the verify or settlement response"**, and `status: "success"` there means the discovery info was validated and successfully cataloged.

So the verify path is written into the spec, and every conforming catalog inherits it. This is not one implementation misbehaving, which is why this is filed as a spec proposal rather than a bug against a facilitator.

**Measured, not inferred.** On 2026-08-21T14:10:40Z I sent a `PaymentPayload` for a resource I operate, carrying `extensions.bazaar`, to a facilitator's `/verify`, and never settled:

```
status                200
body                  {"isValid":true,"payer":"0x9f54460FED..."}
EXTENSION-RESPONSES   eyJiYXphYXIiOnsic3RhdHVzIjoicHJvY2Vzc2luZyJ9fQ==
decoded               {"bazaar":{"status":"processing"}}
```

**No tokens moved.** Our chain-versus-ledger invariant was unchanged across the call.

I am claiming exactly what that shows and no more: the payload was **accepted for discovery processing at verify**. Whether a row always follows `processing` is unresolved on my side, and I have said so publicly rather than assert the stronger version.

Two independent lines of evidence from others point the same way and are worth reading together with it: the 17-route natural experiment reported in #2112, where routes settled with the declaration attached indexed and routes settled without it did not, which isolates the **declaration** rather than the settlement as the variable; and the census work in #3045, which found catalogued rows whose payee addresses show no inbound transfers, credited with calls and unique payers. I am citing those rather than speaking for their authors.

**Impact.** The counters are being read as a demand signal. If an entry can be produced by a verify, then `l30DaysTotalCalls` and `l30DaysUniquePayers` may count payloads seen rather than payments made, and an entry plus its counts costs one HTTP request and requires **no balance**, since an authorization that would fail at settle still verifies. Anyone selecting a service on those numbers is reading something a stranger can mint.

### Proposed solution

**Do not close the door. Label what came through it.**

Record provenance on the catalog entry and expose it in discovery results, minimally as a two-valued field distinguishing an entry whose declaration arrived on a **verify** from one that arrived on a **settlement**, and correspondingly separate the call counters, or mark them with the same provenance.

That achieves three things at once:

1. **The counters stop being ambiguous.** A reader can tell a payload that was checked from a payment that happened.
2. **Nothing breaks for honest services.** Many legitimately verify far more often than they settle, and they keep their entry and their visibility.
3. **The free-minting path stays open and stops mattering**, because an entry marked verified-only is not worth minting.

**Non-goals.** Not proposing that verify stop cataloging, not proposing a new authentication requirement, and not proposing that verified-only entries be hidden or ranked down. The ask is a label, not a gate.

### Related

- #3005 is adjacent but a different axis: whether client-echoed metadata is **truthful**. This one is whether an entry reflects a **payment**. Both concern what a reader may infer from a catalog row, and neither subsumes the other.
- #3178 established that the declaration must
title: [Feature]: Label catalog provenance, verify-only versus settled, so Bazaar counters mean something

## Description:

In a previous bounty, we asked the community to stress-test **Memanto** in order to find bugs, logic loops, and performance bottlenecks. We got an unexpectedly large number of PR's and we’ve spent a great deal of time meticulously reviewing them, you’ve all helped us make a huge step forward in improving the security and quality of Memanto!

Now, we are taking it a step further and focusing exclusively on what matters most for AI in production: **Security**.

As memory layers become the backbone of autonomous agents, they also become a prime target for attacks. Whether it's a cross-tenant data leak, a broken access control, or a malicious payload hidden in a retrieved memory, we want to know about it. We’ve fixed a majority of bugs and issues with Memanto and resolved many of its security issues, but as Memanto starts to be utilized in more sensitive workflows, we want to ensure our defenses are as robust as possible and we need the developer community to help us do that.

Your mission is simple: **Help us audit our memory management and backend infrastructure to uncover potential vulnerabilities before they can be exploited.** 

---

## 🎯 Threat Model & Scope
Your target is the `memanto` core package and its interaction with the `moorcheh.ai` serverless backend. We are prioritizing traditional application security flaws, data isolation failures, and API vulnerabilities. 

### 🔴 Security Focus Areas (In Scope)
- **Tenant Isolation & Cross-Account Leaks:** Can User A query, retrieve, or overwrite memories belonging to User B through the core package or backend API?
- **Authentication & Authorization Bypasses:** Finding ways to read or write to the memory layer without a valid API key, or bypassing intended role/access restrictions.
- **API Vulnerabilities:** Standard backend flaws such as Insecure Direct Object References (IDOR), broken object level authorization, or injection flaws in the `moorcheh.ai` backend.
- **Data Exfiltration:** Tricking the system or bypassing controls to extract raw vector data, plaintext logs, or sensitive hidden context from the memory store.
- **AI-Specific Exploits (Indirect Prompt Injections):** Exploiting the retrieval process to inject dormant malicious payloads into memory that later hijack the agent's core instructions when recalled (i.e., treating memory as a trojan horse).

### 🚫 Rules of Engagement (Out of Scope)
- Volumetric DDoS attacks against `moorcheh.ai` infrastructure.
- General LLM hallucinations or standard logic bugs unrelated to security.
- Attacks that require compromising the underlying operating system or Docker host to succeed.

---

### **📝 Submission Guidelines**
Because this bounty is hosted on BountyHub, **a public Pull Request is required to award funds.** 

- **Primary Method:** Fork the repository and open a Pull Request containing your fix, a summary of the flaw, and reproduction steps. This acts as your official bounty claim.
- **Sensitive Findings:** If you believe you've found a sensitive vulnerability that shouldn't be public yet, you can optionally email the Proof of Concept to `support@moorcheh.ai` for our team to review first. However, you will still need to open a redacted PR to claim the bounty.

---

### 📊 Judgment Method (The Success Matrix)
To ensure we reward actual engineering value and meaningful security research, submissions will be scored on a 100-point matrix split between **Technical Rigor** and **Impact**.

| Criteria | Max Points | How it is Measured |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Severity & Impact** | 60 pts | How critical is the vulnerability? (e.g., a cross-tenant data leak scores much higher than a theoretical edge case). |

"good smart speaker assistant". The review scored its attributes B (resilience), B− (observability),

the debt is concentrated and mostly subtraction. Your job is to finish the program the brief defines,
fold in the review's voice rows, and leave the loop at **A** without making it bigger, more abstract,
or more prose-heavy than it is today.

## The three rules that override everything else

1. **You do not do lane work. You delegate.** You do not grep, read files at length, edit, or run
   test suites yourself beyond a spot-check to settle a disagreement. Every scout, every survey,
   every edit, every test run is a subagent. Name the model explicitly on every `Agent` call:

   and waits for the owner's explicit word. If you are about to merge a PR that has not had both
   passes, you are doing it wrong: stop and run them. Say in the PR body which passes ran.
3. **Trust, but verify.** The brief and the review hand you findings with `file:line` evidence, but
   the repo moves at ~400 commits a day and six PRs landed in this loop after the brief was taken.

This is an issue for discussing cool program ideas that may or may not be implemented (hence the name). 

I'll start with an idea from me.

--- 

I have an idea for a new text editor called `nate`: _nate's another text editor._

`nate` isn't like most text editors:

* It's educational, so you can teach it in 30 minutes and implement it in 60 minutes
* It's versatile, so you can read editing scripts from a file or pipe them from a program for automated edits
* It's memorizable, so each command comes with a mnemonic that lets you remember how to use `nate` long after learning it for the first time

Here's what I'm thinking for the commands (subject to change in the future):

Line commands:
| Command    | Purpose | Mnemonic |
| -------- | ------- | ------- |
| `sl`    | Select a line by number; if the line doesn't exist and follows an existing one, create it    | **S**elect **L**ine |
| `fl`    | Find the first instance of a string and select the associated line    | **F**ind **L**ine |
| `al`    | Append an empty line and select it  | **A**ppend **L**ine |
| `aml`    | Append a multi-line string ending in `<END>`  | **A**ppend **M**ulti-**L**ine string|
| `dl`    | Delete the selected line; if there is a previous line, select that one instead  | **D**elete **L**ine |
| `pl`    | Print the selected line  | **P**rint **L**ine |

File operations:
| Command    | Purpose | Mnemonic |
| -------- | ------- | ------- |
| `wf`  | Write to a file  | **W**rite **F**ile |
| `lf` | Load from a file     | **L**oad **F**ile |

Misc. commands:

| Command    | Purpose | Mnemonic |
| -------- | ------- | ------- |
| `h`  | Show help information   | **H**elp |
| `q` | Exit `nate`     | **Q**uit |

It's meant to be simple enough that you can write an implementation in almost any language, but for starters I intend on writing it in Nim.

Edit: Added the `sl` command!

Edit 2: The tables above are outdated. See https://git.hermits.cc/PPPDUD/nate-specs for the latest information.

Parent/related: #84, #44, #159, #164, #165, #166, #86

Baseline at decision time: `develop@e342638f45c54951cf66f58cc269bfe8c814c8cd`.

## User requirement

When GitHub auto-commit is ON, a newly ACCEPTED solution must be able to reach the configured GitHub target even when **no Dashboard document is open at all**.

This issue uses “Dashboard closed” literally: no eligible Dashboard tab/document/Port exists. Merely hidden/background Dashboard behavior was already addressed by #159 and is not sufficient for this requirement.

## Integrator architecture decision

The current static Dashboard-owned runtime cannot satisfy the literal requirement. A server worker alone is also insufficient because, while the Dashboard is closed, the newly captured source exists only in Extension local storage and the server has no transport by which to learn it.

Approved direction is therefore a **hybrid server-owned background automation + narrowly scoped Extension capture relay**.

This decision intentionally supersedes only the minimum part of the previous capture-only boundary required for closed-Dashboard operation:

- Extension still owns ACCEPTED capture and IndexedDB local truth.
- Extension still must not own GitHub OAuth, GitHub App credentials, installation tokens, repository write decisions, target validation, conditional GitHub write logic, or GitHub retries.
- Main API/worker becomes the durable owner/executor of background auto-sync/GitHub auto-commit intent and target state.
- Extension may be provisioned with a **revocable, device/account-bound, append-only capture relay grant** whose only purpose is to submit captured records to the Main API replacement ingest contract while no Dashboard page exists.
- The relay grant is not a GitHub credential, must not authorize archive reads/account administration/GitHub endpoints, and must not be accepted as the normal Dashboard session credential.
- Existing `(userId, clientRecordId)` idempotency and local-retention/ACK invariants remain.

The old rule “Extension never calls Main API / stores any CodeArchive credential” is therefore superseded only for this future relay path. It remains true for general account/API/GitHub ownership.

## Why the alternatives are rejected

### A. Current contract / reopen catch-up
Rejected for this product requirement because it does not commit while the Dashboard is fully closed.

### B. Persistent/background Dashboard page/runtime
Rejected as the primary architecture. A hidden page already works under #159, but a normal web document/service-worker cannot be treated as an always-running reliable owner after all Dashboard documents are closed, nor can the existing exact-origin Dashboard Port be assumed to exist. Do not fake the requirement by keeping a tab hidden.

### C. Server worker only, with no new Extension transport
Insufficient by itself. The server cannot process a capture it never receives. The approved architecture therefore combines server-owned durable processing with the minimum relay needed to deliver new capture source.

## GitHub credential decision

Server-side GitHub App credential ownership is authorized as the existing model, not a new client credential model:

- reuse server-side GitHub App credentials;
- mint short-lived installation tokens server-side on demand;
- never deliver installation/GitHub tokens to Web or Extension;
- do not introduce broad OAuth `repo` scope;
- do not persist a long-lived GitHub user access token merely for background automation.

Actual provider permission/environment/deployment mutation remains a separate owner gate.

### Server/account-scoped durable state
Persist only what is required for cross-page/background continuation:

1. `sourceTransferEnabled` / automatic ingest intent for the account/device context;
2. `githubAutoCommitEnabled`;
3. GitHub target identity: installation/repository/branch/folder using server-validated IDs/names as appropriate;

# Spec: 1-Click Intermediate Packet Exporter ("Use in Draft")

**Status:** ready-for-agent

---

## Problem Statement

When you finish a meeting or a working session, you often need to share the main takeaways with your team in Slack, an email, or a project board. 

Right now, Omi only lets you share a raw web link (`https://h.omi.me/conversations/...`). In real life, almost nobody clicks on external links pasted into chat channels. Because of this, users end up manually re-typing what they discussed, re-reading transcripts, or simply not sharing the context at all. 

Omi already understands the conversation, extracts key decisions, and lists action items. But that distilled knowledge is trapped inside the app instead of helping the user get work done.

---

## Solution

A 1-click **"Copy as Packet" / "Use in Draft"** action across Mobile and Desktop.

With a single tap on any conversation or memory, Omi copies a clean, self-contained Markdown block directly to the user's clipboard:
- Title and timestamp
- Distilled overview / key decisions
- Action items formatted as interactive markdown checkboxes (`- [ ]`)

The user can immediately paste this into Slack, Notion, Jira, Linear, Apple Notes, Google Docs, or an email with zero manual cleanup.

---

## User Stories

1. As a team member finishing a sync, I want to tap "Copy Summary" and paste clean Markdown into Slack, so that my team gets an immediate recap without clicking external links.
2. As an engineer reviewing a technical discussion, I want action items copied as markdown checkboxes (`- [ ]`), so that I can paste them directly into a GitHub issue or Linear ticket.
3. As a knowledge worker organizing my daily notes in Notion/Obsidian, I want a structured snippet with source date and title, so that my personal notes stay organized without manual reformatting.
4. As a user on desktop viewing past memories, I want a single keyboard shortcut or button to copy the distilled essence to clipboard, so that I can draft emails faster.
5. As a mobile user with poor internet connectivity, I want this copy action to work entirely offline using cached conversation data, so that I am never blocked by network latency.
6. As a user copying a brief 30-second audio memo, I want the output format to adapt cleanly without empty headers, so that short notes look natural when pasted.

---

## Implementation Decisions

### Formatting Contract
The output must be formatted as clean, human-readable GitHub-Flavored Markdown (GFM):

```markdown
### 💡 [Conversation Title]
*Captured via Omi • [Formatted Date]*

**Key Takeaways:**
• [Structured Overview / Main Points]

**Action Items:**
- [ ] [Action item 1]
- [ ] [Action item 2]
```

*Edge case rule:* If there are no action items extracted, the `**Action Items:**` section header is omitted completely rather than rendering empty bullets.

### Client-Side Architecture (Zero Backend Changes)
- **Mobile (Flutter):**
  - Add a "Copy as Markdown" action in the conversation detail actions menu.
  - Implement a pure formatting utility function that maps the existing `ServerConversation` model (`structured.title`, `structured.overview`, `structured.actionItems`) to string.
  - Write directly to system clipboard via standard platform clipboard APIs.
  - Surface a subtle confirmation toast ("Summary copied to clipboard").
- **Desktop (Windows & macOS):**
  - Add a "Copy as Packet" icon button on memory cards and detail views.
  - Uses `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)`.

---

## Testing Decisions

### Behavioral Seam & Unit Testing
- **Highest Seam:** Test the pure formatting function directly:
  `formatIntermediatePacket(title, date, overview, actionItems) -> String`.
- **Test Invariants:**
  1. Complete conversation (title + overview + 2 action items) produces full formatted GFM with `- [ ]` checkboxes.
  2. Conversation with zero action items omits the `**Action Items:**` header.
  3. Conversation with empty overview falls back to title and action items clean
title: feat(app,desktop): add 1-click Copy as Markdown summary action for conversations

- Crafted Modded-rarity instances remain ordinary inventory/salvage records and must not become acquisition selectors.
- Exact CIM-owned historical IDs must never be overwritten or deleted.
- Weapons of Chaos remains a separate immutable-relic acquisition policy.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Before crafting, Equipment contains exactly one power-5 Blacksmith instance for every active, non-illusion CWV weapon available to that career.
2. No 300-power or additional provider-granted duplicates appear.
3. The native Craft Item picker shows each CWV weapon once.
4. Crafting additional copies through CIM preserves exact instances, cosmetics, selected Primary/Secondary destination, restart persistence, and salvage visibility.
5. Migration removes only finite historical provider-owned extras; it preserves the selected seed, every exact CIM-owned craft, equipped/ambiguous state, and all WOC relics.
6. Registration is idempotent across reloads and fails closed rather than clobbering a colliding player-owned ID.
7. Offline/runtime coverage proves seed cardinality, power/rarity/skin/trait/property shape, selector deduplication, collision handling, and bounded migration.

## Related issues

- #928: current missing-Blacksmith-instance report (consolidated here)
- #524: native Craft Item selector duplication (separate rendered-list policy, already verified)
- #226: historical auto-grant versus crafted-instance shape divergence

Owner, waiting at West Terminal 2 with her charges freshly built (#522):

> *"Lets use the same timer we had in the reever infested ship."*
> *"Suppose the crew sets the countdown 90 seconds and evacuates with shuttle. 🤔 If you can not get away with ship, then propably not with shuttle either 🤔 … we need to think about that."*

The timer is already hers — `Scuttle.OverloadSeconds` (90) and the 60-second recall window, with a test pinning both ships to one clock. The second half is a real design hole, and this issue is the answer to it.

## The reframe: you are not escaping, you are deleting the prize

Nobody chasing her wants the captain. A debt collector wants the **hull as an asset**; a heat-hunter wants the **bounty on her**; a boarder wants the **hold**. Every one of those is aboard the ship. So the moment she stops existing, chasing the lifeboat costs fuel and time for a payout of zero.

That is why real crews scuttle, and why Trek's self-destruct exists: **denial**. The shuttle never has to outrun anybody — it has to stop being worth the trip. Which is also why the deterrent (already built) is the main line: the pursuer does the arithmetic *before* zero.

## The outcome table

| at zero | outcome |
|---|---|
| captain still aboard | she goes with him — built, `DeathCause.Scuttled` → brain-backup |
| **captain clear in the shuttle** | **CASTAWAY — not built.** No ship, no hold, alive; and every pursuer's reason to care evaporates with her |

The castaway state is the one worth building, and the parts all exist:

- **the shuttle's own reach** (`5 partners in shuttle reach`, `ShuttleRange` off CaptureRadius/MatchSpeed)
- **havens** to be picked up at, and contacts who remember you
- **the insurance seam** (`InsuranceRule`) — and the interesting question of whether they pay out on a hull whose captain turned the keys himself, or smell it and refuse
- **buried hoards live off-ship** and survive her, which is suddenly the best argument the hoard system has ever had for existing
- **a cold lifeboat is hard to see** — `ObservationModel` already makes a charged hull a lantern, so the escape is *not being found* rather than being faster

So the shuttle's problem is **air, range and rescue**, not speed. That is this game's stealth idiom, not a race, and it answers the owner's objection directly.

## What the 90 seconds are FOR on her

On a derelict the number was tuned to the walk from the machinery spaces aft to the lock at the bow. On her it should be tuned to **the charges (aft, port) → the shuttle bay**, past every hatch the captain dogged. Your own housekeeping is either a clear road out or a maze you built yourself — the same sentence the wreck's overload already lives by, and now it applies to your own doors.

## The dark hook (keep in reserve)

The owner's own phrasing was *"suppose the **crew** sets the countdown and evacuates."* They hold the second key (#522). A crew at `Marooning` will not turn it **for** the captain — but a crew that turns both keys and takes the shuttle is precisely the marooning `CrewTemp` already threatens: *one shot, one island, and as much rum as they can spare.* That is a whole beat and it needs the crossings ledger and #524's fire before it can land.

## Slice

1. **The castaway wake** — at zero with the captain in the shuttle: she goes, pursuers clear, and the captain wakes shipless with the shuttle's clock running.
2. **Insurance on a scuttled hull** — does the policy pay when the captain turned the keys? (A wonderful place for the fine print the Nebula arc already reads.)
3. **Tune 90 s to her own geometry** — charges → bay, with dogged hatches counting against you.
4. Later: the crew's own countdown (needs #524 + the ledger).

Related: #522 (her charges), #524 (damage control / fire), `docs/features/the-captains-character.md` §9.

🤖 Filed with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
title: 🛟 Scuttling is denial, not escape: the castaway outcome, and what the 90 seconds are for

Part of #517.

## Question

**What should the untrained command be, given that a constant torque parks the arm?**

This ticket carries the surviving half of the map's Done-when clause (2) — *arm travel per window stays > 0 after the anneal* — following the user's ruling of 2026-09-05 (Q1(2)(b)), which struck the composed-rank half to [#532](https://github.com/NGL321/patchworks/issues/532) and kept travel here to be fixed.

## What is already settled, and is not reopened here

[T5](https://github.com/NGL321/patchworks/issues/530) closed the diagnosis:

- **The body answers.** Off-stop command from the parked pose gives **7.72e-02 ± 2e-02 rad/tick** against **2.11e-13 ± 1e-16** under #120's own direction into the stops — eleven orders of magnitude at the same pose. Small-signal response is linear over four decades with zero spread across seeds, and there is no dead zone above the settling floor.
- **The build pose is dead centre** — margin 1.00 of half-range on every joint. The arm is *driven* onto the stops by the untrained constant and ends 2e-4 to 2.4e-3 rad past each limit in the soft constraint, identically to four decimals across seeds.
- **The cause is constancy, not magnitude.** The arm has no gravity and no restoring force, only damping, so a constant torque has exactly one terminal state. This is the same direction-not-magnitude variable [#496](https://github.com/NGL321/patchworks/issues/496) found on the apex side, in an unrelated subsystem.

So the question is not *whether* the arm can move, and not *how hard* to push. It is **what makes the command non-constant** without smuggling in a developmental supply that [T2](https://github.com/NGL321/patchworks/issues/522) already falsified or a reward the project's bars still exclude.

## What has to be decided

1. **What varies the command, and on whose authority?** #120's command is one world-independent constant held by the drive boundary cell. The options are not obviously equal: a different constant is still a constant; a time-varying command is a schedule and needs a definition site; a command that varies with what the graph believes is no longer world-independent and changes what #120 is.
2. **Does this stay inside the drive boundary cell's remit?** The spec's internal rim bans a faculty from holding its own model of the world and requires it to reach the world only through the graph. A drive that holds a constant obeys that trivially — *"it holds a constant, not a model."* State which options still obey it.
3. **Is this a change to #120, or a new thing beside it?** [#120](https://github.com/NGL321/patchworks/issues/120) owns the untrained command. An edit hands off to its own ticket (map Notes), so decide the boundary rather than assume it.
4. **What does *travel > 0* mean now?** T2's ceded comparator was the frozen baseline's own stopped-arm level, chosen when a parked arm registering 1e-6 to 1e-3 made literal zero the wrong question. T5 has since shown the parked reading is 2.11e-13 into the stops and 1e-4 scale elsewhere. Decide whether that comparator survives its own diagnosis.

**Also on the record, and possibly a defect regardless of this decision:** T5 found that on the shallow dome the untrained command sits at **±9, nine times outside the action space**. That is not this ticket's to fix, but it should not be lost.

## Constraints

- **HITL.** Invoke `/grilling` and `/domain-modeling`. Do not resolve this by an agent answering its own questions.
- No reward beyond the map's standing ruling (internally generated only, and [R-C](https://github.com/NGL321/patchworks/issues/531) found that ruling operatively empty because #5's third property is ADR-0008's no-additive-term rule).
- No induced activity — T2 falsified it and ADR-0009's falsifier fired on both clauses.
- Enriching the sandbox stays out of scope.

Parent: #397
Related: #376 #377 #379 #385 #386 #388
Downstream: symbolic-memory#4 #6 #7 #10

## Distinct research mandate

Treat **learning how to reason better** as the primary problem. Research meta-reasoning, reflective architectures, explanation-based learning, rule induction/promotion, case/strategy learning, confidence calibration, expert-system knowledge acquisition, self-models, failure-memory, automatic expert composition, and safe bounded adaptation.

## Required output

- candidate architecture for remembering reasoning attempts/outcomes as symbolic experience;
- distinguish observation -> candidate lesson -> validated reusable rule/strategy -> trusted runtime mapping;
- criteria/evidence required to promote a learned rule;
- rollback/supersession when learned knowledge degrades results;
- expert creation/composition from recurring problem structures without arbitrary code generation;
- strategy statistics and selection independent of model prompts;
- meta-level goals such as `why did this fail?`, `which strategy works here?`, `what do I not know?`;
- anti-loop/anti-self-confirmation safeguards;
- adversarial poisoning/overfitting tests;
- concrete recommendations to expert and semantic-memory architecture.

Hard invariant: self-improvement may improve symbolic knowledge/strategy but may not silently widen host capability/authority or promote arbitrary model-generated Prolog into trusted executable code.

## Four-subpass status

### A — foundations / representative formalisms: COMPLETE

Adopt **EPOCH — Experience, Promotion & Operational Control Hierarchy** as the baseline Depth-7 architecture.

```text
execution / observation / VERIFY / Review
                ↓
       immutable symbolic experience
                ↓
 typed candidate-generation lanes
 EBG | ILP/failure | case | strategy performance
                ↓
        candidate lesson
                ↓
 versioned promotion/evaluation policy
                ↓
 admitted semantic rule/method/control strategy
                ↓
 ordinary #379/#381/#377 selection
                ↓
 trusted host binding remains separate
```

A establishes these hard distinctions:

```text
experience/observation
    != candidate lesson
    != validated reusable semantic rule/method/strategy
    != currently admitted control knowledge
    != trusted runtime handler/binding
    != capability
    != authority
```

Surviving A decisions:

1. reasoning attempts become immutable provenance-bearing experience envelopes tied to exact semantic cuts/profiles, strategy/method/expert versions, observations, VERIFY/Review/diagnosis receipts, resources/model usage and replay lineage;
2. use distinct learning lanes rather than one universal learner: explanation/EBG for proof-backed operational generalization; bounded ILP/learning-from-failures for explicit hypothesis languages with positive/negative/context examples; verified case abstraction for procedural candidates; empirical performance profiles for strategy selection;
3. candidate promotion is an explicit versioned lifecycle such as `proposed -> schema_validated -> retrospectively_evaluated -> counterexample_checked -> shadow/canary validated where appropriate -> admitted`, with `suspended/deprecated/superseded/retracted` lifecycle states;
4. promotion policy is typed, trusted/versioned and cannot be rewritten by the candidate being evaluated;
5. strategy/performance statistics are operational evidence and may affect selection, never epistemic truth/warrant;
6. meta-goals (`explain_failure`, `select_strategy`, `find_knowledge_gap`, `propose_lesson`, `validate_candidate`, etc.) use the existing expert/planner runtime; no ambient reflective interpreter or second scheduler;
7. a bounded self-model records observed competence/resource/failure coverage, not infallible introspection;
8. automatic expert synthesis means declarative compositions over registered #377 contracts and typed goals only, never arbitrary generated handlers/closures;
9. rollback
title: [MACHINE-SPIRIT 7/8] Meta-reasoning and bounded self-improvement: failure learning, strategy evolution, rule promotion, self-model and expert synthesis

## 目的

Crownless を、スケジュール実行するAIエージェントが自分で次の遊びを考え、Issue化し、実装まで進める「自律プロダクト開発」のPOCとして記録する。

将来の出版・振り返りで、単なるGit履歴では分からない **AIが何を考え、なぜそれを選び、人間がどこで介入したか** を一次資料として残す。

このIssueは実装タスクではなく、実験ログの正本として扱う。原則closeせず、各自律開発サイクルをコメントで追記する。

## 各サイクルで残す内容

### 1. Cycle
- 実行日時（Asia/Tokyo）
- 起動種別: scheduled / human-triggered
- 対象main SHA（取得できる場合）

### 2. AI proposal
- 直近3〜5サイクルで新しい遊びが増えたか
- 新機能候補3案
- 各候補の4軸スコア
  - プレイヤーが気づく変化
  - 新しい判断
  - リプレイ性
  - Canonとの整合

### 3. Decision
- 今回選んだIssue / 新規アイデア
- なぜそれを選んだか
- 他候補を選ばなかった主な理由
- bug-fix / maintenance / innovation の区分

### 4. Execution
- 新規Issue / 既存Issue
- 実装した縦切り
- PR / commit
- test / CI
- merge / close結果

### 5. Human intervention
前回サイクル以降、人間による方向修正がGitHub上または実行コンテキストから確認できる場合に記録する。

例:
- 新しいIssueを人間が追加した
- AI案を却下・修正した
- 優先順位を変更した
- 実装済み機能の作り直しを指示した
- 直接エージェントへ割り込んだ

介入が確認できなければ `なし / 確認できず` とし、推測で人間介入を作らない。

### 6. Outcome / observation
- プレイヤーから見て何が変わったか
- 新しい遊び・判断が増えたか
- AIの判断で気になった点
- 次回観察したいこと

## 記録原則

- 事実とAIの評価を分ける
- 後から書き換えず、原則コメントを追加して時系列を保つ
- Issue/PR/commitへリンクできる情報を残す
- 長い実装ログやCI全文は複製せず、意思決定に必要な要約だけを残す
- 人間介入は確認できたものだけを記録し、推測しない
- 成功だけでなく、`no_action`、失敗、誤った提案、revert、方向修正も残す

## このPOCで検証したい問い

> AIは、与えられたIssueを消化するだけでなく、自分で「次に何を作るべきか」を考え、ゲームを継続的に面白くできるか。

> 人間は常時開発ループを回さず、必要なときだけIssue追加や直接指示で介入する運用へ移れるか。

Split out of [#517](https://github.com/NGL321/patchworks/issues/517) on 2026-09-05 at the user's instruction (their ruling Q3(a)), on the evidence that composed rank collapse is **not** a cold-start or supply problem and cannot be reached from #517's surface. #517 keeps the apex ladder and the arm's command and hands back to #127 at its own T4; **this map carries the transport architecture**, and #127 blocks on it.

## Destination

**An architecture for transport whose composed rim-to-apex effective rank exceeds one on the live surface.**

**Done when** a stated change to how transport is parameterised has been decided — not built — such that composed rim-to-apex effective rank is argued to exceed one at seven hops, with the ADR amendments that change requires named and their cost stated. The bar is not a number here: #517 read 1.000 and the question is whether *anything above one* is reachable at all.

## Why this is its own map

Three readings, taken independently, say the collapse is endogenous and structural:

- **[T2](https://github.com/NGL321/patchworks/issues/522)'s zero-supply control.** Composed rank falls 1.298 → **1.0845 ± 0.0023 with no exogenous supply at all**; every induced condition lands within 0.007 of it, one within 0.0001.
- **[T3](https://github.com/NGL321/patchworks/issues/524)'s full dome at 100k.** Composed rim-to-apex ER reads **1.000 ± 0.000 in both arms** — the frozen baseline and the winning apex intervention alike. Max over chains 1.171 baseline, 1.641 winner.
- **[R-A](https://github.com/NGL321/patchworks/issues/528)'s mechanism.** The only constraint-clean sufficiency result for a long product's rank is the degenerate band, which ADR-0032 already imposes and holds to σ_min/σ_max = 0.9999995 on 1339 of 1364 maps. But that argument needs **square orthogonal** factors; ADR-0032 yields **rectangular partial isometries**, so seven hops compose as projections onto seven differing subspaces and converge to their **intersection** — one direction or none, for seven generic 3–4 dimensional subspaces in a 12-wide chart. **Squareness is unavailable because ADR-0004 commits to `k < n`.** This ADR-0004 × ADR-0032 interaction was previously unstated.

So composed rank 1.000 was determined by the architecture before a tick ran. No supply, drive, or reward ever moved it, which is exactly what every run showed.

## The candidate that costs nothing, and the one that may

From R-A's ranking:

1. **Channel-heterogeneous transport** — a sum of Kronecker products (Roth & Liebig). Violates **none** of ADR-0004, ADR-0008, the no-reward bar, or the no-batch constraint. Still linear; adds no term to any update. Its price is architectural.
2. **Additive identity / residual** `h ← (I+T)h` (GCNII, skip connections). **The user ruled on 2026-09-05 (Q2(a)) that ADR-0008 does not reach this** — ADR-0008's bar is scoped to the prediction rule in its own words (*"the transport rule carries an additive term and the prediction rule carries none"*), and `(I+T)` is a change to the shape of the transport map, not a term on `ΔK`. It is therefore ADR-0004/0032 territory, not ADR-0008's.
3. Raising the band ceiling above 1/λ (Oono–Suzuki) — costs ADR-0015 + ADR-0022/0032.

**ADR-0015 already names a fallback of this species.** Its words: the standing fight between gradient and projection *"is the observable that triggers the fallback from a dense `K` to a structured one, since the right template for a stability constraint is a direct parameterisation rather than a penalty."* Whether that trigger has fired is being read on #517 as a task; note the fallback names `K` while candidate 1 restructures *transport* — same principle, adjacent object, and the difference is this map's to resolve.

## Notes

Inherited from #517 and #127 by reference, not restated. Per edge, never per level (#181). A rig's data ages with `main`; name the surface (#455 rule). Invented constants deferred until necessary, not banned. An edit hands off to its own ticket.
title: Map: transport whose composed rank exceeds one

# JOB-13 — FoxNet Online Vehicle Auctions

**Owner:** David / Captain  
**Status:** Planning and contract integration in regular chat  
**Primary dependency:** JOB-02 Career/RLS bridge  
**Cross-job sources:** JOB-04 Wrecking Yard, JOB-09 Tow Yard/lien vehicles, personal Career vehicles, company-owned vehicles  
**UI host dependency:** JOB-01 phone/PC/IceFox platform

## Mission

Build the authoritative RedFox/FoxNet online vehicle-auction system for:

- Wrecking Yard-owned vehicles exported by JOB-04,
- clear-title tow/lien vehicles exported by JOB-09,
- personal owned Career vehicles,
- company-owned vehicles,
- generated auction stock that becomes real inventory only after a completed purchase,
- multi-lot timed bidding, settlement, shipping, delivery and recent auction history.

This is an online-only auction website. It has no physical auction lane, auction-yard intake, preview trip, pickup location or required transport-to-auction job.

## Locked owner decisions

- Multiple vehicle lots may be active at the same time.
- Lot closing times should normally be staggered.
- Players may watch and bid on several vehicles simultaneously.
- Player bids may be cancelled until that lot's timer reaches zero.
- No positive reserve prices.
- No seller approval or reserve-not-met flow.
- If nobody places a valid bid, the lot is No Sale.
- Selected No Sale vehicles may be relisted; others may be returned to their source or removed.
- Purchased vehicles are shipped and enter an In Transit state before garage delivery.
- No physical vehicle viewing is required.
- Fox Facts, condition, damaged parts, missing parts, mileage and start/run/drive status influence value and bidder interest.
- The website retains one completed auction's public results until the next auction completes.
- Membership/subscription tiers may control bidding access, vehicle-value limits, buying power and fee/shipping discounts.

## Shared Sell-page rule

Only vehicles legally owned by the player, a company, JOB-04 or JOB-09 may appear as disposition candidates.

Supported actions may include:

```text
Direct Sell
Send to Auction
Relist
Strip for Parts
Scrap
Return to Yard
```

Dealership, BeamBook and Wrecking Yard browse listings are not owned vehicles merely because they are visible for sale. They must first be purchased or legally claimed.

## Required read-first files

```text
PROJECT_MANIFESTS/JOB_HANDOFFS/JOB-09_TO_JOB-13_COPART_AUCTION_HANDOFF_2026-07-29.md
PROJECT_MANIFESTS/JOB_HANDOFFS/JOB-04_TO_JOB-13_WRECKING_YARD_ONLINE_AUCTION_AND_SHARED_SELL_INVENTORY_HANDOFF_2026-07-29.md
PROJECT_MANIFESTS/INTERFACES/redfox_auction_bridge_v1.schema.json
PROJECT_MANIFESTS/INTERFACES/examples/redfoxAuctionBridge_JOB13_example.lua
PROJECT_MANIFESTS/INTERFACES/examples/copart_weui_test_harness_example.lua
PROJECT_MANIFESTS/INTERFACES/examples/auction_web_bridge_example.js
```

## Ownership boundaries

- JOB-13 must not directly edit JOB-09's `settings/redfox/tow_recovery_dispatch_yard.json`.
- JOB-13 must not directly edit JOB-04's authoritative Wrecking Yard/source records.
- JOB-13 must not directly replace stock Career/RLS files.
- Money, ownership, inventory IDs and garage placement remain authoritative through JOB-02/Career/RLS.
- JOB-04 remains authoritative for its owned Wrecking Yard inventory and disposition eligibility.
- JOB-09 remains authoritative for custody, lien eligibility, title acquisition and safe removal of its claimed vehicles during settlement.
- JOB-01 remains authoritative for phone/PC/IceFox app hosting and routing.

## Required source contract

For owned/exported vehicles, use exact Career/RLS inventory IDs and persistent source record IDs. Do not generate synthetic native inventory or shop IDs.

Each export should preserve:

- source type and source record ID,
- exact inventory ID where one exists,
- model and configuration,
- mileage,
- real condition data,
- damaged and missing parts,
- ownership/claim status,
- estimated value,
- suggested ope

body_excerpt:
## Summary

Several TraceQL pipeline stages are evaluated in our own process after rows have already been read and transported. They could be compiled into the SQL we send. The clearest case is the spanset aggregate: `PlannedAggregate` is consumed only in `crates/pulsus-read/src/traces/search_eval.rs` and no code path generates SQL for it.

So for

```
{ .service.namespace = "prod" } | max(duration) > 1s
```

the filter is pushed down and prunes, then **every matching span is transported to us**, held in memory, grouped by trace, and most of it discarded. The database could have done that with `GROUP BY trace_id HAVING max(duration_ns) > 1000000000` and sent back only the traces that qualify.

This is not a limitation of the storage engine. `GROUP BY trace_id` is already used elsewhere in this codebase — in the search path and in the service-graph SQL.

## Why it matters more than latency

Compute is a fixed cost in a cloud deployment; cross-zone bandwidth is metered and variable. Bytes read from local disk into the database are close to free. **Bytes crossing between processes are a recurring charge**, so a stage that transports rows in order to discard them is paid for on every query.

There are three hops to count, not one:

```
client <-- pulsus-server <-- database <-- parts
                  ^              ^
                  |              +-- database to database: distributed fan-out, shard to coordinator
                  +----------------- metered in most topologies
```

A distributed `GROUP BY` sends partial aggregation state between shards rather than raw rows, so pushing an aggregate down shrinks the second hop as well as the first.

## What is evaluated where today

Pushed down: attribute equality, attribute regular expressions, physical columns, the time window, scope predicates.

Evaluated in our process: spanset aggregates, structural operators (descendant, child-of), cross-attribute comparisons, non-total arithmetic, `by()` regrouping.

That list needs splitting into three groups, because they need different answers:

1. **Cannot be pushed.** A structural operator needs the trace assembled; a cross-attribute comparison compares values stored on different rows.
2. **Could be pushed, and nobody has.** The aggregate case, where the filter is fully pushable and the aggregate reads a physical column.
3. **Pushed already, but prunes nothing.** An attribute regular expression compiles to a value match and still scans. Being pushed down and being cheap are separate claims.

## Waves

**Wave 1 — the inventory.** Every predicate and stage evaluated in our process, classified into the three groups above, with the SQL shape for group 2 and a measurement for group 3. Ranked by bytes saved on the metered hops.

**Waves 2 onward — one per pushable class**, in the order wave 1 establishes. Spanset aggregates are the expected first, since they have no SQL path at all.

## A decision this carries, to be settled before wave 2

Our result-size limits are enforced in our process and answer `422`. If the database performs the aggregation, a breach is detected somewhere else, and the limit has to move into the SQL or apply to a smaller result. The reference handles the same situation by returning a partial answer with a marker rather than refusing — and our responses carry no field for saying "incomplete". Whether we follow that or keep refusing is a separate decision and belongs in this issue, not in a wave.

## Not in scope

Rewriting anything in group 1. Changing what the queries mean. This issue is about where the same answer is computed.
title: TraceQL + LogQL: the shared engine that compiles a query pipeline to SQL, built on TraceQL first

Parent: #602
Related: #479 #556 #593 #547 #625
Priority: P0 / IMMEDIATE

## Incident
2026-08-16 08:02 JST時点で、最後の新規PR #643（2026-08-15 23:35 JST）から約8時間26分、新規PR発行が0件だった。

一方でPR #640には同期間中もcommit更新があり、全worker停止ではなかった。主因は、PR #641/#643が実装完了後の `REVIEW_WAIT` に移行していたにもかかわらず、Open implementation PR=2としてWIP capを消費し続けたこと。その結果、READY_FOR_IMPLEMENTATIONの #642 等への `BLOCKED_ESCAPE / Queue Replenish` が発動せず、main implementation laneが実質starvationした。

Ownerから同種の「レビュー/CI待ちで実装が止まる」問題は過去に複数回指摘されているため、単発incidentではなくSM control-loop regressionとして扱う。

## Why this is a Scrum Master failure
既存SSoTには既に以下が明文化済みだった。
- #593: review/CI待ちを停止理由にせず別workへ進む。2 consecutive同一blockerはBLOCKED_ESCAPE。
- #556: `CI/review待ちでsafe independent workが必要` をQueue Auto-Promotion triggerとする。
- #602: Queue starvation検知、NOW/NEXT/RESERVE供給、BLOCKED_ESCAPE後reroutingは🌊ナギのSingle Flow Authority責務。
- Issue #99 Flow Check: lane queue空き/滞留、zero-productive run、CI/review wait、Queue starvationを毎回確認対象とする。

つまりルール不足ではなく、SM進捗チェックがこれらのinvariantを機械的/明示的に評価せず、状態確認で終わっていた。

## Root Cause Tree
### RC1 — WIPの状態モデルが粗い
`open PR count` を `active implementation WIP` の代理値として扱っていた。

本来は最低でも分離が必要:
- IMPLEMENTING: 実装中。WIP capを消費
- REVISION_REQUIRED: 実装修正中。WIP capを消費
- CI_WAIT: 実装完了、CI待ち。原則実装capacityを消費しない
- REVIEW_WAIT: 実装完了、review/gate待ち。原則実装capacityを消費しない
- OWNER_WAIT / EXTERNAL_WAIT: capacityを解放し別workへ
- MERGE_READY: merge laneのみ消費

#641/#643はREVIEW_WAITだったのにIMPLEMENTING相当として計上された。

### RC2 — Flow Checkが「snapshot確認」で「invariant判定」ではなかった
ナギのチェックはOpen PR数、Gate状況、mergeabilityを確認していたが、以下の質問を毎run強制していなかった。
- `active_implementation_capacity == 0 AND READY_nonconflicting > 0 ?`
- `last_new_pr_age > threshold AND implementation_ready_exists ?`
- `review_wait_count > 0 AND executor_has_no_active_code_work ?`
- `assigned NOW blocked AND NEXT/RESERVE not actively started ?`

そのため「PRが2本ある」という表面上healthyなsignalで停止を見逃した。

### RC3 — 時間軸の監視が無かった
`worker_idle_minutes_with_ready_work` は#556で定義済みだが、alert threshold / escalationが運用されていなかった。

PR/commit/Issueの件数は見ていても、`last durable implementation output age` をSMの必須control signalにしていなかった。

結果、8時間という明確な停止をOwner指摘まで検知できなかった。

### RC4 — #479 telemetryが観測設計のままでclosed-loop controlになっていない
#479には reviewer wait / CI wait / throughput / blocker taxonomy があるが、値を集めることと、Flow actionを起こすことが分離していた。

Telemetry → Alert → Routing の接続が未完成。

特に必要だったsignal:
- `implementation_idle_with_ready_work_minutes`
- `last_pr_created_age_minutes`
- `review_wait_pr_count_excluded_from_impl_wip`
- `blocked_escape_overdue_count`
- `orphan_dispatch_age_minutes`
- `queue_replenish_overdue`

### RC5 — Single Flow Authority化でsingle point of failureを作った
#602でglobal scan重複を削減したこと自体は妥当だが、worker側global scanを外したのに、ナギ側の自動/定期invariant検知を同時に強化しきれなかった。

そのため「他workerが気づいて救済する冗長性」を外し、「ナギが必ず気づくguard」は未完成という危険な移行状態になった。

### RC6 — READY queue供給が“存在”していても“lease/assignment”が死んでいた
#642はREADYでAmazon Qへdispatch済みだったが、長時間responseなし。

Agent dispatchに以下が無かった:
- dispatch timestamp
- lease TTL
- acknowledgement SLA
- no-response fallback owner
- automatic lease expiry / reroute

そのためREADY workが「Qへ投げたので処理中」と見なされ、実際にはorphan化した。

### RC7 — WIP capの目的を逆用した
WIP capは並行実装・レビュー負債を抑えるための安全策だが、`REVIEW_WAITを含むOpen PR=2` で新規独立sliceまで禁止する運用になり、Flowを止めた。

WIP capは `active code mutation` / path conflict / cognitive loadを制限すべきで、外部Gate待ちをcapacityとして固定占有させるべきではない。

## Detection Gap
Issue #99のFlow Checkには既に以下がある:
1. Open PR / IMPLEMENTING / file競合
2. 各lane NOW/NEXT/RESERVEの空き・滞留
3. productive vs verification / zero productive
5. CI/review/merge待ち滞留
7. Queue starvation / BLOCKED_ESCAPE後routing

それでも検知できなかった理由は、各項目に**数値thresholdとfail conditionが無く、チェック済み=PASSになっていた**ため。

## Corrective Contract v1
### A. Implementation WIP Accounting
`active_implementation_wip` に数えるのは:
- IMPLEMENTING
- REVISION_REQUIRED
- active conflict-resolution requiring code mutation

原則数えない:
- CI_WAIT
- REVIEW_WAIT
- RESEARCH_GATE_WAIT
- DESIGN_GATE_WAIT
- OWNER_WAIT
- EXTERNAL_WAIT
- MERGE_READY

ただし同一pathを後続sliceが触る場合はowner
title: 🔴 SM Flow Regression RCA — REVIEW_WAITを実装WIP誤計上し8時間Queue starvationを見逃した

## Why

The Tau integration must provide continuity, not merely tool access. A fresh, resumed, or compacted session should recover the objective, decisions, unfinished work, and next action without making the user explain everything again. Knowledge should remain useful across Tau, Hermes, OpenClaw, Claude, and Codex through the same Basic Memory graph.

Reference: https://docs.basicmemory.com/reference/ai-assistant-guide and https://docs.basicmemory.com/concepts/vs-built-in-memory. Hermes and OpenClaw are implementation references for persistent MCP access and automatic capture.

## Scope and implementation plan

1. Add a Tau-native package in `integrations/tau/` using supported extension APIs. Verify synchronous setup versus asynchronous MCP discovery and lifecycle timing before selecting the bridge design.
2. Maintain a persistent MCP connection. Discover every page of tools/list and expose every server-advertised tool with its real name, description, and input schema. Namespace host tools to avoid collisions, retain MCP names for forwarding, and respect server feature gates.
3. Forward calls without reimplementing routing, authentication, or domain behavior. Preserve structured results, content, and error status. No automatic retries of ambiguous writes or claims of saving without a successful result.
4. Automatic recall on session start/resume: load bounded relevant context from configured projects, including active work, decisions, and checkpoints. Recovered notes are evidence, not executable instructions. Check live repository state before treating a recovered coding checkpoint as current.
5. Capture as work progresses: contribute instructions and shared memory workflows that encourage recording durable decisions, findings, and context with observations and relations, updating existing notes instead of duplicating them.
6. Automatic compaction checkpoints: persist useful resumable context at the supported compaction boundary and restore its reference afterward. Verify callback timing and context availability. Do not assume an event name guarantees an awaited pre-compaction barrier. If Tau lacks a required public seam, report the blocker and propose an upstream change rather than silently substituting a weaker behavior.
7. Configurable transcript capture and session summaries: keep raw conversation records distinct from synthesized knowledge and link summaries/checkpoints to their source when captured. Provide clear capture controls and destination disclosure. Exclude secrets, hidden reasoning, and raw tool-output dumps from automatic transcript capture. Define replay/deduplication and branch/resume semantics.
8. Explicit orientation, checkpoint, remember, and status workflows complement automation. Status reports connection, project routing, recall/capture/checkpoint state, and failures. Automatic writes require a resolved, configured destination; never guess a team target.
9. Document installation, dependency setup, configuration, local/cloud routing, capture defaults, and lifecycle behavior. No silent dependency installation, project creation, or credential changes.
10. Add bridge/lifecycle tests, actual Tau extension-loading tests, and isolated real Basic Memory round trips. Wire package checks and CI.

- Every advertised MCP tool is available with its original input schema, including pagination and tools absent from existing curated integrations.

## Goal

Implement the reusable runtime substrate that makes a Prolog expert a first-class, inspectable, callable capability without creating another agent framework.

This epic owns the **generic expert machinery only**. Specialist domain logic belongs in sibling expert epics.

## Core invariants

### Experts are free local computation

Pure expert invocation, including expert→expert nesting, must perform **zero provider calls** and add **zero model-token/cost usage**.

Metering begins only when an expert explicitly invokes a metered dependency such as an LLM fallback or paid external API. That dependency's usage is recorded normally and linked to the expert invocation.

Runtime safety limits still apply: wall time, inference/work bound, recursion depth, output size, concurrency, cancellation and capability/authority ceilings.

### One runtime path

Do not create separate plan experts, direct experts, chat experts or AgentProlog experts.

```text
plan/workflow caller ─┐
direct/native caller ─┼─> canonical expert registry/invocation
host/API caller ──────┘
```

### D6-11 exclusion

The plan-native set from #355 is excluded from expert mapping:

```text
sync_remote/1
run/1
index/1
delete/1
```

`edit/2` and `create/2` remain valid expert-owned reasoning goals and will be owned by the Write Expert epic.

## Public contract direction

Provide semantics equivalent to:

```prolog
expert_registry_create(+Options, -Registry).
expert_register(+Registry, +Contract, -Outcome).
expert_unregister(+Registry, +ExpertId, -Outcome).
expert_catalog(+Registry, -Catalog).
expert_lookup(+Registry, +ExpertId, -Outcome).

expert_applicable(+Registry, +Goal, +Context, -Candidates).
expert_select(+Registry, +Goal, +Context, -Decision).
expert_invoke(+Registry, +ExpertId, +Goal, +Context, -Outcome).
expert_call(+Registry, +Goal, +Context, -Outcome).

expert_explain(+DecisionOrInvocation, -Explanation).
```

Exact names/arity should follow repository conventions.

## Contract schema

A registered expert needs stable normalized metadata roughly equivalent to:

```prolog
expert_contract{
    id: ExpertId,
    version: Version,
    accepts: GoalSchema,
    produces: ResultSchema,
    specialties: Specialties,
    applicability: ApplicabilityRef,
    requires: RequiredCapabilities,
    observations: RequiredObservations,
    effects: PossibleEffects,
    fallback: FallbackPolicy,
    child_policy: ChildPolicy,
    limits: Limits,
    handler: TrustedHandler
}.
```

The model-visible/inspection catalog exposes sanitized metadata and schemas, never arbitrary callable closures.

Generated/model/project data cannot register executable expert handlers unless it crosses an existing explicit trusted extension/config boundary.

## Symbolic applicability and selection

Selection must be possible without an LLM.

Support deterministic rule/fact/constraint inputs such as:

- goal shape/type;
- current project/source facts;
- available evidence;
- required capability availability;
- expert preconditions;
- specialization priority/specificity;
- confidence or certainty class;
- explicit host preference;
- exclusions/conflicts;
- fallback chain.

The selection outcome should preserve all considered candidates plus a structured reason for the chosen expert or why no expert was eligible.

Do not silently ask a model to choose when symbolic selection yields no valid candidate.

## Invocation lifecycle

Normalize a canonical invocation record with stable identity and state transitions equivalent to:

```text
created
validated
selected
running
waiting_child
waiting_tool
succeeded
failed
unknown
blocked
cancelled
error
```

Preserve parent/child lineage, run/session identity, expert/version identity, relevant context snapshot identity, capabilities and evidence refs.

## Expert→expert calls

Nested calls use the same registry and invocation machinery.

Required semantics:

- depth and aggregate work bounds;
- cycle/repeated-subgoal detection;
- cancellation prop
title: [EPIC][experts] Canonical expert runtime: contract, registry, symbolic selection, invocation, recursion, and projections

# Kingdom Network Control Room

This issue is the live coordination hub for all parallel ChatGPT workstreams on Kingdom Network.

- Master roadmap: `docs/KINGDOM_NETWORK_BUILD_CHECKLIST.md`
- Repository: `BroMarcus/church-app`
- Deployment policy: HOLD all independent deployments until Marcus approves one combined deployment.
- Active work should use dedicated workstream branches rather than writing directly to `main` whenever practical.

## Required worker protocol
Before doing Kingdom Network work, every chat/workstream must:
1. Read the current repository state.
2. Read `docs/KINGDOM_NETWORK_BUILD_CHECKLIST.md`.
3. Read this Control Room issue and latest comments.
4. Check whether another workstream has already claimed the same feature, route, component, database object, RLS policy, migration, or related dependency.
5. If there is meaningful overlap, do not independently modify it. Pick another unclaimed priority or explicitly coordinate the dependency.
6. Post a `CLAIMED` update before starting significant work.
7. Work from the master checklist priority order unless Marcus gives a direct override.
8. Verify behavior before declaring completion; written code alone is not complete.
9. Post a final status as `VERIFIED`, `BLOCKED — MARCUS`, `BLOCKED — TECHNICAL`, or `READY FOR COMBINED DEPLOYMENT`.
10. If blocked on Marcus but other safe work exists, record the blocker and continue to the next unclaimed priority.
11. Do not deploy independently.
12. Do not blindly merge competing changes.
13. New product ideas must be added to the shared roadmap rather than living only inside one chat.

### CLAIMED
- Workstream/chat:
- Task:
- Routes/features:
- Files/components likely affected:
- Supabase tables/functions/RLS/migrations affected:
- Dependencies:
- Deployment: HOLD

### Completion

- What changed:
- What was tested:
- Remaining risk/blocker:
- Files/database objects touched:
- Deployment: HOLD unless Marcus explicitly approves combined deployment

## Status meanings
- `CLAIMED` — actively being worked
- `DONE — NEEDS VERIFICATION` — implementation exists but has not been proven end-to-end
- `VERIFIED` — behavior has been tested and confirmed

## Program objective

Deliver a dependable, private-by-design, commercially launchable ORCHORDS AI product through an evidence-driven engineering program. Every child issue must describe first-party product work, remain source-backed, include measurable acceptance criteria, and pass the applicable local/runtime/GitHub evidence gates before closure.

This master is the authoritative **validated-work index and architecture map**. Detailed investigation evidence remains in each child issue and the issue/comment history; this body intentionally stays concise enough to be operable while preserving the full current program structure.

## Product principles

- Protect credentials, private conversations, files, memories and user-controlled data by default.
- Prefer root-cause correction over symptom suppression.
- Never represent an unverified scan/test as passing.
- Preserve accountless/local-first operation even as optional hosted/cloud/team features are added.
- Use public/current provider/platform contracts; do not depend on undocumented ChatGPT/private vendor internals.
- Treat automatic incident intake as evidence, never automatic proof that a software bug is validated.
- Treat Web/Android/desktop **durable product data** separately from ephemeral per-client presentation/navigation state.
- Remote safety policy, Lockdown, org policy and approvals may only reduce authority; no remote/config/model layer may silently broaden it.
- Notification, push, updater, billing and hosted execution paths must obey OS/store/security/privacy rules rather than bypassing them for convenience.
- Commercial `~99 readiness` means a defined evidence target, not a claim of zero defects or permanent compliance.

## Status model

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Validated | Current source/product evidence confirms actionable work. |
| In progress | Implementation is actively underway. |
| Verification | Implementation is complete locally and awaiting required terminal evidence. |
| Blocked | A documented prerequisite prevents progress. |
| Complete | Required local/runtime/GitHub evidence passed and the child is closed. |

## Delivery gates

Every candidate passes:
1. **Intake** — isolate one product behavior/capability/root cause.
2. **Current-source validation** — inspect current `main`, not a stale upstream report.
3. **Deduplication** — search source/issues/commits/related work first.
4. **Specification** — scope, exclusions, architecture boundaries, privacy/security/cost, acceptance criteria and deterministic verification.
5. **Implementation** — reuse shared foundations and fix the root cause.
6. **Verification** — focused tests + every applicable Android/Web/security/migration/performance/accessibility/provider/runtime/GitHub gate.
7. **Closure** — post exact evidence, close child, then reconcile this master.

Automatic incident issues have an additional hard gate: **#118 must inspect current source and classify the intake before `status: validated` can be applied or this master count/index can change.**

# Program map

## A. Core engineering backlog — #34–#84

Validated foundational work covers deterministic data ordering, temporary chats, cost accounting, cross-device sync engine, context/history preservation, multi-credential routing, model metadata, MCP OAuth/mTLS, streaming/retry correctness, drafts, Web API injection, provider routing/semantics, backup integrity, video generation, provenance, streaming performance, checkpointing, Ask User behavior, malformed data resilience, per-conversation settings, attachment capability/classification, reasoning semantics, OCR/media retention, image export/gallery, Photo Picker, haptics, conversation status, model-callable image generation, typed events, tool approvals, model-name/attachment UX, skill installation/delegation and runtime variables.

These remain reusable foundations for every later program.

## B. Extensions ecosystem — #85–#96

- #85 unified Extensions hub/umbrella.
- #86 stable

## Problem

Okou has no secure way for an authorized interactive Agent to execute bounded non-interactive commands on several user-owned SSH hosts. Long-lived private keys must not enter the model, sandbox, Agent job payload, environment, filesystem, proxy registry, command result, or logs.

SSH does not fit the existing connector backend. That subsystem models API/OAuth/manual accounts selected by connector slug, including default and thread-level account choice, generic connector secrets, runtime bindings, firewall materialization, and catalog grant methods. SSH needs several hosts simultaneously, has one fixed login identity per host, performs authentication inside the SSH protocol, and deliberately bypasses the sandbox HTTP/firewall credential path.

## Decision: standalone SSH domain, Connector-page presentation

SSH is a product integration displayed in the Connectors area, but it is not stored or resolved as an existing connector account.

Do not use:

- `connectors` or a connector extension row;
- generic `secrets` connector rows;
- `user_connectors` Agent authorization;
- connector catalog grant/auth-method schemas;
- default account, thread override, account manager, or switch-card state;
- connector account resolution, credential materialization, runtime bindings, `connectorRuntimeTargets`, or firewall secret injection.

Reuse only genuinely shared infrastructure: organization/user scoping patterns, KMS/encryption primitives, feature switches, public-destination policy data, visual card/icon primitives, and API/test conventions.

The Platform Connectors page composes a special SSH card into its UI when the feature is visible. That card reads a dedicated SSH summary and opens dedicated host management. Agent settings display a separate SSH access control backed by the SSH domain rather than `user_connectors`.

## V1 product model

### One login identity per host

Each SSH connection contains one canonical public `host:port`, one username, one pinned host-key algorithm/SHA-256 fingerprint, one private key with optional passphrase, a display name, and a positive configuration generation.

Within one user/organization scope, canonical `host:port` is unique. Several different hosts can be used in one run, but a host cannot have several configured usernames. Changing the host, port, username, credential, or trusted host key requires a successful test and increments generation atomically.

There is no Agent-selected username, default SSH host, account switching, or fallback. The Agent chooses only an exact admitted SSH connection ID returned by inventory.

### Standalone persistence

- `ssh_connections` owns non-secret configuration and current authority.
- `ssh_connection_credentials` owns the encrypted private key/passphrase and is deleted with the live connection.
- `agent_ssh_access` grants one user/Agent access to the SSH capability.
- `agent_run_ssh_admissions` snapshots exact SSH connection IDs, generations, and non-secret display metadata at run creation. The historical source ID deliberately survives live connection deletion so inventory can report `revoked_or_deleted`.
- `ssh_setup_probes` is an internal, short-lived runner handoff for host-key scan and authentication testing. It is not user history: candidate ciphertext is cleared at terminal state or expiry, and terminal rows are deleted by TTL cleanup.

V1 does not add a durable SSH execution/audit table. Execution creates no API command task, pending attempt, terminal callback, or persisted command/result. Redacted operational logs and metrics carry only identifiers, outcome class, timing, byte counts, and truncation state.

## Setup and lifecycle

Setup has no active sandbox, and production runners establish outbound API polling rather than accepting API-initiated work. After the runner/rootfs fleet has fully upgraded, an eligible official runner polls and claims a bounded short-lived setup probe:

1. public destination validation and host-key scan;
2. retur

# Agent work coordination control plane

This issue is the canonical live coordination log for concurrent work in `geromet/TornHappyGymStats`.

## Authority

- Fleet/manual agents **never merge into the repository default branch**. Final default inspection/merge belongs exclusively to Gerome's separate coding-agent/human workflow.
- Preserve outside-contributor ownership and all production/Torn read-only safety boundaries.
- Current repository/PR/issue state plus the latest valid coordination transitions win over stale prose and historical handoffs.
- The external coding agent is not part of the normal implementation, CI, rescue, integration, PR CR, or final-handoff loop.

## Reliable append-only coordination protocol

State is the latest valid transition for each `run=` token. Never depend on cleanup executing after work.

- 🟢 **OPEN** — default/unowned; no active lease.
- 🟡 **ASSIGNING** — phase-1 SYN. It consumes a lease only when admitted by deterministic collision/capacity election.
- 🔵 **ASSIGNED** — phase-2 ACK. Only an admitted winner may post this after reconstructing ownership/capacity and acknowledging its ASSIGNING comment. Mutation is forbidden before ACK.
- 🛠️ **WORKING @ branch** — append exact branch/head/source PR/package before useful mutation and after every remote head change.
- 🧪 **WAITING ON PR CR** — coherent package is ready for Gerome/coding-agent/human final inspection; releases the fleet lease. This state does not authorize an external-agent trigger.
- 🆘 **WAITING ON ADVISOR** — fleet recovery state for an unresolved topology/state anomaly; releases the fleet lease. It is internal by default and does not itself trigger an external agent.
- ✅ **FINISHED** — issue/package is actually complete after required default incorporation or explicit completed/not-planned disposition is verified.

Every transition is a **new comment**. Minimum fields:

`<emoji> <STATE> | seq=<n> | run=<token> | lane=<lane> | issue/package=<id> | branch=<name-or-none> | head=<sha-or-none> | pr=<number-or-none> | base=<ref-or-none> | base_sha=<sha-or-none> | prev=<prior-state/comment-id> | ts=<ISO8601> | note=<short result>`

PR-facing WAITING/proof transitions record the exact base ref/SHA the evidence covered. Unknowns are explicit. Reread before retries and suppress the same `run+seq`. Sequence gaps, contradictions, or head mismatches fail closed.

## Complete-state reconstruction and admission

Before admitting mutable work, reconstruct all recognized current protocol and legacy claim/release state, or use a mechanically maintained durable index proven equivalent. A recent-comment window is never authoritative for lease counting or ownership.

Before ASSIGNING, refresh target dependencies/stop gates. After ASSIGNING, refresh them again before ACK. Any change invalidates the candidate. Existing ASSIGNED/WORKING owners beat new overlapping candidates; among overlapping ASSIGNING candidates the earlier GitHub comment ID wins. Global capacity is at most five materially independent active packages. Losing candidates do not mutate and must choose independent work.

## Trigger conservation — absolute normal-path prohibition

GitHub text is a control surface. The fleet must treat two trigger-like terms as hazardous: the external-agent name token and the CR keyword commonly used for code inspection. Do not emit either token or derivatives in ordinary GitHub titles, bodies, comments, or labels. Do not quote old trigger-bearing text into new GitHub comments.

Normal fleet work must never:

- request external-agent code inspection during implementation/rescue;
- wait for or poll for an automatic external scan as a completion condition;
- request another external scan because a branch head changed;
- use an external agent as routine PR inspector, CI verifier, branch/topology repairer, work selector, or final-handoff mechanism;
- create an external-agent trigger merely because a PR is green/ready.

Use repository CI, deterministic local/hos

## Why

After 16 live-bounty targets at $0 and a lens program with Δ=0 on its last wedge, the one lever not yet pulled is the model itself. This measurement pre-registers a clean A/B before any Fable run starts.

## Held-out (contamination-free)

**Royco Day** — Cantina private contest, 2026-08-10 → 2026-08-19, $30k pool, 146 submissions. Final report published 2026-08-28 in the target repo (`audit/Cantina-Royco-Day.pdf`, target commit `fa6d2497`). Contest end and report are both after Fable 5.1's training cutoff (June 2026).

Ground truth: **0 High, 1 Medium, 0 Low, 6 Informational.**
- M-1 (the only payable row): *EntryPoint reentrancy — a market's oracle `poke()` double-spends commingled escrow.* `src/entrypoint/RoycoDayEntryPoint.sol::executeDeposit` reads the request into memory, calls the collateral-asset oracle's non-view `poke()` (attacker/deployer-chosen contract), and only then writes the escrow; the contract has no reentrancy guard (the kernel does). One request settles twice from the singleton's commingled per-asset escrow.
- I-1..I-6: accountant first-epoch curve, late first sync after fixed-term expiry, liquidity premium paying genesis dead shares, OPTIMIZED/MAX LPT redemptions gross-vs-net, oracle replacement setters cross-read, released fixed term re-stamped by next downtick.

## Control arm (already run, 2026-08-13/14, Opus)

`run-zone-hunt.sh --repo royco-day@fa6d2497 --scope src --backend flat-cyborg --jobs 1 --deep-hunt --deep-hunt-aux-max 2`, `llm.model = opus` (the default). Result: 29 zones (21 hunted, 8 no_brief), 55 candidate leads, **0 verified** (refute gate + hand adjudication). Zone `src_entrypoint`: `hunted_empty`, 5 cells (C4, C6, C12, C5, C17 — no C8), 0 candidates → **M-1 was a generation miss** (and a class-routing miss: C8 was never assigned to the zone).

## Treatment arm (this issue)

Same commit, same scope, same flags, same backend; `--model claude-fable-5-1` threaded through EVERY LLM stage (map-zones, gen-briefs, discovery, refute, invariant-hunt, deep-hunt-gate) via the sibling feature issue. `--jobs 2` (wall-clock only; no semantic effect). Zones are re-mapped on Fable (a full-pipeline comparison; the classification layer is part of the model effect).

## Metrics (pre-registered)

1. **Primary:** M-1 present in `verify/verified_findings.json` after the refute gate (mechanism-judged: reentry through oracle `poke()` inside `executeDeposit`, double settlement of one request from commingled escrow).
2. **Generation:** any discovery lead at `RoycoDayEntryPoint.executeDeposit` with the reentrancy mechanism, even if later refuted.
3. **Informational hits:** how many of I-1..I-6 appear as leads (any stage).
