## Proposal type

- Modify column

## Affected scope (files/folders/chains)

- `references/offers/wallets.csv`
- `listings/specific-networks/*/wallets.csv`
- `listings/all-networks/wallets.csv`
- `Wallets.md`, `schema.json`, and CSV/JSON validation

## Motivation / problem statement

The wallet `supportedPlatforms` field currently mixes distribution form,
operating system, and inconsistent aliases. At commit
`f961eb969e0d0fa8a506b314861c92cd01adbeec`, the 106 canonical wallet offers
use these eight values:

| Value | Rows |
|---|---:|
| `Android` | 88 |
| `iOS` | 88 |
| `Browser Extension` | 41 |
| `Web` | 28 |
| `Desktop` | 11 |
| `Hardware` | 8 |
| `Extension` | 2 |
| `Webapp` | 1 |

The wiki examples instead show `Chrome`, `Firefox`, and `Edge`, none of which
currently appear in the canonical data. This leaves several ambiguities:

- `Browser Extension` and `Extension` mean the same distribution form;
- `Web` and `Webapp` are used for the same browser-hosted form;
- a browser name from the documented example is not comparable to a generic
  `Browser Extension` value;
- `Hardware` is both a value here and a separate boolean column, so consumers
  cannot tell whether it means “is a hardware wallet” or “can connect to one.”

As a result, a filter for browser wallets has to guess across aliases, and the
documented browser-specific query cannot be answered by the actual data.

## Detailed proposal

### Column change

- Category/table: `wallets`
- Column name: `supportedPlatforms`
- Change type: modify
- Updated definition: distribution targets on which a user can directly run or
  access the wallet.
- Value type: JSON array using a documented controlled vocabulary.
- Allowed values: `Browser Extension`, `Web App`, `Desktop`, `iOS`, `Android`,
  `Hardware Device`.
- Example: `["Browser Extension","iOS","Android"]`.

### Normalization rules

1. Canonicalize `Extension` to `Browser Extension`.
2. Canonicalize `Web` and `Webapp` to `Web App`.
3. Canonicalize `Hardware` to `Hardware Device` only for wallets whose primary
   user interface is a physical device.
4. Keep the existing `hardware` boolean for the broader capability “is a
   hardware wallet or supports connecting one”; clarify this distinction in
   `Wallets.md`.
5. Remove `Chrome`, `Firefox`, and `Edge` from the examples for this column.
   If browser-specific compatibility is required later, model it in a separate
   `supportedBrowsers` field rather than mixing browser products with platform
   forms.
6. Deduplicate values and store them in the canonical order shown above.

### Migration and validation

- Update the wiki and schema first, then mechanically migrate the three aliases
  in canonical offers and any listing overrides.
- Validate every value against the controlled vocabulary and reject duplicate
  array items.
- During migration, manually verify the eight current `Hardware` rows so the
  new value is not inferred merely from the broader `hardware` boolean.

The proposal intentionally does not add a browser-compatibility column. It
first makes the existing field internally consistent and aligned with what the
dataset already records.

## Contact

GitHub: @beyondskyway

## Rewards address

`0x0b94E34515391060d7118a18Ef3b6b9BAC0Cf105` (Ethereum mainnet, USDC/USDT)
title: [DBIP] Normalize wallet supported platforms and remove ambiguous aliases

I want to use Stride as a 3D renderer for a cross platform project where the render window is integrated in the Avalonia UI.
Now both Stride and Avalonia, theoretically, would support this quite nicely but the issue appears with extending the Stride engine with a new rendering context (this means custom GameContext, GamePlatform, GameForm and GameWindow) which would be based on Avalonia native controls (rather then, for WinForms, based on System.Windows.Forms.Control). This is not a complicated extension as it would be, more or less, equal in implementation with the current WinForms. 

The problem is that when using the Stride nuget packages (or the old Xenko ones), consumers of these packages are not allowed to provide custom instances to these classes because:
- GamePlatforms are created in a static internal method and based on an enumeration so there is no way to provide a custom implementation here;
- GamePlatform itself is marked as internal which means we couldn't inherit from it;
- GameWindow contains internal abstract methods which cannot be overloaded;
- There are various other properties or methods marked as internal that might be required in such an implementation but I don't currently have an exhaustive list for those.

Is there a design limitation for why a consumer of these assemblies couldn't provide custom classes for rendering concepts? From what I can tell, the rest of the code is neatly abstracted and should work regardless of what implementations we might have there.

Exposing the internal members outside the assembly and introducing a new overridable factory pattern for creating game platforms would allow one to fully implement these concepts in separate assemblies without having the need to modify the internal Stride code.

Of course, this would not have any impact on the GameEngine itself but would allow Xenko to be embedded in any kind of contexts.

Lastly, if there are no design limitations with my proposals or other issues I may not notice now, would a merge request be accepted? I can pretty easily fork the repo and maintain my own implementation of it but I feel it would be much better, if there are no downsides, to have it contained in the main repository.
title: Support for Custom render context

When attempting to exit an integrated DeFi Yield Vault (Beefy/Morpho) that had accumulated contaminated funds, the PPOI (Private Proofs of Innocence) defense mechanism triggered a block. Executing the UI's recommended `"Safely unshield to origin"` feature caused the protocol to identify RAILGUN's own Relay/Broadcaster Contract (`0xFA7093CDD...`) as the "origin address." Consequently, **50,551 USDC was unshielded directly back into the Relay Adapt contract**, leaving the funds locked on-chain with a `Missing ❌` PPOI status and zero UI trace in the wallet.

---

### Environment

* **App Version**: Railway Windows Desktop Wallet (Latest)
* **Chain**: Ethereum Mainnet
* **Integrated Protocol**: Beefy / Morpho Yield Vaults (`USDC Clearstar 3Jane V2`, `USDC Steakhouse Reservoir V2`)
* **Affected Contract**: `RAILGUN: Relay / Relay Adapt` (`0xFA7093CDD9EE6932B4eb2c9e1cde7CE00B1FA4b9`)

---

### Sequence of Events & Cross-Wallet Proof

1. **Initial Clean Deposit**:
* Initial shield on **Aug-15-2026 10:48:47 AM UTC** possessed a 100% valid PPOI status (`Valid ✅`).


2. **DeFi Vault Contamination**:
* Deposited funds into Railway’s natively integrated Beefy/Morpho yield vaults.
* Due to external 3rd-party liquidity entering these public yield vaults, the resulting yield shares became contaminated upstream.


3. **Cross-Wallet Deadlock (Proving Platform-Wide Issue)**:
* **Wallet A (Test)**: Deposited ~50 USDC into *Clearstar 3Jane Vault*. Redeem triggered a PPOI block.
* **Wallet B (Main)**: Deposited 50,551 USDC into *Steakhouse Reservoir Vault*. Redeem triggered an identical PPOI block on an entirely separate seed phrase.


4. **Emergency Routing Logic Failure**:
* Navigated to `Activity -> View pending balance -> Restricted` and clicked `"Safely unshield to origin"`.
* The SDK erroneously set the destination `origin` as the Railgun Relay Contract itself (`0xFA70...4b9`).
* The transaction succeeded on-chain, but the funds were transferred into RAILGUN's Relay Contract rather than the user's public EOA.



---

### Root Cause Analysis

* **PPOI Mechanism Overreaction**: Valid user deposits were tainted *after* interaction with native DeFi pools due to aggregated vault liquidity.
* **Fallback Route Invalidation**: The `"Unshield to origin"` feature incorrectly parsed the Relay/Broadcaster contract as the original fund source (or fallback target) instead of the user's actual underlying EOA/0zk balance.
* **State Loss**: The fallback unshield transaction lacks a standard zero-knowledge proof generation step, resulting in a `Missing ❌` status in the PPOI Lookup Tool and leaving the wallet UI unable to recognize or recover the balance.

## Goal

Extend Regelsuche from searching only complete expression states and local rules to searching, validating and learning bounded **schematic proof plans**. A plan may contain typed holes, structural selectors and open obligations, but it becomes an executable search move only after every hole is bound and every obligation has been discharged by an exact checker.

The first target is to remove the externally supplied pairing/sign schedule from the Brahmagupta–Fibonacci composition. Later stages should support coefficient-ansatz discovery, recurrence invariants and eventually a separate logical proof-discovery domain.

## Motivation

Current evidence separates two limitations:

- Sophie-Germain can already be rediscovered under a bounded target-free factorization objective with frozen learned rules.
- Brahmagupta–Fibonacci has an exact eleven-step derivation using one independently frozen learned completion rule twice, but unrestricted all-at-once best-first search exhausted its 20,000-state budget. The successful characterization still supplies a generic phase schedule externally.

The missing capability is therefore not another identity-specific rewrite. Regelsuche must represent and search **partial strategies** that constrain a large expression search without receiving the historical endpoint.

## Delivered first slice

PR #873 introduces the initial exact residual-composition mechanism:

```text
source fragment
  = selected structured fragment
  + exact polynomial residual
```

Several local effects may compose only when they bind a complete disjoint additive source partition and their residuals sum exactly to zero. The composer accepts no target expression or historical reference. Its Brahmagupta characterization learns and freezes the generic sum-of-squares completion rule first, generates all bounded pair/sign effects, freezes the resulting candidates and checks historical correspondence only afterwards.

This is an executable prerequisite, not yet a learned proof plan.

## Intended architecture

```text
source mathematical object
  -> bounded schematic plan grammar
  -> typed holes and structural selectors
  -> mechanically generated obligations
  -> exact hole solving / counterexample search
  -> fully bound plan
  -> compile to ordinary RewriteProgram / proof tactic program
  -> primitive replay and independent checking
  -> candidate freeze
  -> held-out correspondence, utility and later novelty review
```

A schematic plan is never itself an authorized mathematical edge. Only the checked compiled result may enter ordinary search or proof evidence.

## A. Exact residual-effect composition

- [ ] Merge and qualify PR #873.
- [ ] Retain source-derived occurrence identities rather than caller-invented partitions.
- [ ] Require each local transformed fragment to be exactly equivalent to its bound source fragment.
- [ ] Require the selected structured term to occur in the transformed AST.
- [ ] Compute the residual from exact polynomial normal forms; never accept a caller-provided residual as authority.
- [ ] Compose only complete disjoint source covers with exact zero residual.
- [ ] Bound components, effects, composition size, result count and combination work before enumeration.
- [ ] Preserve primitive rule IDs and application identities through the composed candidate.
- [ ] Retain plus-only, overlap, false-effect, forged-residual, forged-occurrence, assumption and work-exhaustion controls.

## B. Versioned schematic-plan IR

Add a canonical bounded `SchematicProofPlan` distinct from executable `RewriteProgram`.

Initial hole kinds:

```text
CoefficientHole
SignHole
TermHole
OccurrenceHole
DisjointTermPairHole
InvariantHole
MeasureHole
WitnessHole
FormulaHole
```

EQUIVALENT
ZERO
NON_ZERO
DISJOINT_OCCURRENCES
COMPLETE_SOURCE_COVER
RESIDUAL_SUM_IS_ZERO
CAPABILITY_UNLOCKED
PRESERVES_INVARIANT
STRICTLY_DECREASES
PROVES
```

## Goal
Test whether the Camellia pattern is one instance of a broader evolutionary architecture rather than a genus-specific story.

Primary question:

> Across clades with a defensible white-like or low-visible-pigment ancestral state, do derived colourful states arise repeatedly through similar molecular modules, and is molecular accessibility broader than long-term phylogenetic realization?

## Why this is stronger than adding one more genus
A single public-data genus can establish a mechanism-rich case study but leaves external generality bounded. A cross-clade atlas creates a new harmonized dataset assembled under one protocol and allows explicit tests of commonality versus lineage-specificity.

This is not a literature vote count. The target is a rebuilt comparative dataset with harmonized trait coding, explicit ancestral-state uncertainty, standardized transition classes, and where possible common molecular module coordinates.

## Tier A candidate clades — white-like / low-pigment ancestral baseline
1. **Camellia** — white ancestral state supported by independent genus-scale work; red/yellow/white diversification; strongest molecular/public-data anchor.
2. **Epimedium sect. Diphyllon** — white plesiomorphic inner-sepal colour with diversification to yellow/red/purple; parallel floral evolution and introgression; multi-species pigment and expression data available.
3. **Linoideae / Linum s.l.** — yellow-white ancestral reconstruction (~41 Ma), later purple/blue/red/pink states; good dated macro anchor, molecular colour resources more uneven.
4. **Angraecinae / Angraecum** — white ancestral flowers with repeated derived green states; useful low-complexity control rather than a full rainbow radiation.
5. **Nicotiana subclades** — some section-level ancestral nodes inferred white; use only if node/state and hybridization history can be frozen defensibly.

## Coloured-ancestor controls
Do not select only white-ancestor clades. Add controls to avoid ascertainment bias:
- **Iochrominae** — blue ancestral flowers, repeated losses to white/yellow and gains to orange/red; strong pathway-level molecular literature.
- **Iris** — purple/anthocyanin ancestral state with repeated derived white/polymorphic states.
- **Antirrhineae** — transition-rich control linking extant polymorphism to macro transition structure.

## Core hypotheses
### H1 — ancestral-baseline asymmetry
White-like/low-pigment ancestral clades show more repeated pigment gains than losses expected under symmetric transition models.

### H2 — latent-capacity hypothesis
Derived colour gains more often involve regulatory redeployment of retained pigment machinery than de-novo pathway invention.

### H3 — modular replay
Across independent gains, recurrence is stronger at pathway-module level than at complete multivariate pigment-state level.

### H4 — accessibility-realization gap
The number/diversity of molecularly accessible colour states exceeds the number/diversity of long-term realised phylogenetic states.

### H5 — ecological filtering
Where sensory/reward/pollinator data exist, flowering-window pollinator filtering explains realised state persistence better than coarse annual climate or human-visible hue alone.

## Phase 1 — macro atlas admission
For each candidate clade record:
- current accepted phylogeny and taxon coverage;
- ancestral colour state with uncertainty/model sensitivity;
- number and direction of reconstructed transitions;
- visible-colour coding source and wild/cultivar status;
- presence of within-species colour variation;
- public molecular / metabolomic / spectral / pollination data availability.

# AUTO-GHOST REWRITE — CODER COMMUNICATION HUB

Issue này là **cổng giao tiếp chính thức giữa User / Planner / Coder** cho kế hoạch viết lại AutoGhost.

> **GREENFIELD REWRITE**
> Không refactor/port code cũ. Không lấy kiến trúc Python/MVP cũ làm ràng buộc. Repo cũ chỉ được dùng như nơi chứa tài liệu tham khảo. Nguồn nghiệp vụ chính hiện tại là `SƠ ĐỒ.docx` và các quyết định mới được ghi trong issue này.

## 1. Mục tiêu sản phẩm hiện tại

Xây dựng app Windows quản lý nhiều client `qnyh.exe` với 4 khu vực chính:

1. **Client**
   - User tự thêm `Client ID` vào app.
   - Khi `qnyh.exe` được mở, app tự quét các cửa sổ/client đang chạy.
   - Chỉ bind/điều khiển cửa sổ có `Role ID` khớp `Client ID` đã đăng ký.
   - `Role ID` là danh tính lâu dài; PID/HWND chỉ là runtime/session tạm thời.
   - Client không match phải bị ignore và tuyệt đối không nhận input automation.

2. **Nhiệm vụ**
   - Nhiệm vụ cá nhân.
   - Nhiệm vụ cần party.
   - Mỗi nhiệm vụ có lịch ngày/tuần, giờ mở/chạy/reset cụ thể.
   - Automation dùng thao tác mẫu của user nhưng phải có state/verify/retry/timeout, không chỉ macro click mù.

3. **Tiện ích**
   - Các chức năng quản lý client/cửa sổ/reconnect/log/debug sẽ được xác định chi tiết tiếp từ tài liệu và cập nhật của user.

4. **Đồng bộ client**
   - Chọn một client gốc (master).
   - Đồng bộ thao tác được phép sang các follower.
   - Có filter sự kiện; không mặc định mirror 100% mọi input.
   - Tọa độ phải ưu tiên relative/semantic thay vì tuyệt đối.

## 2. Quy tắc nguồn dữ liệu

Thứ tự ưu tiên khi có xung đột:

1. Quyết định mới nhất của User trong issue này.
2. Tài liệu `SƠ ĐỒ.docx`.
3. Tài liệu kế hoạch mới được tạo sau thời điểm rewrite.
4. Code/spec cũ: **không phải source of truth**.

Nếu coder thấy tài liệu mâu thuẫn, **không tự đoán**. Đăng câu hỏi vào issue này.

## 3. Cách coder phải báo cáo

Mỗi đợt triển khai, coder comment theo mẫu:

```md
## STATUS UPDATE
Phase: P0/P1/...
State: PLANNING | IMPLEMENTING | BLOCKED | VERIFYING | DONE

### Đã làm
- ...

### File/Module thay đổi
- ...

### Kiểm thử thực tế
- Test:
- Kết quả:
- Evidence/log/screenshot:

### Chưa làm
- ...

### Blocker / cần quyết định
- Q-xxx: ...

### Next
- ...
```

Không được chỉ báo `PASS` mà không ghi cách kiểm thử/evidence.

## 4. Cách đặt câu hỏi

Mọi điểm chưa rõ dùng ID:

```md
### Q-001 — Cách xác định Role ID
Context: ...
Observed: ...
Options:
A. ...
B. ...
Recommendation: ...
Need decision: ...
```

Một quyết định đã được User xác nhận thì ghi lại:

```md
### DEC-001
Decision: ...
Reason: ...
Impact: ...
```

Coder không được tự thay đổi DEC đã chốt nếu chưa mở lại thảo luận.

## 5. Luật triển khai

- Không viết lại theo code cũ chỉ vì nó đã tồn tại.
- Không hard-code Role ID, Client ID, giờ nhiệm vụ hoặc party vào source.
- Tách definition/config khỏi runtime session.
- Không bind client chỉ dựa vào PID/HWND/window order.
- Không gửi input tới client chưa xác minh `Role ID == Client ID`.
- Automation phải có state, precondition, action, verification, timeout, retry và failure path.
- Party phải có coordinator; không để các member tự chạy độc lập khi task yêu cầu phối hợp.
- Sync phải có master/follower + event filter + kill switch.
- Unknown state phải dừng an toàn, log và chụp evidence nếu cấu hình cho phép.
- Không đọc/ghi memory game, inject DLL, sửa binary hoặc bypass anti-cheat.

## 6. Giai đoạn khởi đầu bắt buộc

### P0 — Discovery / Feasibility
Coder chưa được lao vào full UI hoặc full task automation. Trước hết phải chứng minh:

- phát hiện nhiều `qnyh.exe`;
- map process ↔ top-level window;
- xác định được nguồn đọc Role ID khả thi;
- bind đúng Role ID ↔ Client ID;
- client không match không nhận input;
- kiểm tra cơ chế input/capture khi foreground/background;
- xác định giới hạn kỹ thuật thực tế của game client.

Deliverable P0 phải có báo cáo evidence trước khi sang P1.

### P1 — Client Registry + Runtime Binding
- CRUD Client ID;
- auto scan khi qnyh mở;
- Role ID resolver;
- bind/unbind/rebind session;
- state
title: [REWRITE] AutoGhost — Cổng giao tiếp & điều phối coder

This issue tracks the active implementation ticket and review state for Misyra. Development is performed as a single-agent, specification-driven workflow. GitHub history, the approved specifications, ticket acceptance criteria, tests, PR diffs, and verification evidence are authoritative.

## Authoritative sources

- `docs/specifications/product-specification.md`
- `docs/specifications/technical-specification.md`
- `docs/specifications/implementation-tickets.md`

The product specification is authoritative for user-facing behavior. The technical specification is authoritative for implementation architecture and engineering constraints. The implementation-ticket document defines dependency order, ticket scope, acceptance criteria, TDD evidence, and review gates.

## Development workflow

1. Read the exact active ticket and relevant product/technical specification sections from current `main` before modifying code.
2. Verify the required `main` base SHA and dependencies.
3. Work on exactly one ticket branch and one implementation PR at a time.

body_excerpt:
`#20` is closed and correctly so: the template placeholder is gone and the enclave now runs Helico's own re-centre decision. But the prize wording asks for more than a real decision — it asks that the workflow be *"a meaningful part of the application"* and rules out *"an isolated example that does not contribute"*.

Today the verdict is computed and then goes nowhere. Nothing on-chain consumes it. An assessor reading the repo would be right to call that isolated.

## What closes the gap

The standard CRE delivery path, verified on both sides while reviewing #34 and #36:

1. The vault implements `IReceiver` and an `onReport(bytes metadata, bytes report)` that only the `KeystoneForwarder` may call.
2. `report` is exactly the bytes the enclave emits with `encoderName: 'evm'`, so the vault does `abi.decode(report, (bool act, int24 tickLower, int24 tickUpper, bytes32 mandateHash))`, requires `mandateHash == keccak256(abi.encode(m))` for the account it is acting on, and then runs the existing `recenter` logic.
3. `AGENT_ROLE` moves from an EOA to the forwarder, so the only thing that can propose an action is a decision that came out of the enclave.
4. On the workflow side it is one call: `EVMClient.writeReport(don, { receiver: vault, report, gasConfig })`.

That is what makes the confidential workflow load-bearing rather than adjacent: with it, no re-centre can happen that the enclave did not decide.

## The constraint that shapes it

A `KeystoneForwarder 1.0.0` is deployed on **Robinhood Chain Testnet** at `0x8E6E6A1f2B2D4dF503bfd67951CF28F27BF3AF19`; the same address has **no code on Robinhood mainnet**, and mainnet is not in Chainlink's forwarder directory (verified on-chain by @rifkyeasy on #33).

So the DON-delivered path is demonstrable on the testnet today. Doing it on mainnet would mean our own relayer carrying DON signatures — which is exactly the shape of thing the twelve-agent audit just showed is hard to make safe, and not something to build in the last week.

**This decides which chain the demo video runs on**, so it should be settled before #22 rather than during recording.

## The shape that is not yet decided

`recenter` takes `RecenterParams`: `owner`, the two ticks, `liquidityToMint`, four slippage bounds and a deadline. The report carries four of those. The rest has to come from somewhere — widened report, on-chain derivation, or mandate fields — and that choice interacts with the missing `liquidityToMint` floor recorded in #34.

## Done when

- [ ] The vault accepts a verdict from the forwarder and rejects one from anywhere else, with a test for each
- [ ] `AGENT_ROLE` is held by the forwarder in the deployed configuration, not by an EOA
- [ ] A re-centre on Robinhood Chain Testnet, triggered by the workflow, with the transaction hash recorded for #21
- [ ] The package README stops saying the vault does not consume the report
title: Deliver the enclave's verdict to the vault through the CRE forwarder

### Problem or use case

A Bazaar catalog entry, and the quality counters attached to it, cannot be distinguished between **a payment that happened** and **a payload that was merely checked**. Both produce an entry, and the spec is the reason.

`specs/extensions/bazaar.md` Facilitator Behavior says a facilitator receiving a `PaymentPayload` containing the `bazaar` extension should validate `info` against `schema` and extract the discovery information. **Settlement appears nowhere in that section.** The response-header section is consistent with this: a facilitator MAY append `EXTENSION-RESPONSES` to **"the verify or settlement response"**, and `status: "success"` there means the discovery info was validated and successfully cataloged.

So the verify path is written into the spec, and every conforming catalog inherits it. This is not one implementation misbehaving, which is why this is filed as a spec proposal rather than a bug against a facilitator.

**Measured, not inferred.** On 2026-08-21T14:10:40Z I sent a `PaymentPayload` for a resource I operate, carrying `extensions.bazaar`, to a facilitator's `/verify`, and never settled:

```
status                200
body                  {"isValid":true,"payer":"0x9f54460FED..."}
EXTENSION-RESPONSES   eyJiYXphYXIiOnsic3RhdHVzIjoicHJvY2Vzc2luZyJ9fQ==
decoded               {"bazaar":{"status":"processing"}}
```

**No tokens moved.** Our chain-versus-ledger invariant was unchanged across the call.

I am claiming exactly what that shows and no more: the payload was **accepted for discovery processing at verify**. Whether a row always follows `processing` is unresolved on my side, and I have said so publicly rather than assert the stronger version.

Two independent lines of evidence from others point the same way and are worth reading together with it: the 17-route natural experiment reported in #2112, where routes settled with the declaration attached indexed and routes settled without it did not, which isolates the **declaration** rather than the settlement as the variable; and the census work in #3045, which found catalogued rows whose payee addresses show no inbound transfers, credited with calls and unique payers. I am citing those rather than speaking for their authors.

**Impact.** The counters are being read as a demand signal. If an entry can be produced by a verify, then `l30DaysTotalCalls` and `l30DaysUniquePayers` may count payloads seen rather than payments made, and an entry plus its counts costs one HTTP request and requires **no balance**, since an authorization that would fail at settle still verifies. Anyone selecting a service on those numbers is reading something a stranger can mint.

### Proposed solution

**Do not close the door. Label what came through it.**

Record provenance on the catalog entry and expose it in discovery results, minimally as a two-valued field distinguishing an entry whose declaration arrived on a **verify** from one that arrived on a **settlement**, and correspondingly separate the call counters, or mark them with the same provenance.

That achieves three things at once:

1. **The counters stop being ambiguous.** A reader can tell a payload that was checked from a payment that happened.
2. **Nothing breaks for honest services.** Many legitimately verify far more often than they settle, and they keep their entry and their visibility.
3. **The free-minting path stays open and stops mattering**, because an entry marked verified-only is not worth minting.

**Non-goals.** Not proposing that verify stop cataloging, not proposing a new authentication requirement, and not proposing that verified-only entries be hidden or ranked down. The ask is a label, not a gate.

### Related

- #3005 is adjacent but a different axis: whether client-echoed metadata is **truthful**. This one is whether an entry reflects a **payment**. Both concern what a reader may infer from a catalog row, and neither subsumes the other.
- #3178 established that the declaration must
title: [Feature]: Label catalog provenance, verify-only versus settled, so Bazaar counters mean something

### E01b — Go EscrowClient: wallet balance + event creation

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Code** | E01b |
| **Phase** | Phase 2 — escrow core |
| **Size** | M |
| **Depends on** | #23 (E01a, core tx pipeline), #19 (contract's `AdminWallet`/`Event` data model + `deposit_funds`/`withdraw_funds`/`create_event`) |
| **Money path** | Yes — `security` label, extra review |

**Executive summary**
Wraps the three contract calls that manage an organizer's balance and create events against it: `deposit_funds`, `withdraw_funds`, and `create_event` (ADR-006's shared per-organizer ledger model). Supersedes what used to be described here as "initialize + fund" — the contract no longer deploys per event or exposes those functions; this issue was rewritten to match the current `AdminWallet` design.

**Product context**
See ADR-006 in docs/architecture.md and the contract's own #19. The Go service is the only thing allowed to build these transactions — `apps/web` never talks to the contract directly.

**User stories**
- As the frontend (via the Go API), I want to fetch an organizer's current free balance, request a deposit, request a withdrawal, and create an event — each as one call, not hand-built XDR.

**Prerequisites**
- #23 (core tx pipeline) merged.
- The contract's `deposit_funds`/`withdraw_funds`/`create_event` deployed to testnet (from #19).

**Scope — In**
- `BuildDeposit(admin, token, amount)`, `BuildWithdraw(admin, amount)`, `BuildCreateEvent(admin, prizes []Prize)` — each returning unsigned XDR for the frontend to sign, per the build-sign-submit pattern (docs/architecture.md).
- A read call for the organizer's current `AdminWallet` free balance (needed by U01b's live balance-vs-total check).

**Scope — Out**
- `cancel_event`/`close_event` (#25).
- `dispute`/`resolve_dispute`/the emergency withdraw (#26).
- The two-signature emergency withdraw specifically is out of scope here — it's a distinct, resolver-co-signed exception (see #26), not part of the normal `withdraw_funds` path.

**Architecture & conventions**
Build-sign-submit: this package only builds unsigned XDR using #23's pipeline; signing happens in the organizer's wallet, submission happens after the frontend returns the signed transaction. `create_event`'s `prizes` argument is a list (ADR-002's corollary — ranked and category prizes are the same shape), not a single amount.

**Files to create/modify**
- `services/core-go/internal/escrow/wallet.go`

**Implementation guide**
1. Build argument-encoding for `deposit_funds`/`withdraw_funds`/`create_event` on top of #23's pipeline.
2. Build the free-balance read call.
3. Write tests against a local/testnet instance of the contract from #19.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Each of the three build functions produces XDR that the contract accepts when signed and submitted.
- [ ] The balance read call returns the correct free balance (excluding funds already reserved by created events).
- [ ] `create_event` correctly encodes a prize list of any length (1..N).

**Test plan**
- **Unit:** argument encoding for each function, against #23's pipeline with a mocked RPC client.
- **Manual:** deposit, check balance, create a real event with 2+ prizes on testnet.

**Risks & pitfalls**
- Don't let this package assume a single-prize event as the common case — per ADR-002's corollary, N=1 is just the short list, not a special path.

**Definition of done**
- [ ] Merged, verified against a real testnet `AdminWallet`/`Event`.

---

**Source:** [docs/build-plan.md](https://github.com/Astrea-Payouts/astrea/blob/develop/docs/build-plan.md), sub-task of #9

### E01c — Go EscrowClient: cancel_event + close_event

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Code** | E01c |
| **Phase** | Phase 2 — escrow core |
| **Size** | M |
| **Depends on** | #23 (E01a, core tx pipeline), #20 and #21 (contract's `cancel_event`/`close_event`) |
| **Money path** | Yes — `security` label, extra review |

**Executive summary**
Wraps the two contract calls that end an event normally: `cancel_event` (pre-launch refund) and `close_event` (pays 1..N winners in one call). Supersedes what used to be described here as "approve + release" — the contract's role model changed (ADR-006/ADR-002); this issue was rewritten to match.

**Product context**
See ADR-006 (`cancel_event` only works pre-`Active`) and ADR-002's corollary (`close_event` takes a winners list, not a single winner) in docs/architecture.md.

**User stories**
- As an organizer, I want to cancel an event I created by mistake, before anyone registers.
- As a judge, I want to close an event and pay every winner (one or several) in a single action.

**Prerequisites**
- #23 (core tx pipeline) merged.
- #20 and #21 (contract's `cancel_event`/`close_event`) deployed to testnet.

**Scope — In**
- `BuildCancelEvent(admin, eventId)` — fails if the event is already `Active` (surface the contract's own rejection, don't pre-validate state client-side only).
- `BuildCloseEvent(releaseSigner, eventId, winners []Address)` — `winners` length must match the event's prize list length.

**Scope — Out**
- The two-signature pre-launch emergency withdraw (#26 — it's an exception path, not part of normal cancellation).
- `dispute`/`resolve_dispute` (#26).

**Architecture & conventions**
Build-sign-submit, on top of #23's pipeline. `close_event`'s `winners` list must be built in the same order as the event's prize list — mismatched ordering pays the wrong person the wrong amount.

**Files to create/modify**
- `services/core-go/internal/escrow/lifecycle.go`

**Implementation guide**
1. Build argument-encoding for `cancel_event` and `close_event` on #23's pipeline.
2. Write tests against #20/#21's contract, including the negative case (cancel after `Active` fails).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] `BuildCancelEvent` succeeds pre-launch, and the contract itself rejects it post-launch (verified, not just assumed client-side).
- [ ] `BuildCloseEvent` correctly pays every winner in the list for both N=1 and N>1 events.
- [ ] A winners-list/prize-list length mismatch is caught before submission, not left to fail on-chain.

**Test plan**
- **Unit:** argument encoding for both functions; the winners/prizes length-mismatch guard.
- **Manual:** cancel a pre-launch testnet event (confirm refund), close a multi-prize testnet event (confirm every winner is paid).

**Risks & pitfalls**
- Winner/prize ordering is the sharpest edge here — get this wrong and the wrong wallet gets paid. Test it explicitly, don't assume list order is preserved through every layer.

**Definition of done**
- [ ] Merged, verified against real testnet cancel and multi-prize close calls.

## Anlass
Der Live-Check am 20.08.2026 zeigt für Baden-Württemberg auf `/laender/baden-wuerttemberg/mandat-und-praxis` nur die verifizierte Mandatsbasis. Die Seite sagt selbst: `vollständige Commitment-Zerlegung wird fortlaufend ergänzt`.

Der kanonische WÖk-Bestand bestätigt die Fachlücke:
- `/WOEK/WOEK-LAENDER-DAILY/BASELINE/baden-wuerttemberg/BASELINE-2026-08-18.md`: offene Aufgabe `Koalitionsvertrag vollständig in CoalitionCommitments zerlegen`.
- `/WOEK/WOEK-LAENDER-DAILY/CONTROL/LAENDER-COVERAGE-AND-HANDOFF-FINAL-2026-08-18.md`: Koalitionsvertrag 2026-2031 nur `als Mandatsbasis vorgesehen`.
- `/WOEK/WOEK-LAENDER-DAILY/FACHREVIEW/baden-wuerttemberg/INITIAL-IMPACT-CASES-2026-08-18.md`: fünf initiale Regierungswirkungsfälle, aber keine vollständige Koalitionsvertrags-Wirkungsanalyse.

Aktuelle Production ist nicht stale: `dpl_6CefNPFgRYrVXzYTFZeEezsArEX2`, READY/production, Git SHA `fb07fab799a34bbda0e2efc03f90066945c95802`, entsprechend aktuellem main-Basisstand von PR #235. Das BW-Problem ist daher nach aktuellem Befund keine bloße falsche Vercel-Promotion, sondern eine echte fachliche/Publikations-Coverage-Lücke - vorbehaltlich historischem Restore-Fund.

## Rollen
Human out of loop. **CodeX ist technischer Ausführungs- und Deployment-Aktor.** WÖk/Controller liefert Fachbestand, Priorität, Audit und exact-commit Freigabe. CodeX implementiert, testet, merged und deployt bis Production, sobald die Gates grün sind. Kein zusätzliches Human-Gate.

## P0-1 Baden-Württemberg: Restore-first
Vor Neuanalyse Git-Historie, Branches und kanonischen `/WOEK`-Bestand nach einer früher bereits fachlich freigegebenen Koalitionsvertragsanalyse durchsuchen. Wenn vorhanden: exakt/provenienzgebunden wiederherstellen. Keine Neufassung, die einen vorhandenen historischen Fachstand still ersetzt.

Wenn keine vollständige freigegebene Analyse existiert, ist die Fachlücke ausdrücklich zu schließen: amtlichen Koalitionsvertrag 2026-2031 vollständig sichern/versionieren, Commitments mit Source Locator extrahieren und dem WÖk-Fachreview zuführen. CodeX erzeugt **keine** Wirkungsurteile selbst.

## P0-2 Vollständigkeitsaudit alle 16 Länder
Für jedes Land getrennt inventarisieren und öffentlich korrekt abbilden:
- `election_cycle_state` und `government_lifecycle_state` - strikt getrennte Achsen,
- ElectionDocuments/Wahlprogramme und freigegebene Programmanalysen,
- Koalitions-/Mandatsdokumente und Coalition-/MandateCommitments,
- GovernmentActions und WÖkImpactCases,
- AnalysisVersions/RecommendationVersions,
- EvidenceEvents/RealityChecks,
- Quellen, Kompetenz, höherrangiges Recht/Schutzgrenzen,
- öffentliche Routen, Navigation, Overview-Projektion und Detailakten.

Fehlende Fachlayer nicht technisch erfinden. Vorhandenen Fachbestand niemals verkürzen oder verstecken.

## P0-3 Übersicht: Wirkungspotenzial klar sichtbar
Portalweit auf Wahlprogramm-, Koalitions-/Mandats-, Regierungs-, Parlament-, EU- und Länderübersichten muss die WÖk-Einordnung vor Prozessmetadaten verständlich sichtbar sein. Soweit fachlich freigegeben mindestens:
- qualitativer Wirkungspotenzialbefund,
- stärkste positive Potenziale,
- wichtigste materielle Risiken/Zielkonflikte,
- Evidenz/Unsicherheit getrennt von Richtung,
- Richtungsprofil nur für redaktionell/fachlich geprüfte Pfade,
- Nichtkompensation/Schutzgrenzen,
- **alle** freigegebenen Key Findings - keine `slice(0,2)`-Verkürzung,
- keine Partei-/Regierungs-Gesamtnote oder künstliche Saldierung.

Detailseiten müssen die vollständige freigegebene Fachakte und Quellen enthalten, nicht nur Mandats-/Fakten-Teaser.

## P0-4 Golden-State / kein Datenverlust durch Release
Jeder Kandidat gegen letzten akzeptierten Production-Stand **und** kanonischen `/WOEK`-Fachbestand prüfen:
- vorhandene Routen/Navigation,
- Fachakten/Analyseachsen,
- `required_content_paths` vs. `rendered_content_paths`, Pflichtbestand `unrendered_content_paths=[]`,
- Wirkungspotenzial/Key Findings/Wirkpfade/Evidenz,
- Kompetenz/Higher Law/Schutzgrenzen,
- Rec

## Outcome
Reduce the required CI feedback loop toward a warm-run median below five minutes without dropping acceptance coverage. Treat this as an optimization target to measure, not a new flaky timing gate.

## Evidence
At main SHA a9555a7d643bfcd6430e3f0473d37267d9267a5f, https://github.com/titan-engine/titan/actions/runs/34027341007 took 11m24s. Native took 11m19s: workspace tests/build 120s; collection room 92s, adventure 97s, arena 23s and factory 100s ran serially; cache restore/save took 85s + 72s. WASM took 9m25s, also with serial game builds. Jobs started within seconds. The native cache was about 3.08 GB compressed; configured game caches include arena but omit collection room, adventure and factory. Repository cache usage at inspection was about 10.7 GB across seven entries. Eviction as the cause of misses is not established. A cold WASM job in https://github.com/titan-engine/titan/actions/runs/34024130343 took 17m35s and logged misses for both Cargo and bindgen caches.

## Scope
Refactor .github/workflows/ci.yml into bounded parallel native/WASM workloads (workspace, independent games, copied-starter acceptance as appropriate). Design job boundaries and caches together: avoid restoring the existing giant cache into every shard. Cover actual Cargo output paths/profiles, including the newer standalone games; retain copied-project isolation. Inspect dependency duplication, stale outputs, cache scope, immutable keys and refresh policy. Use job/toolchain/platform isolation and a deliberate default-branch cache warming strategy. Keep cache misses correctness-neutral and exclude runtime captures/discovery data.

## Acceptance and verification
- [ ] Map every existing required command to its new job; preserve native, actual-WASM, macOS/GPU, copied-starter, failure-evidence and cleanup checks.
- [ ] Run independent native/WASM workloads concurrently on separate runners; retain the three existing required check names as aggregate gates where needed. Aggregates must explicitly fail on a failed, cancelled or unexpectedly skipped necessary job, including upstream failure cases.
- [ ] Preserve PR supersession cancellation, main/merge-group independence, bounded deadlines, evidence retention and merge_group checks_requested support. Do not temporarily weaken protections during rollout.
- [ ] Use bounded caches covering each workload's actual build outputs. Demonstrate a cold run and subsequent warm restore; explain save/refresh behavior and default-branch versus PR cache scope. Preserve independent copied-game verification.
- [ ] Compare at least three completed representative warm CI runs with the baseline, plus one observed cold run. Report trigger, SHA, runner wait, end-to-end required-check time, per-job time, restore/save time, cache size and total runner-minutes. Target a warm median under five minutes; if unmet, provide the measured remaining bottleneck and an explicit maintainer disposition before closing rather than silently accepting the target miss.
- [ ] Verify aggregate failure propagation with a controlled failing check on an isolated branch, then restore the passing implementation. Verify required checks on PR, merge queue and resulting main revision under the workflow policy then in force.
- [ ] Update docs/workflow.md and relevant verification documentation for job layout, cache policy and measurement procedure. Keep future TODOs in issues.

No open blocking prerequisite. Coordinate edits to CI and workflow documentation with other latency work. HIGH-FLIP-RISK: whether a RAW box rate is defensible as a BOX verdict given 23.1% site-caused mass, and whether the three-way absence split is genuinely tri-state rather than a fallthrough by a new route. An independent second reviewer is owed before merge.

THE DEFECT, re-derived 2026-08-07 04:27Z. Guerrilla failed 46.28% of its 1,290 terminal deploys in 24h and `bp cloud status` prints `ok` for it, from a bare `default:` arm at internal/cli/cloud_status_cmd.go:70 that read no vital at all. The control plane assembles a 14-signal pressure block (router.ex merge_pressure/2) and `git grep -c Pressure origin/main -- internal/cloudclient` returns NOTHING: the vitals never cross into the process that renders the verdict. And the number that proves the box is sick sits one JOIN away in the same database — deployments.site_id -> sites.barkpark_id -> barkparks — read by nothing (`barkpark_id` appears ZERO times in deploy_ledger.ex).

WHAT YOU BUILD. One slice, both sides of the wire, per charter D136 (server key + Go field + rendered column in the SAME PR) — split it and the vital lands unread, which is this epic's own bug.

(1) SERVER. ADD a new public `box_rates/3` at the END of cloud/lib/barkpark_cloud/deploy_ledger.ex. It takes a list of barkpark ids and a pinned half-open {from,to} window, runs ONE grouped query (never per-row: the router already paid for that N+1 once — see the dr-w4-s4 comment at router.ex ~:1890), joining deployments -> sites on site_id and grouping by sites.barkpark_id. YOU MUST NOT TOUCH census/3, rate/2, @classes, @labels or classify/2 — those regions belong to dr-w9-s6, which merges after you; editing them turns a clean merge into the #10014 conflict this epic already paid for once.
  Each box's node carries, INSEPARABLY (charter D107 + D152): terminal rate via the EXISTING rate/2 (numerator = failed, denominator = failed + live) so the sample, min_sample, refused flag and refusal reason ride inside it by construction; `absorption` = rate/2 over (deferred, all rows in window); `box_caused` = the box-caused share of the failure numerator; `sites` = the count of distinct sites contributing terminal rows in the window.
  `box_caused` is derived from classify/2's CLOSED class enum by a pure class -> agency map — NEVER a substring regex over failure_reason (charter D148: the substring numerator is MORE window-shoppable, is 52.6% recall, is 4.1% contaminated by BUILD-stage rows, and classify/2's own landed comment forbids the technique verbatim). The map must be exhaustive over the class list and must fail to AMBIGUOUS, never to SITE (failing to SITE would silently shrink the box numerator). ## Outcome
Avoid a redundant full required-CI execution after merge when successful merge-queue verification already covers exactly the same main commit, while retaining auditable exact-revision verification and a full-run fallback.

## Evidence
The same SHA a9555a7d643bfcd6430e3f0473d37267d9267a5f passed queue CI in https://github.com/titan-engine/titan/actions/runs/34026940070 (8m35s), then full push CI in https://github.com/titan-engine/titan/actions/runs/34027341007 (11m24s). The current workflow explicitly requires verifying the resulting main revision, and agents can treat the second execution as a further completion barrier. Exact-SHA queue evidence can satisfy the revision requirement if the reuse decision is reliable and documented.

## Scope
Implement a narrow main-push verification decision that recognizes successful trusted merge_group CI for the exact main SHA and complete required gate set. Update docs/workflow.md and concise AGENTS.md guidance to accept that evidence. Preserve full PR and merge-group CI. Keep main-only publication/deployment and any cache warming needed by the optimized CI explicit; do not silently remove their triggers or assume queue caches are reusable from main.

## Acceptance and verification
- [ ] Define and implement trusted evidence matching: same repository, exact full merged SHA, expected CI workflow identity/revision, merge_group event, completed successful result and all expected required gates. A matching tree, PR head, ancestor or different-SHA success is insufficient.
- [ ] A main push with qualifying evidence records a visible verification result linking the full SHA and successful queue run, without rerunning the full suite. Establish that the unchanged verification covers the same code and commands under both events before permitting reuse.
- [ ] Missing, pending, failed, cancelled, incomplete, ambiguous or inaccessible evidence selects full CI on main; never report success based on an unverified lookup. Workflow/API errors must not silently skip required verification.

- [ ] Preserve Browser demos deployment and document the default-branch cache warming strategy, since removing main builds may otherwise degrade PR/queue caches. Measure net latency/runner-minute benefit including necessary warming work.
- [ ] Cover exact-match reuse, mismatched SHA, incomplete/failed/missing evidence and lookup failure in focused tests. Demonstrate actual queue-to-main reuse and an actual fallback execution; record public evidence.
- [ ] Update completion/reporting instructions so agents link the exact merged SHA and accepted run, with no unnecessary wait for a second full run. Explicitly state that PR-head success alone remains insufficient.

No hard prerequisite; coordinate the required-gate contract, cache warming and shared ci.yml/docs edits with the parallel-CI work. ## Summary

Add an optional workflow that connects product requirements, technical planning, test-driven development, browser acceptance checks, and completion evidence. Separately offer optional managed installation of Free Claude Code (FCC), Ollama/local models, and RTK, followed by bounded background research/review workers.

All additions are independently opt-in. Existing installations must continue working without downloads, additional processes, model configuration, or workflow migration.

Background workers may use user-budgeted local, free-tier, subscription, or paid backends. They perform research and review, with the main agent retaining implementation responsibility.

The objective is measurable efficiency with reliable acceptance evidence. Background execution still consumes inference tokens; routing changes whose quota or compute supplies them. FCC explicitly supports multiple funding sources and warns that fallback can consume multiple providers' usage. [FCC documentation](https://github.com/alishahryar1/free-claude-code)

This is an umbrella issue for later execution. Deliver the phases as separate reviewable changes. Creating this issue does not start implementation, install tools, or authorize provider spending.

## Planning-audit evidence and dependencies

The planning audit inspected a checkout based on `2cfbe8b` with an ongoing TypeScript/BAML migration:

- Requirements/spec skills provide PRD-like planning and behavioral test-first guidance, but do not enforce an integrated workflow.
- Importing a Markdown specification does not populate task acceptance criteria. A completed task with no required criteria can currently become verified.
- Acceptance verification already supports CLI, HTTP, and optional Playwright checks with revision-bound evidence.
- Normal task-controller construction defaults to an advisory gate handler; the quality-gate engine is not automatically connected to ordinary spec sessions.
- Browser assertions inspect some values immediately, which can fail before asynchronous UI rendering settles.
- Existing review orchestration already supplies bounded concurrency, worktrees, cancellation, and structured findings. Usage remains unknown.

**Observed test result during the planning audit:** `npm run test:browser -- --project=chromium` exited **1 during TypeScript compilation**, before Playwright launched, on Windows `10.0.26200`, Node `v26.8.1`, npm `11.19.0`. This is evidence about the changing local checkout, not a confirmed defect in released Latchkit. No provider sessions were run. These observations must be rechecked against the execution checkout.

Reuse [usage accounting #32](https://github.com/willahealm/latchkit/issues/32) for worker accounting and budgets. Persistent services and recurring schedules remain with [scheduled workflows #25](https://github.com/willahealm/latchkit/issues/25), outside this issue.

Recheck merged interfaces before implementation. Resolve migration/build prerequisites separately rather than absorbing unrelated cleanup into this epic.

## Delivery phases

- [ ] Phase 1: Connect requirements and specifications to durable task state.
- [ ] Phase 2: Add TDD evidence and reliable acceptance execution.
- [ ] Phase 3: Reduce unnecessary context and implementation.
- [ ] Phase 4: Provide optional managed setup for FCC, Ollama, and RTK.
- [ ] Phase 5: Add budgeted background research/review workers.
- [ ] Complete shared interfaces, workbench integration, documentation, and acceptance validation.

### 1. Connect requirements and specifications to durable task state

Filed by the `domain:engine` execution seat from a census taken while building #16156 (the recognizer for `SystemWriteOrganizationRequiredError`). ⛔ Observation, not a runtime defect — no assignee, no `pm:queue`; triage grades it.

## The census

`packages/objectql/src`, non-test source. 18 classes extend `Error`; **17 carry a `readonly code` field**. Of those:

- **5 read from a named exported constant** — `DUPLICATE_RECORD_CODE`, `HOOK_TARGET_REBIND_ERROR_CODE`, `HOOK_UNSCOPED_DATA_ACCESS_CODE`, `MULTI_UPDATE_HOOK_KEY_DIVERGENCE_CODE`, `EMPTY_CREDENTIAL_REFUSAL_CODE`. Four are exported from the package barrel. A sixth joins them when #16156 lands.
- **1 uses a `typeof` annotation** — `nav-contribution-diagnostics.ts:93`.
- **11 still spell the code as an inline string literal:**

| file:line | code |
| --- | --- |
| `driver-connect-errors.ts:99` | `ERR_DRIVER_CONNECT` |
| `driver-connect-errors.ts:174` | `ERR_DATASOURCE_UNAVAILABLE` |
| `readonly-strict-errors.ts:161` | `ERR_READONLY_FIELD_REJECTED` |
| `registry.ts:1292` | `NAMESPACE_CONFLICT` |
| `registry.ts:1404` | `DUPLICATE_ARTIFACT_OBJECT_NAME` |
| `registry.ts:1463` | `OBJECT_OWNERSHIP_CONFLICT` |
| `summary-errors.ts:24` | `ERR_SUMMARY_RECOMPUTE` |
| `transaction-errors.ts:26` | `ERR_TRANSACTION_UNSUPPORTED` |
| `transaction-errors.ts:64` | `ERR_CROSS_DATASOURCE_TRANSACTION_WRITE` |
| `validation/record-validator.ts:136` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` |
| `tenancy/system-write-organization.ts` | `ERR_SYSTEM_WRITE_ORGANIZATION_REQUIRED` — **discharged by #16156** |

## Why this is worth a card rather than a shrug

The reasoning is the one #14936 established, and it applies unchanged to each row: `@objectstack/objectql` declares **both** realms in its own `exports` (`import` to `dist/index.mjs`, `require` to `dist/index.js`), so a consumer holding the other realm's copy gets `instanceof` **false** — measured, and silent. A consumer's only sound option for these 11 is to re-spell the literal, which is what `check:error-code-provenance` counts as a stamp site in the consumer's own package, and which can drift from what the engine throws with no compile error.

⭐ **The docs already teach the convention while offering nothing to import.** `content/docs/kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx:361` says, of `ReadonlyFieldRejectedError`:

> Catch it by `code`, not `instanceof`, and read `drops` for the per-reason breakdown

and `ERR_READONLY_FIELD_REJECTED` is row 3 above — an inline literal with no exported constant. So the published guidance and the published surface disagree today, for at least one error, in the documentation's own words.

Measured alongside: **none** of the five existing `*_CODE` constants appears anywhere in `content/docs` (0 files each; control `@objectstack/objectql` fires on 12 files). So no page enumerates these, and no page becomes stale by adding one.

## Suggested shape, for triage rather than a ruling

Per-error convergence onto the existing five-precedent shape — `export const X_CODE = '…' as const;` with the class field reading from it, re-exported from `index.ts`. ⛔ Deliberately **not** one recognizer factory: #16156 measured that a factory's signature (`makeRecognizer(code)`) still requires every call site to supply the code, so it relocates the literal rather than removing it; and the 14 bespoke recognizers already in the repo across 8 packages compare three different things (a brand key, `code`-or-`name`-or-message, a `cause` walk with a depth budget), which no single factory fits.

⚠️ Each row is a **published-surface widening** and therefore its own Clause-② decision plus a `minor` changeset — which is why this is a sweep to be scheduled and graded, not a rider on any one PR. Splitting it per file (or per error family) is probably right.

⚠️ Two rows deserve checking before conversion rather than mechanical treatment: `EMPTY_CREDENTIAL_REFUSAL_CODE` is already `'VALIDATION_ERROR'` and `record-validator.ts` uses `'VALIDATION_FAILED'` — two different spel

## Goal
Prove that GameYer can continue operational execution for 72 hours without requiring the Founder for routine technical/growth/ops work, while keeping all production-critical approvals Founder-gated.

## Operating gates
Every active task must be classified in its issue/thread as one of:

- `AUTO` — CEO/operator + executor may proceed through implementation, tests, PR and verification without Founder input.
- `FOUNDER_APPROVAL` — preparation may proceed automatically, but production deploy, DNS/nameserver/canonical changes, critical production decisions, budget increases/new paid SaaS, schema/real-data authenticity changes require Founder approval.
- `HUMAN_ACTION` — an external human action is inherently required (for example club-owner call/DM, ad-platform/SMM action, partnership response).

## 72h trial scope
Use the existing GitHub Issues ledger; do not build a new dashboard or OS.

During the trial, prioritize only:
1. P0 production/reliability blockers.
2. P1 September 10K real-unique-user traffic blockers: acquisition attribution, conversion leakage, supply quality on high-traffic club profiles.
3. P2 optimization/systemization only when it directly reduces Founder dependency.

## Detection inputs
Start with existing signals; do not build new infrastructure unless a real gap is proven:
- production health / GitHub CI / reliability signals
- PostHog real-traffic and attribution anomalies
- high-traffic incomplete club profiles using verified Supabase data only

## Execution contract
For an `AUTO` task:
problem → issue → acceptance criteria → implementation → tests → PR → independent verification → ready-for-approval/close.

Do not merge/deploy production unless the task explicitly falls outside Founder approval policy.

## Founder interrupt policy
Interrupt the Founder only for:
- production deploy / production merge when approval is required
- DNS, nameserver or canonical cutover
- budget increase or new paid SaaS
- Supabase schema/RLS/real-data authenticity decisions
- external human outreach/partnership/ad-platform action that cannot be done via connected tools
- severe blocker with no safe autonomous path

Do not interrupt for routine status updates.

## Success metrics after 72h
Record:
- tasks detected/created
- AUTO tasks completed to verified PR/result
- tasks blocked on Founder approval
- HUMAN_ACTION tasks prepared
- unnecessary Founder interrupts (target: 0)
- production-impacting changes made without approval (target: 0)

## Initial proof already completed
Issue #326 → PR #328 demonstrated autonomous cloud execution to verified PR: CI, Security, CodeQL and Responsive PASS; Vercel preview Ready; no merge/deploy.

## Safety
- no fake club data
- no takeover of SMM/content workflow
- no production deploy/DNS/nameserver changes without explicit Founder approval
- no big new dashboard/system until this trial proves the workflow

# Autonomous roadmap — stabilize core before scaling

The product is still in test mode with only part of the future manager/source pool connected. Immediate goal: remove software/state/routing/notification/dialogue defects and simplify the architecture so adding managers and traffic later does not multiply edge cases.

## Autopilot rules
- Prioritize real live conversations, handoffs and user requests over commit history.
- Confirm a defect from evidence where possible; otherwise add diagnostics/tests first.
- Safe reversible flow: branch → PR → required CI → merge only when green → verify production SHA, migrations, smoke/health and relevant live behavior.
- Do not make unrelated changes or edit other AnyTour projects from this roadmap.
- Do not silently enable off-shift managers, auto-assign conversations or add aggressive SLA escalation during test mode.
- Stop only for irreversible/high-risk decisions, missing secrets/credentials or unresolved product decisions.
- Prefer eliminating a class of bugs over adding another one-off guard when repeated live evidence points to the same architectural weakness.

# Milestone 1 — Dialogue Core Stabilization
Goal: make dirty input, repeated callbacks and natural text predictable before scaling traffic.

## 1A. Interaction safety
- [x] Existing live fixes for stale/concurrent date, month, forward wizard and edit-menu callbacks (#88/#102/#103/#109/#113).
- [x] Shared `InteractionGuard` foundation (#114): callback lock paths, duplicate-window checks, recent-burst checks and forward-step expectations are centralized without changing current behavior.
- [x] Structured callback suppression diagnostics foundation (#116): current guarded stale/duplicate/concurrent paths emit `interaction_guard / callback_suppressed` with reason, scope and canonical current/expected state where known; legacy text logs remain for compatibility.
- [x] Unknown callback fallback now uses the same structured suppression channel (#118): valid non-empty callbacks with no owning action emit reason `unknown_action`, scope `callback_controller`, payload and chat id while preserving the existing unhandled return behavior.
- [x] Move remaining callback-safety decisions behind the shared guard instead of adding per-action lock/debounce implementations. Known direct action-owned file-lock/timestamp paths are centralized through #637; future additions remain evidence-driven.
- [x] Add callback generation/version support so buttons rendered by an older interaction can be rejected generically after state changes. Final-check surface generation shipped in #633.
- [x] Extend structured suppression reason to obsolete generation once that path exists. `obsolete_generation` shipped in #633.
- [ ] Verify intentional back/edit/reopen actions are not incorrectly suppressed.

## 1B. Formal dialogue state machine
- [x] Canonical wizard states and forward/back/edit/reset transition rules are defined in `DialogueStateMachine` (#115), including conditional child-age flow and current AI missing-field behavior.
- [x] Forward callback status expectations in `InteractionGuard` now resolve through the canonical state machine instead of a duplicate status map (#115).
- [x] Observe-first diagnostics are live on guarded invalid forward/date/month callback attempts (#116), without introducing any new blocking semantics.
- [x] Explicit edit-flow state preservation foundation from live conversation 311 (#122): edit completion restores missing unchanged values from a snapshot while the edited value remains authoritative and reset clears the snapshot.

# Cron incident feed

**Do not close.** This issue is the notification surface for the auto-capture system wired up in `.github/workflows/log-cron-incident.yml`.

## How it works

- When any allowlisted cron workflow finishes with `conclusion: failure`, the listener appends a row to [`docs/cron-rebuild-failures.md`](../blob/main/docs/cron-rebuild-failures.md) with `Status: OPEN` and posts a comment on this issue with the failed run URL + a log-tail excerpt.
- When the next scheduled run of the same workflow succeeds, the listener flips the most-recent `OPEN` row to `RESOLVED (auto)` and posts a `✅` comment here.
- `BLOCKED`, `FLAKE`, and human-set `RESOLVED` rows are never touched by auto-resolve.

## Kill switches

Repo Settings → Variables:

| Variable                                   | Effect                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `CRON_INCIDENT_LOGGER_ENABLED=false`       | Disable everything (no capture, no auto-resolve, no comments). |
| `CRON_INCIDENT_AUTO_RESOLVE_ENABLED=false` | Keep failure capture; disable auto-resolve only.               |
| `CRON_INCIDENT_ISSUE_NUMBER`               | Issue number for this feed (set once during initial setup).    |

## What goes in a comment

Each failure comment shows:

- Workflow name (human-readable + kebab id)
- Run URL
- Status flag
- Link back to the ledger row
- Last 30 lines of the failed step's logs (in a collapsed `<details>` block)

Each auto-resolve comment shows:

- ✅ marker
- Workflow name + date
- The next-success run URL that triggered the flip

## Manual override

If a row gets auto-resolved but is actually still broken: edit the ledger row directly, change Status back to `OPEN` (or `BLOCKED`), and add context to the Root Cause column. The listener will re-flip it on the NEXT successful scheduled run if the underlying issue is fixed.

If a row should be left OPEN forever (waiting on external action): change Status to `BLOCKED` — auto-resolve skips that exact value.

## Links

- Ledger: [`docs/cron-rebuild-failures.md`](../blob/main/docs/cron-rebuild-failures.md)
- Listener: [`.github/workflows/log-cron-incident.yml`](../blob/main/.github/workflows/log-cron-incident.yml)
- Script: [`.github/scripts/log-cron-incident.mjs`](../blob/main/.github/scripts/log-cron-incident.mjs)

I want to use Stride as a 3D renderer for a cross platform project where the render window is integrated in the Avalonia UI.
Now both Stride and Avalonia, theoretically, would support this quite nicely but the issue appears with extending the Stride engine with a new rendering context (this means custom GameContext, GamePlatform, GameForm and GameWindow) which would be based on Avalonia native controls (rather then, for WinForms, based on System.Windows.Forms.Control). This is not a complicated extension as it would be, more or less, equal in implementation with the current WinForms. 

The problem is that when using the Stride nuget packages (or the old Xenko ones), consumers of these packages are not allowed to provide custom instances to these classes because:
- GamePlatforms are created in a static internal method and based on an enumeration so there is no way to provide a custom implementation here;
- GamePlatform itself is marked as internal which means we couldn't inherit from it;
- GameWindow contains internal abstract methods which cannot be overloaded;
- There are various other properties or methods marked as internal that might be required in such an implementation but I don't currently have an exhaustive list for those.

Is there a design limitation for why a consumer of these assemblies couldn't provide custom classes for rendering concepts? From what I can tell, the rest of the code is neatly abstracted and should work regardless of what implementations we might have there.

Exposing the internal members outside the assembly and introducing a new overridable factory pattern for creating game platforms would allow one to fully implement these concepts in separate assemblies without having the need to modify the internal Stride code.

Of course, this would not have any impact on the GameEngine itself but would allow Xenko to be embedded in any kind of contexts.

Lastly, if there are no design limitations with my proposals or other issues I may not notice now, would a merge request be accepted? I can pretty easily fork the repo and maintain my own implementation of it but I feel it would be much better, if there are no downsides, to have it contained in the main repository.
title: Support for Custom render context

**Priority:** Medium  ·  **Difficulty:** Medium  ·  **Area:** Soroban contract / reentrancy  ·  **Est. effort:** 5–8 h

## 📌 Problem

`onchain/contracts/stello_pay_contract/tests/test_reentrancy.rs` is the contract's double-claim and reentrancy suite. Most of it runs. One test does not:

```rust
#[test]
#[ignore = "requires escrow balance storage setup - covered by test_claim_payroll_state_updated_prevents_double_claim"]
fn test_claim_time_based_state_updated_prevents_double_claim() {
```

(`test_reentrancy.rs:221-223`)

The stated justification does not hold. `test_claim_payroll_state_updated_prevents_double_claim` exercises `claim_payroll`. The ignored test exercises `claim_time_based` — a **different entrypoint** with its own state transition. One does not cover the other; they only look similar.

The real blocker is the one named in the skip reason: the test needs escrow balance storage set up, and the helper to do it was never written. `fund_agreement_escrow` exists at `test_reentrancy.rs:49` for the payroll path, but the time-based path needs its own arrangement.

So the guarantee "a time-based claim cannot be drained twice" is currently unproven.

## 🧩 Requirements and context

- **Do not delete this test.** The deliverable is making it run.
- Write the missing escrow-balance setup as a reusable helper next to `fund_agreement_escrow`, not as inline setup — the milestone helper `setup_milestone_agreement` at `test_reentrancy.rs:287` is the pattern to follow.
- The test must fail for the right reason before it passes. Confirm that removing the state guard in the contract makes it red, and say so in the PR. A test that passes against broken code is worse than no test.
- `advance_time` at `test_reentrancy.rs:61` exists — time-based claims depend on ledger time, so use it rather than inventing a second mechanism.
- If, while writing this, you find the time-based path genuinely *is* vulnerable, stop and say so in the PR rather than adjusting the test to pass.

## 🎯 Design decision required

The suite currently proves double-claim resistance two different ways — via state update (`test_claim_payroll_state_updated_prevents_double_claim`) and via an explicit reentrancy guard (`test_reentrant_claim_payroll_rejected`, `test_guard_released_allows_subsequent_claim`). Decide which model applies to `claim_time_based`, and justify it: does the time-based path rely on the same guard, on its own state transition, or on both? Your test must assert the mechanism that actually protects it, not a generic "second call fails".

## 🛠️ Suggested execution

1. Remove the `#[ignore]` and run it. Record the actual failure.
2. Write the escrow-balance setup helper.
3. Get the test passing.
4. Prove it is a real test: temporarily break the guard in the contract, show it red, restore, show it green. Both outputs go in the PR.
5. Check whether `claim_milestone` and any other claim entrypoint have equivalent coverage; list any further gaps in the PR without fixing them here.

## ✅ Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `test_claim_time_based_state_updated_prevents_double_claim` runs and passes; no `#[ignore]` remains in `test_reentrancy.rs`.
- [ ] Escrow-balance setup is a named reusable helper, not inline.
- [ ] The PR shows the test failing against deliberately broken contract code, then passing against the real code.
- [ ] The PR states which protection mechanism the test asserts and why.
- [ ] `cargo test -p stello_pay_contract` passes with no ignored tests in this file.
- [ ] Any remaining claim-path coverage gaps are listed in the PR.

## 🚫 Out of scope

- The three `#[ignore]`d tests in `price_oracle` — tracked separately.
- Changing contract logic, unless you find a genuine vulnerability, in which case report it rather than patching quietly.
- Other test files.

## 🧪 Verification

```bash
cd onchain
cargo test -p stello_pay_contract --test test_reentrancy -- --include-ignored
grep -c "#\[ignore" contracts/stello_pay_contract/te
title: `test_claim_time_based_state_updated_prevents_double_claim` is `#[ignore]`d, leaving the time-based claim path without its own double-claim proof

## Scope and ownership

Owner: @xsmccc, following the **DiT stage → Runtime integration and compilation → CUDA graphs** assignment in #7075.

Enable and validate CUDA graph capture/replay for the MammothModa2 **DiT denoising transformer**. Start with MammothModa2-Preview text-to-image, CUDA, request-mode execution, one request and one output (`max_num_seqs=1`). Keep scheduler updates, random-latent initialization, AR execution/transfer, and VAE decode outside the captured region.

Requested tracking: parent **#7075**, formal assignee **@xsmccc**, milestone **[v0.30.0](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/milestone/10)**.

## Source findings and implementation plan

Source inspection on 2026-09-06 used main `715b8b8746db9b0e4a49456b2413df9a7432399f` and runtime-migration PR #7134 at `17c9bee50f442adbf8a167aa3db9f968fc463df6`. No GPU execution or performance measurement has been performed for this issue.

The current transformer path has capture blockers: [RoPE preparation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/blob/715b8b8746db9b0e4a49456b2413df9a7432399f/vllm_omni/diffusion/models/mammoth_moda2/rope_real.py#L158) reads CUDA mask lengths with `.tolist()`; the [FlashAttention-varlen path](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/blob/715b8b8746db9b0e4a49456b2413df9a7432399f/vllm_omni/diffusion/models/mammoth_moda2/mammothmoda2_dit_model.py#L334) uses `nonzero()` and `.item()`. Merely changing `enforce_eager` does not establish graph support.

Planned work:

- Agree on the runtime entry point and an explicit graph enable/disable contract. Graph-only execution must be distinguishable from `torch.compile`, and disabling graphs must preserve the reference path.
- Prepare capture-safe shape/mask/RoPE and attention metadata outside capture, coordinating with the existing metadata and attention owners rather than introducing a competing attention implementation.
- Warm up and capture the transformer with stable input/output storage. Refresh latents, timestep, conditioning and any request-varying metadata before replay.
- Handle spatial dimensions, conditioning lengths, mask layout, dtype/device and conditional/unconditional branches explicitly. Use bounded graph storage; do not assume equal tensor shapes imply equal conditioning or mask contents.
- Preserve the current sequential CFG semantics, including CFG disabled, empty unconditional conditioning and partial `cfg_range`. Avoid overwriting the conditional prediction when replaying the unconditional branch.
- Provide observable capture/replay/fallback behavior and documented eager fallback for unsupported configurations. Connect graph cleanup to the shared runner's existing `release_captured_graphs()` lifecycle where applicable.
- Add focused configuration/metadata tests, CUDA capture/replay parity coverage, and reproducible real-weight A/B evidence.

## Dependencies and coordination

- **Runtime foundation:** #7086 / Draft PR #7134, owned by @Levius-Fubuki. Target the shared diffusion request-mode interface, not a second long-lived wrapper around the legacy LLM runner. Real-weight E2E validation of that migration is still pending.
- **Compilation:** coordinate setup/capture boundaries with @Xenoryn. Compilation and DiT graphs remain separate PRs; do not imply combined support without testing.
- **Metadata / attention:** coordinate request-invariant metadata with @TonybotNi and attention changes with @MrlixiangWE (#7094).
- **CFG:** coordinate shapes and branch/output lifetime with @ShengleiFu (#7123); packed CFG is not a prerequisite for the initial sequential-CFG implementation.
- Reuse golden-test and benchmark inputs from #7090 / @cyq1017 and @quan-yi-ai where available. This feature remains responsible for its own paired measurements.

## Validation and hardware plan

Preferred primary target: **NVIDIA B300**, using a fixed BF16, no-cache, no-quantization/offload baseline if supported by the pinned runtime. Alternative: the course **RTX 5090 cluster**, initially assess
title: [Performance] MammothModa2 DiT: enable and validate CUDA graph capture/replay

> Telegram (ask questions / claim the issue here first): https://t.me/+DOylgFv1jyJlNzM0

**Labels:** `bug`, `frontend`

The memo field validates by character count, but Stellar `MEMO_TEXT` caps at 28 bytes, not 28 characters, so localized memos break at submit time.

`RemittanceForm` sets `maxLength=28` and rejects `memo.length > 28`. A multibyte UTF-8 memo, accented Spanish or Tagalog, an emoji, can pass the 28-character check and still blow past 28 bytes. When that happens the transaction fails at encode/submit, and it fails for exactly the es/tl users this app is built for. The error shows up late, at submission, instead of during input validation where it belongs.

**What the fix has to hold to**
- Measure UTF-8 byte length: `new TextEncoder().encode(memo).length <= 28`.
- The textarea cap and character counter reflect bytes, or drop the `maxLength` cap in favor of byte-aware validation.
- Pure-ASCII memos up to 28 bytes still pass, unchanged.
- Rejection shows a clear user-facing message.

**Done when**
- [ ] Memo validation uses UTF-8 byte length (`new TextEncoder().encode(memo).length <= 28`).
- [ ] The textarea limit and counter reflect bytes, or the `maxLength` cap is replaced by byte-aware validation.
- [ ] A memo that's under 28 characters but over 28 bytes gets rejected with a clear message.
- [ ] Pure-ASCII memos up to 28 bytes still pass.
- [ ] Unit test covers the multibyte-over-28-bytes rejection and the ASCII pass; lint/format green, CI passes.

**Where to start**
Update validation in `frontend/src/app/components/remittance/RemittanceForm.tsx` and add a multibyte case to the component test. Out of scope: backend memo construction and submission. Small frontend fix, 1-2 days.
title: [Frontend] Remittance memo is validated by character count instead of Stellar 28-byte limit

初回監査は `2c0d0c4e83b74cc7edabd7c702bf3cae22773f27` を基準としていたが、その直後に PR #1099 が merge commit `b96702dd72bff3a8a789e62aa899222d75db3c02` として main へ入ったため再監査した。

**旧class契約を current vNext の実行経路・検証経路・測定経路から完全に外し、starting kit + equipment / medium / Rune / Core / Support を唯一の current-run ownership にする。**
