body_excerpt:
Raised on #2163 during review and never filed. Both halves are still present on `origin/main`.

## 1. Five script purposes have no required-redeemer check in any era

`UtxoValidateRequiredRedeemers` (`ledger/common/script/redeemers.go:73-77`) builds `spendIndexes` from `redeemers.Indexes(lcommon.RedeemerTagSpend)` alone, and the loop below it reports `MissingRedeemerForScriptError` only with `Tag: lcommon.RedeemerTagSpend`.

`cardano-ledger` checks the whole set. `hasExactSetOfRedeemers` compares the transaction's redeemer pointers against those derived from every purpose — mint, cert, reward, vote and propose as well as spend. A Plutus minting policy carrying no mint redeemer is accepted here, and the policy script is never executed.

The direction is under-requiring, so this does not reject anything the chain accepts. It does mean a validating node skips script execution the reference performs, which is the half that matters for anything relying on this package to validate rather than to follow.

#2147 closed the reference-script spend case only; the remaining purposes were left to a follow-up that was never opened.

## 2. The spend walk excludes Dijkstra sub-transaction inputs

The loop iterates `SortInputs(tx.Inputs())` (`redeemers.go:85`), which does not include sub-transaction inputs. The available-script view it checks against does: `availableScripts` folds `lcommon.SubTransactionWitnessSetsFromTransaction(tx)` (`ledger/common/script/needed.go:294`).

So a script-address input inside a Dijkstra sub-transaction contributes its script to `view.Available` but is never walked, and no redeemer is ever required for it.

## Acceptance criteria

- The required-redeemer check derives its expected set from every script purpose the transaction carries, not spend alone, matching `hasExactSetOfRedeemers`.
- The spend walk covers Dijkstra sub-transaction inputs, so the set it validates and the set `availableScripts` builds come from the same inputs.
- A test per purpose asserts a Plutus script of that purpose without its redeemer is rejected, and a sub-transaction script input without a redeemer is rejected. Each must fail without the change.
title: ledger: the required-redeemer check covers only the spend purpose, and skips Dijkstra sub-transaction inputs

body_excerpt:
`sortedConwayWithdrawalAddresses` (`ledger/eras/conway.go:874`) orders withdrawals by raw address bytes:

```go
slices.SortFunc(ret, func(a, b *lcommon.Address) int {
    aBytes, aErr := a.Bytes()
    bBytes, bErr := b.Bytes()
    ...
    return bytes.Compare(aBytes, bBytes)
})
```

A reward address' first byte carries its credential type, so key-hash credentials (`0xe0`) sort before script credentials (`0xf0`). `cardano-ledger` orders by `Credential`, whose derived `Ord` places `ScriptHashObj` before `KeyHashObj` (`libs/cardano-ledger-core/src/Cardano/Ledger/Credential.hs:98-101`).

The two orders differ for any transaction whose withdrawals include **both** a key credential and a script credential. Since this ordering determines the `Rewarding` redeemer index, a script in such a transaction is evaluated against the wrong redeemer, or a redeemer index resolves to the wrong withdrawal.

This is the same defect gouroboros carried as **#2187**, fixed there by **#2202** (`fix(ledger): order withdrawals by credential`, merged and currently unreleased above `v0.202.9`). The dingo-side copy was not updated with it.

Found while implementing gouroboros #2250 (PR #2259); not fixed there because it is a different repository.

## Acceptance criteria

- Conway withdrawal ordering matches `Credential`'s derived `Ord` — script credentials before key credentials — rather than raw address bytes.
- A test covers a transaction carrying both a key-credential and a script-credential withdrawal and asserts the resulting `Rewarding` redeemer indices, failing without the change.
- Check whether dingo carries the same ordering anywhere else before fixing only this call site.
title: ledger/eras: Conway withdrawal ordering sorts by address bytes, not by Credential

body_excerpt:
Owner, playtesting Miranda 2026-07-31:

> *"the map is kind of boring... no door or enclosed places... we should have some more here? Something to discover, some loot reward for venturing deep."*
> *"we have so much more fancy rescue ship scenes here that were developed after these original landing sites... we should cherry pick stuff from those like lockable doors"*
> *"Do we really need the square border around the area … it seems artificial on a Moon"*
> *"I have never seen the landing site area expand yet... we should test it."*
> *"There should be huts . i.e lockable spaces there not just U shapes."*
> *"there could be an overrun illegal space there that was abandoned ... some story that tells the player about the game universe"*
> *"but the rectangular fence spoils the site feeling... what is it supposed to be in the game world... if our space has limits for some technical reasons then let's not advertise it, more like hide that fact."*

## The audit (Lab 43, deterministic, no browser)

Miranda offers **3** sites. What each one actually generates into a 78 x 64 du field:

| site | name | scheme | wall segments | landmarks | % of field |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | The Wild Plain | THE MONOLITH MAZE | **12** | 1 | 12% |
| 1 | The Shadowed Rille | THE DEEP RUINS | 20 | 1 | 23% |
| 2 | The Ridge Camp | THE DEEP RUINS | 25 | 1 | 21% |

The canon ground — the authored maze, the one with the story on it — is the **thinnest ground on the moon**. Every seeded site beats it.

`DeckPlan`'s entire vocabulary is walls / doors / consoles / labels / backdrops / droids. **There is no prop type**, so there are no rocks, no debris, no scatter — a surface is line segments and text, and nothing else.

### The ground can never grow — anywhere

| body | sites | secret lab (1-in-40) | expedition regions | can the ground expand? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Miranda | 3 | no | no | **NEVER** |
| Luna | 4 | no | no | **NEVER** |
| Phobos | 4 | no | no | **NEVER** |
| Europa | 2 | no | no | **NEVER** |
| Titan | 2 | no | no | **NEVER** |

`DeckPlan.AppendRegion` — "the world grows, nobody teleports" — is reachable on **two of the three `expedition-site-*` rocks** and nowhere else in the solar system. That is why the owner has never seen a landing site expand: on every real moon, it cannot happen.

### The fence is literally spaceship

`MoonSurface.cs:218-223` builds five rim walls flagged `IsHull: true` — the same ink the ship's pressure hull is drawn in — as an axis-aligned rectangle. The comment calls it "a fenced rim of hull lines."

And it is not only the rim: on The Ridge Camp, **16 of 25** generated segments are `IsHull` too. Most lines on a moon are currently drawn as spaceship.

## Correction to the premise (matters for what we port)

Forced doors, appended rooms and concealed doors are **already a landing-site feature** — `ExpeditionRegions` and `SecretLab`. **Wrecks do not have them**; #537 is OPEN and unimplemented and proposes bringing that idea *to* hulls. So "cherry-pick doors from the wrecks" is backwards. The door machinery is already ours — it is merely gated behind body ids no moon can have.

What the wrecks genuinely have that landing sites lack:

1. **An A\* walkability audit in CI.** `DeckReachability` takes `(spawn, targets, walls, radius, bounds)` — no ship types at all. Wreck layouts are tested for *every compartment can be entered*, *doorways are wider than the captain*, *no two stations share a doorstep*, and *damage may never seal the spine*. **Surfaces have none of this.** Highest-value import in the comparison, and it costs nothing: a moon's walls are already `SurfaceCollision.Segment`.
2. **Cause-varies-the-geometry.** One enum, one `switch`, damage drawn *into* the base geometry, with an invariant pinned by A\* for every enum value (`WreckLayout.DamageWalls`). Landing sites have no per-site "what happened here" identity at all.
3. **`ShipLayout.Room`** — a real compartment record carrying its own door, already gene
title: 🏚 Landing sites got left behind: no rooms, no doors, a spaceship-hull fence — and ground that can never grow

Turn real Spark-X2.5 runs into reproducible, discussable edge-agent use cases.

For this challenge, obtain XHToken/Spark-X2.5-4B or Spark-X2.5-1.7B from Hugging Face (or a mirror such as ModelScope), conduct a real inference, agentic, coding, long-context, multilingual, quantization, or training experiment, and publish the complete use case in the corresponding model's Hugging Face Discussions. After publishing it, reply to this event's GitHub Issue with the Discussion link to enter.

- Event page (GitHub Issues): https://github.com/XHToken/Spark-X2.5/issues
- Hugging Face model collection: https://huggingface.co/collections/XHToken/spark-x25
- Spark-X2.5-4B: https://huggingface.co/XHToken/Spark-X2.5-4B

## Schedule

- Submissions open: September 1, 2026
- Challenge period: September 1–6, 2026
- Submission deadline: September 6, 2026, 24:00 Beijing Time (UTC+8)
- Judging and award distribution: September 7–13, 2026

## Challenge Tracks

Choose one track or combine several:

- Official Quick Start reproduction: deploy with vLLM / SGLang / llama.cpp, run locally with Ollama / LM Studio, and test structured output and tool parsing (`--tool-call-parser spark25`)
- Agentic workflows: integrate with harnesses such as Codex, Claude Code, OpenClaw, or Hermes to complete multi-step tool use, planning, and automation tasks
- Coding: complete real repository-level fixes, programming contest / online judge tasks, or end-to-end coding-agent runs
- Long context: use the native 1M context window for long-document Q&A, codebase understanding, or long-range retrieval
- Multilingual: test understanding, generation, or translation across 200+ languages, or demonstrate a real multilingual business scenario
- Edge efficiency and hardware adaptation: 4B/1.7B quantization (GGUF), throughput, TTFT/TPOT, VRAM/RAM use, or adaptation to NVIDIA / Ascend / Hygon / HOUMO.AI and other hardware
- Instruction following and reasoning: evaluate complex instructions, format compliance, mathematics, or reasoning tasks with real tests
- Safety boundaries: examine high-risk actions, unauthorized tool calls, ambiguity detection, confirmation steps, and safe refusal
- Data and training: use legally obtained data, mine hard examples, or run SFT/RL with LLaMA-Factory and report before-and-after comparisons
- Comparative evaluation: compare Spark-X2.5 with larger models, rule-based systems, or other open models of a similar size under the same methodology

## How to Submit

1. Spark-X2.5 is licensed under Apache 2.0 and requires no additional usage agreement. Follow the repository's CODE_OF_CONDUCT and SECURITY policies.
2. Install and sign in with the official Hugging Face CLI:

       pip install -U huggingface_hub
       hf auth login

3. Download and record a pinned revision:

       hf download XHToken/Spark-X2.5-4B --revision <commit-sha>

   Participants in Mainland China may use ModelScope / Modelers / SCNet / SourceFind mirrors. State the source and revision used.

4. Complete a real experiment and retain publishable run logs, inputs, raw outputs, environment details, and screenshots.
5. Create a public post in the Discussions section for the model you actually used:

   - Spark-X2.5-1.7B: https://huggingface.co/XHToken/Spark-X2.5-1.7B/discussions

       [HER Hack-Astron #5] <use-case title>

6. Reply to this event's GitHub Issue with the direct link to your Discussion post. This completes your sub

## Anlass
Der Live-Check am 20.08.2026 zeigt für Baden-Württemberg auf `/laender/baden-wuerttemberg/mandat-und-praxis` nur die verifizierte Mandatsbasis. Die Seite sagt selbst: `vollständige Commitment-Zerlegung wird fortlaufend ergänzt`.

Der kanonische WÖk-Bestand bestätigt die Fachlücke:
- `/WOEK/WOEK-LAENDER-DAILY/BASELINE/baden-wuerttemberg/BASELINE-2026-08-18.md`: offene Aufgabe `Koalitionsvertrag vollständig in CoalitionCommitments zerlegen`.
- `/WOEK/WOEK-LAENDER-DAILY/CONTROL/LAENDER-COVERAGE-AND-HANDOFF-FINAL-2026-08-18.md`: Koalitionsvertrag 2026-2031 nur `als Mandatsbasis vorgesehen`.
- `/WOEK/WOEK-LAENDER-DAILY/FACHREVIEW/baden-wuerttemberg/INITIAL-IMPACT-CASES-2026-08-18.md`: fünf initiale Regierungswirkungsfälle, aber keine vollständige Koalitionsvertrags-Wirkungsanalyse.

Aktuelle Production ist nicht stale: `dpl_6CefNPFgRYrVXzYTFZeEezsArEX2`, READY/production, Git SHA `fb07fab799a34bbda0e2efc03f90066945c95802`, entsprechend aktuellem main-Basisstand von PR #235. Das BW-Problem ist daher nach aktuellem Befund keine bloße falsche Vercel-Promotion, sondern eine echte fachliche/Publikations-Coverage-Lücke - vorbehaltlich historischem Restore-Fund.

## Rollen
Human out of loop. **CodeX ist technischer Ausführungs- und Deployment-Aktor.** WÖk/Controller liefert Fachbestand, Priorität, Audit und exact-commit Freigabe. CodeX implementiert, testet, merged und deployt bis Production, sobald die Gates grün sind. Kein zusätzliches Human-Gate.

## P0-1 Baden-Württemberg: Restore-first
Vor Neuanalyse Git-Historie, Branches und kanonischen `/WOEK`-Bestand nach einer früher bereits fachlich freigegebenen Koalitionsvertragsanalyse durchsuchen. Wenn vorhanden: exakt/provenienzgebunden wiederherstellen. Keine Neufassung, die einen vorhandenen historischen Fachstand still ersetzt.

Wenn keine vollständige freigegebene Analyse existiert, ist die Fachlücke ausdrücklich zu schließen: amtlichen Koalitionsvertrag 2026-2031 vollständig sichern/versionieren, Commitments mit Source Locator extrahieren und dem WÖk-Fachreview zuführen. CodeX erzeugt **keine** Wirkungsurteile selbst.

## P0-2 Vollständigkeitsaudit alle 16 Länder
Für jedes Land getrennt inventarisieren und öffentlich korrekt abbilden:
- `election_cycle_state` und `government_lifecycle_state` - strikt getrennte Achsen,
- ElectionDocuments/Wahlprogramme und freigegebene Programmanalysen,
- Koalitions-/Mandatsdokumente und Coalition-/MandateCommitments,
- GovernmentActions und WÖkImpactCases,
- AnalysisVersions/RecommendationVersions,
- EvidenceEvents/RealityChecks,
- Quellen, Kompetenz, höherrangiges Recht/Schutzgrenzen,
- öffentliche Routen, Navigation, Overview-Projektion und Detailakten.

Fehlende Fachlayer nicht technisch erfinden. Vorhandenen Fachbestand niemals verkürzen oder verstecken.

## P0-3 Übersicht: Wirkungspotenzial klar sichtbar
Portalweit auf Wahlprogramm-, Koalitions-/Mandats-, Regierungs-, Parlament-, EU- und Länderübersichten muss die WÖk-Einordnung vor Prozessmetadaten verständlich sichtbar sein. Soweit fachlich freigegeben mindestens:
- qualitativer Wirkungspotenzialbefund,
- stärkste positive Potenziale,
- wichtigste materielle Risiken/Zielkonflikte,
- Evidenz/Unsicherheit getrennt von Richtung,
- Richtungsprofil nur für redaktionell/fachlich geprüfte Pfade,
- Nichtkompensation/Schutzgrenzen,
- **alle** freigegebenen Key Findings - keine `slice(0,2)`-Verkürzung,
- keine Partei-/Regierungs-Gesamtnote oder künstliche Saldierung.

Detailseiten müssen die vollständige freigegebene Fachakte und Quellen enthalten, nicht nur Mandats-/Fakten-Teaser.

## P0-4 Golden-State / kein Datenverlust durch Release
Jeder Kandidat gegen letzten akzeptierten Production-Stand **und** kanonischen `/WOEK`-Fachbestand prüfen:
- vorhandene Routen/Navigation,
- Fachakten/Analyseachsen,
- `required_content_paths` vs. `rendered_content_paths`, Pflichtbestand `unrendered_content_paths=[]`,
- Wirkungspotenzial/Key Findings/Wirkpfade/Evidenz,
- Kompetenz/Higher Law/Schutzgrenzen,
- Rec
title: P0: Länder-Fachvollständigkeit - Mandate, Wirkungspotenzial und Golden-State für alle 16 Länder

## 🎉 Add`Smart Heading` Recognition Feature For Word Document

Starting from v1.5.5, LightRAG's built-in DOCX parser introduces the **Smart Heading** feature -- enabling better section-based chunking even for poorly formatted DOCX documents.

Many DOCX documents have visually clear section structures but lack properly configured Word outline levels, or retain incorrect heading styles from editing, copying, and concatenation processes. In the past, these issues could cause section titles to be treated as body text, or regular text to be misidentified as headings, resulting in chunking boundaries that deviate from the document's true semantic sections. For P chunking strategies that rely on heading structures, this creates fragmented context or mixed content from different sections, affecting subsequent indexing and retrieval.

**Smart Heading** targets such poorly formatted but semantically clear documents, restoring their true heading structures as much as possible:

1. **Recover Missing Section Titles**: Identify content that visually appears as titles but lacks properly configured outline levels, reducing loss of section structures.
2. **Reduce False Positives of Body Text as Headings**: Restore regular body text, complete clauses, captions, dates, and version notes that incorrectly carry heading styles back to body text, avoiding meaningless chunking boundaries.
3. **Improve Inconsistent Heading Hierarchies**: Reduce issues such as inconsistent sibling heading levels, inverted parent-child hierarchies, and skipped levels, making section structures more coherent.
4. **Distinguish Multiple Contents in Merged Documents**: Identify main titles and document boundaries of each piece of content, preventing section level interference between different documents.
5. **Reduce Noise from Long Tables of Contents**: Compress excessively long table of contents, minimizing the interference of duplicate information on indexing and retrieval.

By providing more reliable section structures for subsequent chunking, Smart Heading helps maintain semantic associations between titles and their corresponding body text, making chunking results align better with the document's original content organization.

Opt-in per project. An absent block changes nothing, byte for byte, exactly like `reward.reviewBudget`.

## Problem

Wasting a maintainer's attention costs the submitter nothing. Merge-gated scoring already means low-value work is never paid, but it is still reviewed, and review is the one input that does not scale. #261 documents the local version: coverage farming, one-helper PR swarms, copied test bodies. The scoring contract cannot fix this because the cost lands before scoring does. Every analog that paid for submissions without pricing attention (OnlyDust, Code4rena, the curl bounty) was closed by volume, not by tooling.

## Proposal

A project may set a price a contributor pays to have a pull request reviewed under Slop. The fee goes directly to the project's published receiving address. If the PR is merged, the fee is refunded at cycle settlement on top of whatever the recipient's allocation is. If it is not merged, the project keeps it as compensation for the review it did.

The sponsor sets whether it is on, the amount, and the mode. Different projects can set different prices, and later different prices for different kinds of PR.

### Manifest sketch

```json
"reward": {
  "postage": {
    "mode": "required",
    "currency": "USDC",
    "chain": "solana",
    "amountMinor": "5000000",
    "refund": "on-merge-at-settlement",
    "effectiveAt": "2026-11-01T00:00:00.000Z",
    "overrides": [
      { "match": { "label": "documentation" }, "amountMinor": "1000000" }
    ]
  }
}
```

v1 is one flat amount per project and `required` mode only. `mode` is an enum so a softer `priority` mode (unpaid PRs still score, paid PRs are surfaced first to reviewers) can be added later without a breaking change, but v1 accepts only `required`. Priority needs a reviewer-facing queue Slop does not own, and it delays the attention cost instead of pricing it. Keeping the enum also leaves a fallback if the legal read below says a hard gate is a problem. Per-label or per-path overrides are a follow-on.

### Flow

1. The contributor's run reaches intake. For a project with postage on, intake answers `402` with the project's receiving address, the amount, and a binding memo (project id, actor node id, PR identity). This is the x402 shape.
2. The client pays directly from the contributor's wallet to the project address. Slop is not in the transfer. The receipt binds the transaction signature.
3. Slop's existing read-only verifier confirms exact recipient, exact amount, memo, success, and finality. Same code path as `verified-on-chain` funding records. Network errors fail closed.
4. Scoring: in `required` mode a merged PR with no verified postage is `held`, not scored. Verified postage never changes score, rank, reward share, or payment. This is the same rule Score v2 already applies to token evidence.
5. Cycle close: the proposal carries a `lines.postageRefund` entry per merged PR next to `lines.sharedPool` and `lines.reviewBudget`. The creator signs one transfer per recipient for the combined total, the way #322 already handles two lines. The dust floor is evaluated on the combined total. Postage on unmerged PRs is not a cycle line at all; it already belongs to the project.

### Where the money sits

Nowhere new. Payer to project, directly, exactly like `funding.mode: direct-noncustodial`. Slop never receives, holds, or refunds a fee.

No escrow. An escrow contract has to be told "this PR merged" before it releases, and whoever holds that key is the admin position this project refuses to have. It is also the custody exposure the design was built to avoid. The refund is instead a public settlement obligation, enforced the same way every payout is enforced: it is on the record in the proposal, verified fail-closed on chain, and shows as unpaid if the project does not send it.

### Guardrails

- Postage may only be enabled on a pool that is `committed` and payment-enabled. A project must not collect fees while its refund path is unfunded. Same a

## Destination

A buildable spec plus ADRs for Radar's digest pipeline — every open architectural
decision locked and written down, so a build session can execute without further
design. No production code is written while working this map.

## Notes

**Domain.** Radar (`apps/radar`, served at `/radar`) publishes an architectural
digest. Today it is produced by a Claude cloud scheduled task — *"Architecture
Digest — weekday morning"*, 07:00 weekdays, Opus 5, auto-approve — which runs a
232-line Python fetcher over ~20 RSS/Atom sources plus one scraper, curates ~13
items from ~66 candidates against a fixed persona, and hand-writes a ~476-line
self-contained HTML artifact. The rebuild keeps the agent for curation and
writing, and makes everything around it deterministic and stored.

**The motivation.** The irreducible agent work is small — pick the leads, write a
summary and a "why this matters" line. Almost everything else the session spends
tokens on is mechanical: re-reading the runbook, re-writing the fetcher to disk,
reading 66 candidate items, and emitting HTML by hand every weekday.

**Settled while charting** — constraints, not tickets:

- Orchestration moves to a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow. The Claude cloud
  scheduled task retires.
- Agent usage stays on the Claude **subscription** via
  `secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` — already configured, see
  `.github/workflows/claude.yml:53` — not metered API billing.
- `/radar` is **public read, private write** — and the private write surface is
  **GitHub**, not the web app. A deep-dive request or a promotion from the backlog
  is a `workflow_dispatch` with a URL; GitHub already authenticates Jamie. The app
  has no sign-in, no private role and no private pages. *(Redrawn 2026-09-06.)*
- Articles sit on a **depth ladder**: `candidate` (raw feed metadata) → `brief`
  (agent-written summary + "why this matters", i.e. what a digest entry is today)
  → `deep` (a requested full analysis). Everything fetched is stored forever; an
  article gets a public page from `brief` upward, and raw candidates stay a
  private backlog Jamie can promote from — by URL, via the workflow, with cuts
  listed in the run's job summary. There is no backlog UI in the first build.
  *(Redrawn 2026-09-06.)*
- **Source text is not retained.** The database holds relations; a source is
  identified by its URL. Each writing attempt records a fingerprint of what it
  was shown. If an author takes an article down, so be it. *(Added 2026-09-06,
  revising ADR-0017.)*
- **The first build is the original problem, solved, and no more.** Scheduled
  Action, fetch → dedupe → enrich → triage → write → publish, Neon, `/radar`,
  dated issues, article pages, archive, sitemap. Everything the model supports
  but the first build does not need is listed under *Out of scope* with a note
  that it is deferred, not rejected. *(Redrawn 2026-09-06, after a step back:
  the "settled while charting" constraints had each grown a subsystem.)*
- The daily digest survives as the **executive summary**, linking out to article
  pages rather than containing everything.
- Redesigning Radar's visual identity is **in** scope, not just porting the
  existing blueprint-navy identity.

**Skills every session should consult**: `/grilling` and `/domain-modeling` by
default; `/research` for AFK tickets; `/prototype` for UI and flow questions;
`/codebase-design` when placing a seam.

**Standing preferences**: ADRs per `CLAUDE.md`, numbered from `0017`, using
`docs/adr/0000-template.md`. No `CONTEXT.md` exists yet — create it when the
first term is resolved. Constraints that bite: ADR 0006 (static rendering by
default), the microfrontends rules in `CLAUDE.md`, and no `@/*` imports inside
`packages/ui`.

## Decisions so far

<!-- one line per closed ticket: gist plus link -->

- [Research: Claude on the subscription from a scheduled GitHub Action](https://github.com/jeasmith/ithilien/issues/86)
  — Viable, and no API billing. Anthropic explic

# Kingdom Network Control Room

This issue is the live coordination hub for all parallel ChatGPT workstreams on Kingdom Network.

## Source of truth
- Master roadmap: `docs/KINGDOM_NETWORK_BUILD_CHECKLIST.md`
- Repository: `BroMarcus/church-app`
- Deployment policy: HOLD all independent deployments until Marcus approves one combined deployment.
- Active work should use dedicated workstream branches rather than writing directly to `main` whenever practical.

## Required worker protocol
Before doing Kingdom Network work, every chat/workstream must:
1. Read the current repository state.
2. Read `docs/KINGDOM_NETWORK_BUILD_CHECKLIST.md`.
3. Read this Control Room issue and latest comments.
4. Check whether another workstream has already claimed the same feature, route, component, database object, RLS policy, migration, or related dependency.
5. If there is meaningful overlap, do not independently modify it. Pick another unclaimed priority or explicitly coordinate the dependency.
6. Post a `CLAIMED` update before starting significant work.
7. Work from the master checklist priority order unless Marcus gives a direct override.
8. Verify behavior before declaring completion; written code alone is not complete.
9. Post a final status as `VERIFIED`, `BLOCKED — MARCUS`, `BLOCKED — TECHNICAL`, or `READY FOR COMBINED DEPLOYMENT`.
10. If blocked on Marcus but other safe work exists, record the blocker and continue to the next unclaimed priority.
11. Do not deploy independently.
12. Do not blindly merge competing changes.
13. New product ideas must be added to the shared roadmap rather than living only inside one chat.

## Standard status format
### CLAIMED
- Workstream/chat:
- Task:
- Routes/features:
- Files/components likely affected:
- Supabase tables/functions/RLS/migrations affected:
- Dependencies:
- Deployment: HOLD

### Completion
- Status: VERIFIED / BLOCKED — MARCUS / BLOCKED — TECHNICAL / READY FOR COMBINED DEPLOYMENT
- What changed:
- What was tested:
- Remaining risk/blocker:
- Files/database objects touched:
- Deployment: HOLD unless Marcus explicitly approves combined deployment

## Status meanings
- `CLAIMED` — actively being worked
- `DONE — NEEDS VERIFICATION` — implementation exists but has not been proven end-to-end
- `VERIFIED` — behavior has been tested and confirmed
- `BLOCKED — MARCUS` — needs a decision, approval, credential, content, or other user input
- `BLOCKED — TECHNICAL` — genuine technical blocker after reasonable alternate approaches
- `READY FOR COMBINED DEPLOYMENT` — verified and queued for integration
- `DEPLOYED` — included in an explicitly approved combined deployment

## Conflict checks
Check overlap at all four levels before work begins:
1. Route/page
2. Component/service
3. Database table/function/RLS policy
4. Migration/schema change

## Active workstream branches
- Finance / Reporting / Multi-Church Licensing: `workstream/finance-reporting-licensing`

## Active work summary
- Finance / Reporting / Multi-Church Licensing: CLAIMED. Other workers should avoid `finance_*`, legacy `church_finance_*`, finance role/permission helpers, finance RLS, and overlapping `church_roles` / `church_role_assignments` changes unless coordinated.

- Pilot hardening reconciliation / PR #23: CLAIMED; explicitly excludes finance/role/RLS overlap.
- Pre-Pro Pilot Hardening / PR #24: branch-level VERIFIED but not yet ready for combined deployment; explicitly avoids finance/role/RLS overlap.

- multi-church sellable/licensed product; church-specific fiscal year, giving categories, group structure, classes, campaigns, and reporting settings must be configuration rather than code changes

# 🤖 Claude Coordination Board

Live cross-session comms for parallel Claude sessions. **Standing/pinned, never closed.**

## ⚠️ POST WITH `add_issue_comment`. `issue_write method=update` DESTROYS THIS BODY.

`issue_write method=update` is the **edit-the-issue** tool, not the comment tool. The comment tool is **`add_issue_comment`**.

**Why it keeps recurring, and why a careful reader still hits it:**

- **The MCP's return value is indistinguishable from a successful comment.** Both return an id and a URL. Nothing errors, nothing warns — the session moves on believing it posted, and the damage is found later by someone else. *(This is exactly how the 2026-08-29 clobber went unnoticed until the next read.)*
- **Instructions that say "post a comment" without naming the tool leave the choice to inference**, and `issue_write` is the plausible-looking guess for "write to an issue".
- **Nothing enforces it.** `.claude/settings.json` hooks are inert on Claude Code on the web (`BL-20260820-PROJECT-HOOKS-INERT-ON-WEB`), so this is self-discipline.

**Recorded clobbers (8):** 2026-07-30 · 2026-08-09 · 2026-08-15 · 2026-08-19 · 2026-08-20 08:52Z · 2026-08-20 08:56Z (four minutes apart, two sessions neither of which could see the other) · 2026-08-23 18:13Z · **2026-08-29 17:59Z (this one)**.

**If you clobber it anyway:** say so on the board immediately, restore from `docs/claude/coordination-board.md`, and **label the result a reconstruction** — do not pass a rebuild off as the original. When restoring, note that **GitHub strips `<…>` as HTML even inside code fences**, so use `{braces}` in the body.

## Why this board exists

Multiple Claude sessions run in parallel and **still collide** even with the merge queue. `docs/claude/session-board.json` + branch protection serialize only the *one merge slot*; they do nothing to stop two sessions editing the same file, redoing the same workstream blind to each other, or blocking on a question only another live session can answer. A committed file propagates only through a merge + pull — too late. **An issue's comments are visible to every session immediately.** That is the board.

|---|---|---|
| Purpose | Live comms — updates, questions, heads-ups | Merge serialization |
| Gated on merging? | **No** — instant, API-visible | Yes — a committed file |
| When | Continuously, during work | Session start, and around each merge |

Using the board is **MANDATORY for every session**, including every review sub-session (`/health-review`, `/performance-review`, `/ml-review`, `/system-review`).

# Cron incident feed

**Do not close.** This issue is the notification surface for the auto-capture system wired up in `.github/workflows/log-cron-incident.yml`.

## How it works

- When any allowlisted cron workflow finishes with `conclusion: failure`, the listener appends a row to [`docs/cron-rebuild-failures.md`](../blob/main/docs/cron-rebuild-failures.md) with `Status: OPEN` and posts a comment on this issue with the failed run URL + a log-tail excerpt.
- When the next scheduled run of the same workflow succeeds, the listener flips the most-recent `OPEN` row to `RESOLVED (auto)` and posts a `✅` comment here.
- `BLOCKED`, `FLAKE`, and human-set `RESOLVED` rows are never touched by auto-resolve.

## Kill switches

Repo Settings → Variables:

| Variable                                   | Effect                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `CRON_INCIDENT_LOGGER_ENABLED=false`       | Disable everything (no capture, no auto-resolve, no comments). |
| `CRON_INCIDENT_AUTO_RESOLVE_ENABLED=false` | Keep failure capture; disable auto-resolve only.               |
| `CRON_INCIDENT_ISSUE_NUMBER`               | Issue number for this feed (set once during initial setup).    |

## What goes in a comment

Each failure comment shows:

- Workflow name (human-readable + kebab id)
- Run URL
- Status flag
- Link back to the ledger row
- Last 30 lines of the failed step's logs (in a collapsed `<details>` block)

Each auto-resolve comment shows:

- ✅ marker
- Workflow name + date
- The next-success run URL that triggered the flip

## Manual override

If a row gets auto-resolved but is actually still broken: edit the ledger row directly, change Status back to `OPEN` (or `BLOCKED`), and add context to the Root Cause column. The listener will re-flip it on the NEXT successful scheduled run if the underlying issue is fixed.

If a row should be left OPEN forever (waiting on external action): change Status to `BLOCKED` — auto-resolve skips that exact value.

## Links

- Ledger: [`docs/cron-rebuild-failures.md`](../blob/main/docs/cron-rebuild-failures.md)
- Listener: [`.github/workflows/log-cron-incident.yml`](../blob/main/.github/workflows/log-cron-incident.yml)
- Script: [`.github/scripts/log-cron-incident.mjs`](../blob/main/.github/scripts/log-cron-incident.mjs)

`dag.json` still reports the cycle:

```json
"cycles": [["CE-9", "ET-7", "CE-9"], ["CRE-4", "DIST-3", "DIST-1", "CRE-4"]]
```

`docs/roadmap/plans/CHANNEL-EXPANSION.md` already ruled on this on 2026-08-28 ("OWNER RULING — the `CE-9` ⇄ `ET-7` deadlock is broken by cutting ONE edge"). The ruling's last line: "The `dag.json` dep edit follows in the next tracking batch." It never did. Both atoms are still `todo`, both sit on `gated_frontier`, and neither can reach `ready_frontier` no matter what ships.

That makes the `CE-9` row in #2490 wrong today. Approving the risk-policy paragraph does not unblock `ET-7` while the cycle stands.

## Ground truth on the four deliverables the two gates name

Measured against code on `origin/main`, not against plan logs.

1. **channel scaffold template — EXISTS.** `personalclaw app new <name> --type channel` emits the full six-file app with a real `ChannelTransportProvider` stub; the type table is derived from `PROVIDER_TYPES` + the provider registry at runtime (`src/personalclaw/cli_app_new.py`). Shipped by `ET-1`, which is already a direct dep of `ET-7`. CHANNEL-EXPANSION never shipped a scaffold template.
2. **app-registered trigger source types — EXISTS.** `WF2AUT-8` is not a phantom: `trigger_source` is in `PROVIDER_TYPES` (`src/personalclaw/apps/manifest.py`), `TriggerSourceTypeHandler` is registered (`src/personalclaw/providers/registry.py`), and `app:<name>:<event>` namespacing plus the fenced ingestion path live in `src/personalclaw/trigger_sources/registry.py`.
3. **bounty board — DOES NOT EXIST.** No `bounty` label in this repo, no `community-tier` label, no issue with "bounty" in the title. It is `ET-7`'s own output.
4. **channel wants-list (T7.3) — did not exist.** The string appeared only in `ECOSYSTEM-TOOLING.md`, `CHANNEL-EXPANSION.md`, `ET.md` and `dag.json`. #2550 lands it as `docs/maintainers/app-bounty-wants-list.md`, machine-checked.

So `CE-9`'s dep is void on one half and circular on the other: the scaffold half was delivered by `ET-1` (`done`), and the bounty-board half is the output of the very atom the edge points at. The ruling is right. Drop it.

## The two dag edits, which must land together

1. Remove `"EXT:ECOSYSTEM-TOOLING:channel scaffold template + bounty board"` from `CE-9.deps`.
2. Remove its `resolved_edges` entry: `{"atom": "CE-9", "ext_ref": "EXT:ECOSYSTEM-TOOLING:channel scaffold template + bounty board", "to_atom": "ET-7"}`.

Leaving (2) behind makes `tools/regen_dag_derived.py` exit with "N EXT resolution(s) name a dep that plans[] no longer has ... drop the entry".

Keep `ET-7`'s edge. It resolves to `CE-9` and that is the real ordering: the wants-list comes first, the board points at it. Its prose should stop naming CHANNEL-EXPANSION as the owner of the scaffold template, since `ET-1` shipped that and is already a direct dep. Suggested: `EXT:CHANNEL-EXPANSION:channel wants-list (T7.3) the channel bounties draw from`.

## Neither atom is agent-closable even after the cut

Both terminate in owner acts, so the cut makes `CE-9` startable rather than done.

- `CE-9` clause 2 (scaffold registration) and clause 3 (the WF2AUT coordination line, plus no bespoke event glue) are **MET**. Clause 1 waits on the risk-policy paragraph (owner task 5, tracked in #2490).
- `ET-7` needs the reward-model call (owner task 3), the `bounty` and `community-tier` labels created, the issues posted, and the showcase thread seeded. The wants-list it was blocked on is in #2550.

## Adjacent, not fixed here

`docs/roadmap/atomic/ET.md` shows `ET-1` as ✅ in the table while its "Atom scopes" sub-header reads `**Status:** todo`; `CE.md` does the same for `CE-8` (✅ in the table, `in_progress` in the scope). `dag.json` has both `done`. This is the "plan headers lie" class the docs-lint ratchet exists for, and the ratchet only looks at `docs/roadmap/plans/`, never `docs/roadmap/atomic/`.
title: The CE-9 / ET-7 dag cycle is still live, so the 2026-08-28 owner ruling that broke it never took effect

## Goal

Build one excellent conversation-first product with two experiences, not two codebases:

- **Personal / community:** an inviting place for friends, creators, small groups, and their agents to hang out and get things done. Chat works before tasks, integrations, or administrative setup.
- **Organization:** the same room experience with centrally enforced identity, access, data lifecycle, agent controls, and operational evidence.

This issue makes the existing [production plan](https://github.com/Uuriko/project-room/blob/9d0601e84c22852ca8f3afa81072c8a8ac309694/docs/PRODUCTION-PLAN.md) executable. It is a planning/acceptance backlog, not a new policy engine, a funded bounty, or a readiness claim. No migration or product change is performed by opening it. Existing managed/reviewed work must not be silently downgraded by a simpler consumer UI.

## Verified baseline, not promises

Reference: PR #5 at `9d0601e84c22852ca8f3afa81072c8a8ac309694`.

- Both contract and Chromium browser jobs succeeded in [run 33962842494](https://github.com/Uuriko/project-room/actions/runs/33962842494). This covers that branch/run, not unmerged integration changes, physical devices, restore drills, or enterprise compliance.
- The [current UI](https://github.com/Uuriko/project-room/blob/9d0601e84c22852ca8f3afa81072c8a8ac309694/src/app.js) hardcodes `independentVerificationRequired: true` and `ownerDecisionRequired: true` for every work item. We need proportionate work UX, not a universal approval ceremony. Discussion, reactions, and ordinary agent replies must stay useful without any work item.
- [Drafts are memory-only](https://github.com/Uuriko/project-room/blob/9d0601e84c22852ca8f3afa81072c8a8ac309694/docs/CONVERSATION.md): reload, leaving, session end, and mobile process termination are not durable recovery paths.
- The [service](https://github.com/Uuriko/project-room/blob/9d0601e84c22852ca8f3afa81072c8a8ac309694/server/store.mjs) is room-scoped SQLite with provisioned keys, not organization identity or tenant-scoped PostgreSQL. It deliberately caps the pilot at 10,000 events, 100 members, 500 work items, and 5,000 retained credential rows per room.
- Message content is stored in both event bodies and projections. Adding a delete button alone cannot establish deletion, retention, or restore semantics.
- Addressed messages are room-visible, not DMs. Membership, connection, attention, and authorized agent context remain distinct.

## Product decisions to preserve

1. Home is the conversation. Work and administration progressively appear when useful.
2. Consumer defaults change presentation and defaults, not server authorization. Organization policy wins over local preferences; an unknown policy cannot downgrade a managed space.
3. A personal space and an employer-owned space never silently share history, drafts, search results, files, or agent memory. Moving information between them is an explicit operation.
4. Reuse the existing six work states and evidence/check/decision distinction. For optional low-risk personal work, separately design a lightweight path; do not remove independent checks from work that requires them.
5. Do not promise confidentiality from an agent or its runtime provider when they receive plaintext. Do not claim end-to-end encryption just because transport is encrypted.
6. No arbitrary new service, policy language, universal workflow engine, or second task object is needed for these requirements.

## A. Entry and consumer simplicity

- [ ] **A1 — Hosted entry and identity.** Replace manually exchanged pilot keys in ordinary onboarding with a maintained identity-provider flow. A new person joins through an explicit invitation and signs in without an API key, wallet, developer console, or knowledge of an agent protocol. Preserve provisioned keys for the bounded development pilot only.
- [ ] **A2 — Real room lifecycle.** Create, join, leave, switch, and archive rooms. Acceptance: a membership change affects navigation and acces
title: Consumer + enterprise readiness: one core, two experiences, 36 acceptance tasks

Extend the shared dummy lifecycle with one real managed test dragon and permission-gated arena setup, spawn, status, reset and frozen-result inspection. The human Cursor Play workflow must be able to configure and use this production feature from a fresh checkout.

## Dependencies and ownership

Requires integrated T08/#11 and T02b/#38, including T08’s T04/T05/T06/T09d prerequisites. Own the bounded paper.encounter backend, arena configuration boundary, command additions and feature scenarios. The lead coordinates bootstrap, plugin.yml, existing configuration/command integration and shared contracts.

Consume T08’s combat/proc and managed-target lifecycle, T06’s settled physical claim/mapping/native-suppression/retirement boundary, and T02b’s immutable type/table selection. Do not create another engine, impact listener or independent death authority. Publish this same backend for T10 countdown/hatch/prefire.

## Arena setup and operator workflow

- Provide an explicit permission-gated setup operation that persists the single development arena’s validated world/location/bounds and selected configuration. The command owner may choose consistent syntax under the existing development permission boundary and must document it.
- Fresh installations and existing legacy configurations without arena keys start safely as unconfigured. Preserve existing settings; status explains the missing setup, and spawn fails closed. Never choose an arbitrary world, current position or origin as a hidden fallback.
- Validate complete candidates before persistence/adoption: missing or unloaded world, malformed identifiers, non-finite/out-of-bounds coordinates and unusable arena bounds reject without losing the previous valid configuration. Permission denial must neither change the in-memory arena nor write configuration.
- Prove saved configuration is read back after an ordinary restart, including upgrading a legacy configuration. Keep configuration failure observable; do not require the companion plugin, protocol client or a hidden test bootstrap for production setup/spawn.
- Document a clean-main operator procedure: Cursor “Minecraft: Build and test”, existing Play.cmd or mcdev play, in-game permitted arena setup and dragon controls, then mcdev restart and repeat status/spawn/reset. Keep Build, actual Play/authentication and visual observations distinct. Unattended agents validate equivalent behavior through the isolated runner; they do not operate the human profile.

## Managed lifecycle and controls

Allow one active development encounter in the configured arena. Expose a target only after successful initialization. Status/result output identifies encounter generation, native UUID, selected definition/profile revisions, actual state and separate HP/credit totals. Reject unset/invalid arena configuration, duplicate/stale operations and attempts to affect another generation or unmanaged entity.

Actual accepted owned-arrow damage must drive one managed lethal transition, one frozen result and one native death path. Retain the accepted phase policy; reject late arrows/procs and retire terminal work once. Reset, removal, failed spawn and disable unwind owned state without publishing ordinary defeat or a second completion. Preserve unrelated entities/arenas.

Keep actual rewards disabled, including native loot/XP on managed test-dragon death; no command, configuration or callback may enable inventory, world-drop, currency or reward grants. Optional administrative test completion must be visibly diagnostic and fabricate neither player damage nor ordinary reward eligibility; omitting it does not block required controls. T08b owns ranking presentation and T08c owns personal preview calculations.

## Acceptance

Bind managed-dragon-development to actual pinned Paper with a real dragon, player-owned arrows and T09d’s existing action/observation helpers. Verify native suppression, one accepted damage/result boundary, same-tick/

## 目的

Crownless を、スケジュール実行するAIエージェントが自分で次の遊びを考え、Issue化し、実装まで進める「自律プロダクト開発」のPOCとして記録する。

将来の出版・振り返りで、単なるGit履歴では分からない **AIが何を考え、なぜそれを選び、人間がどこで介入したか** を一次資料として残す。

このIssueは実装タスクではなく、実験ログの正本として扱う。原則closeせず、各自律開発サイクルをコメントで追記する。

## 各サイクルで残す内容

### 1. Cycle
- 実行日時（Asia/Tokyo）
- 起動種別: scheduled / human-triggered
- 対象main SHA（取得できる場合）

### 2. AI proposal
- 直近3〜5サイクルで新しい遊びが増えたか
- 新機能候補3案
- 各候補の4軸スコア
  - プレイヤーが気づく変化
  - 新しい判断
  - リプレイ性
  - Canonとの整合

### 3. Decision
- 今回選んだIssue / 新規アイデア
- なぜそれを選んだか
- 他候補を選ばなかった主な理由
- bug-fix / maintenance / innovation の区分

### 4. Execution
- 新規Issue / 既存Issue
- 実装した縦切り
- PR / commit
- test / CI
- merge / close結果

### 5. Human intervention
前回サイクル以降、人間による方向修正がGitHub上または実行コンテキストから確認できる場合に記録する。

例:
- 新しいIssueを人間が追加した
- AI案を却下・修正した
- 優先順位を変更した
- 実装済み機能の作り直しを指示した
- 直接エージェントへ割り込んだ

介入が確認できなければ `なし / 確認できず` とし、推測で人間介入を作らない。

### 6. Outcome / observation
- プレイヤーから見て何が変わったか
- 新しい遊び・判断が増えたか
- AIの判断で気になった点
- 次回観察したいこと

## 記録原則

- 事実とAIの評価を分ける
- 後から書き換えず、原則コメントを追加して時系列を保つ
- Issue/PR/commitへリンクできる情報を残す
- 長い実装ログやCI全文は複製せず、意思決定に必要な要約だけを残す
- 人間介入は確認できたものだけを記録し、推測しない
- 成功だけでなく、`no_action`、失敗、誤った提案、revert、方向修正も残す

## このPOCで検証したい問い

> AIは、与えられたIssueを消化するだけでなく、自分で「次に何を作るべきか」を考え、ゲームを継続的に面白くできるか。

> 人間は常時開発ループを回さず、必要なときだけIssue追加や直接指示で介入する運用へ移れるか。

Related: #228
title: POC: AI自律開発の意思決定・人間介入ログ

body_excerpt:
## 背景

実機playtestの結果、現在の Crownless は小さな改善を積み上げても **根本的な楽しさが足りない** という判断に至った。

現在の Canon は `Location × Expedition RPG` として、

> **Walk → Discover → Prepare → Dispatch → Wait → Report → Adapt**

を中心に据え、North Star を

> **After dispatching an expedition, does the player want to reopen the game to see what happened?**

としている。

しかし、直近の実機感想では、探索・遠征・Report・地点固有判断などを増やしても、ゲーム全体が「次もやりたい」へ十分つながっていない。

Orna の分析では、短い戦闘・loot・成長の高頻度ループは強い一方、長期的には「自分を強くするために自分を強くし続ける」ハムスター感が負担になる。

Crownless ではこの弱点をそのままコピーせず、**強くなる目的を世界への影響へ接続する**。

本Issueでは、地点支配をゲームの主目的候補として扱い、

> **自分を強くするために遊ぶのではなく、世界を広げるために仲間・装備・遠征を使う**

構造が実際に面白いかを、最小vertical sliceで検証する。

---

## Human decision / Canon change

これは現行 Canon 内の小改善ではない。

以下を意図的に再検討する。

- 遠征そのものを gameplay center とする前提
- North Star を「遠征結果を見たくなるか」に置く前提
- faction / territory を base loop の後へ deferred している前提

そのため、本Issueは **Canon変更を伴う human-approved Reforge** とする。

実装前に `docs/adr/0003-territory-driven-reforge.md` 相当のADRを追加し、`AGENTS.md` / `docs/game-system-design.md` の current Canon と矛盾しない状態へ更新すること。

旧Canonを履歴として残してよいが、main上で複数の相反するNorth Starを同時に正本扱いしない。

---

## 新しいProduct hypothesis

> **現実を歩いて発見した地点を、偵察・準備・攻略・支配し、その結果として地図と次の攻略条件が変わるなら、Crownless は「遠征結果を見るゲーム」から「自分の勢力圏を広げるRPG」へ進化できる。**

### 新しいNorth Star候補

> **自分の行動で勢力圏が広がった地図を見たとき、次の地点を取りたくなるか？**

補助質問:

- 次の地点を「どこから取るか」で迷えるか
- その地点を取るために仲間・装備・偵察が欲しくなるか
- 支配によって地図や選択肢が明確に変わるか
- 1地点取った直後に「もう1地点」が自然に見えるか
- 単なる数値蓄積ではなく攻略判断として感じられるか

---

## Core loop candidate

まず以下を仮説として実装する。

```text
Walk
  ↓
Discover
  ↓
Scout / Learn
  ↓
Prepare
  ↓
Contest / Expedition
  ↓
Control
  ↓
Exploit / Defend / Expand
  ↓
次の地点へ
```

日本語:

> **歩く → 発見する → 偵察する → 攻略を準備する → 地点を争う → 支配する → 利用する／守る → 次へ広げる**

遠征は削除しない。

ただし位置づけを変える。

**遠征 = ゲームの最終目的ではなく、地点へ働きかける主要手段の1つ。**

既存の deterministic expedition resolver、仲間、装備、地点知識、Report は可能な限り再利用する。

---

## 最重要設計原則

### 1. 支配ゲージGrindingを作らない

以下のような実装は禁止する。

```text
支配度 4,280 / 10,000
敵を倒すたび +20
```

これは経験値バーを支配度へ名前変更しただけであり、Ornaで問題になったハムスターループを再導入する。

地点攻略は主に **判断と準備** で差が出るようにする。

例:

- 敵構成を偵察する
- 地元特性を持つ仲間を送る
- 補給路を先に押さえる
- 正面突破する / 潜入する / 迂回する
- 貴重な装備をここで使うか温存する

### 2. 最初からPvPを作らない

Phase 1 は NPC勢力のみ。

プレイヤー間同期、常時server、不正対策、season、ranking、clan war は面白さ検証を妨げるため deferred。

### 3. 支配は地図と次の判断を変える

「支配済み」badgeだけでは不十分。

取得した地点によって最低1つ、次の攻略条件・選択肢・利用可能資源が変わること。

### 4. 永続だが静的にしすぎない

Phase 1では防衛・奪還の本格simulationは作らないが、将来以下へつながるdomain contractを壊さない。

- NPC勢力の反攻
- regional event
- faction pressure
- rescue / disruption
- supply line

ただし always-on world simulation は今回作らない。

---

## Phase 1 — 最小vertical slice

大規模な territory engine を作らない。

**3地点だけ**で「1地点を取ると2地点目の攻略判断が変わる」ことを検証する。

### 代表地点

既存discoveryを再利用してよい。概念上は以下の3種類を用意する。

#### A. 拠点 / 小砦
- NPC勢力が保持
- 攻略可能
- 取得すると周辺への足場になる

#### B. 街道 / 渡河点
- 取得前は別地点への遠征に不利
- 取得後、別地点へのrisk / duration / approachのいずれかが変わる

#### C. 資源地 / 特殊地点
- 取得すると特定装備・補給・地域能力の利用理由が生まれる

3種類すべてを汎用システム化する必要はない。
代表3地点のauthored vertical sliceでよい。

---

## Golden slice

```text
1. 現実移動 / simulated location で3地点を発見
   ↓
2. Atlasで各地点の勢力 / 未知情報 / 価値が見える
   ↓
3. 1地点目を選ぶ
   ↓
4. 偵察するか、情報不足のまま攻めるか判断
   ↓
5. 仲間 / 装備 / approach を選ぶ
   ↓
6. 既存expedition resolverを使って攻略を解決
   ↓
7. successなら地点controlがNPC → playerへ変わる
   ↓
8. Atlas上で支配変化が明確に見える
   ↓
9. その地点を取った効果で2地点目の攻略条件が変わる
   ↓
10. 「次はどこを取る？」の判断が生まれる
```

---

## 地点状態 MVP

最小限、game-facing state として以下を表現できること。

```text
unknown
known
controlled_by_npc
controlled_by_player
```

必要なら `contested` を追加してよいが、Phase 1で不要なら増やさない。

各地点は最低限:

- stable place id
- controlling faction / owner kind
- strategic role
- known danger / unknown information
- control effect

を持てる。

大規模な faction data model は作らない。
NPC勢力は1勢力で十分。

---

## 攻略判断 MVP

1地点目で最低2つの意味ある判断が必要。

候補:

### 偵察
- 時間を使って情報を得る
- 敵 / hazard / approach の一部が分かる
- 直接control progressを貯める行動にはしない

### 攻略方針
例:
- 正面から攻める
- 迂回して侵入する

既存companion trait / geographic equipment / destination approach と接続可能なら再利用する。

「二択UIを置いただけ」ではなく、少なくとも1つは結果確率・傷害・loot・次状態のいずれかへ因果が出ること。

---

## 支配効果 MVP

取得した地点の価値を即座に感じられること。

最低1種類、できれば2種類:

- 隣接地点の攻略risk低下
- 遠征duration短縮
- 新approac
title: Crownless 2.0: 地点支配をコアに据えた Territory-driven Reforge を縦切り検証する

## Objetivo y alcance

Convertir este fork en un **laboratorio de simulación programable, reproducible e inspeccionable** para investigar representaciones predictivas y world models. El caso consumidor inicial es `murillo128/nfl-world-model`, pero el motor y sus contratos deben ser independientes de NFL, PyTorch, JEPA, LeJEPA y cualquier proveedor de LLM.

La estrategia de investigación es ascendente: reproducir primero un JEPA/LeJEPA conocido en un proyecto de aprendizaje separado; después aprender dinámica en un entorno pequeño conocido; finalmente usar Bot Bowl como mundo externo complejo, empezando por escenarios acotados y ampliando hasta el juego completo implementado. **Modernizar Bot Bowl no debe convertirse en otro gran proyecto que impida empezar a experimentar.** Esta issue es una carta a los Reyes Magos y una épica de requisitos, no una orden de implementar todo de golpe.

El éxito no consiste en entrenar al mejor bot ni en maximizar victorias. Queremos poder estudiar qué información representa un modelo sobre el pasado y el presente, qué futuros considera plausibles, cómo cambian esas expectativas tras una acción y qué distingue sorpresa, impacto y calidad táctica. Los bots sirven para generar experiencias y como políticas de referencia; RL y planificación son consumidores opcionales.

**Prioridades:** `P0` = necesario para el primer laboratorio fiable; `P1` = muy recomendable después de ese mínimo; `P2` = exploración o comodidad avanzada. Las prioridades son locales a cada capacidad: un requisito P0 no obliga a implementar los P1/P2 de su sección. Los identificadores permiten abrir issues hijas sin perder trazabilidad. Los nombres de API propuestos aquí son orientativos; su semántica sí es un requisito.

## Punto de partida verificado

Inspección estática de `main`, commit [`3e550bda3666c39efe478fb9465646af24576665`](https://github.com/murillo128/botbowl/tree/3e550bda3666c39efe478fb9465646af24576665), el 6 de septiembre de 2026. No se ha instalado ni ejecutado el proyecto durante esta revisión; las capacidades existentes deben confirmarse mediante pruebas antes de darlas por satisfechas.

- El motor ya dispone de `Game`, acciones, reglas, semillas, registros y un forward model con `enable_forward_model`, `get_step`, `revert` y `forward`. **No hay que reconstruirlo desde cero.** La documentación advierte que el rebobinado no restaura el estado del generador aleatorio; por tanto, ese mecanismo por sí solo no equivale a un snapshot reproducible completo. Referencias: [motor](https://github.com/murillo128/botbowl/blob/3e550bda3666c39efe478fb9465646af24576665/botbowl/core/game.py), [forward model](https://github.com/murillo128/botbowl/blob/3e550bda3666c39efe478fb9465646af24576665/docs/forward-model.md).
- El entorno actual incluye configuraciones `1`, `3`, `5`, `7` y `11`, observaciones procesadas, máscaras, formaciones y asistencia de pathfinding. Las entradas predeterminadas incluyen, entre otras, `OwnTackleZoneLayer`, `RollProbabilityLayer` y `BlockDiceLayer`. `Game.step` puede avanzar automáticamente acciones de bots hasta la siguiente petición de entrada externa. Estas facilidades son reutilizables, pero requieren contratos explícitos para no ocultar transiciones ni dar al modelo las respuestas que luego pretendemos evaluar. Referencias: [entorno](https://github.com/murillo128/botbowl/blob/3e550bda3666c39efe478fb9465646af24576665/botbowl/ai/env.py), [motor](https://github.com/murillo128/botbowl/blob/3e550bda3666c39efe478fb9465646af24576665/botbowl/core/game.py).
- El empaquetado usa `setup.py`, importa `distutils`, fija dependencias e incluye web, Docker, tests y visualización en la instalación general. La CI inspeccionada cubre Python 3.8–3.11. El transporte de competición utiliza sockets con serialización `pickle`; eso no debe convertirse en la API remota pública del nuevo laboratorio. Referencias: [setup](https://github.com/murillo128/botbowl/blob/3e550bda3666c39efe478fb9465646af24576665/setup.py), [CI](https:

## 背景

#512 / PR #514 を実機確認したところ、Territory reward surface によって支配変化そのものは見えやすくなった一方、**モバイル幅で地点・装飾・ラベルが重なりすぎて Atlas が読みにくい**問題が出た。

実機スクリーンショットでは、近接する地点の marker / badge / label がほぼ同一箇所に重なり、地点名・支配状態・次候補の識別が困難になっている。

これは単なる見た目調整ではなく、#512 の North Star である

> 自分の行動で勢力圏が広がった地図を見たとき、次の地点を取りたくなるか？

を阻害するUX課題。

Related #512 #503 / PR #514

---

## Problem

情報を増やした結果、モバイルでは地図の可読性が落ちている。

特に:

- 近接地点の marker / badge / label が重なる
- 地点同士を見分けにくい
- 支配済み / NPC支配 / 選択中 / 次候補の差が重なりの中で読みにくい
- `次の標的` や拠点役割等の補助情報が地図本体を覆う
- Atlas が reward surface になる前に、情報過密なUIとして見えてしまう

---

## Goal

**支配変化の手触りは維持したまま、モバイルでも地点を選べて、次の判断がしやすい Atlas に戻す。**

最低限:

- 地点が近接していても個別に識別・選択できる
- 支配済み / NPC支配 / 選択中 / 前線・次候補が区別できる
- 次に狙う地点を追える
- Territory Build 情報は残るが、地図の可読性を壊さない
- 412px前後でも Atlas が主役のまま成立する

---

## Scope / MVP

### 1. 常時表示情報を減らす

モバイルでは全地点に文字情報を出し続けない。

常時表示は原則:

- marker本体
- 支配状態の印
- 前線 / 次候補の最小記号

文字ラベルや拠点役割は、以下へ寄せる。

- 選択中の地点
- 必要なら次候補のみ
- detail panel

### 2. 近接 marker の overlap を回避する

近い地点は少量の視覚オフセット等で、marker が完全に重ならないようにする。

- 地理的厳密さより **読めること / タップできること** を優先
- authored 3-territory slice に必要な最小実装でよい
- 汎用クラスタリングエンジンは作らない
- manuscript / woodcut visual canon を維持する

### 3. detail を選択時中心に寄せる

Atlas上に補助テキストを載せすぎず、詳細情報は選択後のdetailへ寄せる。

Territory Build の `斥候所 / 補給所` 等も、非選択時には小さな記号・短縮表現で十分。

### 4. Territory summary をモバイル向けに圧縮

`支配 n/3 · 前線 n · 次候補` は残すが、地図を覆わないサイズ・配置にする。

---

## Non-goals

今回はやらない。

- 大規模な地図クラスタリングシステム
- 汎用レイアウトエンジン
- GPS / exact location history の変更
- Territory reward / Territory Build のゲームルール変更
- Phase C のNPC / World Trace追加

まず #512 A+B のプレイテストを成立させるための可読性回復を優先する。

---

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] 412px前後で、近接する3地点を個別に認識できる
- [ ] 近接地点があっても各markerを選択できる
- [ ] 支配済み / NPC支配 / 選択中の差が重なりの中でも分かる
- [ ] 非選択地点の常時ラベルが Atlas を覆わない
- [ ] `次に狙う地点` が視覚的に追える
- [ ] Territory Build の役割情報は維持される
- [ ] Territory summary が主要地点を隠さない
- [ ] grayscale / low-saturationでも状態差が残る
- [ ] existing Atlas / Territory / expedition tests green
- [ ] browser regression に「近接地点がある状態でも3地点を識別・選択できる」確認を追加する

---

## 実装順序

1. 非選択地点のラベル常時表示を削減
2. 近接markerを最小限オフセット
3. detail / summary のモバイル圧縮
4. 実機で再確認

いきなりクラスタ化せず、**最小変更で地図の可読性が戻るか**を先に検証する。
title: Atlas mobile declutter: 近接地点の重なりを解消して支配/次候補を読めるようにする

## Relación y dependencias

Hija de #2; cubre EVAL-06. **Depende de #12, #15, #30, #52 (API-02) y #65 (DATA-02).** Estado inicial blocked por prerrequisitos. Reutiliza las correcciones de #3; #12 corrige casualties y rewards, pero no establece una cadena explicativa general. #65 define primero el envelope base y esta entrega lo amplía: no introducir una dependencia inversa ni exigir explicaciones completas para grabar una transición básica.

Base `d392c00a9b77899ea6523de59e2eee3d61c7f5f6`: los procedimientos generan `Outcome` y reportes; `Game.to_json` expone nombres de pila, no una explicación estructurada de condiciones y consecuencias. Reutilizar esos puntos de emisión, sin inferir retrospectivamente reglas a partir de textos ni duplicar un segundo motor.

## Diseño resuelto

Extender el envelope #65 con un payload explicativo versionado: `rule_id`, participantes por IDs estables, decision_id, `parent_event_ids`, condiciones evaluadas, modificadores y umbral cuando existan, tirada efectivamente consumida y resultado realizado. Las aristas enlazan antecedentes anteriores del mismo episodio/rama; una consecuencia automática no es una acción de un jugador. Identificar decisiones opcionales (reroll, selección de dado, médico) por su evento de decisión, no como inevitables efectos de la tirada.

Instrumentar primero las familias realmente implementadas: movimiento/dodge/GFI y pickup, block/push/follow-up, pase/intercepción/catch, lesión/médico, rerolls y cambio de turno/drive. Un registro de cobertura enumera emisores instrumentados y no soportados; prohibido fabricar condiciones para rellenar campos desconocidos. Una rule_id identifica la regla aplicada del descriptor #30, no una afirmación de conformidad con otra edición.

La emisión ocurre una sola vez en el punto que toma la decisión/regla, se asocia al contador de #52 y no añade tiradas ni cambia el orden de procedimientos. El mismo suceso no se vuelve a contar como casualty/reward. El tracing se puede activar/desactivar sin alterar eventos deportivos ni estado; si una restricción de recursos impide conservar el trace, debe reportarse incompleto, no parecer completo.

Los resultados de tiradas históricas visibles pueden exportarse conforme al canal declarado; RNG interno y futuros permanecen privilegiados. El grafo describe causalidad operacional dentro del simulador, no utilidad táctica ni efecto contrafactual identificado. Hipótesis estratégicas y estimaciones de intervención usan categorías/canales distintos. No generar explicaciones de lenguaje natural con un proveedor externo.

## Tests y aceptación

`tests/lab/test_rule_traces.py`: fixtures deterministas de cada familia con condiciones/modificadores/umbral y dados conocidos; comprobar participantes, rule_id, orden y aristas exactos. Detectar ciclos, referencias inexistentes y cruces de rama/episodio. Un reroll forma dos intentos enlazados a su decisión, no una explicación que oculta el primer fallo.

Comparar tracing on/off con mismas acciones y RNG: estado, tiradas consumidas y resultados deportivos idénticos. Pasar regresiones #12 de multiplicidad de casualty/reward. El trace reconstruye una jugada compuesta hasta su consecuencia final y el validador rechaza un antecedente posterior. Tests de límites, consumidor que falla y redacción de datos privilegiados. Medir sobrecoste sobre corpus fijo sin umbral ruidoso de CI. Revisión final-capable independiente de cobertura, invariancia del motor y alcance de las afirmaciones causales.
title: [P1 · EVAL-06] Emitir eventos explicativos de reglas con antecedentes y contexto verificables

## Problem

Part of **#140 — roadmap(assets): remaining asset resolution, overrides, and report work**.

A principal can already override asset identity and inclusion through completed **#149 — feat(assets): let principals override asset identity and inclusion**. They cannot yet correct the price or factual classification of one token movement while preserving the system's original facts and an audit trail. That can leave a calculation partial or produce a result based on a value or classification the principal disputes.

Grounded against merged main `8c669aaf49324c5c3b7c2ef21533a955b8ac510d` on 2026-09-06. The foundation exists, but it is asset-wide: `PrincipalAssetOverrideRepositoryLive.ts`, `PrincipalAssetOverrideDecisionLoader.ts`, and `SourceReplayScheduling.ts` already implement audited streams, source replay, and run coverage. `FactualLedgerRepositoryLive.ts` builds the accounting inputs. `SourceReplayRepositoryLive.ts` deletes and rebuilds derived legs; a leg UUID is therefore not a correction target. The engine's existing valuation facts distinguish provider consideration from market quotes and currently have no truthful user-valuation variant.

The earlier acquisition-basis example was corrected on this issue: that historical staking case belongs to completed **#266 — fix(accounting): give Coinbase passive staking payouts a cost basis and income result**. It is not evidence of a missing price. This spec uses synthetic missing-price and factual-correction fixtures instead. No other issue is absorbed.

## Solution

A principal selects an owned movement, inspects TaxMaxi's current facts, and creates, replaces, or withdraws a price or factual-classification correction with a reason. The API and SDK expose the same operations.

User-visible behavior:

- Discover stable correction targets for the token movements of an owned canonical transaction, including swap acquisitions/disposals, receipts, and explicit fees where applicable.
- Enter either a price per token or a total value for the selected movement, in the calculation's reporting currency. Read both values without losing the entered value.
- Replace a supported factual cause, such as an unknown receipt with a purchase or passive staking reward. The engine derives the resulting tax treatment.
- Inspect the original system facts, the active correction, effective facts, history, and the calculation run that actually used a correction.
- See updating, partial, complete, failed, or needs-attention outcomes truthfully. A correction does not make unrelated blockers disappear.
- Keep corrections across normal source replay. Keep other principals' facts and results unchanged.

This spec is CLI/API-first through REST and the SDK. It adds no web or TUI editor. Existing asset-identity and inclusion operations remain separate.

## Decisions

The maintainer confirmed the following scope in the defining conversation on 2026-09-06: individual movement targets; original provider facts retained; unit-price and total-value entry; reporting-currency-only input in the first version; price and factual classification as the two correction kinds; tax treatment always derived by the engine. The final clarification was: “users can override price and classification, asset overrides are already possible via #149.” Here that reference means **#149 — feat(assets): let principals override asset identity and inclusion**.

The shared architectural boundary is in **ADR 0013 — Movement corrections change accounting inputs, not tax conclusions**, at `docs/adr/0013-movement-corrections-feed-accounting-inputs.md`. Its draft and the corresponding ADR 0011 clarification and core glossary entries have been written in the originating working copy. T01 publishes them before later PRs rely on them; do not cite a nonexistent main-branch document as merged. ADR 0005/0006/0007/0008/0010/0011/0012 continue to apply. The decisions below specify this issue's delivery behavior.

### D01 — Exact movement targeting

A

## TL;DR

Implement asynchronous RL in MarinSkyRL and build the observability needed to measure the tradeoff between policy lag, training performance, and reward quality. The goal is to establish how far off-policy we can go to improve performance before quality degrades.

## Description

Marin orchestrates the experiments; MarinSkyRL provides the async trainer and rollout execution. We start with non-agentic Qwen3-0.6B/GSM8K on H100s, using Megatron, GRPO advantages, and rule-based rewards, then progress to Snowball.

This workstream covers async correctness, reproducible experiments, and useful metrics through W&B, Finelog, and Grafana. Substantial vLLM optimizations remain in a separate workstream. Easy existing settings are downstream options only when measurements show a rollout-throughput bottleneck.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Allowing rollouts to lag behind the learner may improve performance by overlapping generation and training and reducing synchronization waits. That lag can also affect learning quality.

Build the infrastructure to measure these effects together: how far off-policy the consumed rollouts are, the reward and evaluation quality achieved, and the time and compute required. Controlled experiments will establish the tradeoff across resource allocations and freshness settings, and identify where additional lag stops being worthwhile.

## Status

This section is a running summary; milestone comments preserve the progression and evidence.

- Qwen and Snowball async Megatron training are qualified on H100s. Metrics-only completion separates experiments from native checkpoints and HF export. W&B step histories, durable receipts and Finelog work accounting are independently audited.
- The Async RL Training Grafana dashboard has 40 data panels covering progress, waits, publication, policy drift, reward, memory, resource normalization, the wire-weight survey, TIS correction skips, age-conditioned diagnostics, and evaluation termination/response cost.
- Qwen100 completed. The original matched Qwen20 pair took 252.7 seconds sync versus 320.8 async. A subsequent 25-update cadence screen measured 250.5 seconds sync, 339.5 async with publication every update, and 256.4 every two updates; consumed work differed. [Cadence results](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8936#issuecomment-5558891614).
- Snowball memory measurements support retaining 32 learner GPUs: PPO/publication peaks were 56.6/58.1 GiB, reconfirmed in the latest block. The response-budget pilots support a provisional 4,096-token cap to reduce truncation. [Memory](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8936#issuecomment-5558104237), [token budgets](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8936#issuecomment-5558461338).
- All three Snowball25 timing controls completed cleanly: sync 1,652.8 seconds, async publication-every-update 1,182.2 seconds, and publication-every-two-updates 959.7 seconds. Corresponding task-running GPU-hours were 24.87, 21.02 and 19.00. The two-update cadence's 47.5% rollout-wait share motivated the subsequent inference-allocation comparison. [Measurements and allocation decision](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8936#issuecomment-5559147975).
- Frozen Qwen evaluations show repeat variation at fixed weights; the actual-wire survey and real-worker capped-TIS numerical gate are qualified. Snowball diagnostics and Qwen stale-data experiments extend those measurements. [Diagnostic results](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8936#issuecomment-5558977502).

- Shared-order Qwen controls now show a stronger cadence result: C4/A3 took 207.5 seconds versus C1/A3 336.1 seconds, with nearly equal consumed tokens and higher measured probability drift. The subsequent three 100-update Qwen development arms all passed strict audits: C1/A1, C4/A3 and C4/A3 regular+TIS took 1,298.8, 754.8 and 770.1 core seconds, with final development scores 85, 91 and 96 out of 128. Token work differed substantiall

## Player report and requested behavior

The doorkeeper's corpse immediately behind the Forbidden Woods password door still gives vanilla Madman's Knowledge. Suppress that reward and make examining/looting the corpse an AP location check.

The player has separately live-confirmed that an AP password opens this door before Amelia; preserve that access behavior. Do not add an Amelia requirement to this check.

## Confirmed source

- Bundled `event/m24_00_00_00.emevd.dcx.js`, event `12400403`, waits for interaction flag `72400441` and calls `AwardItemLot(37000)`. It has host/alive and completed-event guards.
- `research/joined/lot_items.tsv`: lot `37000` is named as the gatekeeper's mummified-corpse inspection reward; slot 01 awards category 4 / goods 1500 (Madman's Knowledge), quantity 1.
- The lot's acquisition flag is `50002000`.
- Neither this lot nor this acquisition flag currently appears in the world's location/runtime catalogs.

This is a scripted interaction award, outside the normal fixed-treasure catalog. The door-opening flag (`12400131`) and door interaction flag (`72400440`) are separate and must not themselves complete the corpse check.

## Implementation scope

1. Add a stable location identity with a descriptive name such as `Forbidden Woods entrance - Doorkeeper's corpse`.
2. Place it behind the AP password door in logic, using the actual accessible side of that boundary rather than assigning free Cathedral Ward access from its map name. Confirm the region representation handles access before Amelia correctly.
3. Use acquisition flag `50002000` as the candidate runtime witness, after verifying its uniqueness and save persistence. Check only when the corpse reward is collected.
4. Add an explicit lot-scoped suppression declaration for `37000`, category 4 / goods 1500. Preserve its acquisition flag and all unrelated Madman's Knowledge lots. Do not globally search-and-suppress goods 1500.
5. Add the matching pool contribution and update generated location names, suppression plan/lineage pins and build artifacts as required.

## Acceptance and tests

- Without the password, the location is inaccessible in logic; with the password it is reachable without defeating Amelia.
- Opening the door alone does not send the check.
- Inspecting the corpse grants the normal AP placeholder instead of vanilla Madman's Knowledge and sends the check exactly once.
- Save/reload and repeated inspection do not duplicate the check or reward; verify already-collected save reconciliation against the persisted witness.
- CI validates lot identity, slot, quantity and acquisition flag, preserves unrelated lots, and covers both access gating and check-vs-door separation.
- Live-test collection, the observed flag transition, reward suppression and reload persistence.

Der kanonische WÖk-Bestand bestätigt die Fachlücke:
- `/WOEK/WOEK-LAENDER-DAILY/BASELINE/baden-wuerttemberg/BASELINE-2026-08-18.md`: offene Aufgabe `Koalitionsvertrag vollständig in CoalitionCommitments zerlegen`.
- `/WOEK/WOEK-LAENDER-DAILY/CONTROL/LAENDER-COVERAGE-AND-HANDOFF-FINAL-2026-08-18.md`: Koalitionsvertrag 2026-2031 nur `als Mandatsbasis vorgesehen`.
- `/WOEK/WOEK-LAENDER-DAILY/FACHREVIEW/baden-wuerttemberg/INITIAL-IMPACT-CASES-2026-08-18.md`: fünf initiale Regierungswirkungsfälle, aber keine vollständige Koalitionsvertrags-Wirkungsanalyse.

Aktuelle Production ist nicht stale: `dpl_6CefNPFgRYrVXzYTFZeEezsArEX2`, READY/production, Git SHA `fb07fab799a34bbda0e2efc03f90066945c95802`, entsprechend aktuellem main-Basisstand von PR #235. Das BW-Problem ist daher nach aktuellem Befund keine bloße falsche Vercel-Promotion, sondern eine echte fachliche/Publikations-Coverage-Lücke - vorbehaltlich historischem Restore-Fund.

## Rollen
Human out of loop. **CodeX ist technischer Ausführungs- und Deployment-Aktor.** WÖk/Controller liefert Fachbestand, Priorität, Audit und exact-commit Freigabe. CodeX implementiert, testet, merged und deployt bis Production, sobald die Gates grün sind. Kein zusätzliches Human-Gate.

## P0-1 Baden-Württemberg: Restore-first
Vor Neuanalyse Git-Historie, Branches und kanonischen `/WOEK`-Bestand nach einer früher bereits fachlich freigegebenen Koalitionsvertragsanalyse durchsuchen. Wenn vorhanden: exakt/provenienzgebunden wiederherstellen. Keine Neufassung, die einen vorhandenen historischen Fachstand still ersetzt.

Wenn keine vollständige freigegebene Analyse existiert, ist die Fachlücke ausdrücklich zu schließen: amtlichen Koalitionsvertrag 2026-2031 vollständig sichern/versionieren, Commitments mit Source Locator extrahieren und dem WÖk-Fachreview zuführen. CodeX erzeugt **keine** Wirkungsurteile selbst.

## P0-2 Vollständigkeitsaudit alle 16 Länder
Für jedes Land getrennt inventarisieren und öffentlich korrekt abbilden:
- `election_cycle_state` und `government_lifecycle_state` - strikt getrennte Achsen,
- ElectionDocuments/Wahlprogramme und freigegebene Programmanalysen,
- Koalitions-/Mandatsdokumente und Coalition-/MandateCommitments,
- GovernmentActions und WÖkImpactCases,
- AnalysisVersions/RecommendationVersions,
- EvidenceEvents/RealityChecks,
- Quellen, Kompetenz, höherrangiges Recht/Schutzgrenzen,
- öffentliche Routen, Navigation, Overview-Projektion und Detailakten.

Fehlende Fachlayer nicht technisch erfinden. Vorhandenen Fachbestand niemals verkürzen oder verstecken.

## P0-3 Übersicht: Wirkungspotenzial klar sichtbar
Portalweit auf Wahlprogramm-, Koalitions-/Mandats-, Regierungs-, Parlament-, EU- und Länderübersichten muss die WÖk-Einordnung vor Prozessmetadaten verständlich sichtbar sein. Soweit fachlich freigegeben mindestens:
- qualitativer Wirkungspotenzialbefund,
- stärkste positive Potenziale,
- wichtigste materielle Risiken/Zielkonflikte,
- Evidenz/Unsicherheit getrennt von Richtung,
- Richtungsprofil nur für redaktionell/fachlich geprüfte Pfade,
- Nichtkompensation/Schutzgrenzen,
- **alle** freigegebenen Key Findings - keine `slice(0,2)`-Verkürzung,
- keine Partei-/Regierungs-Gesamtnote oder künstliche Saldierung.

Detailseiten müssen die vollständige freigegebene Fachakte und Quellen enthalten, nicht nur Mandats-/Fakten-Teaser.

## P0-4 Golden-State / kein Datenverlust durch Release
Jeder Kandidat gegen letzten akzeptierten Production-Stand **und** kanonischen `/WOEK`-Fachbestand prüfen:
