## Purpose

Persistent intake queue for **gathered but not-yet-implemented scientific/data enrichment**. This queue is deliberately separate from implementation WIP: research can be collected, verified, deduplicated, and ranked here even when the sprint has no legal implementation slot.

This is **not** a second scientific authority and does not bypass the enrichment governor, source registry, workbook/normalized-data contracts, provenance requirements, or merge gates. Canonical mutation still requires the normal governed implementation path and a legal WIP slot.

## Queue lifecycle

Each candidate moves through:

`DISCOVERED → VERIFIED → DEDUPED → READY_FOR_GOVERNED_IMPLEMENTATION → IMPLEMENTING → MERGED`

Other terminal/holding states:

- `REJECTED` — source/entity/claim is unsuitable or misleading.
- `BLOCKED_TOOLING` — evidence is good but current ingestion tooling cannot represent it safely.
- `BLOCKED_SEMANTIC` — identity/claim boundary needs resolution.
- `STALE_REVALIDATE` — evidence or external assumption needs freshness review before promotion.

## Required fields per queue item

- target entity / slug
- candidate source identity: PMID / DOI / canonical URL / title
- study class and population
- formulation / preparation / species boundary
- exact claim or field the source can support
- important null findings / limitations / uncertainty
- safety / interaction boundaries when relevant
- funding / conflict / supplier provenance when relevant
- repository dedup result
- current-site defect or missing field addressed
- proposed normalized destination
- status
- confidence
- priority rationale
- dependency / blocker
- discovered date / last verified date

## Ranking guidance

Highest priority generally goes to:

1. published factual/source integrity defects;
2. held profiles that can be safely unlocked with human evidence;
3. missing human evidence on already-indexed profiles;
4. high-value safety/interaction evidence;
5. recent systematic reviews/meta-analyses/RCTs that materially change certainty;
6. entity-resolution fixes that prevent a class of bad enrichment;
7. depth-only enrichment for already well-covered profiles.

Safety/scientific integrity overrides numeric convenience. Negative/null evidence is first-class and must not be discarded merely because it does not support a positive claim.

## Seed queue — 2026-08-27

### Q-001 — Sage (`sage`) — HIGH / integrity
**Status:** VERIFIED / READY_FOR_GOVERNED_IMPLEMENTATION once a legal WIP slot exists

**Current defect:** published Sage profile says none of the recorded studies measured outcomes in people, while genuine human clinical evidence exists. Current source set also contains PMID `40302443`, *Huntington's disease clinical trials update: March 2025*, which concerns SAGE-718 / Sage Therapeutics rather than botanical *Salvia officinalis*.

**Candidate evidence:**

- PMID `18350281`, DOI `10.1007/s00213-008-1101-3` — randomized double-blind crossover human trial of *Salvia officinalis* extract in older adults.
- PMID `33466627` — randomized placebo-controlled human cognition study using a combined *S. officinalis* polyphenol + *S. lavandulaefolia* terpene preparation; combination boundary must remain explicit.

**Required implementation boundary:** remove/reject the unrelated SAGE-718 source, correct the human-evidence rationale, preserve species/preparation differences, and add a resolver regression so `sage` cannot match company/drug uses such as Sage Therapeutics / SAGE-718 solely by token overlap.

## Summary

Once a resource is recorded as `provisionedBy: 'cc-api'`, `ProviderRegistry.getProviderFor`'s rule 2 pins it to Cloud Control forever. Backfilling the property into the SDK Provider's `handledProperties` does NOT bring that existing resource back to the SDK path — it only changes routing for resources created afterwards. `STICKY_CC_MIGRATION_EXEMPT` is the only exit, and its admission criteria deliberately exclude exactly this case.

So the [issue 609](https://github.com/go-to-k/cdkd/issues/609) backfill lane delivers its speed benefit only to NEW resources. Every stack that hit the auto-route before the backfill landed keeps paying Cloud Control latency permanently, with no user-visible way out short of a destroy and recreate.

## Why the existing exit does not cover it

`STICKY_CC_MIGRATION_EXEMPT` in `src/provisioning/provider-registry.ts` admits a type only when BOTH hold:

1. the CC handler **cannot correctly manage** the resource — "not a perf choice";
2. the SDK provider uses the SAME `physicalId` the CC path stored, so the re-route is churn-free.

Condition 2 is the safety property and is the right bar. Condition 1 is what blocks the backfill case: a backfilled type's CC routing is not broken, it is merely slower, so by the rule as written it may never be exempted. The set has exactly one member today (`AWS::Scheduler::Schedule`, [issue 961](https://github.com/go-to-k/cdkd/issues/961)).

## Why this is getting more load-bearing now

[issue 2718](https://github.com/go-to-k/cdkd/issues/2718) measured the drift rate: AWS adds roughly 3 writable top-level properties per month across cdkd's Tier 1 surface. Each one that a user adopts before cdkd wires it flips that resource to `cc-api` permanently. The auto-route is the correct behavior — a silently dropped property is strictly worse than a slower but correct deploy — but with the fixture-freshness job of [issue 2718](https://github.com/go-to-k/cdkd/issues/2718) in place, the flip becomes a routine, recurring event rather than a rare one. Without an exit, the cc-api population only ever grows.

## The decision to make

Whether condition 1 can be relaxed from "CC routing is broken" to "the SDK provider now fully covers the properties this resource uses", while keeping condition 2 (physicalId parity) as a hard requirement.

Sub-questions that a proposal has to answer:

- **How is physicalId parity established, per type, as evidence rather than as an assumption?** The parity is what makes the flip churn-free; asserting it from the provider source is not the same as observing it on a real resource. This is the part that most likely needs an integ arm: deploy under the CC route, upgrade the binary, redeploy, and assert the physical id is unchanged AND the state record flipped to `provisionedBy: 'sdk'`.
- **Is the flip safe mid-life, or only on a full property match?** A resource may carry a property the SDK provider still does not handle even after a partial backfill. Re-routing it would reintroduce the silent drop the auto-route existed to prevent, so the flip has to be conditioned on the resource's ACTUAL property set, not on the type having "some" coverage.
- **Per-type opt-in, or automatic?** An automatic flip keyed on "no actionable silent drops remain for this resource" is more useful but has a wider blast radius than a curated set. A per-type list keeps review in the loop at the cost of someone remembering to add entries during a backfill.
- **What does the user see?** A routing change on an existing resource is currently a debug-level log line. If it can move a live resource between two provisioning paths, it likely deserves a plan-time annotation.
- **Is an escape hatch needed** for a user who wants a resource pinned to CC regardless?

## Not in scope

Changing the auto-route itself. The default of routing a silent drop through Cloud Control is correct and is not what this issue questions — only the one-way-ness of the resulting state is.

## Classification
title: A cc-api-routed resource can never return to the SDK path, so the issue-609 backfill lane benefits only newly created resources

## Summary

Nothing in the repo watches whether `tests/fixtures/cfn-schemas/*.json` is still current with what AWS publishes. When AWS adds a top-level property to a type cdkd has an SDK Provider for, cdkd does not error and does not auto-route to Cloud Control — it **silently drops the property**, because the property is absent from the committed schema fixture and `findSilentDropProperties` treats "not in the CFn schema" as a user typo / `addPropertyOverride` escape hatch and passes it through.

This is the same user-visible failure [issue 614](https://github.com/go-to-k/cdkd/issues/614) was filed to eliminate (deploy reports success, the setting never reaches AWS), reachable through the one input the [issue 614](https://github.com/go-to-k/cdkd/issues/614) machinery cannot see.

## Mechanism

`ProviderRegistry.getProviderFor` decides SDK vs Cloud Control from the baked-in table `src/provisioning/property-coverage.generated.ts`, which `scripts/gen-property-coverage.ts` derives from the fixtures. There is no runtime `DescribeType` in that path (the live `DescribeType` calls in `create-only-properties.ts` / `write-only-properties.ts` serve replacement classification and update patches, not coverage routing).

So the outcome splits on fixture membership alone:

| The new property is... | Outcome |
|---|---|
| in the fixture, unhandled by the provider | `silentDrop` entry -> auto-route via Cloud Control (`provisionedBy: 'cc-api'`, sticky). Correct behavior. |
| in the fixture, unhandled, on a `NON_PROVISIONABLE` type or a provider with `disableCcApiFallback` | pre-flight throw with a per-property message. Correct behavior. |
| **not in the fixture** | `src/provisioning/property-coverage.ts` -> `rationale === undefined` -> `continue`. Stays on the SDK Provider, the property is dropped, no warning. |

Every AWS-side addition lands in the third row: all 134 fixtures carry `generatedAt` in 2026-08, so anything AWS published after that snapshot is invisible to cdkd.

## Why no existing mechanism catches it

- `tests/unit/provisioning/property-coverage.test.ts` compares providers against the fixture. It can only fail after someone refreshes the fixture.
- `scripts/refresh-cfn-schemas.mjs` is the refresh, and it is manual: it needs AWS credentials with `cloudformation:DescribeType` and is not registered as a Vite+ task.
- CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs only offline critics (`audit:coverage:check`, `audit:stateful-candidates:check`, ...); its own comments record that every AWS-calling regeneration "stays a manual / future-cron job".
- No workflow in `.github/workflows/` has a `schedule:` trigger, and no hook or markgate gate covers fixture age.
- The only `generatedAt` assertion in the tree is `gen-nested-key-coverage.test.ts`'s `>= '2026-08-10'` floor, which fences the SHAPE of a capture (that it carries `definitionShapes` / `nestedPropertyPaths`), not its freshness.

## Prior art and the trade to decide

- [issue 398](https://github.com/go-to-k/cdkd/issues/398) closed by choosing "offline check in CI, regeneration stays manual" for the type-level provider-coverage audit. That decision was about the Tier 1/2/3 catalog, not about per-type property fixtures, so it does not dispose of this.
- `gen:aws-cli-removals` is the closest precedent and is deliberately NOT in CI, with the rationale written into `vite.config.ts`: a `--check` in CI "would go red whenever AWS ships a CLI that removes one more command — noise on a schedule nobody controls".

That rationale argues against a red-CI staleness gate here too, and toward a scheduled job that OPENS A PR with the refreshed fixtures (and lets `property-coverage.test.ts` fail inside that PR, forcing each new property into `handledProperties` / `unhandledByDesign` / `_todo-backfill.json`). Deciding between that and a cheaper TTL warning is part of this issue.

## Candidate shapes

1. Scheduled GitHub Actions workflow (weekly / monthly) on a CI-only IAM role with `cloudformation:DescribeType`
title: No mechanism watches CFn schema fixture freshness, so a property AWS adds after the snapshot is silently dropped instead of auto-routing to Cloud Control

Unblocks the **secondary** shipping route. Needed for milestone **M0 (Sun 7 Sept)**.

Galaxy Store is our store route — free to join, free to publish. It unlocks the store-dependent categories (Grand Prize, Design, Growth Loop, OneSignal). It is **not** load-bearing: Next Gen is the primary entry and requires no store release at all, so nothing here blocks the critical path. If it stalls, we still have a complete submission.

## Tasks

- [ ] Register at [Samsung Seller Portal](https://seller.samsungapps.com) with a Samsung account
- [ ] Register as an **Individual** seller, not Commercial (see below)
- [ ] Complete identity verification
- [ ] Add Siphosihlemorabe as a co-seller / team member if the portal allows it, so we both have dashboard access
- [ ] Confirm the app name is available as a listing name (blocked on the app name decision — see PLAN.md immediate action #2)
- [ ] Note the seller account email + which Samsung account it's tied to, so build uploads don't stall on a login nobody has

## Individual, not Commercial — deliberate

This is risk **R2** in PLAN.md. Commercial-seller status is what lets you sell in-app on Galaxy Store, and it can require a D-U-N-S number and bank verification, each up to 10 business days. That's most of the runway to 30 Sept for a route we've already agreed is a bonus.

So: register as an individual, publish the app **free**, and put the RevenueCat purchase through **Web Billing**. The Shipaton rules accept "in-app **or** web purchase", so this keeps the HAMM and monetization categories intact without touching seller verification at all.

If individual registration turns out to also need lengthy verification, stop and say so rather than pushing through — this is the first thing on the cut list after Layers and OneSignal.

## Not part of this ticket

Store assets (screenshots, feature graphic, description), the APK/AAB upload, and content rating. Those come after M3 when there's a recordable build. This ticket is just the account existing.

## Done when

The Samsung Seller Portal account is registered and verified, both of us can reach the dashboard, and we know whether the account can upload a build without further verification steps.

## Context

PLAN.md — M0, M6, risk R2, and the "Cut order if time slips" note.

## Goal
Prove that GameYer can continue operational execution for 72 hours without requiring the Founder for routine technical/growth/ops work, while keeping all production-critical approvals Founder-gated.

## Operating gates
Every active task must be classified in its issue/thread as one of:

- `AUTO` — CEO/operator + executor may proceed through implementation, tests, PR and verification without Founder input.
- `FOUNDER_APPROVAL` — preparation may proceed automatically, but production deploy, DNS/nameserver/canonical changes, critical production decisions, budget increases/new paid SaaS, schema/real-data authenticity changes require Founder approval.
- `HUMAN_ACTION` — an external human action is inherently required (for example club-owner call/DM, ad-platform/SMM action, partnership response).

## 72h trial scope
Use the existing GitHub Issues ledger; do not build a new dashboard or OS.

During the trial, prioritize only:
1. P0 production/reliability blockers.
2. P1 September 10K real-unique-user traffic blockers: acquisition attribution, conversion leakage, supply quality on high-traffic club profiles.
3. P2 optimization/systemization only when it directly reduces Founder dependency.

## Detection inputs
Start with existing signals; do not build new infrastructure unless a real gap is proven:
- production health / GitHub CI / reliability signals
- PostHog real-traffic and attribution anomalies
- high-traffic incomplete club profiles using verified Supabase data only

## Execution contract
For an `AUTO` task:
problem → issue → acceptance criteria → implementation → tests → PR → independent verification → ready-for-approval/close.

Do not merge/deploy production unless the task explicitly falls outside Founder approval policy.

## Founder interrupt policy
Interrupt the Founder only for:
- production deploy / production merge when approval is required
- DNS, nameserver or canonical cutover
- budget increase or new paid SaaS
- Supabase schema/RLS/real-data authenticity decisions
- external human outreach/partnership/ad-platform action that cannot be done via connected tools
- severe blocker with no safe autonomous path

Do not interrupt for routine status updates.

## Success metrics after 72h
Record:
- tasks detected/created
- AUTO tasks completed to verified PR/result
- tasks blocked on Founder approval
- HUMAN_ACTION tasks prepared
- unnecessary Founder interrupts (target: 0)
- production-impacting changes made without approval (target: 0)

## Initial proof already completed
Issue #326 → PR #328 demonstrated autonomous cloud execution to verified PR: CI, Security, CodeQL and Responsive PASS; Vercel preview Ready; no merge/deploy.

## Safety
- no fake club data
- no takeover of SMM/content workflow
- no production deploy/DNS/nameserver changes without explicit Founder approval
- no big new dashboard/system until this trial proves the workflow
title: [P1 Ops] Run 72h Founder-absence autonomous execution trial

## Incident summary

Palmistry Path has exceeded the corporate 48-hour stall threshold on PP-RELAY-060 / PR #110.

- PR #110 remains open and mergeable at exact head `6456699258ea18a80142e5f53c8048ac310846f6`.
- Worker terminal result is `READY_FOR_REVIEW` and the task has already passed independent Director review.
- `main` still has `state.status = READY_FOR_CLAUDE` with no `approved_pr` / `approved_head_sha`.
- `relay-merge-gate` remains failing because the exact-SHA `MERGE_APPROVED` state write never landed.
- Branch rules require `relay-merge-gate`; the normal connected writer cannot bypass. A specific GitHub App/Integration is configured as a bypass actor.
- The Palmistry Codex Director workflow is still trapped in unmerged PR #111 and is Phase 1 observation-only, so it cannot mutate repository state even if installed.

## Root-cause hypothesis

The worker/review side is functioning; the missing consumer is the operational Director control-plane writer. Palmistry never completed the same Phase 2 controlled-autonomy installation that is active in Dead Zone Dash. The current normal GitHub writer is not the ruleset-bypass GitHub App identity required for the protected approval-state commit.

## Working-reference comparison

Dead Zone Dash has its Codex Director workflow on `main` with controlled write authority and explicit state/dispatch actions. Palmistry has only an observation-only workflow in PR #111.

## Bounded recovery plan

1. Preserve Palmistry source-sensitive/editorial governance and current branch protection.
2. Install a Palmistry Phase 2 controlled-autonomy Director on `main` through an approved bootstrap path.
3. Give the Director only the bounded repository-state authority needed for independent review, exact-SHA approval/rework, next-task selection, and worker dispatch.
4. Route protected `MERGE_APPROVED` state writes through the already-configured trusted GitHub App/Integration bypass identity rather than weakening rules.

## Strategic Improvement

The build loop currently uses a fixed default iteration cap regardless of issue complexity, causing simple issues to over-allocate iterations (wasted cost) and complex ones to hit exhaustion and restart unnecessarily. Using `shipwright decompose`'s existing complexity signal plus historical iteration-to-success counts from memory/events data lets the loop pick a starting iteration budget instead of a static default.

### Acceptance Criteria
- - New function reads past pipeline runs (`events.jsonl`) grouped by issue complexity bucket (already computed elsewhere, e.g. decompose/triage) and computes median iterations-to-success per bucket
- - Build loop's default `--max-iterations` is set from this computed value when historical data exists (minimum sample size threshold to avoid noisy estimates), falling back to the current static default otherwise
- - Computed value and fallback reason are logged to `progress.md` so a fresh session can see why the cap was chosen
- - Config override (`daemon-config.json` / env var) still takes precedence over the computed value
- - Unit tests cover: sufficient historical data, insufficient data (fallback), and missing events file (fallback)

### Context
- **Priority**: P2
- **Complexity**: standard
- **Generated by**: Strategic Intelligence Agent
- **Strategy alignment**: P2: Intelligence & Learning

This is an issue for discussing cool program ideas that may or may not be implemented (hence the name). 

I'll start with an idea from me.

--- 

I have an idea for a new text editor called `nate`: _nate's another text editor._

`nate` isn't like most text editors:

* It's educational, so you can teach it in 30 minutes and implement it in 60 minutes
* It's versatile, so you can read editing scripts from a file or pipe them from a program for automated edits
* It's memorizable, so each command comes with a mnemonic that lets you remember how to use `nate` long after learning it for the first time

Here's what I'm thinking for the commands (subject to change in the future):

Line commands:
| Command    | Purpose | Mnemonic |
| -------- | ------- | ------- |
| `sl`    | Select a line by number; if the line doesn't exist and follows an existing one, create it    | **S**elect **L**ine |
| `fl`    | Find the first instance of a string and select the associated line    | **F**ind **L**ine |
| `al`    | Append an empty line and select it  | **A**ppend **L**ine |
| `aml`    | Append a multi-line string ending in `<END>`  | **A**ppend **M**ulti-**L**ine string|
| `dl`    | Delete the selected line; if there is a previous line, select that one instead  | **D**elete **L**ine |
| `pl`    | Print the selected line  | **P**rint **L**ine |

File operations:
| Command    | Purpose | Mnemonic |
| -------- | ------- | ------- |
| `wf`  | Write to a file  | **W**rite **F**ile |
| `lf` | Load from a file     | **L**oad **F**ile |

Misc. commands:

| Command    | Purpose | Mnemonic |
| -------- | ------- | ------- |
| `h`  | Show help information   | **H**elp |
| `q` | Exit `nate`     | **Q**uit |

It's meant to be simple enough that you can write an implementation in almost any language, but for starters I intend on writing it in Nim.

Edit: Added the `sl` command!

Edit 2: The tables above are outdated. See https://git.hermits.cc/PPPDUD/nate-specs for the latest information.

Master journal: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1wYeFB-Ia6LVP5vK7IAPG_Bymn1dsD5y3bMco9mnYSmo/edit

## Source of truth
- Live GitHub `main`, exact PR heads, reviews and GitHub Actions are technical truth.
- Drive is the human-readable routing/report/handoff mirror, not code or CI authority.
- Before every cycle, every worker rereads live `main`, `AGENTS.md`, binding docs, this issue, Issue #1, open PRs/branches/claims and current Actions.
- `СТАРТ` and `ПРОДОВЖУЙ` never authorize reuse of a stale snapshot.

## Hard ownership rules
- One production writer per source slice.
- Every source-changing cycle MUST post a unique `CLAIM` here before mutation and then reread current claims.
- Separate branch per lane. No unrelated branch stacking.
- Shared-contract edits require an explicit compatibility decision.
- If another active owner already owns the same source or root defect, yield, audit, route, or choose another independent slice. Do not fork a competing production implementation.
- Existing current candidate/repair lineage is preferred over a new implementation.
- REUSE -> ADAPT -> CUSTOM(thin).

## Communication markers
Every worker uses these markers in comments when applicable:

`[NIKA-P10:<ROLE>:CLAIM]`
`[NIKA-P10:<ROLE>:HANDOFF]`
`[NIKA-P10:<ROLE>:RECOMMENDATION_TO:<ROLE>]`
`[NIKA-P10:<ROLE>:DEPENDENCY_REQUEST_TO:<ROLE>]`
`[NIKA-P10:<ROLE>:DEPENDENCY_READY_FOR:<ROLE>]`
`[NIKA-P10:<ROLE>:AUDIT_REQUEST]`
`[NIKA-P10:<ROLE>:BLOCKED]`
`[NIKA-P10:<ROLE>:CYCLE_REPORT]`

A CLAIM must contain exact starting main, intended branch, owned files/root defect, existing PR/successor being reused, and collision decision.

## Mandatory cycle report
No report = cycle is NOT complete. Every cycle, including read-only/audit/blocked cycles, MUST end with a comment here and a matching entry in that worker's Drive log. Report:
- exact starting main SHA;
- role/lane;
- branch and PR, or `NO_SOURCE_MUTATION`;
- what was done and why it is the highest-value unowned coherent batch;
- REUSE/ADAPT/CUSTOM decision;
- changed files and shared contracts;
- tests/checks actually executed;

# Autonomous roadmap — stabilize core before scaling

The product is still in test mode with only part of the future manager/source pool connected. Immediate goal: remove software/state/routing/notification/dialogue defects and simplify the architecture so adding managers and traffic later does not multiply edge cases.

## Autopilot rules
- Prioritize real live conversations, handoffs and user requests over commit history.
- Confirm a defect from evidence where possible; otherwise add diagnostics/tests first.
- Safe reversible flow: branch → PR → required CI → merge only when green → verify production SHA, migrations, smoke/health and relevant live behavior.
- Do not make unrelated changes or edit other AnyTour projects from this roadmap.
- Do not silently enable off-shift managers, auto-assign conversations or add aggressive SLA escalation during test mode.
- Stop only for irreversible/high-risk decisions, missing secrets/credentials or unresolved product decisions.
- Prefer eliminating a class of bugs over adding another one-off guard when repeated live evidence points to the same architectural weakness.

# Milestone 1 — Dialogue Core Stabilization
Goal: make dirty input, repeated callbacks and natural text predictable before scaling traffic.

## 1A. Interaction safety
- [x] Existing live fixes for stale/concurrent date, month, forward wizard and edit-menu callbacks (#88/#102/#103/#109/#113).
- [x] Shared `InteractionGuard` foundation (#114): callback lock paths, duplicate-window checks, recent-burst checks and forward-step expectations are centralized without changing current behavior.

- [x] Move remaining callback-safety decisions behind the shared guard instead of adding per-action lock/debounce implementations. Known direct action-owned file-lock/timestamp paths are centralized through #637; future additions remain evidence-driven.
- [x] Add callback generation/version support so buttons rendered by an older interaction can be rejected generically after state changes. Final-check surface generation shipped in #633.
- [x] Extend structured suppression reason to obsolete generation once that path exists. `obsolete_generation` shipped in #633.

## 1B. Formal dialogue state machine
- [x] Canonical wizard states and forward/back/edit/reset transition rules are defined in `DialogueStateMachine` (#115), including conditional child-age flow and current AI missing-field behavior.
- [x] Forward callback status expectations in `InteractionGuard` now resolve through the canonical state machine instead of a duplicate status map (#115).

## Problem

The relay seeds `sender_state.next_expected_nonce` from Hiro on first contact, then advances it only from relay-observed confirmations/recovery paths. If a publisher account later submits its own transactions outside the relay, the relay's sender frontier can remain stale low indefinitely.

Observed failure mode:
- Publisher account true next nonce: `140`
- Hiro `last_executed_tx_nonce`: `139`
- Relay `sender_state.next_expected_nonce`: `94`
- Relay keeps reporting a sender gap starting at `94` and never converges

This creates a deadlock for sender accounts that mix relay-sponsored traffic with direct/local publishing.

## Current Behavior

Relevant code paths:
- `seedSenderState()` seeds once from Hiro and returns early if a row already exists
- `getHandGapInfo()` uses cached `sender_state.next_expected_nonce` as the sender frontier
- `checkWouldDispatch()` / `checkAndAssignRun()` treat any higher nonce as a gap relative to that cached frontier
- `/sponsor` uses `mode: "immediate"`, so gap cases are rejected without queueing
- `/relay` may queue/hold, but the stale frontier itself is not repaired

Net effect: once a sender is seeded, normal external nonce advancement is invisible unless the relay later observes confirmations that explicitly call `advanceSenderNonce()`.

## Why This Is A Bug

This is not just caller misuse. The relay currently has no sender-side resync path for normal `seeded_from = "hiro"` rows. There is a retry reseed path only for `seeded_from = "first_tx"`, which does not help with ordinary stale-low sender state.

That means a valid sender can become permanently blocked from sponsored submission after using the same account outside the relay.

## Constraints

We do not want to fix this by querying Hiro on every request:
- extra latency on the hot path
- higher Hiro query volume
- Hiro responses may be inconsistent across load-balanced backends

The relay's hand/queue model is still useful because it provides stable local sequence evidence.

## Proposed Fix

Add an alarm-driven stale-sender recovery path for held sender hands.

### High-level strategy

- Keep the current hot path for normal submissions.
- Do not query Hiro inline on every sender gap.
- When a sender hand has been held long enough, evaluate whether the cached sender frontier is probably stale low.
- Use a single Hiro nonce query as a forward hint, bounded by the local hand sequence.
- If safe, bump `sender_state.next_expected_nonce` forward and immediately retry dispatch.

### Repair trigger

During the alarm sweep, inspect senders with non-empty held hands and only consider repair when:
- hold age exceeds a threshold, e.g. 30-90s
- sender was not refreshed recently (cooldown)
- hand shape suggests stale-low cache rather than an active low-nonce recovery

Examples of useful local signals:
- all held entries are far above `next_expected_nonce`
- hand contains a dense/contiguous cluster at a much higher nonce
- no entries exist near the old frontier

### Single-query repair rule

For a candidate sender:
1. Fetch Hiro `/extended/v1/address/:addr/nonces` once
2. Let `lowestHeldNonce` be the lowest nonce currently in `sender_hand` at or above the cached frontier
3. Compute `safeTarget = min(hiro.possible_next_nonce, lowestHeldNonce)`
4. If `safeTarget > next_expected_nonce`, update:

```ts
next_expected_nonce = safeTarget
```

Important properties:
- monotonic only: never move sender frontier backward
- bounded by local hand evidence: never skip past a locally unseen range
- single Hiro query only on aged held hands, not on every request

Examples:
- Hiro=140, lowestHeld=140, cached=94 => bump to 140
- Hiro=145, lowestHeld=140, cached=94 => bump to 140
- Hiro=100, lowestHeld=140, cached=94 => bump to 100 only if we decide that is acceptable, or do nothing if we require Hiro to reach the local floor
- Hiro=94, lowestHeld=140, cached=94 => do nothing

I recommend the conservative variant:
- only bump when `hiro.possible_next_nonce >=

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ram0verflow/ram0verflow.git rofl && cd rofl
python3 wallet.py new
python3 miner.py --miner YOUR_GITHUB_HANDLE --message "gm"
```

Standard library only — no dependencies. Mining runs on your machine; this workflow only checks the answer.

Your GitHub handle is hashed into the block header, which seeds your puzzles. Nobody can submit your block as their own, and a solution copied out of this thread answers a question only its author was asked.

## Parent

## What to build

实例部署门槛与真实基座 smoke（spec #15 里程碑 M0 六条 + M4；范围随 ADR-0005 平台迁移改写，原「zzeshell 单节点 8 卡 + 多节点 RCCL + 跨 sbatch」作废）。在曙光云 SothisAI DCU 实例（BW/gfx936、4×64GB、DTK 26.04）上执行：

**M0 六条开工前门槛**：

1. DTK 环境 `import torch` 通过（source DTK 后）；钉 `numpy==1.26.4`，装 ML 依赖后回验
2. BW（gfx936，64GB/卡）上 bf16 autocast + fp32 master 生效（profile 验证 dtype）
3. 单实例 4 卡 RCCL allreduce 正常（FSDP 分片 + 梯度同步）
4. G=12 × 30 步轨迹 + MGAI 终点的实际显存（64GB/卡）实测；不够则降 G 或逐 k 释放
5. rollout 吞吐 profile（真正绑定项）：单实例 4 rank 的每 iter wall-clock，确认三组实验 wall-clock 预算（已定决策：iteration 数 200–500 不动，接受 wall-clock ×2）
6. 实例冒烟脚本一键跑通（双 source + hy-smi + `torchrun --nproc_per_node=4` + import 回验）——脚本由 #34 入仓

**M4**（依赖 T04–T09 fixture 施工）：FSDP + 判别器 DDP + barrier；G=12 显存实测；真实基座开工门槛两项——噪声注入 sanity（扰动 + ODE 续跑分布 vs 原模型、η=0 对照）与组内 reward 方差检查（组1/组2 各自 G 方向 std 非零）。

需集群访问（`sugon-bootstrap` skill；SSH 端口随实例变，从平台控制台实例页取）。产物与 checkpoint 只落 `/root/private_data` 持久分区，绝不落易失系统盘。

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] M0 六条全部通过并留档（冒烟脚本一键可重复执行）
- [ ] 4 卡 RCCL allreduce 正常（FSDP + 判别器 DDP）
- [ ] G=12 × 30 步轨迹显存实测落盘（64GB/卡内达标；不达标则降 G 或逐 k 释放的结论落盘）
- [ ] rollout 吞吐 profile 报告落盘（4 rank 每 iter wall-clock、train:rollout 比例、三组实验 wall-clock 预算结论）
- [ ] 真实基座噪声注入 sanity 与组1/组2 组内 reward 方差检查通过
- [ ] 续训跨实例重启恢复实测一次（checkpoint 从持久分区恢复，轨迹与指标可复现）

- #24, #34

## Background

共享中心的 Redis 被通用 KV 前缀枚举接口当作有序 KV 使用。跨地域访问把权限检查中的重复枚举延迟放大到语音边界处理，普通 Realtime 对话也受到影响。业务服务将 owner、名称和关联关系编码在 key 中，难以使用关系数据库索引、约束和事务。

本 Issue 直接拥有存储 contract 切换：共享中心保留 Redis，业务列表转为 SQL 查询，实时输入不逐轮等待远程权限查询。独立的 Provider 消息组装修复由原生子 Issue #1128 拥有；通用 E2E 工具与 SDK 测试客户端生命周期由原生子 Issue #1129 拥有。它们是本次最终验收的依赖，不把这些实现混入存储 ownership。

## Goal

- 删除未使用的 Agent Memory、Recall 和 KV Graph，保留正在使用的 Flowcraft Memory。
- 将实时权限判断改为连接本地快照与后台刷新；进入或切换 Workspace 必须重新准入。
- KV 只保留精确记录、明确集合、有序范围及原子条件更新；彻底删除通用 List/ListAfter 和扫描恢复。
- Workspace、RuntimeProfile、ProviderTenant、Contact、Voice、Model、Credential、Gameplay Catalog、PeerRun、Workflow、Firmware、MemoryLayout、Toolkit 和 Flowcraft State 使用业务 SQL 表与统一连接。
- 保留必要业务列表、Admin 本机 Peer 列表、对象存储与 Memory 检索，验证跨服务器索引一致性和撤权行为。

### Non-goals

不更换共享 Redis 中心，不新增 HSet，不保留旧存储格式兼容、迁移或双写；数据库按新结构初始化。部署、数据导入和合并由维护者另行安排。

## Code Changes Tree

以下列出本 Issue 的存储 ownership 与受影响调用边界。各业务 service 的 SQL 表、查询和同目录单测一起交付；独立 Provider 和通用测试工具的具体改动树分别由 #1128、#1129 定义。

```text
pkgs/agent/memory/ (delete) # 删除未接入正式链路的旧 Memory 包及专属测试文档
pkgs/agent/recall/ (delete) # 删除旧 Recall 包及专属测试文档
pkgs/store/graph/ (delete) # 删除 KV Graph 实现及专属测试文档
pkgs/store/kv/kv.go # 将 Store contract 限定为精确记录、集合、有序范围及原子 mutation
pkgs/store/kv/sets.go # 定义成员操作、条件及记录和索引的原子 mutation
pkgs/store/kv/sets_redis.go # 用 Redis Set 与 Lua 实现条件原子更新
pkgs/store/kv/sets_badger.go # 用事务维护独立成员命名空间
pkgs/store/kv/sets_sql.go # 用成员关系表和事务维护集合一致性
pkgs/store/kv/sets_memory.go # 实现进程内集合与 mutation 语义
pkgs/store/kv/sets_prefix.go # 对集合和 mutation key 应用同一前缀隔离
pkgs/store/kv/ordered.go # 实现精确有序集合的有界查询
pkgs/store/stores.go # 向业务服务借出统一 SQL 连接
cmd/internal/server/server.go # 为业务服务注入 SQL DB，共享记录继续注入 KV
pkgs/gizclaw/peer_input_permissions.go # 管理权限快照、刷新、过期、撤权及 worker 生命周期
pkgs/gizclaw/peer_input_permissions_test.go # 验证慢查询、逐轮零查询和撤权边界
pkgs/gizclaw/peer_manager_sfu.go # 普通 Workspace 先本地分类，SFU 使用精确绑定索引
pkgs/gizclaw/internal/socialutil/workspace_locator.go # 精确定位 Workspace ID 与名称绑定
pkgs/gizclaw/services/runtime/peer/store_ops.go # SN/IMEI 集合与 Peer 记录条件原子更新
pkgs/gizclaw/services/runtime/peerrun/directory.go # 从本机 SQL 目录分页查询 Admin Peer
pkgs/gizclaw/services/system/apikey/server.go # 独立 Key 记录与 owner 集合原子维护
pkgs/gizclaw/services/social/friend/admin_index.go # 分片有序好友管理索引

pkgs/gizclaw/services/system/pendingdeletion/kv_index.go # 按状态和到期时间查询分片删除索引
pkgs/gizclaw/services/ai/workspace/sql_records.go # Workspace 身份、owner/name 唯一性和标签关系表

pkgs/gizclaw/services/system/runtimeprofile/sql.go # Profile、owner 绑定和注册 token 表与索引

pkgs/gizclaw/services/gameplay/workspace_reward_sql.go # 在共享连接上复用奖励事务
pkgs/gizclaw/services/runtime/peerrun/server.go # Peer 状态与 Agent 选择业务列

pkgs/gizclaw/services/runtime/flowstate/store.go # owner/workspace/agent/context 状态表及退役隔离

```

## 目的

Crownless を、スケジュール実行するAIエージェントが自分で次の遊びを考え、Issue化し、実装まで進める「自律プロダクト開発」のPOCとして記録する。

将来の出版・振り返りで、単なるGit履歴では分からない **AIが何を考え、なぜそれを選び、人間がどこで介入したか** を一次資料として残す。

このIssueは実装タスクではなく、実験ログの正本として扱う。原則closeせず、各自律開発サイクルをコメントで追記する。

## 各サイクルで残す内容

### 1. Cycle
- 実行日時（Asia/Tokyo）
- 起動種別: scheduled / human-triggered
- 対象main SHA（取得できる場合）

### 2. AI proposal
- 直近3〜5サイクルで新しい遊びが増えたか
- 新機能候補3案
- 各候補の4軸スコア
  - プレイヤーが気づく変化
  - 新しい判断
  - リプレイ性
  - Canonとの整合

### 3. Decision
- 今回選んだIssue / 新規アイデア
- なぜそれを選んだか
- 他候補を選ばなかった主な理由
- bug-fix / maintenance / innovation の区分

### 4. Execution
- 新規Issue / 既存Issue
- 実装した縦切り
- PR / commit
- test / CI
- merge / close結果

### 5. Human intervention
前回サイクル以降、人間による方向修正がGitHub上または実行コンテキストから確認できる場合に記録する。

例:
- 新しいIssueを人間が追加した
- AI案を却下・修正した
- 優先順位を変更した
- 実装済み機能の作り直しを指示した
- 直接エージェントへ割り込んだ

介入が確認できなければ `なし / 確認できず` とし、推測で人間介入を作らない。

### 6. Outcome / observation
- プレイヤーから見て何が変わったか
- 新しい遊び・判断が増えたか
- AIの判断で気になった点
- 次回観察したいこと

## 記録原則

- 事実とAIの評価を分ける
- 後から書き換えず、原則コメントを追加して時系列を保つ
- Issue/PR/commitへリンクできる情報を残す
- 長い実装ログやCI全文は複製せず、意思決定に必要な要約だけを残す
- 人間介入は確認できたものだけを記録し、推測しない
- 成功だけでなく、`no_action`、失敗、誤った提案、revert、方向修正も残す

## このPOCで検証したい問い

> AIは、与えられたIssueを消化するだけでなく、自分で「次に何を作るべきか」を考え、ゲームを継続的に面白くできるか。

> 人間は常時開発ループを回さず、必要なときだけIssue追加や直接指示で介入する運用へ移れるか。

Related: #228
title: POC: AI自律開発の意思決定・人間介入ログ

# English

## HER Hack-Astron #5 | Spark-X2.5 Edge Agent Real-World Use Case Challenge

Turn real Spark-X2.5 runs into reproducible, discussable edge-agent use cases.

For this challenge, obtain XHToken/Spark-X2.5-4B or Spark-X2.5-1.7B from Hugging Face (or a mirror such as ModelScope), conduct a real inference, agentic, coding, long-context, multilingual, quantization, or training experiment, and publish the complete use case in the corresponding model's Hugging Face Discussions. After publishing it, reply to this event's GitHub Issue with the Discussion link to enter.

- Event page (GitHub Issues): https://github.com/XHToken/Spark-X2.5/issues
- Hugging Face model collection: https://huggingface.co/collections/XHToken/spark-x25
- Spark-X2.5-4B: https://huggingface.co/XHToken/Spark-X2.5-4B
- Spark-X2.5-1.7B: https://huggingface.co/XHToken/Spark-X2.5-1.7B
- Spark-X2.5-4B Discussions: https://huggingface.co/XHToken/Spark-X2.5-4B/discussions
- Spark-X2.5-1.7B Discussions: https://huggingface.co/XHToken/Spark-X2.5-1.7B/discussions
- Mainland China mirror (recommended): https://www.modelscope.cn/collections/XHToken/Spark-X25

## Schedule

- Submissions open: September 1, 2026
- Challenge period: September 1–6, 2026
- Submission deadline: September 6, 2026, 24:00 Beijing Time (UTC+8)
- Judging and award distribution: September 7–13, 2026

## Challenge Tracks

Choose one track or combine several:

- Official Quick Start reproduction: deploy with vLLM / SGLang / llama.cpp, run locally with Ollama / LM Studio, and test structured output and tool parsing (`--tool-call-parser spark25`)
- Agentic workflows: integrate with harnesses such as Codex, Claude Code, OpenClaw, or Hermes to complete multi-step tool use, planning, and automation tasks
- Coding: complete real repository-level fixes, programming contest / online judge tasks, or end-to-end coding-agent runs
- Long context: use the native 1M context window for long-document Q&A, codebase understanding, or long-range retrieval
- Multilingual: test understanding, generation, or translation across 200+ languages, or demonstrate a real multilingual business scenario
- Edge efficiency and hardware adaptation: 4B/1.7B quantization (GGUF), throughput, TTFT/TPOT, VRAM/RAM use, or adaptation to NVIDIA / Ascend / Hygon / HOUMO.AI and other hardware
- Instruction following and reasoning: evaluate complex instructions, format compliance, mathematics, or reasoning tasks with real tests
- Safety boundaries: examine high-risk actions, unauthorized tool calls, ambiguity detection, confirmation steps, and safe refusal
- Data and training: use legally obtained data, mine hard examples, or run SFT/RL with LLaMA-Factory and report before-and-after comparisons
- Comparative evaluation: compare Spark-X2.5 with larger models, rule-based systems, or other open models of a similar size under the same methodology

## How to Submit

1. Spark-X2.5 is licensed under Apache 2.0 and requires no additional usage agreement. Follow the repository's CODE_OF_CONDUCT and SECURITY policies.
2. Install and sign in with the official Hugging Face CLI:

       pip install -U huggingface_hub
       hf auth login

3. Download and record a pinned revision:

       hf download XHToken/Spark-X2.5-4B --revision <commit-sha>

   Participants in Mainland China may use ModelScope / Modelers / SCNet / SourceFind mirrors. State the source and revision used.

4. Complete a real experiment and retain publishable run logs, inputs, raw outputs, environment details, and screenshots.

`bp task get <slug>` returns HTTP 500 `internal_error` for every doc_id that exists in more than one dataset. Eleven task rows are in that state today, and they are **unreachable through the entire `bp task` verb surface** — not just `get`, but `claim`, `close` and `stage` too. They cannot be read, adjudicated, or closed by any agent.

## How it was found

The parent/child coherence audit (2026-08-23) needed to close `akbr-feedback-2026-08-epic` — a genuine "open parent, all children done" row (0 own acceptance criteria, 18/18 children done). Every `bp task` call against it 500s, so the close could not be performed. That is the concrete cost: a correct ledger fix is blocked by a resolver bug.

## Reproduction

```
bp task get akbr-feedback-2026-08-epic       # 500 internal_error, every time
bp task get akbr-10-marina-side              # 500
bp task get drafts.stw1-basepath-redirect-fix # 500
bp task get onix-quality-goal                # 200 — control, unique slug
```

**Interleaved A/B, 56 reads in one window** (alternating duplicate and unique slugs, never sequenced, because guerrilla is concurrently serving intermittent 500s on `task-d89e42ea727bffb7` and a sequenced test would not separate the two):

```
DUPLICATE-slug reads: 28 total, 28 non-200  (100% fail)
UNIQUE-slug    reads: 28 total,  0 non-200  (  0% fail)
```

The two failures are also **different error classes**, which settles it independently of the rates:

- duplicate slug → `internal_error: unknown error (Ecto.MultipleResultsError)`
- the live incident → `internal_error: unknown error (DBConnection.ConnectionError)`

`Ecto.MultipleResultsError` is `Repo.one/2` raising because the query matched more than one row. This is deterministic and structural, not the flake.

Writes fail identically: `bp task claim akbr-feedback-2026-08-epic parent-child-audit --yes` → `server error (GM6OPmg3YVymY28AAKAh)`. `--dry-run` shows the CLI posting to `/v1/tasks/akbr-feedback-2026-08-epic/claim`, i.e. the slug is sent bare with no dataset qualifier.

## Cause

`/v1/tasks/:doc_id` resolves the row by `doc_id` alone with no dataset filter, through a `Repo.one/2`. When two datasets hold the same `doc_id` the query returns two rows and `Repo.one/2` raises `Ecto.MultipleResultsError`, which surfaces as a bare 500. Nothing disambiguates and nothing refuses honestly. `bp task get` exposes no `--dataset` escape hatch (`bp task get <slug> --dataset production` and `-d production` both still 500), and the UUID `id` is not accepted either (`not_found`).

## The eleven affected rows

Ten are `aker-brygge` ↔ `production` twins:

| doc_id | datasets | status |
|---|---|---|
| `akbr-feedback-2026-08-epic` | aker-brygge, production | open / open |
| `akbr-01-forside-mobil-kort-overflow` | aker-brygge, production | done / done |
| `akbr-02-oversikt-default-restaurant` | aker-brygge, production | done / done |
| `akbr-03-oversikt-karusell-mobil` | aker-brygge, production | done / done |
| `akbr-04-hva-skjer-kortdesign` | aker-brygge, production | done / done |
| `akbr-05-tekstboks-luft` | aker-brygge, production | done / done |
| `akbr-06-artikkelbilder-layout` | aker-brygge, production | done / done |
| `akbr-07-midtstilling-seksjon` | aker-brygge, production | done / done |
| `akbr-09-kontakt-oss-bokser` | aker-brygge, production | done / done |
| `akbr-10-marina-side` | aker-brygge, production | done / done |

The eleventh is a `production` ↔ `tasks` twin: `drafts.stw1-basepath-redirect-fix` (cancelled / cancelled).

## Why it matters

`bp task ls --all` happily returns all 7,486 rows including both twins, so these rows are VISIBLE to every audit and board but ADDRESSABLE by nothing. An auditor finds them, judges them, and then cannot act. `akbr-feedback-2026-08-epic` has sat open since 2026-08-06 with all its work done purely because it cannot be closed.

Note this is distinct from the ghost-slug orphan defect on `task-ea8e58e4d10519b4` (children pointing at an unpublished bare slug). Both ar

## Diagnosis scope

Read-only review of the published `z-audio-production` and `z-video-production` skills, plus Rocky and Vivian live media capability and runtime checks. No production configuration or skill changes were made.

## Verified current state

- GitHub audio release: `f1ae3b1`; video release: `ebc8310`.
- Rocky and Vivian installed `SKILL.md` copies match those GitHub versions.
- Both run OpenClaw `2026.8.2`, have FFmpeg/FFprobe, and have an installed Remotion project with dependencies.
- Both have a live Percify connector exposing 11 tools.
- Vivian routes native video to `openrouter/google/veo-3.1-fast`, with `openai/sora-2` fallback and a 180-second timeout.
- Rocky routes native video to `xai/grok-imagine-video`, with no fallback and a 600-second timeout.
- Percify exposes roughly 70 video models, reusable voice routes, InfiniteTalk lip-sync, and saved Zeke/Maggie avatars with voice attached where configured.

## Findings

- The approved dry-master and scene-extract rules already address voice drift and spillover into the next scene, but they are not enforced by automation.
- The video skill already says to add exact text, captions, logos, prices, and calls to action in an editable composition. Generated pixels should not be trusted for exact text.
- Vivian's native Veo route is expected to produce 4/6/8-second clips. A 30-second Reel must be assembled from clips and other media; it should not be requested as one generation.
- Slow generation remains normal provider behavior. OpenClaw's async task ledger should reduce the old wait/retry failure pattern, but a paid end-to-end proof was not run during this diagnosis.
- The skills do not explicitly require structured attachment delivery, an exact requested-output check, or a saved scene/job ledger. Those gaps explain link-only audio, image/audio substitution when video was requested, and repeated retries.
- The Remotion project is an assembly template, not a polished motion-design system. Bland slideshow motion will remain until reusable branded motion components are added.

## Recommended change package — approval required

- Add a strict output contract to both skills: requested media type must be delivered, saved locally, and attached with a structured media field; a plain URL is backup only.
- Add a scene manifest/job ledger and helper that cuts exact audio from the approved master, records provider job IDs/status, downloads results, and prevents duplicate paid retries.
- Add three tested production profiles: talking-avatar scene, realistic B-roll/hero clip, and stock/screen-recording scene.
- Upgrade the Remotion project with branded captions, lower thirds, title cards, logo/CTA screens, and better motion/transitions.
- Run one controlled Rocky proof and one Vivian proof using the same short brief, then choose model presets by quality, cost, and turnaround.

## Status

Diagnosis complete. Implementation awaits Jack's confirmation under Diagnose Mode.

One of the most important questions that a visualization attempts to answer is, "Compared to what?" Comparisons are at the heart of understanding quantitative information. To help with easy comparison, we do one or more of the following:

1. Translate -- Apply appropriate measurement scales to comprehend the data. Raw numbers to percentages, time into years, months, days, hours, minutes or seconds, lengths/distances into cms, mts or kms, areas into sq.units, volumes, weights, temperatures, and so on. Negative & log scales.
2. Transform -- Convert measurement scales into something more familiar & relatable to the reader.

# Proposals ledger

**This issue is never built.** It is infrastructure: the durable home for
improvement proposals between the report that raises one and the call that
decides it. It is held — assigned and labelled — so no unattended loop picks it
up, and it stays open permanently. Do not close it, do not put it on the board,
and do not treat its comments as a queue.

## What lands here

An **improvement** — a hole, a gap, a could-be-better — is proposed, never
filed (`skills/review-discipline/SKILL.md` → *bugs are filed; improvements are
proposed*). A proposal is raised in a report's **Proposals** section and
appended here as one comment, so it survives the session that raised it.

One entry per comment:

- **The case**, in one line.
- **Provenance** — the ticket or session it came from.
- **Suggested home** — the file or surface the change would touch. An entry
  whose suggested home is `skills/review-discipline/references/craft.md` is a
  craft candidate; the admission call happens at the drain, not here.

## What happens to an entry

Entries **accumulate**. They are memory, explicitly not promises: nothing here
is scheduled, nothing auto-expires, and nothing is dropped for going unread.

`/digest` **surfaces** new entries since its window, one line each, and carries
no duty to decide them.

`/assess` **drains**: it reads the accumulation, groups and abstracts (several
minor entries may become one pattern-level candidate), prioritises, and puts a

# NIKA PERMANENT WORKERS CONTROL PLANE

Це канонічний координаційний issue для десяти постійних чат-воркерів Nika Core.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/13ShU1yQmQlgweXHZsO9njawB0g-m8-pL
Master journal: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1wYeFB-Ia6LVP5vK7IAPG_Bymn1dsD5y3bMco9mnYSmo/edit

## Source of truth
- Live GitHub `main`, exact PR heads, reviews and GitHub Actions are technical truth.
- Drive is the human-readable routing/report/handoff mirror, not code or CI authority.
- Before every cycle, every worker rereads live `main`, `AGENTS.md`, binding docs, this issue, Issue #1, open PRs/branches/claims and current Actions.
- `СТАРТ` and `ПРОДОВЖУЙ` never authorize reuse of a stale snapshot.

## Hard ownership rules
- One production writer per source slice.
- Every source-changing cycle MUST post a unique `CLAIM` here before mutation and then reread current claims.
- Separate branch per lane. No unrelated branch stacking.
- Shared-contract edits require an explicit compatibility decision.
- If another active owner already owns the same source or root defect, yield, audit, route, or choose another independent slice. Do not fork a competing production implementation.
- Existing current candidate/repair lineage is preferred over a new implementation.
- REUSE -> ADAPT -> CUSTOM(thin).

## Communication markers
Every worker uses these markers in comments when applicable:

`[NIKA-P10:<ROLE>:CLAIM]`
`[NIKA-P10:<ROLE>:HANDOFF]`
`[NIKA-P10:<ROLE>:RECOMMENDATION_TO:<ROLE>]`
`[NIKA-P10:<ROLE>:DEPENDENCY_REQUEST_TO:<ROLE>]`
`[NIKA-P10:<ROLE>:DEPENDENCY_READY_FOR:<ROLE>]`
`[NIKA-P10:<ROLE>:AUDIT_REQUEST]`
`[NIKA-P10:<ROLE>:BLOCKED]`
`[NIKA-P10:<ROLE>:CYCLE_REPORT]`

A CLAIM must contain exact starting main, intended branch, owned files/root defect, existing PR/successor being reused, and collision decision.

## Mandatory cycle report
No report = cycle is NOT complete. Every cycle, including read-only/audit/blocked cycles, MUST end with a comment here and a matching entry in that worker's Drive log. Report:
- exact starting main SHA;
- role/lane;
- branch and PR, or `NO_SOURCE_MUTATION`;
- what was done and why it is the highest-value unowned coherent batch;
- REUSE/ADAPT/CUSTOM decision;
- changed files and shared contracts;
- tests/checks actually executed;
- exact candidate head and exact GitHub Actions truth;
- independent audit/review truth;
- merge/integration truth;
- blockers/dependencies and explicit routed recommendations to other roles;
- current product capability gained on integrated main, not merely candidate code;
- what remains unverified;
- `HUMAN_TESTED` truth;
- `NVDA_VERIFIED` truth;
- next highest-value coherent batch.

If Drive write is temporarily unavailable, the GitHub report is still mandatory and must state `DRIVE_REPORT_BLOCKED=true`. If GitHub reporting/claiming is unavailable, do not begin a new source mutation that lacks a durable visible claim.

## Review and integration protocol
- Developers do not self-award independent audit clearance.
- Peer review is read-only by default; reviewers post findings/recommendations and do not edit the owner's branch unless an explicit ownership handoff is accepted.
- New QA_ONLY branches are allowed only for materially new exact-parent attack families. Never duplicate an existing equivalent oracle.
- QA_ONLY never merges as production.
- Integrator merges only exact-current, dependency-ready, audit-clear, non-QA candidates with unchanged expected head and required terminal green evidence.
- After every merge, integrator rereads `main`, Actions, ownership and dependent candidates before the next merge.
- Never weaken a gate to obtain green and never transfer GREEN from an older SHA.

## Safety / acceptance truth
- Least privilege and R0-R4 boundaries remain binding.
- No secrets, tokens, sessions, browser profiles, cookies or private logs in code, commits, reports or artifacts.
- Trader/Sportsbook work remains paper/research only; no real-money execution.
- Auto

Sub-issue of #7075 — DiT stage → Shared kernels and attention backends, **first item**.
Owner: @Jerry2423

## Scope

Files: [`mammothmoda2_dit_model.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/blob/main/vllm_omni/diffusion/models/mammoth_moda2/mammothmoda2_dit_model.py), [`pipeline_mammothmoda2_dit.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/blob/main/vllm_omni/diffusion/models/mammoth_moda2/pipeline_mammothmoda2_dit.py).

- **Config update.** Thread `quant_config` and `prefix` from the pipeline through `Transformer2DModel` into `TransformerBlock` and its submodules, following the Wan2.2 transformer. Neither constructor accepts them today, so no vLLM parallel or quantized linear can be built inside the DiT. No numerics change.
- **RMSNorm.** Replace `transformers.Qwen2RMSNorm` with the shared `vllm_omni.diffusion.layers.norm.RMSNorm` at all construction sites.
- **Merged gate/up + SiluAndMul.** In `LuminaFeedForward`, fuse the gate and up projections into one `gate_up_proj` and replace the local `swiglu` with the shared `SiluAndMul`.
- **Weight loading.** Add the `stacked_params_mapping` for the merged projection. The pipeline loads through `AutoWeightsLoader`, whose generic path passes no shard id and so cannot merge two checkpoint tensors into one parameter; an explicit `load_weights` is the repo's standard fix. This changes the checkpoint key surface — `feed_forward.linear_1` / `linear_3` become `feed_forward.gate_up_proj` under `gen_transformer.*` and under both refiner layouts.

## Exclusions

- **Residual/modulation fusion.** No shared component to reuse. The shared `RMSNorm`'s fused add-then-norm exists only on NPU — on CUDA and ROCm it falls through to the native implementation. Fusing the remaining elementwise `tanh`-gated scale-and-add means writing a new kernel. If a new kernel is required, @Jerry2423 can also take up on that.
- Attention kernel, QKV layout, RoPE, and fused QK-norm/RoPE — those are #7094 (@MrlixiangWE). Only the QK norm modules are in scope here.

## PR breakdown

| PR | Content | Base | PR-ready | Target merge (UTC) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Config update | #7094 | 2026-09-09 | **2026-09-11** |
| 2 | RMSNorm | #7094 | 2026-09-10 | **2026-09-12** |
| 3 | Merged gate/up + SiluAndMul + weight loading | #7094 | 2026-09-15 | **2026-09-17** |

PR 1 is first because it is a prerequisite for @xRay2016's FP8 work and for DiT TP, and because it can carry a `prefix` into the shared attention layer while #7094 is still open. All three carry `Refs #7075`.

## Dependencies

**Blocking**

| Blocked | Depends on | Why |
|---|---|---|
| PR 1 | #7094 | Both edit `TransformerBlock.__init__`, where #7094 inserts the shared attention layer directly above the `LuminaFeedForward` and `LuminaRMSNormZero` constructions that PR 1 must pass the new arguments to. New arguments will be optional and appended so #7094's positional `TransformerBlock(...)` test constructions keep working. |
| PR 2 | #7094 | Rewrites `attn.norm_q` / `norm_k` and drops the `Qwen2RMSNorm` import, both inside #7094's hunks. |
| PR 3 | #7094 | No textual overlap — the edits are in `LuminaFeedForward` and the pipeline. Branched from it for the test package #7094 creates and for the A/B baseline. |
| @xRay2016 — online FP8 | PR 1 | Carries `quant_config` into the DiT constructors. Necessary, not sufficient: only `LuminaFeedForward` becomes quantizable, and only in PR 3. |
| DiT tensor parallelism (unowned) | PR 1 | Same. |
| #7094 passing a `prefix` to the shared attention layer | PR 1 | Gives each DiT attention a stable layer identity for KV-cache metadata and quantization scoping. Backend selection uses `role` / `role_category` and is independent of this. Improvement, not a blocker. |
| A later QKV merge in the attention path | PR 3 | Its rows go into the single `stacked_params_mapping` owned here, not a second `load_weights`. |

**Alignment**

- **@quan-yi-ai, @MrlixiangWE** — baseline commit and image-quality threshold. #7094 changes DiT at

Two Explorer nodes in `docs/Empire_Development_Tree_Final.json` pay the player
loot quantity for having removed days from a dungeon's run time. One of them
carries a cap and the other does not, and the uncapped one grows without bound
with dungeon depth.

| Node | Points | Text | Cap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Efficiency Premium | 1 (keystone) | "+5% Loot Quantity for every Day removed from default run time (cap 50%)." | **yes, 50%** |
| Speed Runner | 10 | "+5% bonus Loot Quantity per 2 days under default run time per point." | **none stated** |

## What that comes to

Found while checking, for
[#1383](https://github.com/sdubois777/Cataclysm/issues/1383), what each of the
two is worth under the shipped Explorer branch. The branch removes enough days
that a dungeon walks in one, so "days under default run time" is very nearly the
dungeon's whole floor count.

At 10 points Speed Runner gives +50% loot quantity for every 2 days under default
run time. Against `TREE_EXPLORER_AS_DESIGNED`'s flat 70:

| Dungeon | Walk | Days under default | Speed Runner |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8-floor Basic at an Outpost | 1 day | 7 | +150% |
| 20-floor Basic at a Bulwark | 1 day | 19 | +450% |
| 40-floor Basic at a Sanctuary | 1 day | 39 | **+950%** |
| 125-floor earned Cataclysm dungeon | 55 days | 70 | **+1750%** |

Efficiency Premium reaches its 50% cap at 12 floors and stops. Speed Runner does
not stop.

## Why this looks like an oversight rather than a design

The two nodes do the same thing in the same branch, phrased almost identically,
and one has a cap written into its text while the other does not. A ten-point
basic node granting an order of magnitude more loot quantity than a keystone in
the same branch is also the wrong way round: keystones are supposed to be the
larger effect.

**It is not sensitive to how the walk-time reduction is shaped.** Under the
multiplicative shape proposed on
[#1383](https://github.com/sdubois777/Cataclysm/issues/1383) at x0.15 the same
40-floor dungeon still gives +850%, because most of the floor count is still
"under default run time" whatever shape the reduction takes. Whatever is ruled
there, this stays.

## What is needed

A ruling on whether Speed Runner should carry a cap, and if so what it is. It is
not fixed here because it is a balance decision on a design document rather than
a defect with an obvious repair, and because
[#1383](https://github.com/sdubois777/Cataclysm/issues/1383) is under an
instruction to change no tuning constant.

**Neither node is modelled, so no campaign figure is affected.**
`sim/cataclysm_sim/loot.py` does model loot quantity, but `EmpireTree` in
`sim/cataclysm_sim/config.py` has no loot field at all -- its eight fields are
`run_days_flat`, `run_days_mult`, `floor_delta`, `city_damage_mult`,
`city_health_mult`, `resolve_bonus_days`, `surge_bonus_days` and `name` -- so
nothing carries an empire tree's loot nodes into the loot model. No existing
measurement needs revisiting. The exposure is in the game, once Explorer loot
nodes are implemented.
title: Speed Runner has no cap where Efficiency Premium does, so it grants +950% loot quantity on a 40-floor dungeon

Parent: #2

## 研究目标

从关系科学、社会心理学、人格心理学、认知科学、神经科学、行为生物学、进化行为科学，以及已有 computational relationship / social simulation 项目中，寻找比日常语言更基础、更精确、可操作化的候选构念。

目标不是“把学术名词塞满表格”，而是回答：**哪些构念在理论与测量上足够独立，值得成为 LHRM primitive；哪些只是别的构念的指标、结果或高阶合成。**

## 重点方向

- attraction / incentive salience / reward valuation / attachment / bonding
- perceived partner responsiveness / trust / security / self-disclosure / intimacy
- commitment / investment / dependence / alternatives / interdependence
- similarity / complementarity / value congruence / goal alignment
- dominance / power / control / autonomy
- jealousy / mate guarding / exclusivity
- sexual desire / arousal / sociosexuality / sexual compatibility
- affective forecasting / ideal standards / revealed preference / preference construction
- uncertainty / belief update / expectation violation / deception detection
- synchrony / coordination / reciprocity / cooperation / conflict / repair
- costly signaling / resource investment / parental investment / caregiving
- familiarity / mere exposure / habituation / novelty / reward prediction error
- attachment-related and neurobiological constructs only when they improve semantic precision and have defensible measurement meaning

## 核心问题

1. 每个候选构念的**最小语义边界**是什么？
2. 哪些构念在人类语言里经常混为“爱、喜欢、投入、三观合、成熟、靠谱”？
3. 哪些构念统计上常高度相关，但理论上仍不能合并？哪些应直接合并/降级？
4. 哪些术语看似“更科学”，其实只是在更底层重复同一现象？
5. 年龄、收入、外貌、陪伴、花钱、学历、婚史等常见变量分别更可能是 primitive、proxy、constraint、state 还是 observation？
6. 找到适合 LHRM 的候选 latent variable，同时明确可由哪些现实观测反推。

## 方法要求

- 优先 meta-analysis、review、经典量表/理论、纵向研究、可重复测量构念；
- 对神经/生物术语保持克制，不能因为“多巴胺/催产素/脑区”听起来基础就自动升级为 primitive；只有当其比心理/行为层构念更有解释力和可测量价值时才保留；
- 对已有计算项目/agent-based model/relationship model，分析其状态变量设计和可复用抽象。

## 交付

提交 `RESEARCH_REPORT_SCIENTIFIC_RELATIONSHIP_PRIMITIVES.md`，按 #2 统一字段输出，并额外提供：

1. 候选 primitive 分层图；
2. `primitive / latent construct / observable proxy / derived outcome` 四类判定；
3. 易混淆构念对照表，例如 commitment vs investment、trust vs security、bond vs attachment、alignment vs similarity；
4. 建议合并/淘汰列表；
5. 至少 30 个日常代理词 → 学术构念映射；
6. 对当前 LHRM Relationship 候选维度（Attraction / Bond / Trust / Commitment / Alignment / Dependence）逐项做 KEEP / SPLIT / MERGE / REJECT 审查。

不要直接修改 canonical ontology。

# Misyra Development Ledger

This issue tracks the active implementation ticket and review state for Misyra. Development is performed as a single-agent, specification-driven workflow. GitHub history, the approved specifications, ticket acceptance criteria, tests, PR diffs, and verification evidence are authoritative.

## Authoritative sources

- `docs/specifications/product-specification.md`
- `docs/specifications/technical-specification.md`
- `docs/specifications/implementation-tickets.md`

The product specification is authoritative for user-facing behavior. The technical specification is authoritative for implementation architecture and engineering constraints. The implementation-ticket document defines dependency order, ticket scope, acceptance criteria, TDD evidence, and review gates.

## Development workflow

1. Read the exact active ticket and relevant product/technical specification sections from current `main` before modifying code.
2. Verify the required `main` base SHA and dependencies.
3. Work on exactly one ticket branch and one implementation PR at a time.
4. Use strict **RED → GREEN → REFACTOR → verification** for behavior/configuration changes.
5. Do not implement later-ticket scope.
6. Run focused and all affected format, lint, typecheck, test, build, audit, privacy, localization, infrastructure, and integration checks required by the ticket/specifications.
7. Review the actual PR diff and resolve every Important or Critical finding before merge.
8. Merge only through a PR after exact-head verification and review.
9. Record completion, then advance only to the next dependency-ready ticket.
10. Never deploy, activate production resources, introduce production credentials, mutate external providers, perform store submission, or make another gated external change without explicit user approval.
11. Preserve the approved specification documents and unrelated/user work.

## Repository protection

During the restart, `main` should use pull-request, branch-deletion, and non-fast-forward/force-push protections. Do not require legacy CI status contexts before **MTS-007 — Establish CI quality gates** creates stable checks.

## Goal
Implement a reproducible tabular Q-learning baseline for the deterministic 4×4 FrozenLake environment, the first step in the proposed learning path.

## Scope
- Use `FrozenLake-v1` with `map_name="4x4"` and `is_slippery=False`.
- Implement a Q-table, epsilon-greedy exploration, and the Bellman update without a reinforcement learning algorithm library.
- Separate training from evaluation and allow seeds and training hyperparameters to be configured.
- Handle episode termination and time-limit truncation correctly when computing learning targets.
- Document the environment, algorithm, dependencies, runnable commands, and observed results.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Training and evaluation can be reproduced using documented commands and seeds.
- [x] Evaluation uses a greedy policy without training updates and reports success rate and episode length.
- [x] Evaluation results are recorded for at least three training seeds and compared with a random-policy baseline.
- [x] Focused tests cover Q-learning targets, including terminal and truncated transitions.
- [x] Learned artifacts are saved under ignored output paths.

The learning path is a suggested educational sequence, not a delivery schedule or a list of completed implementations. This issue covers only the first environment.


## Acceptance verification

Implemented on [`codex/issue-2-frozenlake`](https://github.com/ruddyscent/gymnasium-playbook/tree/codex/issue-2-frozenlake) and merged in PR #4 as `35e65dbb3da53574df4fe4ae85a230a9b5aaf3fa`.

- **Reproducibility:** the [implementation README](https://github.com/ruddyscent/gymnasium-playbook/blob/35e65dbb3da53574df4fe4ae85a230a9b5aaf3fa/environments/toy_text/frozen_lake/README.md) documents locked uv setup, training, evaluation, seeds, and the three-seed benchmark. Repeatability tests pass.
- **Evaluation:** a separate greedy evaluator reports success rate and episode length; the regression test verifies that evaluation does not modify the Q-table.
- **Three seeds and baseline:** the [recorded results](https://github.com/ruddyscent/gymnasium-playbook/issues/2#issuecomment-5564941383) cover training seeds 0, 1, and 2. Each learned policy achieved 100% success with six mean steps; random policies achieved 1.5%, 1.2%, and 1.1%.
- **Learning targets:** all 14 regression tests passed again on September 7, 2026, including real terminal, time-limit truncation, and simultaneous termination/truncation transitions.
- **Artifacts:** default Q-tables, training histories, configuration, and benchmark reports are stored under `runs/frozen_lake/`; `git check-ignore` confirms the output path is ignored.

[PR CI](https://github.com/ruddyscent/gymnasium-playbook/actions/runs/34082553918) passed on Ubuntu 24.04, Windows 2022, and macOS 14 (Apple Silicon). This supersedes the earlier comment's pending-CI status. The full three-seed benchmark results were measured on macOS ARM64; CI checks environment smoke tests and regression tests, not the full benchmark or graphical replay on every platform.
title: feat: implement tabular Q-learning for FrozenLake

Run log for the cloud maintenance routines that maintain this repo (scheduled Claude Code agents, run by Anthropic — not on a dev machine). They mirror the set running against `pawellisowski/floless.app`, adapted to this repo's actual gates: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test`, on the pinned toolchain.

Every run posts one line here as its final action, **including runs that do nothing**. That is the point: these routines are designed to open no PR when there is nothing to fix, which makes a correct quiet run indistinguishable from a crashed one unless each run says so explicitly.

Each line records: date, which review ran, gate results, and either the PR opened or the reason none was.

**On the Codex rule.** CLAUDE.md §"PR review — non-negotiable" says Codex reviews first. Codex is not installed in the routine container and cannot be without an OpenAI credential in the environment plus egress that has not been tested. These routines therefore run the documented fallback — the local reviewer — and must say so explicitly on every PR rather than implying a cross-model pass happened. Cross-model review of routine PRs happens on the maintainer's machine, where Codex is installed.

**Nothing merges itself.** Every run ends at a reviewable PR against `main`, or at silence. Pushing and merging to `main` still require explicit approval, per CLAUDE.md §"Git workflow".

Close this issue only if the routines are retired.

**Eleven merges on `main` are squashed**, so eleven pull requests appear as one commit each rather than as the work that produced them: #67 (19 commits), #70, #72, #75, #77 (4), #84 (10), #98 (7), #102 (2), and three more. That is 11 of 215 commits, and the rest of the history is proper merges.

The rule this touches is the one with teeth: judges inspect commit history, and *"you cannot just have three commits with a million lines"* is a finalist-track disqualification. We are nowhere near that shape — 215 commits, 63 merges, small and frequent — but #67 and #84 in particular each hide double figures of real commits.

**The work is not lost.** Every head branch still exists and every original commit is fetchable from `refs/pull/N/head`, which is how I checked. A judge reading `git log` on `main` will not see them, and a judge reading the pull requests will.

Squash and rebase merging are **off** in the repository settings now, so this cannot grow. Three options, and this is Ghoza's call:

1. **Leave it.** The pull requests carry the detail, the history is otherwise clean, and eleven commits out of 215 is not the failure mode the rule describes.
2. **Restore the eleven**, by reverting each squash and re-merging its branch with a merge commit. No history is rewritten; `main` gains the real commits and eleven reverts. It is honest but noisy, and the noise is itself something a judge reads.
3. **Say it in the README** — one sentence pointing at the pull requests for the fine-grained history of those eleven.

We have two of our three partner slots spent: **Uniswap Foundation** ($3,000) and **Chainlink** ($2,000). This is the case for the third, read off the prize page rather than from memory, and measured against what Helico actually is with six days left.

One rule shapes everything below: **a sponsor with several tracks still costs one slot.** So the right question is not "which track" but "which sponsor gives the most, for work that makes the product better rather than work that decorates it".

## Recommendation: The Graph

**Best AI Tooling or AI Use Case with The Graph (From Scratch), $5,000**, 1st $2,500. Larger than either prize we are already chasing, and a second track from the same sponsor — *Best Use of Composable or Standardized Graph Products*, another $5,000 — costs no extra slot if we reach it.

Its requirements, and where we stand:

| Requirement | Us |
|---|---|
| The Graph as a **load-bearing** part | not yet, and this is the work |
| Consume **live** data from a Graph provider, not a mocked dataset | not yet |
| Meaningful work with the data: reasoning, decisions, automation, or a natural-language interface | we do three of the four already |
| Open source with a clear README | done |
| Demo video, 2–4 minutes | scripted in #83, unrecorded |
| Begun during the hackathon | yes, 4 September |

**The work, and why it is not decoration.** The enclave can only see *now*: one `eth_call` batch giving the current tick, the pool's liquidity and the position's range. Every question worth asking about a re-centre is historical. Has the price genuinely drifted, or is it oscillating across the band and about to come back? Does this pool earn enough in fees to pay for the move? How wide should the band be, given how much this pair actually moved today?

A subgraph answers all three, and Uniswap publishes one for v4 that already supports `arbitrum-one` — I checked `Uniswap/v4-subgraph`'s `networks.json`. So the decision the confidential workflow makes becomes better because of Graph data, which is exactly "load-bearing".

**It strengthens the Chainlink story rather than competing with it.** A confidential workflow reads an HTTP API **once and trusts the result**, where a normal workflow reads it ten times and takes consensus. The Graph query key becomes a second private input processed inside the enclave, alongside the mandate thresholds — and Chainlink's own qualifying list names "workflows that process private inputs" and "protect API credentials".

**What to verify before committing**, because two of these could sink it:

1. A published Uniswap v4 subgraph for Arbitrum One must be queryable on the Graph Network with our own API key. The repository supports the network; a *published, indexed* deployment is a different claim and I have not verified it. Falling back to deploying that subgraph ourselves is possible but costs a day.
2. The enclave's HTTP budget. The simulator prints a 90-second ceiling; a subgraph query is fast, but it is another round trip inside a run that already makes two.

## The alternatives, and why not

**Ledger — AI Agents x Ledger, $3,500.** The best *thesis* fit on the page: *"agents that hold secrets they cannot leak, systems that ask for a human before anything irreversible"* is a description of this project. Two problems. It wants the Ledger Agent Stack and the Key Ring CLI, and a convincing demo of device-backed security wants a device on camera. And our agent key living inside a Chainlink enclave **is** our Chainlink claim; moving it onto a Ledger would weaken the prize we are already chasing to win one we are not.

**Privy — Best Financial Flow, $2,500.** Wants a Privy wallet and one completed financial flow. Our swap conversation ends in an intent that somebody signs — a wallet is the missing half. But `app.helico.site` does not exist yet, and building a wallet-connected app in six days would take the time the vault deployment needs.

**1inch — Build an Aqua App, $5,000.** Requires their SwapVM

### **Description:**

In 2026, agentic memory has a dirty secret: **your agent's memories are trapped.** Every memory platform stores your agent's accumulated knowledge — learned preferences, resolved contradictions, hard-won context — in its own proprietary schema. Switch tools, and it all evaporates. Your agent starts over with amnesia.

We believe agentic memory should belong to *you*. That's why Memanto ships with a full migration and portability toolchain, built on the **[Open Knowledge Format (OKF)](https://docs.memanto.ai/integrations/okf)** — Google Cloud's open, vendor-neutral spec for knowledge as plain markdown. With Memanto today you can already:

- **Migrate in** from Mem0, Letta, or Supermemory with a single command: [`memanto migrate`](https://docs.memanto.ai/cli/migrate/migrate) — complete with dry-run previews and token/latency/storage savings reports
- **Export out** to a portable, git-friendly, human-readable OKF bundle: `memanto memory export --okf`
- **Import any OKF bundle** losslessly: `memanto migrate okf ./bundle` — unmapped fields are preserved, nothing is lost
