## Provenance

- **Origin date:** 2026-09-07
- **Origin type:** Owner direction informed by current schoolwork, prior learning prototypes, and two-child playtest needs.
- **Source/context:** During Emberworks learning design, the Owner clarified that GalaQuest should not treat `math only` as the long-term learning model. Learning should vary by profile and current learning need while staying embedded in the adventure/reward loop.
- **Decision state:** **Owner-selected direction; dedicated implementation lane not started.** Keep this separate from the active combat/enemy writer.

## Product outcome

Build GalaQuest learning so the game can deliver **profile-specific, current, useful practice** without becoming a separate school mode.

The child-facing loop should remain fun-first:

`want progress/reward -> do a short meaningful learning interaction -> receive clear feedback/reward -> continue the adventure`

Learning content should be data-driven enough that subject, topic, difficulty, reading load/audio needs, and current emphasis can vary by profile without rebuilding the world interaction each time.

## Current playtest-profile direction

For the current two-profile release proof:

- **Grade 2 profile:** literacy may appropriately outrank math. Current priority is grapheme recognition, decoding, and spelling practice. Exact grapheme sequences, markings, spelling rules, and examples must come from current source material rather than being invented.
- **Grade 5 profile:** current near-term emphasis is place value, number/word/expanded form, then estimation and rounding.

These are current-profile targets, **not universal grade-level prescriptions**. Future profiles/topics should be driven by current curriculum/program sources and observed need.

## Source / privacy boundary

Raw schoolwork, homework, teacher-provided program material, and other child-specific learning sources belong in the Owner-controlled private Drive source store, not the public repository.

The public repo must contain only the **distilled product requirement / task data / generic learning target** needed to implement GalaQuest. Do not publish child names, teacher emails, school identifiers, classroom codes, or other family-identifying details. Private source files must not become an undocumented startup prerequisite for ordinary contributors.

## Historical evidence worth reusing, not reviving wholesale

A prior private learning prototype established useful evidence to test in GalaQuest:

- separate child/profile learning history;
- low-reading-load / audio-first delivery for the younger profile;
- read-aloud for learning prompts/choices and a simple replay control;
- data-driven task metadata by grade/subject/topic/difficulty;
- recent-question avoidance and adaptive difficulty;
- wrong answers did not remove earned value or block play;
- reward value had to scale enough to remain meaningful rather than becoming a rounding error as normal progression grew.

That older implementation is **historical evidence only**. GalaQuest should reuse proven product lessons where they survive current scrutiny, not port the old system wholesale.

## First release proof

Issue #46 remains the release owner. Emberworks is a suitable first proof because one world mechanism can present different personalized content while keeping the same fantasy and multiplayer state:

- Grade 5: place-value / number-form / rounding forge calibration;
- Grade 2: grapheme / decoding / spelling rune-forge calibration.

The later-arriving sibling must retain a safe path to complete their own personalized task and receive their own durable reward without resetting the other player's world state.

- #43 / the progression contract owns learning as a material progression source.
- #147 separately explores a premium-feeling learning-earned reward economy and should not be conflated with the learning-content architecture.

## Objective

tau2의 Agent contract에 맞는 최소 Tool-Using Agent를 현재 프로젝트에 구현하고 기존 mock 평가 환경에 연결한다.

공식 MinimalAgent 실행을 관찰한 #1을 바탕으로, 직접 작성한 코드가 LLM 호출, 도구 호출 요청, 도구 결과 처리, conversation state에 어떻게 관여하는지 이해한다. Agent의 책임과 tau2 Orchestrator·Environment가 담당하는 실제 도구 실행 및 실행 흐름 진행의 경계를 코드와 trajectory로 설명할 수 있는 것을 목표로 한다.

## Scope

- `HalfDuplexAgent`의 입력·출력 계약을 따르는 최소 Agent를 구현한다.
  - `get_init_state(message_history)`: domain policy를 포함한 시스템 메시지와 초기 대화 이력을 구성한다.
  - `generate_next_message(message, state)`: 사용자 메시지 또는 도구 결과를 이력에 반영하고, 다음 응답과 갱신된 state를 반환한다.
  - 공식 입력 계약인 `UserMessage`, `ToolMessage`, `MultiToolMessage`를 처리한다.
- 지침, 누적 대화 이력, 공식 도구 명세를 LLM에 전달하고, 반환된 일반 응답 또는 도구 호출 요청을 이력에 보존한다.
- LLM API 형식 변환과 응답 파싱에는 기존 `tau2.utils.llm_utils.generate()`를 활용한다. 도구와 arguments는 LLM이 선택·생성하도록 하며 task 정답이나 호출 순서를 하드코딩하지 않는다.
- 현재 `scripts/run_mock_task.py`의 모델 연결, 공식 평가 실행, 결과 저장 기능을 활용해 자신의 Agent를 연결한다.
- 기존 llama.cpp 연결과 Agent·User Simulator 모델 및 평가 설정을 유지하여 `mock/create_task_1` 한 건을 실행한다. 실행 전 서버와 설정 상태를 확인한다.
- 기존 결과물을 보존하고, 새 실행의 설정·trajectory·종료 사유·평가 결과·최종 상태를 구분해 저장한다.
- 실제 LLM 호출 전에는 초기 이력 보존, 입력과 응답의 순서, 도구 결과의 다음 입력 포함, 실행 간 state 분리를 작은 검증으로 확인한다.
- 하위 작업은 작은 학습 목표 단위로 나누어 진행한다. 각 작업의 구현 범위와 완료 조건은 시작 전에 함께 논의한다.

## Out of Scope

- `../tau2-bench` 코드 수정 및 공식 policy·tools·tasks·User Simulator·Orchestrator·evaluator 변경
- 별도 Tool executor, Environment 또는 Agent Loop orchestration 구현
- LLM API 클라이언트, 도구 schema 변환기, 응답 파서를 새로 구현하는 작업
- mock 전체 평가, challenge domain 확장, 체계적인 실패 탐색 및 개선 전후 비교 실험 — 로드맵 3·4단계에서 다룬다.
- 성능 개선을 위한 프롬프트 튜닝, Reflection, Explicit Planning, 복잡한 Agent framework
- RAG, MCP, Multi-Agent, 장기 메모리, 별도 DB·서비스·Frontend·배포·observability platform
- 사전 논의와 동의 없는 새로운 architecture 또는 dependency 추가

## Success Criteria

- [ ] 현재 프로젝트의 Agent가 tau2 Agent contract에 맞게 초기 state와 다음 메시지를 생성한다.
- [ ] 초기 대화 이력이 보존되고, 입력과 응답이 순서대로 반영되며, 서로 다른 실행의 state가 섞이지 않는 것을 검증한다.
- [ ] 도구 결과가 다음 LLM 입력에 포함되는 것을 확인하고, ToolCall과 ToolMessage의 대응 관계를 설명한다.
- [ ] 자신의 Agent로 `mock/create_task_1`의 실행과 공식 평가를 완료하고 재현 명령·실행 설정·원본 결과를 남긴다. 인증 키 등 비밀정보는 저장하지 않는다.
- [ ] 실제 trajectory를 통해 사용자 입력 → state 갱신 → LLM 호출 → 도구 호출 요청 반환 → tau2의 도구 실행 → 결과 재입력 → 후속 응답을 코드 위치와 연결해 설명한다.
- [ ] 자신이 작성한 부분, 기존 LLM 호출 유틸리티가 담당하는 부분, tau2 Orchestrator·Environment가 담당하는 부분을 구분한다.
- [ ] 종료 사유와 평가 상세를 읽고 결과를 설명한다. 실패가 발생했다면 Agent 구현·연결 오류와 모델의 판단 문제를 근거로 구분하며, 불확실한 원인은 가설로 기록한다.

특정 reward 달성이나 공식 MinimalAgent 대비 성능 향상은 이 에픽의 완료 조건이 아니다. 다만 인증·환경·구현 오류로 실제 실행과 평가가 완료되지 않았다면 연결 검증은 미완료로 둔다.

## Outcome

Make retrieval authority, fresh challenge/response, byte verification and audit coverage correct before accelerating the existing proof/session path. Reduce native verification cost and amortize provider submissions without weakening those claims. Qualify the resulting finite-gas capacity through #260. Channels remain a separate product decision in #259; multicore and cross-provider aggregation require measured activation evidence.

This is an implementation plan, not a claim that its proposed changes or speedups have been validated. The September 2026 review checked live issues and `origin/main` at **50a5cb2f999f5c455b8055a933eda941168e55fe**. Recheck affected paths after each predecessor merges.

## Verified starting point and corrections

- [Historical #244 artifact](https://github.com/Polynomialstore/polystore/blob/50a5cb2f999f5c455b8055a933eda941168e55fe/bench/retrieval_session_capacity/ac0fa173.json): approximately 19.9 ms per one-proof FFI verification and 43.72 **derived** sessions/block. Block gas was unlimited and the sustained client waited for each commit. Neither figure establishes saturated network capacity.
- Production is `SubmitRetrievalSessionProof` -> `verifyPolyFSChainedProof` in `polystorechain/x/polystorechain/keeper/msg_server.go` -> `VerifyMdu0RootTableProof` plus `VerifyMduProof` in `polystorechain/x/crypto_ffi/binding.go`. The active PolyFS root is **32-byte Merkle**, with root-table and blob KZG openings. The legacy 48-byte manifest verifier is not this path.
- Mode 2 sessions cannot cross a placement slot or MDU. `stripeParamsForDeal` gives `rows=64/K`: default K=8 permits at most **8 proofs/session**; the historical `General:rs=2+1` fixture permits 32. `buildBenchSubmitPlan` splits its 64-proof workload across sessions/providers. Do not label it one 64-proof session.
- The existing benchmark uses zero-filled content. Retain it for historical comparison; add deterministic nonzero/nonconstant content for representative cryptography measurements. Identity commitments/proofs remain valid edge cases.
- `SubmitRetrievalSessionProof` accepts registered deputy submitters and pins the first successful submitter for payout. `PROOF_SUBMITTED` retries currently re-enter accounting, including `Mode2EpochSlotServed`; pin checks only cover OPEN/USER_CONFIRMED. #255 owns the regression and repair before acceleration.
- Cosmos already supports multiple existing messages in one atomic transaction. #257 starts there. A new batch message, durable queue, scheduler, or cross-session crypto layer is not a prerequisite for transport batching.
- One funded OPEN session already permits segmented or parallel requests within its authorized range. A transport request is not automatically a new session or a billable logical transfer.

Sources of authority: `DOCS.md`, `spec.md` §7.2, `docs/runtime-personas.md`, the mandatory-session/batching and frozen pricing/escrow RFCs. Roadmap checkboxes and RFC future-work sections do not override the current code or establish implementation evidence. New text uses `user-gateway` and `provider-daemon`.

## Correctness review: blockers before acceleration

The deeper review found defects in the baseline, not merely missing optimization tests. #255 is the first safety milestone and must resolve these before #256 is enabled. Four active children remain sufficient; no new tickets are needed.

| Layer / invariant | Concrete baseline gap | Gate owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Authenticated attribution | A public valid proof can be copied by another registered provider; session proof verification does not authenticate that submitter as the chosen server. First-writer pinning plus session-ID-only confirmation can select the wrong payee. | #255: authenticated payee contract and copy/race regression |
| Complete state and money lifecycle | Confirmation can fall back to the assigned provider if the proof-provider pin is missing/unreadable; zero-fee completion skips pin cleanup. Retry fixes a

Across two measured Terminal-Bench panels — 17 tasks (match `b8e93d3f0c60`) and 9 tasks (match `13f7f2bb533d`) — Stella called `search` **zero times**. The second panel was selected specifically so it could not be a task-shape excuse: every task ships at least 3 files into the workspace and `schemelike-metacircular-eval` ships 66.

## The measurement

Tool mix, match `13f7f2bb533d`, clean basis (198 model calls):

```
bash 172,  write_file 7,  edit_file 6,  read_file 5,  get_environment 2,  search 0
```

Match `b8e93d3f0c60`, 17 tasks (349 tool calls): `bash 299, edit_file 29, write_file 16, delete_file 4, read_file 1, search 0`.

So the agent routes essentially all discovery through `bash` — `cat`, `ls`, `grep` — and uses the dedicated read tool ~3% of the time. Claude Code, on the same tasks, used its `Read` tool 28 times against 145 `Bash` calls.

## Why this matters beyond tool aesthetics

1. It is the mechanism behind the output-token gap. Measured on the 17-task panel, per *action* the two agents are within 1.10–1.16x; the whole ~1.9x output difference is **action count** — Stella issued 2.06x the bash calls, each 1.30x longer. Fewer, higher-yield calls is the lever.
2. The semantic index is now built at `stella init` (the embedding handoff landed in this branch) and nothing consumes it. That work is currently unrealised.
3. The system prompt explicitly instructs `search` first — "one call usually replaces a run of grep and read_file round trips" — and it is not happening. Either the instruction is not landing, the tool description is not competitive with `bash` at decision time, or `search` genuinely does not answer the questions these tasks ask.

## What would settle which

- Instrument: does `search` get *considered*? A trial-level count of `search` calls is already derivable from `stella-events.jsonl` (`tool_start` names).
- Try the panel with `bash` withheld (`tools.bash: "off"` in project settings) on 2–3 tasks and read what the agent reaches for instead. That distinguishes "prefers bash" from "search does not answer".
- Compare tool *descriptions* head to head: `bash`'s description now runs several sentences including scratch guidance; `search`'s may simply be losing the selection.

## Files

- `crates/stella-tools/src/catalog.rs` — the tool table and descriptions
- `crates/stella-tools/src/search/` — the search implementation
- `crates/stella-cli/src/agent/prompt.rs` — `tool_steering!` and the system prompt text
- evidence: `~/.arenabench/matches/13f7f2bb533d/jobs/*stella*/*/agent/stella-events.jsonl`

## Definition of done

Rewritten 2026-09-07 after a count over this workspace's own `store.db` closed one arm of the original wording. The original read: *"Either `search` is used on tasks where it answers better than a grep, demonstrated on a measured panel, or the tool surface/prompt is changed to stop advertising a path the agent never takes."* The second arm is struck — on the current tool surface `search` is called in 14 of 36 runs here, 208 calls against 1647 `bash`, so it is not a path the agent never takes and removing it would be the wrong change. The working is in the comment below.

- [x] A panel measures how often `search` is called on Terminal-Bench shapes, reported on the same clean basis as the counts above. **Answered 2026-09-08 from match `19f239f62acb`, a `terminal-bench-2.1` panel recorded 2026-08-19 that was already on disk: 20 trials over two models, 603 tool calls, `bash` 533, `read_file` 16, `search` 0 — and 0 on the 18-trial basis that drops the two `NonZeroAgentExitCodeError` trials. `search` was in the request `tools` array and the "call search first" steering line was in the system prompt in 20 of 20 trials, so the instruction is landing and hypothesis 1 is out. The working is in the comment below.**
- [ ] That panel answers whether `search` beats a grep on those shapes, or records that it does not.

The second box needs a human to supply three things this repository cannot: the rig, whic
title: Stella never used its file-search tool across two benchmark panels, even one picked to reward search

Put Spark-X2.5's mathematical reasoning to a real, honest, reproducible test.

For this challenge, obtain XHToken/Spark-X2.5-4B or Spark-X2.5-1.7B from Hugging Face (or a mirror such as ModelScope), run a real math-reasoning evaluation or case study, and publish the complete, reproducible result in the corresponding model's Hugging Face Discussions. After publishing it, reply to this event's GitHub Issue with the Discussion link to enter.

- Event page (GitHub Issues): https://github.com/XHToken/Spark-X2.5/issues
- Hugging Face model collection: https://huggingface.co/collections/XHToken/spark-x25

- Challenge period: September 7–13, 2026
- Submission deadline: September 13, 2026, 24:00 Beijing Time (UTC+8)
- Judging and award distribution: September 14–20, 2026

## Challenge Tracks

Choose one track or combine several:

- Standard math benchmarks: evaluate on public sets such as GSM8K, MATH, MATH-500, AIME 2024/2025, OlympiadBench, or MinervaMath, and report pass@1 (and pass@k where relevant) with a clear scoring script
- Competition and olympiad problems: run AMC / AIME / IMO-style or national-olympiad problems and analyze where the model succeeds or fails
- Step-by-step reasoning quality: assess chain-of-thought correctness, not just final answers — catch right-answer-wrong-reasoning and arithmetic slips
- Tool-assisted math: combine the model with a code interpreter / Python / SymPy (program-aided reasoning) and compare against no-tool baselines
- Formal and proof-oriented math: theorem proving, proof sketching, or Lean/Coq-style formalization attempts, with honest reporting of verification
- Multilingual math: test math word problems and reasoning across languages (e.g. MGSM), and report per-language accuracy
- Robustness and contamination checks: perturbed / paraphrased / numerically-swapped problems, and evidence that results are not from memorized test data
- Decoding and prompting study: effect of temperature, self-consistency / majority voting, sampling budget, and prompt format on math accuracy — with cost trade-offs
- Comparative evaluation: compare Spark-X2.5 with larger models or other similar-size open models under one identical methodology

## Goal

Formalize the stronger results of [BCHKS25, *On Proximity Gaps for Reed–Solomon Codes*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/2055), with **Theorem 4.6—list/mutual correlated agreement for polynomial curves—as the principal target**.

Also reconcile and complete coverage of the paper’s unique-decoding results and their curve extensions.

Scope: mathematical agreement and exceptional-set bounds. Decoder implementation and runtime analysis are not prerequisites. This is a planning/tracking issue, not a claim that the target theorem is already verified.

## Target theorem

For arbitrary words u₀,…,u_M, consider u_z = ∑ⱼ zʲuⱼ.

Below the Johnson radius, outside an explicitly bounded exceptional set of challenges z, **every sufficiently large agreement set A** for u_z admits simultaneous codeword extensions of all the uⱼ on that same A.

The full target retains:

- arbitrary curve degree M;
- arbitrary finite fields and evaluation sets;
- the strict Johnson-radius condition;
- the same-agreement-set quantifier;
- BCHKS25’s explicit exceptional-set bound, linear in Mn for fixed rate and slack.

The affine-line theorem is the specialization M = 1, not the full endpoint. Use the source’s exact finite bound and hypotheses in the final theorem.

## Current status in ArkLib

Baseline: canonical main [a527b514](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/ArkLib/tree/a527b514e029ecf9da40d66b5531a0707c686edc). Recheck status before assigning implementation work. This inventory is based on source inspection and the committed axiom baseline, not a fresh full validation run.

| Area | Current situation |
|---|---|
| Ordinary Guruswami–Sudan interpolation and divisibility | Proved; reusable |
| Older symbolic GS interpolation for lines | Proved, but its degree budget does not supply BCHKS25’s improved bound |
| Factor/candidate-pair bookkeeping | Partially proved |
| Factorization, good specialization, and useful-factor analysis | Central obligations remain admitted |
| Johnson-range ordinary correlated agreement | List-decoding branch remains incomplete |
| BCHKS25 Johnson-range MCA | Existing affine-line numerical endpoint is admitted; full curve theorem remains to be established |
| Unique-decoding MCA | Existing n/q bound proved |
| BCHKS25 unique-decoding CA | A source-facing two-radius bound is proved; exact paper coverage and finite-length conventions need reconciliation |

Relevant entry points:

- [Symbolic interpolation and its contract](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/ArkLib/blob/a527b514e029ecf9da40d66b5531a0707c686edc/ArkLib/Data/CodingTheory/ProximityGap/BCIKS20/ListDecoding/Guruswami.lean)
- [Factor extraction](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/ArkLib/blob/a527b514e029ecf9da40d66b5531a0707c686edc/ArkLib/Data/CodingTheory/ProximityGap/BCIKS20/ListDecoding/Extraction.lean)
- [Useful-factor agreement obligations](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/ArkLib/blob/a527b514e029ecf9da40d66b5531a0707c686edc/ArkLib/Data/CodingTheory/ProximityGap/BCIKS20/ListDecoding/Agreement.lean)
- [Admitted Johnson MCA endpoint](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/ArkLib/blob/a527b514e029ecf9da40d66b5531a0707c686edc/ArkLib/Data/CodingTheory/ProximityGap/CapacityBounds.lean#L180)
- [Proved unique-decoding CA bound](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/ArkLib/blob/a527b514e029ecf9da40d66b5531a0707c686edc/ArkLib/Data/CodingTheory/ProximityGap/CapacityBounds/UniqueDecoding.lean#L102)
- [Canonical MCA event](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/ArkLib/blob/a527b514e029ecf9da40d66b5531a0707c686edc/ArkLib/Data/CodingTheory/ProximityGenerator/Basic.lean#L100)

**Status caveat:** a wrapper with a proof body is not necessarily admission-free. Completion must be checked transitively.

## Work packages

### A. Statement alignment and acceptance tests

- [ ] Map BCHKS25’s degree-≤k convention to ArkLib’s degree-<K convention.
- [ ] State full Theorem 4.6 as an exceptional-set cardinality bound.
- [ ] Prove the bridge to ArkLib’s existing `IsMCA`/`mcaError`.
- [ ] Record exact radius,

# JOB-13 — FoxNet Online Vehicle Auctions

**Owner:** David / Captain  
**Status:** Planning and contract integration in regular chat  
**Primary dependency:** JOB-02 Career/RLS bridge  
**Cross-job sources:** JOB-04 Wrecking Yard, JOB-09 Tow Yard/lien vehicles, personal Career vehicles, company-owned vehicles  
**UI host dependency:** JOB-01 phone/PC/IceFox platform

## Mission

Build the authoritative RedFox/FoxNet online vehicle-auction system for:

- Wrecking Yard-owned vehicles exported by JOB-04,
- clear-title tow/lien vehicles exported by JOB-09,
- personal owned Career vehicles,
- company-owned vehicles,
- generated auction stock that becomes real inventory only after a completed purchase,
- multi-lot timed bidding, settlement, shipping, delivery and recent auction history.

This is an online-only auction website. It has no physical auction lane, auction-yard intake, preview trip, pickup location or required transport-to-auction job.

## Locked owner decisions

- Multiple vehicle lots may be active at the same time.
- Lot closing times should normally be staggered.
- Players may watch and bid on several vehicles simultaneously.
- Player bids may be cancelled until that lot's timer reaches zero.
- No positive reserve prices.
- No seller approval or reserve-not-met flow.
- If nobody places a valid bid, the lot is No Sale.
- Selected No Sale vehicles may be relisted; others may be returned to their source or removed.
- Purchased vehicles are shipped and enter an In Transit state before garage delivery.
- No physical vehicle viewing is required.
- Fox Facts, condition, damaged parts, missing parts, mileage and start/run/drive status influence value and bidder interest.
- The website retains one completed auction's public results until the next auction completes.
- Membership/subscription tiers may control bidding access, vehicle-value limits, buying power and fee/shipping discounts.

## Shared Sell-page rule

Only vehicles legally owned by the player, a company, JOB-04 or JOB-09 may appear as disposition candidates.

Supported actions may include:

```text
Direct Sell
Send to Auction
Relist
Strip for Parts
Scrap
Return to Yard
```

Dealership, BeamBook and Wrecking Yard browse listings are not owned vehicles merely because they are visible for sale. They must first be purchased or legally claimed.

## Required read-first files

```text
PROJECT_MANIFESTS/JOB_HANDOFFS/JOB-09_TO_JOB-13_COPART_AUCTION_HANDOFF_2026-07-29.md
PROJECT_MANIFESTS/JOB_HANDOFFS/JOB-04_TO_JOB-13_WRECKING_YARD_ONLINE_AUCTION_AND_SHARED_SELL_INVENTORY_HANDOFF_2026-07-29.md
PROJECT_MANIFESTS/INTERFACES/redfox_auction_bridge_v1.schema.json
PROJECT_MANIFESTS/INTERFACES/examples/redfoxAuctionBridge_JOB13_example.lua
PROJECT_MANIFESTS/INTERFACES/examples/copart_weui_test_harness_example.lua
PROJECT_MANIFESTS/INTERFACES/examples/auction_web_bridge_example.js
```

## Ownership boundaries

- JOB-13 must not directly edit JOB-09's `settings/redfox/tow_recovery_dispatch_yard.json`.
- JOB-13 must not directly edit JOB-04's authoritative Wrecking Yard/source records.
- JOB-13 must not directly replace stock Career/RLS files.
- Money, ownership, inventory IDs and garage placement remain authoritative through JOB-02/Career/RLS.
- JOB-04 remains authoritative for its owned Wrecking Yard inventory and disposition eligibility.
- JOB-09 remains authoritative for custody, lien eligibility, title acquisition and safe removal of its claimed vehicles during settlement.
- JOB-01 remains authoritative for phone/PC/IceFox app hosting and routing.

## Required source contract

For owned/exported vehicles, use exact Career/RLS inventory IDs and persistent source record IDs. Do not generate synthetic native inventory or shop IDs.

Each export should preserve:

- source type and source record ID,
- exact inventory ID where one exists,
- model and configuration,
- mileage,
- real condition data,
- damaged and missing parts,
- ownership/claim status,
- estimated value,
- suggested ope

## Goal
Deliver the hidden-placeholder-directory watch fix and assess watch growth on large ad-hoc roots. Record the chosen resource policy and its coverage trade-offs, document limits accurately and report limited coverage clearly. Preserve ignore behaviour and validate creation of the first note in a hidden-only directory.

## Requirements
M2-R4

## Adopts
- #13 — Watch coverage: hidden-only directories and watch count on large roots

## Plan

### What the watch set is today

`tree.Dirs` returns the root, every directory holding a file ripgrep lists (any
file, not only markdown), their ancestors, and any subtree beneath those that
holds **no files at all**. `watch.New` places one inotify watch per returned
directory; a directory appearing at runtime recomputes the whole set.

Two consequences, both from M1 QA (#13):

1. A directory whose only file is hidden — a `.gitkeep` placeholder — has no
   file ripgrep lists (so nothing puts it in the set) and is not fileless (so
   the empty-subtree arm rejects it). It is never watched, and the first note
   created there produces no live update until the directory next appears in a
   batch or the daemon restarts.
2. The set grows with the whole tree, not with the notes in it, because
   directories holding only non-markdown files are watched too.

### Measurements (this machine, before any change)

| root | watched dirs | holds markdown + ancestors | no listable files | only non-markdown files | markdown files |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| this repo | 21 | 3 | 3 | 15 | 6 |
| `~/projects` | 1,590 | 642 | 55 | 893 | 1,402 |
| `/usr/share` | 5,790 | 311 | 1,503 | 3,976 | 392 |
| `/usr/lib` | 12,690 | 303 | 1,318 | 11,069 | 479 |
| `~/.cache` | 82,684 | 13,616 | 11,673 | 57,395 | 19,244 |

`/usr/share` reproduces QA's 5,790-against-310 figure exactly. The third column
is the navigator's own directory set. Directories holding only non-markdown
files are 69–87% of the watch set on every large root, and `~/.cache` alone
would take 82,684 of the 524,288 watches this system allows a user — roughly
87 MB of unswappable kernel memory — for a root whose notes live in 13,616
directories.

### Change 1 — hidden-only directories are watchable

Make the empty-subtree test in `tree.Dirs` ignore hidden files: a directory
holding only dotfiles is exactly as empty as one holding nothing, because
nothing in it is listed by ripgrep, the navigator or search.

Ignored files keep counting as files. Skipping them would make `node_modules`
look fileless and pull whole ignored trees back into the watch set — the bug
`dd961f3` fixed — so a directory whose only files are *ignored* stays unwatched,
as the M1 milestone document records. That asymmetry is deliberate and gets
stated in the docs.

### Change 2 — a per-root watch budget, filled in priority order

`tree.Dirs` returns its directories in priority order and `watch.New` takes a
budget, watching in that order and stopping when the budget is spent:

1. the root, every directory holding a markdown file, and their ancestors —
   the navigator's own set, where notes actually change;
2. directories with no listable files — empty and hidden-only ones, where a
   first note can appear that nothing else would report;
3. everything else — directories holding only non-markdown files.

So a small root is watched exactly as it is today, and a large one loses the
tier that is 69–87% of it before it loses anything a user is likely to edit.

Default budget 8,192 directories per root: it covers `/usr/share` whole, is
1.6% of the 524,288 watches a typical Linux desktop allows, ~8 MB of kernel
memory, and matches the smallest `fs.inotify.max_user_watches` still found in
the wild so one ad-hoc root cannot exhaust an unraised system on its own.
Configurable as `max_watches` in `config.yml` and `--max-watches` on
`mdn serve`; `0` means no budget.

### Change 3 — reporting when coverage is limited

`watch.Watcher` tracks coverage (watched, skipped, and why: budget sp
title: Watch hidden-only directories and define large-root resource policy

Found while building the platform pin for #15330 (the compiled list-view group queries through `POST /data/:object/query`). Reported first on #14556 per that card's deliverable 3; filed here as its own card because #15330 is a `tests` card that changes no behaviour, and its two candidate repair sites were held by open PRs at the time.

## The measurement

One `ObjectQL` engine, one better-sqlite3 `SqlDriver`, one seeded table, one compiled header query. The only thing that moves between the two runs is whether the driver exposes `aggregate` — which is exactly what `ObjectQL.aggregate` forks on (`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`, the line reading `if (typeof drv.aggregate === 'function' and allStructuredSupported and ...)`).

Rows:

| id | business_unit | amount | notes |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| v1 | void_unit | NULL | NULL |
| v2 | void_unit | NULL | NULL |
| v3 | void_unit | NULL | NULL |
| f1 | full_unit | 10 | 'x' |
| f2 | full_unit | 20 | NULL |

Query (the output of `compileListViewGroupQuery` for a view grouping on `business_unit` with a `sum` summary on `amount`), posted through `POST /api/v1/data/:object/query`:

```json
{ "groupBy": ["business_unit"],
  "aggregations": [ { "function": "count", "alias": "count" },
                    { "function": "sum", "field": "amount", "alias": "sum_amount" } ] }
```

Answers for the `void_unit` group — a group with THREE rows, every one of them holding NULL in the summed column:

| face | `sum_amount` | type |
|:--|:--|:--|
| driver-sql pushdown (SQL `SUM(amount)`) | `null` | null |
| engine in-memory tier (`applyInMemoryAggregation`) | `0` | number |
| the spec's own reducer, `packages/spec/src/ui/view-grouping-query.test.ts` | `0` | number |

`avg`, `min` and `max` agree (`null` on both faces), and `count_distinct` agrees (`0` on both). `sum` is the only divergence. A group with SOME nulls also agrees, because `applyInMemoryAggregation`'s `toNumber(null)` is `0` and SQL `SUM` skips NULLs — so the divergence needs a group in which the column is null in EVERY row, which is why nothing has caught it.

## Which face is wrong

`0`, on the reading the platform has already written down. `emptyGroupValueFor` in `packages/spec/src/data/aggregation-policy.ts` rules that counting and summing no rows is `0` — "those are measured facts, not missing data" — while averaging, minimising or maximising nothing stays null. Summing three rows that each contribute nothing is the same act as summing no rows: the addend set is empty either way. So the in-memory tier and the spec reducer agree with the declared policy, and **driver-sql is the face that disagrees**.

Stated as an assumption to be confirmed rather than as a settled reading: `emptyGroupValueFor` is written for a group the runtime evaluates with an EMPTY row set, and this group is not empty — it is three rows whose aggregand is absent. If the maintainer reads those as different cases, then the ruling to record is which one this is, and the repair may land on the spec reducer instead. Either way the two platform faces must stop disagreeing.

## Why it is unmeasured today

`packages/spec/src/data/aggregation-conformance.ts` is the vocabulary's conformance table and it does not reach this cell. Its `stage` column is nullable and every `count_distinct` case turns on it, but its two numeric aggregands are non-null by declaration — `score` is documented as "a non-null numeric column for the arithmetic aggregates" and `flag` is 3 true / 3 false. So no case in the table ever asks any face what `sum` over an all-null column is.

Nearest neighbours, same defect CLASS and different cells, all closed: #11065 (`avg` over a boolean: driver-memory `null` vs sqlite a number), #11151 (driver-mongodb, `avg`/`sum` over a boolean), #11455 / #11635 (driver-sql boolean aggregands on PG). The shape those cards settled — a face answering `null` where the ruled answer is a number — is this one, one column type over.

## Blast radius

This is on the live compiled-query
title: `sum` over a column that is NULL in every row of a group: driver-sql answers `null`, the engine's in-memory aggregate tier answers `0` — same query, same rows, fork chosen by a driver capability bit

Coordination issue for the architecture migration the owner asked for on 2026-09-06. **Two agent sessions commit to this repo** — please claim a phase here before starting, and keep to the file boundaries below.

## The finding that shapes everything

The divergence is **generational, not architectural**. `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`'s rules are real and are being followed — by everything written after the seed commit:

- All **27 `XService` classes** date from the 2026-08-31 seed. Every one of the **18 service modules added since** is plain `verb_noun` functions. Zero new classes.
- Post-seed view modules average **35 lines**; all six modules over 140 lines are seed-era.
- `tokens/services/register.py` (post-seed) escapes CSV cells in the service; `whitelist/views/entry.py` (seed) hand-rolls them unescaped in the view.

This is a **half-finished migration**, not an absent standard. The destination already exists: `offerings/` is the reference implementation (924 service lines vs 138 view lines).

## The standard

Logic lives in `services/` as plain module-level functions; tenancy lives in `querysets/`; state transitions live in `models/` behind `_require_status`; everything else is a thin adapter. The API contract should be **generated** from the DRF serializers rather than hand-mirrored in TypeScript.

## The meta-rule

> A rule enters `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` only with two things attached: **the file that is its reference implementation, and the gate that enforces it.** A rule that gets neither is demoted to a documented exception or deleted.

ARCHITECTURE.md currently concedes most rules are "held by review" — which, as it says itself, means a green pipeline means nobody checked. Every new gate ships with a `LEGACY` allowlist of today's offenders so it is green on day one; the allowlist **is** the backlog, and CI fails if it grows.

## Explicitly NOT doing

**No big-bang conversion of the 27 service classes.** The direction is settled by every commit since the seed. A 19-module rewrite conflicts with everything in flight and buys nothing a written rule does not. Write the rule; convert opportunistically. The 8 genuinely stateful chain clients stay classes.

## Phases

**Phase 0 — the standard and its gates** (docs + scripts only, no code moves)
- Rewrite the "Backend layers", "Tenancy model" and "Coding rules" sections so each rule cites its reference file and its gate
- `scripts/check-layers.py` in the `check-comments.py` mould, with a LEGACY allowlist
- `backend/shared/tests/test_route_coverage.py` — walk the URLconf and assert every registered route is in the tenancy matrix or in an EXEMPT tuple with a stated reason

**Phase 0b — three things that must NOT wait for backend-first** (no dependency on backend or shared)
- Wire the existing Playwright smoke into CI. It is configured and runs nowhere, so every later step's claim to "leave the codebase working" rests on nothing
- Give mobile a test runner. Only tree with zero tests, and it holds the seed-phrase generation code
- Two mobile correctness bugs: `useFeatureFlags` drops `&& flag.enabled`, so **the trading kill switch is inert on mobile**; `useMockData()` defaults to **true** when the env var is unset, so a build without `.env` **fakes a successful broadcast**

**Phase 1 — backend**, ordered by conflict-safety rather than severity. Known correctness items: CSV formula injection in the whitelist export; **14 logged email addresses**; `POST /api/wallets/batch-check-balances/` unscoped and absent from the route matrix; four `ValueError` guards in `tokens/models/` that surface as 500s.

**Phase 2 — `packages/shared`** as the generated contract. Add `react` + `@tanstack/react-query` as peerDependencies early — it is the structural unlock for ~2,650 lines of client duplication.

**Phase 3 — dashboard.** **Phase 4 — mobile.**

| Session | Takes | Touches |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Ledova Omarch** (this one) | Phase 0 and Phase 1 | `docs/ARCHI

## Summary
The signed-in internal-test route can leave a learner permanently stuck on the generic “We need to check your progress” recovery screen. Reloading and selecting “Try again” return to the same state.

This report is specifically for:

- `https://www.edenia.study/?internal_test=1`

The public route `https://www.edenia.study/` uses a separate storage namespace and must not be used as evidence for this failure.

## Observed reproduction

1. Open the internal-test URL in an already authenticated Chrome session.
2. The page shows:
   - “Edenia could not open your progress yet. Your saved copies are safe.”
   - “Try again” and “Sign out” actions.
3. Select “Try again.”
4. The page briefly enters “Getting your progress ready…” and then returns to the same generic recovery screen.
5. Reloading the exact internal-test URL produces the same result.

Browser-visible verification showed the deployed internal configuration and current application assets, but the route remained in `recovering`. Live local storage, cookies, session tokens, account identifiers, and provider response bodies were intentionally not inspected, so the exact persisted marker combination is not yet identified.

## User impact

A signed-in learner can have no actionable path to their town. “Try again” does not change the state, and signing out is not an acceptable recovery path for a user who wants to keep the account and town.

## Expected behavior

Profile opening must be live for every signed-in state:

- If a valid cloud head exists, activate it even when local sync/import metadata is malformed or stale.
- If the current cloud head is unusable, present trusted local/protected recovery candidates.
- If no trusted recovery candidate exists, show onboarding language selection so the account can create a fresh town.
- Reserve the generic retry screen for genuinely transient cloud unavailability or a recovery condition that has an actionable recovery path; it must not be a terminal state caused only by malformed durable metadata.
- Preserve untrusted or protected records for later repair/export where applicable; do not silently overwrite meaningful learner data.
- Keep the public accountless route and its behavior unchanged.

## Investigation notes

The likely remaining paths are the client-side durable recovery/sync guards around:

- malformed durable import markers;
- malformed sync records;
- an explicit `recovery_required` resolution response;
- conversion of an empty internal local namespace into onboarding or a verified cloud activation.

Existing related work is in PRs #281, #284, and #285. The internal route must be tested directly; a healthy public-root town does not prove the internal route works.

## Acceptance criteria

- Add browser regression coverage for the exact `?internal_test=1` route and separate internal storage namespace.
- Cover empty local state plus malformed durable markers and prove the learner reaches either the verified cloud town or onboarding, never an inert generic gate.
- Cover `recovery_required` with no candidates and prove it reaches onboarding.
- Cover a truly recoverable local/protected candidate and prove the recovery UI remains available.
- Prove that the public root remains accountless and unchanged.
- Verify the deployed internal URL in Chrome after release, including reload and the retry action.

## Summary

Several TraceQL pipeline stages are evaluated in our own process after rows have already been read and transported. They could be compiled into the SQL we send. The clearest case is the spanset aggregate: `PlannedAggregate` is consumed only in `crates/pulsus-read/src/traces/search_eval.rs` and no code path generates SQL for it.

So for

```
{ .service.namespace = "prod" } | max(duration) > 1s
```

the filter is pushed down and prunes, then **every matching span is transported to us**, held in memory, grouped by trace, and most of it discarded. The database could have done that with `GROUP BY trace_id HAVING max(duration_ns) > 1000000000` and sent back only the traces that qualify.

This is not a limitation of the storage engine. `GROUP BY trace_id` is already used elsewhere in this codebase — in the search path and in the service-graph SQL.

## Why it matters more than latency

Compute is a fixed cost in a cloud deployment; cross-zone bandwidth is metered and variable. Bytes read from local disk into the database are close to free. **Bytes crossing between processes are a recurring charge**, so a stage that transports rows in order to discard them is paid for on every query.

There are three hops to count, not one:

```
client <-- pulsus-server <-- database <-- parts
                  ^              ^
                  |              +-- database to database: distributed fan-out, shard to coordinator
                  +----------------- metered in most topologies
```

A distributed `GROUP BY` sends partial aggregation state between shards rather than raw rows, so pushing an aggregate down shrinks the second hop as well as the first.

## What is evaluated where today

Pushed down: attribute equality, attribute regular expressions, physical columns, the time window, scope predicates.

Evaluated in our process: spanset aggregates, structural operators (descendant, child-of), cross-attribute comparisons, non-total arithmetic, `by()` regrouping.

That list needs splitting into three groups, because they need different answers:

1. **Cannot be pushed.** A structural operator needs the trace assembled; a cross-attribute comparison compares values stored on different rows.
2. **Could be pushed, and nobody has.** The aggregate case, where the filter is fully pushable and the aggregate reads a physical column.
3. **Pushed already, but prunes nothing.** An attribute regular expression compiles to a value match and still scans. Being pushed down and being cheap are separate claims.

## Waves

**Wave 1 — the inventory.** Every predicate and stage evaluated in our process, classified into the three groups above, with the SQL shape for group 2 and a measurement for group 3. Ranked by bytes saved on the metered hops.

**Waves 2 onward — one per pushable class**, in the order wave 1 establishes. Spanset aggregates are the expected first, since they have no SQL path at all.

## A decision this carries, to be settled before wave 2

Our result-size limits are enforced in our process and answer `422`. If the database performs the aggregation, a breach is detected somewhere else, and the limit has to move into the SQL or apply to a smaller result. The reference handles the same situation by returning a partial answer with a marker rather than refusing — and our responses carry no field for saying "incomplete". Whether we follow that or keep refusing is a separate decision and belongs in this issue, not in a wave.

## Not in scope

Rewriting anything in group 1. Changing what the queries mean. This issue is about where the same answer is computed.
title: TraceQL + LogQL: the shared engine that compiles a query pipeline to SQL, built on TraceQL first

### **Description:**

In 2026, agentic memory has a dirty secret: **your agent's memories are trapped.** Every memory platform stores your agent's accumulated knowledge — learned preferences, resolved contradictions, hard-won context — in its own proprietary schema. Switch tools, and it all evaporates. Your agent starts over with amnesia.

We believe agentic memory should belong to *you*. That's why Memanto ships with a full migration and portability toolchain, built on the **[Open Knowledge Format (OKF)](https://docs.memanto.ai/integrations/okf)** — Google Cloud's open, vendor-neutral spec for knowledge as plain markdown. With Memanto today you can already:

- **Migrate in** from Mem0, Letta, or Supermemory with a single command: [`memanto migrate`](https://docs.memanto.ai/cli/migrate/migrate) — complete with dry-run previews and token/latency/storage savings reports
- **Export out** to a portable, git-friendly, human-readable OKF bundle: `memanto memory export --okf`
- **Import any OKF bundle** losslessly: `memanto migrate okf ./bundle` — unmapped fields are preserved, nothing is lost
- **Sync** a browsable memory wiki into any project: `memanto memory sync --okf`

The tools exist. What the world hasn't seen yet is the **movement**. We want the open-source community to show every agent builder — vividly, virally, with real data — what it looks like to *escape lock-in and own your memory*.

### **The Challenge:**

Build a **compelling, reproducible migration showcase** that takes memories from another tool into Memanto and out again as portable OKF — proving the full freedom loop: **in → owned → portable**.

⚠️ **Do NOT reinvent the wheel.** The `memanto migrate` CLI and OKF export/import are shipped and documented. Your job is to build *on top of* them — real-world showcases, new migration paths for tools we don't support yet, and creative OKF workflows. Submissions that re-implement what the CLI already does will score poorly on engineering value.

### 💡 Pick Your Path (or Invent Your Own):

- **Path A: The Real-World Escape (Supported Providers)**

    Build (or use) a genuinely lived-in agent on Mem0, Letta, or Supermemory — weeks of evolving preferences, corrections, contradictions. Run `memanto migrate` on it. Show the savings report. Export to OKF. Then prove the round trip: same questions before and after, zero amnesia.

  * *The Goal:* The definitive "switching costs are dead" demo — before/after recall parity plus hard token/latency/storage numbers straight from the migration report.

- **Path B: The New Frontier (Unsupported Sources)** ⭐ *highest engineering value*

    Build a **new migration adapter** for a source we don't support yet — Zep/Graphiti, Hindsight, LangMem, LangGraph checkpoints, or exported ChatGPT/Claude conversation memory. Your adapter should transform the source into either a provider-style export JSON consumable by `memanto migrate --file`, or directly into a valid OKF bundle consumable by `memanto migrate okf`.

  * *The Goal:* A permanent new migration path merged into `/examples/migrations/` that future users can run against their own data. The ChatGPT/Claude angle in particular — "liberate the memory your assistant has built about you" — has massive viral potential with everyday users, not just developers.

- **Path C: The OKF Renaissance (Portability Workflows)**

    Show what becomes possible *once* memory is portable markdown: a git-versioned memory wiki with meaningful diffs across sessions, an OKF viewer/diff utility, a team workflow where agents and humans read the same synced bundle, or a multi-source consolidation where two migrated stores merge into one coherent OKF export.

  * *The Goal:* Make people *feel* why an open at-rest format changes everything — memory you can read, version, review, and carry anywhere.

## Question

What primary data table or documented reproducible query matches all nine values below for Roi Et province (TH45), males not in the labor force because of studies, Quarter 2? Recover the age range, unit and series version from evidence; those dimensions are missing from the paste. Thailand’s National Statistical Office (NSO) is a proposed source family, not an authenticated publisher of this series.

## Starting evidence

The held native API `/raw` field of [1fad07cb](https://pastebin.k4be.pl/view/1fad07cb) contains this complete 197-byte UTF-8 body, including its final newline (SHA256 `d1fa02c2009b9bdc5f861a85dfb204c59c2dca2ff8b35b53d9f8395aa5e065f7`):

```text
Roi Et province (TH45) - Males not in labor force because of studies, Quarter 2
2013: 46,308
2014: 32,212
2015: 35,083
2016: 36,227
2017: 40,810
2018: 36,313
2019: 35,040
2020: 38,827
2021: 37,842
```

The separate native title is `Roi Et province (TH45) male studies Q2 2013-2021`. The completed independent review of three objects distinguishes two partial titles from their actual bodies:

| Native object | Complete title | Complete body |
|---|---|---|
| [6db42cfc](https://pastebin.k4be.pl/view/6db42cfc) | `ROIETA1 2013 46308 2014 32212 2015 35083` | `x` |
| [d826348b](https://pastebin.k4be.pl/view/d826348b) | `ROIETA 2013 46308 2014 32212 2015 35083` | `Roi Et data segment1` |

The two titles carry the 2013–2015 pairs in order. Removing only the comma from each full-table value yields the title’s digit string; the strings are not literally equal before that transformation. Neither fragment body contains those pairs. These titles do not independently supply the full task filter or the 2016–2021 rows, and their correspondence establishes no parent/reply relationship.

The wider retained set includes five value-only titles, `ROIETA4`–`ROIETA8` ([8812970e](https://pastebin.k4be.pl/view/8812970e), [21c68f36](https://pastebin.k4be.pl/view/21c68f36), [5d1004ff](https://pastebin.k4be.pl/view/5d1004ff), [64d1bc5e](https://pastebin.k4be.pl/view/64d1bc5e), [e3657127](https://pastebin.k4be.pl/view/e3657127)), whose complete bodies are `x`. These titles carry ordered value chunks without explicit years; their order alone supplies neither literal year labels nor the complete filters.

## Acceptance criteria

An answer should provide:

- An exact public source URL and table/series identifier, or a documented query with enough filter and extraction detail to reproduce the result.
- Evidence for the entire selector conjunction: Roi Et/TH45, males, not in the labor force, studies, Quarter 2; document the source’s age range, unit and version/revision explicitly. Preserve a missing dimension as unresolved.
- A year-by-year comparison of all nine values, retaining original strings and identifying any comma removal, scaling, rounding or calendar conversion. A wrong province, sex, status, reason or quarter is a nonmatch. A complete match requires all nine year/value pairs under documented equivalent transformations and a supported series version; unexplained differences remain partial.
- Source captures and hashes, acquisition clocks, and the source’s own publication/version assertions separately. Preserve reproducible comparison steps.

An official hostname, an annual average, a different-quarter table or a coincident single value is insufficient. A prior indexed NSO table concerns Quarter 3 of 2003; it supports only the proposed source family and cannot supply missing filters for this series.

## Partial results and limits

A retained source table or reproducible query that establishes only part of the series can be a useful partial result. Missing dimensions, rows or unexplained differences remain open; a partial does not satisfy all criteria.

### What

CI emits a `transformers` log warning from `Trainer.train()` on essentially every trainer test:

```
[transformers] The tokenizer has new PAD/BOS/EOS tokens that differ from the model config and generation config. The model config and generation config were aligned accordingly, being updated with the tokenizer's values. Updated tokens: {'eos_token_id': 151645, 'bos_token_id': None, 'pad_token_id': 151643}.
```

462 lines in a single job, across 22 distinct `Updated tokens: {...}` variants. It is by far the largest single source of warning output in the run (about 84% of all warning lines).

CI run: https://github.com/huggingface/trl/actions/runs/34088542293/job/101637190203

Top variants by count:

| Count | `Updated tokens` |
|---|---|
| 313 | `{'eos_token_id': 151645, 'bos_token_id': None, 'pad_token_id': 151643}` |
| 24 | `{'eos_token_id': 151645}` |
| 21 | `{'eos_token_id': 1, 'bos_token_id': 2, 'pad_token_id': 0}` |
| 14 | `{'eos_token_id': 200002, 'bos_token_id': 199998, 'pad_token_id': 199999}` |
| 13 | `{'eos_token_id': 151645, 'bos_token_id': None, 'pad_token_id': 151645}` |
| 12 | `{'bos_token_id': None, 'pad_token_id': 151643}` |
| 65 | 16 further variants |

Affected tests: the warning is emitted from `Trainer.train()`, so it fires in every test that trains, across `tests/test_sft_trainer.py`, `tests/test_dpo_trainer.py`, `tests/test_grpo_trainer.py`, `tests/test_rloo_trainer.py`, `tests/test_kto_trainer.py`, `tests/test_reward_trainer.py` and `tests/test_distillation_trainer.py`.

Note: unlike the warnings tracked in #6447, #6466, #6555, #6580, #6848, #6849 and #7018, this one is a `logging` record, not a `warnings` warning. It does not appear in the pytest warnings summary and cannot be silenced with a `filterwarnings` entry in `pyproject.toml`. It reaches the job log because `make test` passes `-s`.

The tests themselves pass; for now this is warning noise only.

### When it started

This is not a recent regression. The warning was introduced upstream in `transformers` 4.56.0, by https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/38441 (merged 2025-08-12), which is at or below TRL's declared floor of `transformers>=4.56.2`. It has therefore been present across the whole supported range, and there is no commit or dependency bump to bisect to.

### Next steps

Investigate the root cause, then decide what is actionable on the TRL side, what belongs to the tiny test models, and what should be reported upstream.
title: CI emits 462 `transformers` `Trainer` log warnings: "The tokenizer has new PAD/BOS/EOS tokens that differ from the model config and generation config"

## Responsibility

Persistent coordination/progress record for the **early-release Exploration & Colonization** workstream.

## Branch

`work/exploration-colonization`

Created from validated shared `integration` head `fc46e90afd09e7dbd2fea8a3fd5f006f6416da79`.

## Scope ownership

This workstream owns the exploration/colonization simulation seams needed for the first playable release: exploration missions, per-civilization survey state/progress, fair-information acquisition, scout/science role behavior, colonization eligibility/mission flow, extrasolar settlement founding, and narrow outpost foundations when appropriate.

It does **not** own ship construction, economy/logistics internals, strategic Civilization AI, UI presentation, diplomacy, combat, Adaptive Research internals, or secret discovery content.

## Existing foundation found

- `ExplorationSimulation` already moves physical fleets through fog of war and triggers contact.
- `CivilizationKnowledgeState` currently stores only known-system/known-civilization sets; it has no survey depth/progress/confidence/timestamps.
- scout/science roles exist physically, but arrival currently treats an unknown system as immediately surveyed; science differs mostly in sensor range/event wording.
- `ColonizationSimulation` already uses physical colony fleets, but a known system is treated as sufficient knowledge for colonization and colony founding hard-codes 85M population.
- integrated Shipbuilding reserves 250M population for a colony ship during construction, but that reserved population is currently discarded when the completed fleet is created rather than carried into the colony mission.
- shared `integration` currently uses save format v7 for shipyard persistence.

## Dependencies / coordination

- Shipbuilding/Fleets (`dev/0.0.7-shipbuilding-reconcile`, integrated): vessel roles and colony-ship population reservation/handoff.
- Solar Economy & Logistics (`work/solar-economy-logistics`): future authoritative operational reach, supply/support and colony-support contracts.
- Civilization AI (`work/civilization-ai`): will consume legitimate known-system/survey/colonization-candidate views.
- UI (`work/ui-player-experience`): will consume read-only survey/mission/candidate state and issue player commands.
- Testing/Release (`work/testing-release`): save/load, deterministic and regression coverage.
- Species/Race (`work/species-race-mechanics`): future species-relative habitability; its current candidate save-v8 work means this branch will not independently claim a conflicting save-v8 migration without coordination.

## First implementation target

Introduce staged per-civilization system survey knowledge and make scout/science roles mechanically distinct: sensor detection remains detection, scouts produce a first-pass reconnaissance state, science vessels perform deeper survey progress, and colonization requires legitimately acquired full survey information before authoritative planet/resource facts may be used.

The colony-population handoff and persistence migration are the next tightly coupled correctness items and will be coordinated through the shared integration/save boundary rather than silently creating a competing schema.

Run log for the cloud maintenance routines that maintain this repo (scheduled Claude Code agents, run by Anthropic — not on a dev machine). They mirror the set running against `pawellisowski/floless.app`, adapted to this repo's actual gates: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test`, on the pinned toolchain.

Every run posts one line here as its final action, **including runs that do nothing**. That is the point: these routines are designed to open no PR when there is nothing to fix, which makes a correct quiet run indistinguishable from a crashed one unless each run says so explicitly.

Each line records: date, which review ran, gate results, and either the PR opened or the reason none was.

**On the Codex rule.** CLAUDE.md §"PR review — non-negotiable" says Codex reviews first. Codex is not installed in the routine container and cannot be without an OpenAI credential in the environment plus egress that has not been tested. These routines therefore run the documented fallback — the local reviewer — and must say so explicitly on every PR rather than implying a cross-model pass happened. Cross-model review of routine PRs happens on the maintainer's machine, where Codex is installed.

**Nothing merges itself.** Every run ends at a reviewable PR against `main`, or at silence. Pushing and merging to `main` still require explicit approval, per CLAUDE.md §"Git workflow".

Close this issue only if the routines are retired.
title: Routine log — cloud maintenance routines

# English

## HER Hack-Astron #6 | Spark-X2.5 Math Reasoning Challenge

Put Spark-X2.5's mathematical reasoning to a real, honest, reproducible test.

For this challenge, obtain XHToken/Spark-X2.5-4B or Spark-X2.5-1.7B from Hugging Face (or a mirror such as ModelScope), run a real math-reasoning evaluation or case study, and publish the complete, reproducible result in the corresponding model's Hugging Face Discussions. After publishing it, reply to this event's GitHub Issue with the Discussion link to enter.

- Event page (GitHub Issues): https://github.com/XHToken/Spark-X2.5/issues
- Hugging Face model collection: https://huggingface.co/collections/XHToken/spark-x25
- Spark-X2.5-4B: https://huggingface.co/XHToken/Spark-X2.5-4B
- Spark-X2.5-1.7B: https://huggingface.co/XHToken/Spark-X2.5-1.7B
- Spark-X2.5-4B Discussions: https://huggingface.co/XHToken/Spark-X2.5-4B/discussions
- Spark-X2.5-1.7B Discussions: https://huggingface.co/XHToken/Spark-X2.5-1.7B/discussions
- Mainland China mirror (recommended): https://www.modelscope.cn/collections/XHToken/Spark-X25

## Schedule

- Submissions open: September 7, 2026
- Challenge period: September 7–13, 2026
- Submission deadline: September 13, 2026, 24:00 Beijing Time (UTC+8)
- Judging and award distribution: September 14–20, 2026

## Challenge Tracks

Choose one track or combine several:

- Standard math benchmarks: evaluate on public sets such as GSM8K, MATH, MATH-500, AIME 2024/2025, OlympiadBench, or MinervaMath, and report pass@1 (and pass@k where relevant) with a clear scoring script
- Competition and olympiad problems: run AMC / AIME / IMO-style or national-olympiad problems and analyze where the model succeeds or fails
- Step-by-step reasoning quality: assess chain-of-thought correctness, not just final answers — catch right-answer-wrong-reasoning and arithmetic slips
- Tool-assisted math: combine the model with a code interpreter / Python / SymPy (program-aided reasoning) and compare against no-tool baselines
- Formal and proof-oriented math: theorem proving, proof sketching, or Lean/Coq-style formalization attempts, with honest reporting of verification
- Multilingual math: test math word problems and reasoning across languages (e.g. MGSM), and report per-language accuracy
- Robustness and contamination checks: perturbed / paraphrased / numerically-swapped problems, and evidence that results are not from memorized test data
- Decoding and prompting study: effect of temperature, self-consistency / majority voting, sampling budget, and prompt format on math accuracy — with cost trade-offs
- Comparative evaluation: compare Spark-X2.5 with larger models or other similar-size open models under one identical methodology

## How to Submit

1. Spark-X2.5 is licensed under Apache 2.0 and requires no additional usage agreement. Follow the repository's CODE_OF_CONDUCT and SECURITY policies.
2. Install and sign in with the official Hugging Face CLI:

       pip install -U huggingface_hub
       hf auth login

3. Download and record a pinned revision:

       hf download XHToken/Spark-X2.5-4B --revision <commit-sha>

   Participants in Mainland China may use ModelScope / Modelers / SCNet / SourceFind mirrors. State the source and revision used.

4. Run a real math evaluation and retain publishable run logs, the exact command lines, the scoring/parsing script, raw model outputs, environment details, and screenshots.
5. Create a public post in the Discussions section for the model you actually used:

   - Spark-X2.5-1.7B: https://huggingface.co/XHToken/Spark-X2.5-1.7B/discussions
   - Spark-X2.5-4B: https://huggingface.co/XHToken/Spark-X2.5-4B/discussions

   The title only needs to contain `HER Hack-Astron #6`, for example:

       [HER Hack-Astron #6] <math evaluation title>

6. Reply to this event's GitHub Issue with the direct link to your Discussion post. This completes your submission. Examples:

       https://huggingface.co/XHToken/Spark-X2.5-1.7B/discussions/<number>
       https

### Working name

`mermail-release-handoff`

### What workflow does it cover?

A read-only-first release handoff workflow for a user-selected Mermail email thread. It would turn release discussion into an evidence-linked handoff containing the stated version, artifact links, verification instructions, rollback notes, outstanding questions, and explicitly recorded acceptance decisions.

The aim is to make a release handoff reproducible for the next person, not to send another generic email summary. Each confirmed field would retain its source message reference. Missing or conflicting facts would remain unresolved rather than being filled in. A proposed reply would stay local until the user separately approves the exact recipients and content.

The workflow would use the live Mermail tool schemas for bounded thread retrieval and email context. It would not execute attachment contents, follow verification links, change workspace settings, or use wallet/PayBox tools.

Planned verification would include incomplete release instructions, conflicting version numbers, a delivery message without acceptance, and instructions embedded in email that attempt to change the workflow. A client demo would use a dedicated test mailbox and show the actual Mermail calls and resulting handoff. That integration test has not been run yet.

Reported from this repository's own 0.9.2 release run, on 0.9.1. Follows #237, which is what makes the remaining prompts visible.

## The shape, before the detail

The consent record #237 introduced buys silence for a command that is *nothing but* worktree creation. A command that is worktree creation **plus anything else** still asks — and the guard already has a third answer for exactly that case, on its other entry point, with the argument for it written out.

## What happens

`hooks/worktree-guard.py:1785`, the Bash path:

```python
consented=("allow" if only_creates_a_worktree(command, cwd) else "ask"),
```

So with a consent record present, `git worktree add ../wt f` is silent and `git worktree add ../wt f 2>&1 | tail -2` asks. One pipe is the difference.

`only_creates_a_worktree`'s docstring gives the right reason for not saying `allow` there, and it is not in dispute: `permissionDecision: "allow"` bypasses the user's own permission settings for the **whole tool call**, and the eleven shapes measured at `d82a02c` — a command substitution, backticks, `>`, `>>`, `<`, a subshell, a heredoc, `sudo`, `env VAR=`, a bare `VAR=` and a trailing `&` — are what an unbounded allow signs for. Two of them were run in a real shell and did what the shell says they do.

**The question this issue raises is not whether to widen the allow. It is whether `ask` is the right other answer.**

## The guard already answers this, one entry point over

`guard_worktree_creation` takes a third value, and the Agent/Task path passes it (`:1849`) with the reasoning written beside it:

> Silent rather than `allow`, where the Bash path allows. This call is a worktree creation PLUS an agent with a prompt, and the record is about the first half only; silence is the guard withdrawing its objection, which is the whole of what the record establishes. Whatever the harness wants to ask about running the agent is not the guard's to remove.

Every clause of that applies unchanged to a compound Bash command. It is a worktree creation plus other segments; the record is about the first half only; whatever the harness wants to ask about the rest of the command line is not the guard's to remove — and it is also not the guard's to *ask*, which is what it does today.

`silent` grants nothing. `guard_worktree_creation` returns without responding (`:1499-1500`), and the harness's own permission system then judges the command on its own terms. The user's `permissions.deny` on `Bash(sudo:*)` still fires; it is simply not a worktree guard that fires it.

## What it costs, measured on this run

The 0.9.2 release run created five worktrees. Two of the confirmations it paid were this case, both because the command carried a pipe or a `cd` — and the repository's own `CLAUDE.md` instructs sessions to batch independent runs into one call, which is what produces a compound command in the first place.

So the rule that shapes the command and the arm that stays quiet for it disagree, and the session pays a stop for following the rule. `[worktree-ok]` is no way out either: that site asks too, by design.

## What would close it

`consented=("allow" if only_creates_a_worktree(command, cwd) else "silent")` on the Bash path, with the Agent path's argument moved somewhere both entry points read from rather than duplicated.

**The behaviour change, stated as what a person sees:**

| Command, with a consent record present | Now | After |
|---|---|---|
| `git worktree add ../wt f` | silent | silent |
| `git worktree add ../wt f \| tail -2` | confirm | judged by the user's own permission settings |
| `sudo git worktree add ../wt f` | confirm | judged by the user's own permission settings, where `Bash(sudo:*)` already lives |

The third row is the one to argue about, and it is why this is an issue rather than a one-line change.

## Not verified

**Whether `silent` on this path leaves every shape in the `d82a02c` list judged by something.** The claim rests on the harness applying its normal per
title: fix: a consent record buys silence only for a bare creation, so batching the command back costs the prompt #237 removed

A SHAPE, not a bug: seven measured instances across the 2026-09-05/07 campaign, in six different verbs. In each one bp REFUSES correctly and then describes a way forward that the caller cannot take -- a flag that does not exist, a field the response withheld, a discriminator documented nowhere but inside the refusal string itself. The refusal is honest about the NO and dishonest about the next step, which is worse than a bare refusal because it sends the caller somewhere that does not exist.

THE SEVEN:
(1) The dedup 409 demanded an id it withheld from its own response. THIS ONE IS FIXED (#14383, 'make the dedup 409 appealable -- it named a required id it withheld'), and it is the corrected sibling that vouches for the other five: the class was accepted as real and repaired once, in isolation, without anyone looking for the shape.
(2) A refusal hints at ?dataset= while get and claim expose no --dataset flag.
(3) --miss reads as a correction verb; met never flips, so an operator who reaches for it to lower a wrong met is silently not doing that. The verb that DOES lower it (--withdraw) is not named at the point of confusion.
(4) The criteria_override discriminator ('unpayable in principle', not merely 'unmet at close time') is discoverable ONLY by reading a refusal string. It gates a write that is as permanent as a stamp.
(5) THE PAGER. Omitting --cursor selects the limit/offset pager, which returns has_more: true with NO next_cursor -- the caller is told there is more and handed nothing to fetch it with. This appears in TWO verbs FIVE WEEKS APART, which is the argument that the fix belongs in the PAGER and not in the callers: fixing the callers leaves the next paginated endpoint born broken.
(6) Measured 2026-09-07 while filing this row: three verbs of the same CLI return their rows under THREE different envelope keys -- bp task ready under 'docs', bp doc ls tag --all under 'documents', bp task get under 'doc' -- and no --help names any of them. This is the same hazard the fleet already took a hit on when a parser keyed on 'tasks'/'id' read ZERO rows out of a 310 KB response and printed a confident EMPTY QUEUE. An empty read and an empty result are indistinguishable downstream.

(7) FOUND 2026-09-07 WHILE FILING THIS ROW, AND IT IS THE SHARPEST INSTANCE IN THE SET, because the named remedy is not merely unreachable -- it is the WRONG remedy for the refusal that names it. `bp auth me` refuses with hint "Send a valid token via the Authorization: Bearer header; tokens are dataset-scoped." But capabilities.ex:2853 declares auth.me as GET /v1/auth/me, "the current user's account for the ACTIVE SESSION" -- a user LOGIN session. The endpoint does not want a bearer token; it wants a login. An operator who follows the hint supplies a credential that was never the missing thing, and concludes their token is bad when it is fine. Measured on a box where `bp whoami` simultaneously reports auth_tier: admin off the API token -- the two verbs measure different identities and both answers are true at once, which is exactly why the hint's misdirection is so convincing. Instances (2) through (6) are remedies the caller cannot REACH; this one actively sends them somewhere wrong, so it costs MORE than silence would.

<!-- barkpark:acceptance:start -->
### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] RE-DERIVE THE POPULATION FROM THE CODE; DO NOT TRUST THIS LIST. The figures here are a measurement with a timestamp (2026-09-08) over a hint table any lane can edit: 14 DEFECTIVE is load-bearing and was independently re-derived, while the 60 refusal/hint strings across two tables and the 54 naming an actionable remedy are APPROXIMATE and were NOT re-run. A DOC PAGE, A CHANGELOG ENTRY, OR A NOTE IN A BRIEF DOES NOT SATISFY THIS CRITERION. For every DEFECTIVE hint in the derived set, the refusal either EXPOSES the remedy it names -- a flag the caller can actually pass, a field the response actually carries -- or it STOPS naming it. THE SET IS DERIVED BY GREPPING THE REFUSA
title: bp refusals name a remedy the CLI does not expose, and pagers say has_more while handing back nothing to fetch it with

A fresh admitted lane forwards only to its exact authorized public recipient, while duplicate tokens, hostile framing and exhausted resources cannot create work or leak across contexts.

Parent: #50. Depends on: #54.

## Contract and ownership

ADR-0081 and the parent reading route are authoritative. Focused owners:

- `docs/technical/private-admission.md#resource-classes-and-admission`
- `docs/technical/protected-route-protocol.md#bounded-lane-framing`
- `docs/technical/protected-route-protocol.md#flow-control-and-scheduling`

## Implementation mechanism

- Distinguish authenticated outer Carrier OPEN (receiving Node itself, finite inner-handshake lane) from admitted inner forwarding OPEN (exact eligible next Node). Outer identity grants no Endpoint token admission or arbitrary onward dial. Test cross-state frames, old ALPN/profile/LegBinding, direct non-adjacent Endpoint access and invalid optimistic handshake forwarding.
- Implement the exact ARDP generation-3 frame/state machine, channel-local odd/even monotonic lane IDs, authenticated HELLO/profile binding, typed purposes and operation bounds. Reject unknown/oversized/trailing/padding errors before allocation or dialing.
- Endpoint durably marks a token potentially spent before presentation. Receiver validates the deterministic common challenge/signature, commits its exclusive spend tuple and reserves capacity before forwarding; bind accepted state to the local TLS exporter and lane.
- Implement classes: control 64 KiB/30 s; forwarding 32 MiB/1,800 s; publication 1 MiB/600 s. Hour windows bound redemption; a live lease ends at its original earliest authority/deadline bound. Replenishment adds bytes only, never time, peer or context.
- Enforce 256 work children plus two control lanes per forwarding channel, 1,024 role channels/1,024 children per duty, 64 KiB lane credit, 4 MiB prefix/64 MiB Node queues, 128 verifications/s and four concurrent checks. Child work charges the same parent reserve.
- Use bounded round-robin 16 KiB frames, reserved control capacity and at most 1 ms coalescing of available work. EOF preserves reverse traffic; CLOSE/cancel joins descendants and owned readers/writers.
- Retain only actual-work Node Carriers for 120 s, with exact current peer/profile keys and 32-per-Node cap. Fresh child TLS/admission remains mandatory. State changes invalidate reuse; no eager empty pool or Endpoint-identity forwarding field.

## Acceptance and evidence

- Concurrent duplicate spend across connections/listeners, ambiguity, journal failure/restore, stolen issuer key and bootstrap/crypto floods cannot exceed honest local limits or authorize a weaker path.
- Malformed kinds/lengths, ID reuse, credit overflow, slow lanes and control floods preserve independent progress and finite memory; rejection performs no forbidden dial/effect.
- Both Carriers support identical receiving semantics and negative vectors. No automatic Carrier/profile fallback or discarded earlier failure.
- P2/P3/P4/P5/P7/P8 boundary tests and required repository checks; record actual queues, work and lifecycle outcomes.

Only one C0 implementation issue may be in progress. Keep changes within the selected contract and actual one-human/Codex capacity. Routine file/algorithm choices remain with the implementer; a changed authority, privacy condition, protocol, dependency selection or required budget returns to design before dependent work. Update factual owners with the implementing change; preserve unrelated work.
title: Enforce receiver-local one-use admission and bounded protected lane forwarding
